issues.title: work_finder: 'main-health gate halted dispatch for N of N repos' fires during every drain — attribute the hold to its real cause
issues.body:
## Problem

`work_finder.rs` (around line 3287 on main) logs

`work_finder: main-health gate halted dispatch for {} of {} repo(s) — their ready issues held until their main is green again`

whenever a workspace is `halted`. But `halted` also covers holds that have nothing to do with main health, most visibly an **auto-update drain**. On 2026-09-29 every drain-and-restart roll produced "halted dispatch for 60 of 60 repo(s)" 30–60 seconds after `drain-and-restart triggered`, even though every main was green. An operator reading the log concludes all 60 mains are red. The same conflation shows up in #9131 (the status capacity line) and #9017 (the queue snapshot).

## Proposal

Attribute the hold to its real cause in this log line, using #9017's typed hold-cause work (PR #9267) once that lands. Until then, at least skip or reword the main-health line while a drain or roll is armed:

`work_finder: dispatch paused (auto-update drain) — N ready issue(s) held`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] While a drain or roll is armed and every main is green, no log line attributes the pause to the main-health gate.
- [ ] A genuinely red main still produces the main-health line.
- [ ] A test covers a drain with all mains green.

issues.title: clippy -D warnings fails on macOS: field_reassign_with_default in host_pressure::sample_macos
issues.body:
`cargo clippy -p loom-daemon --bins --tests -- -D warnings` fails on macOS at current `main` (found while gating #9548 work on 65634118b):

```
error: field assignment outside of initializer for an instance created with Default::default()
   --> loom-daemon/src/host_pressure.rs:207:5
207 |     out.mem_total_bytes = sysctl_u64("hw.memsize");
```

`sample_macos()` is `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`, so Linux CI never compiles it and stays green, while every macOS host running the documented clippy gate is red. Last touched by 64aeb6689 ("fix: correct swap-in/out unit conversion and admission-reason doc gap").

Fix is the one clippy suggests (initialize `mem_total_bytes` in the struct literal with `..HostPressure::default()`); verified locally that clippy is otherwise clean with it applied.

<!-- loom:provenance v1 build=unknown unknown unknown prompts=unknown unknown sweep=none story=rjwalters/loom#9548 trace=40ea34562978f9181fe215b552591177 host=robb-studio base=65634118b23e4db5f6171c13fdaf857badb39324 run=none -->


---

## Curator enrichment

**Complexity**: trivial (one-line refactor in one file).

### Fix
In `loom-daemon/src/host_pressure.rs` `sample_macos()`, replace
```rust
let mut out = HostPressure::default();
out.mem_total_bytes = sysctl_u64("hw.memsize");
```
with
```rust
let mut out = HostPressure {
    mem_total_bytes: sysctl_u64("hw.memsize"),
    ..HostPressure::default()
};
```
`mut` stays: later statements (inside `if let` blocks) still assign `mem_available_bytes`, `mem_compressed_bytes`, `swap_*`.

### Other sites checked
- `sample_linux()`: first field assignment is inside `if let`, so the lint does not fire (and Linux CI is green).
- `parse_meminfo` / `parse_vmstat` / `parse_vm_stat_output`: assignments happen inside a `for` loop, not immediately after construction. No change needed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p loom-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes on macOS.
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p loom-daemon --features otlp --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes on macOS.
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon host_pressure` passes.
- [ ] Pure refactor: no behavior change; diff confined to `sample_macos()`.

issues.title: loom:blocked: enforce a machine-checkable reason at apply-time, and re-check on issue close
issues.body:
## Original Issue

## Summary

Follow-up to #8927, items 1+2 of that issue's own "Suggested fix" list — explicitly out of scope for #8927 itself, which only shipped items 3+4 (a fleet-wide pre-wave advisory scan, `check-stale-blocked.sh` / `loom-daemon check-stale-blocked`).

#8927 closes the *detection* gap: every open `loom:blocked` issue is now re-checked once per sweep pre-flight, and a stale or undocumented block is surfaced to stderr. What is still missing is *prevention* and *instant* re-check:

1. **Require a machine-checkable reason at apply-time.** Nothing currently stops `gh issue edit N --add-label loom:blocked` with no `Blocked by #N` / `Depends on #N` / `## Dependencies` entry anywhere. #8927's own evidence row #180 is exactly this case. Enforcing this would need changes at every call site that applies the label — `curator.md`, `builder.md`, `judge.md`, `champion-*.md` — not a single script.

2. **Re-check triggered at issue-close time.** When an issue closes, look for open issues citing it as a blocker (the same reference vocabulary `dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh` / `check-stale-blocked.sh` already parse) and comment on them immediately, rather than waiting for the next sweep's pre-wave scan. This is the highest-value moment per #8927's own argument (issue #178 would have been surfaced the very next day). Natural home is `merge-pr.sh`'s post-merge/close path, alongside its existing `loom:building` label-strip logic (#6199).

Both are deferred, per #8927's Curator scoping note, because each is an event-triggered/role-prompt-policy change across multiple call sites — a different shape of change from a standalone advisory script, and each deserves its own pressure-testing pass per `.loom/docs/role-prompt-authoring.md` before landing.

## Why now

`check-stale-blocked.sh` (#8927) substantially covers item 2's *intent* already — a sweep pre-flight surfaces staleness within days rather than months — so this follow-up is lower urgency than #8927 was. Item 1 (apply-time enforcement) remains the cheaper, more valuable half: it prevents the #180 shape (no blocker recorded at all) from recurring, rather than only detecting it after the fact.

## Suggested scope

- Item 1: audit and update every `gh issue edit --add-label "loom:blocked"` call site in `curator.md`/`builder.md`/`judge.md`/`champion-*.md` to require a `Blocked by #N`/`Depends on #N`/`## Dependencies` entry be recorded in the same action (or the immediately preceding comment).
- Item 2: extend `merge-pr.sh`'s post-merge/close path to run `check-stale-blocked.sh`'s existing per-issue classifier (`loom-daemon check-stale-blocked` or a narrower single-issue variant) against every open issue citing the just-closed issue/PR number, and comment on any that go stale.

Both should reuse the existing `dep_recheck`/`stale_blocked` Rust modules (`loom-daemon/src/dep_recheck/`, `loom-daemon/src/stale_blocked.rs`) rather than adding new parsing.

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->
<!-- loom:points=8 -->

### Verified correction to scope (2026-09-28, verified against `origin/main` @ `4aeed2e56a`)

The issue body's item 1 lists `judge.md`/`champion-*.md` as call sites needing an update alongside `curator.md`/`builder.md`. A grep of every `add-label "loom:blocked"` occurrence under `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/` against current `main` finds it only in `curator.md`, `builder.md`, `builder-complexity.md`, and `guide.md` (not named in the original list, but a real call site) — `judge.md` has none, and the only `loom:blocked` reference in `champion-pr-merge.md` *removes* the label, never adds it. Re-run this grep before implementing, since it is a point-in-time snapshot:

```bash
grep -rn 'add-label "loom:blocked"' defaults/.claude/commands/loom/
```

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Item 1**: every `gh issue edit --add-label "loom:blocked"` call site found by the grep above (currently `curator.md`, `builder.md`, `builder-complexity.md`, `guide.md`) documents — in the role prompt itself — that applying the label requires a `Blocked by #N` / `Depends on #N` / `Requires #N` line or a `## Dependencies` entry to already exist in the issue body or the immediately preceding comment, in the same pass as the label edit.
- [ ] **Item 1**: the change has gone through a pressure-testing pass per `.loom/docs/role-prompt-authoring.md` before landing, since it touches multiple role-prompt call sites (per the issue's own deferral rationale above).
- [ ] **Item 2**: `merge-pr.sh`'s post-merge/close path runs the existing stale-blocked classifier (`loom-daemon check-stale-blocked`, or a narrower single-issue variant added for this purpose) against every currently-open issue whose body or comments cite the just-closed issue/PR number via the same reference vocabulary `dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh`/`check-stale-blocked.sh` already parse, and posts a comment on any of them found to be newly stale.
- [ ] **Item 2**: this reuses `loom-daemon/src/dep_recheck/` and `loom-daemon/src/stale_blocked.rs` for reference parsing and classification — no second parser is added (per `.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md`, new logic is a daemon subcommand, not a new script).
- [ ] Item 1 and item 2 may land as separate PRs, since they touch disjoint files and the issue itself treats them as two suggested-scope bullets — but both are required before this issue closes.

### Implementation Guidance

- **Item 1** is a role-prompt documentation/policy change, not new executable logic — each named file gets its own reminder text near its existing `add-label "loom:blocked"` call site(s), in the style curator.md's own "Adding Dependencies" section already models (require the `## Dependencies` entry or the `Blocked by #N` line to be present at the point of labeling). There is no single shared script to change for this half; the enforcement is prose the agent follows, exactly like every other labeling rule in these files.
- **Item 2** is the more mechanical half: `merge-pr.sh` already has a post-merge/close section that strips `loom:building` from referenced issues (`_strip_closed_issue_building_labels`, `_strip_one_closed_issue_building_label`, near line 1556-1670 as of `4aeed2e56a` — re-check line numbers before editing, they drift). Add a sibling step there that, for the just-closed issue/PR number, finds open issues citing it as a blocker (reuse `dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh`'s or the Rust `dep_recheck` module's existing reference extraction) and invokes the stale-blocked classifier on each, posting a comment when the classifier reports the block has cleared.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/curator.md` - add/confirm the machine-checkable-reason requirement at its `add-label "loom:blocked"` call sites
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder.md` - same, multiple call sites
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-complexity.md` - same
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/guide.md` - same (not named in the original issue body, found via the grep above)
- `.loom/scripts/merge-pr.sh` - extend the post-merge/close path (near the existing `loom:building` label-strip logic) to invoke the stale-blocked classifier against open issues citing the just-closed issue/PR
- `loom-daemon/src/dep_recheck/` - reused for reference parsing; may need a narrower single-issue entry point for item 2
- `loom-daemon/src/stale_blocked.rs` - reused for per-issue classification; may need a narrower single-issue CLI variant (`loom-daemon check-stale-blocked` today runs fleet-wide)
- `defaults/scripts/check-stale-blocked.sh` - existing thin-stub entry point; item 2 likely wants an equivalent invoked per-issue from `merge-pr.sh` rather than the fleet-wide sweep pre-flight path

### Test Plan

- [ ] Manual verification: attempt to apply `loom:blocked` with no `Blocked by #N`/`Dependencies` reference recorded under the updated role-prompt guidance and confirm an agent following it declines or flags the omission; then apply it with a valid reference and confirm it proceeds normally.
- [ ] Manual verification: close an issue that a second, still-open issue cites as a blocker (`Blocked by #N`), and confirm `merge-pr.sh`'s post-close path comments on the second issue promptly, rather than waiting for the next sweep's pre-wave `check-stale-blocked.sh` scan.
- [ ] Automated tests: extend the existing `dep_recheck`/`stale_blocked` Rust unit tests (and/or `.loom/scripts/tests/test-dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh`-style shell tests) to cover the close-triggered re-check path added to `merge-pr.sh`.
- [ ] Edge cases: an issue closed via merge vs. `gh issue close --reason "not planned"`; a blocker reference that lives only in a comment, not the body; two or more open issues citing the same closed blocker in one close event.

issues.title: CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS: a sibling-renamed credential dir (.loom/tokens.<suffix>/) escapes all four mirrored defences at once
issues.body:
## Problem

`CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` in `loom-daemon/src/init/post_init.rs` is the single
source of truth for "paths that hold a live secret". Its documented matching
contract is:

> a pattern ending in `/` is a directory and matches the directory itself and
> everything under it; any other pattern is an exact file path. **No globs.**

That contract means `.loom/tokens/` matches `.loom/tokens/` and its contents —
and **nothing else**. A *sibling* directory sharing the name as a prefix is
not covered:

```
.loom/tokens/x.token            -> MATCHES .loom/tokens/
.loom/tokens.bak-<timestamp>/x.token  -> NO MATCH
.loom/tokens.disabled-<ts>/x.token    -> NO MATCH
.loom/tokens-old/x.token              -> NO MATCH
```

This is not a one-off. The same literal list is mirrored, **by design and
enforced by CI** (`credential_class_tests`), into:

1. `.gitignore` (`.loom/tokens/`, line ~87)
2. `defaults/scripts/land-resync-commit.sh` — `LOOM_CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS`
3. `defaults/scripts/resync-installed.sh` — the printed `:!` pathspec

So a single rename of a credential directory to a sibling name moves it out
from under **all four defences at once**. The synchronisation CI enforces is
exactly what converts one gap into four: there is no diversity of matching
strategy to fall back on.

Note `.loom/*.bak` happens to catch `.loom/tokens.bak/` in `.gitignore` only —
an accident of a different rule, not covered by the credential class, and not
mirrored into the two shell guards.

Renaming a pool aside (`mv .loom/tokens .loom/tokens.<suffix>`) is a natural
operator move — the `.gitignore` file itself documents the
`name.bak-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)` convention for hand-made backups — which
makes this a foreseeable path, not an exotic one.

## Proposal

Extend the matching contract so a directory pattern also covers sibling paths
that extend its final component, then let `credential_class_tests` propagate
to the three mirrors.

Concretely: for a pattern `<dir>/`, also match `<dir>` followed by any
non-`/` suffix and then `/` or end — i.e. `.loom/tokens*`. Equivalent
`.gitignore` form: `.loom/tokens*/` alongside the existing entry.

Decisions this needs a reviewer to make, not assume:

- The "**No globs**" line is a deliberate design decision (it keeps the Rust
  and shell matchers byte-comparable). This proposal reopens it. Either widen
  the contract for *all* patterns uniformly, or introduce an explicit
  "directory + sibling-prefix" pattern kind. Prefer uniform if the shell
  mirror stays simple.
- Applies to the whole credential class, not just `tokens/`:
  `.loom/claude-config/`, `.loom/api-keys/`, `.loom/gh-config/`,
  `.loom/gh-config-by-owner/` have the identical exposure.
- `.loom/accounts.env` is an exact *file* pattern; decide whether
  `accounts.env.bak` should be covered too (it should).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `is_credential_leak_path(".loom/tokens.disabled-20260101T000000Z/a.token")`
      returns true.
- [ ] Same for the `claude-config`, `api-keys`, `gh-config`,
      `gh-config-by-owner` siblings.
- [ ] `git check-ignore` reports a sibling-renamed pool directory as ignored.
- [ ] `land-resync-commit.sh` refuses to land with a sibling-renamed pool dir
      present, both untracked (excluded, non-blocking) and tracked (hard stop).
- [ ] `credential_class_tests` still passes, i.e. all mirrors stay in sync.
- [ ] Matching contract doc comment in `post_init.rs` updated to state the new
      rule precisely.

## Related

Companion to the pre-commit content-scan issue — that one covers paths nobody
enumerated; this one closes a path we *should* have enumerated.

issues.title: ETA phase 3: start-v1 and land for unstarted issues from dispatch_plan + slot turnover
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Phase 3 of #9289 (ETA as a Loom primitive). Plan: Curator comment https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5867874254, operator decisions https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5869738711. **Depends on #9289 Phase 1** (core, heuristic registry, explanation schema, journal); do not start before it merges.

### Scope
- `start` ETA (and `land` for issues not yet started) from #9288's dispatch plan, merged in #9316: `position`, rows ahead in `next|queued`, `plan.slots.free`/`max_admissions_per_tick`, `tick_interval_secs`, `repo_cap` headroom, `in_slice`/`owning_shard`, and empirical slot-turnover (sweep durations).
- `position: null` gives no estimate (`no_dispatch_plan`/`blocked`). The time-boxed holds from #9311 (`held_until`) feed an honest start where available.
- The same explanation schema and journal, and it is backtestable with the phase-2 harness.

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Problem Statement

Today, any `loom:issue`-labeled issue with no running sweep and no open PR gets a blanket `NoEstimateReason::NoDispatchPlan` refusal — it is never even represented as a trackable item. This phase turns that into a real `start` estimate (when will this be dispatched?) and extends `land` to cover not-yet-started issues, using the dispatch plan (#9288) and empirical slot turnaround (#8929) that already exist on `main`.

### Current state, verified against `origin/main` @ `638bffab1` (2026-09-30)

- **Both stated dependencies are merged.** #9289 Phase 1 merged via PR #9355 (2026-09-28); #9288 (`dispatch_plan()`) merged via PR #9316 (2026-09-28). This phase's own "do not start before Phase 1 merges" gate is clear.
- **Phase 2 has also merged**, same day as this curation pass: #9325 (backfill + backtest harness) via PR #9578 (2026-09-30T01:54 UTC) — a few hours before this pass. Not a stated dependency of this phase, but it means the backtest harness this phase's own Acceptance Criteria reference already exists.
- **The `NoDispatchPlan` stub is already in place but is dead code outside its own unit tests.** `git grep -rn "unstarted_issue_reason" origin/main -- loom-daemon/src` returns only the definition (`loom-daemon/src/eta/labels.rs:78`) and `tests/primitives.rs` — nothing in `tracker.rs` calls it. `Tracker::estimate()`'s kind loop is hardcoded to `[Kind::Finish, Kind::Land]` (`eta/tracker.rs:1120`), and `Kind` (`eta/mod.rs:104`) has only `Finish`/`Land` variants — no `Start`.
- **Ready issues aren't tracked as `Item`s at all today.** `Tracker::on_listing` populates items from open-PR review-label listings; sweep-driven items arrive via bus events. There is no ingestion path today for a `loom:issue` row that has neither.
- **`eta::Stage` (`eta/mod.rs:126`) has 5 variants** (`SweepCurator`, `SweepBuilder`, `ReviewWait`, `Doctor`, `MergeWait`) — none represents "waiting for a dispatch slot."
- **`dispatch_plan` is already on `main` and unused by `eta/`.** `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/dispatch_plan.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/types/dispatch_plan.rs` publish `position` (1-based, plan order), `plan_state` (`running`/`next`/`queued`/`blocked`), `PlanSlots`, `PlanGate`, `tick_interval_secs`, and shard/slice fields per `ReadyQueueRow` — exactly what this issue's own Scope section names. No file under `loom-daemon/src/eta/` references it yet.
- **`SlotLedger` (`observability/ops/turnaround.rs`) already computes empirical turnaround**, but only as a running mean-ratio metric pair (`loom.dispatch.slot_turnaround` / `.samples`) fed by `sweep.global.completed`/`sweep.global.dispatch` bus events — it keeps no per-sample history and is not wired to `eta/history.rs`'s per-`(repo, stage)` quantile-grid model that every other stage uses.

### Implementation Guidance (a starting approach, not a spec — the design is this phase's judgement call)

1. Add a `Stage` variant for "ready, waiting for a dispatch slot" and a `Kind::Start` alongside the existing `Kind::Finish`/`Kind::Land`.
2. Feed `loom:issue` ready-queue rows into the tracker as `Item`s — likely a new `Tracker::on_ready_queue(rows, now)` mirroring `on_listing`'s shape, sourced from wherever the daemon already holds the tick's `dispatch_plan` output (`work_finder::last_tick_summary()` / `TickReport::plan_order`).
3. Build the new stage's per-`(repo, stage)` quantile grid from turnaround samples: extend `SlotLedger::observe` (or add a sibling) to record each sample through `eta/journal.rs` into `eta-stage-samples.jsonl`, not just the metric pair, so `eta/history.rs::StageSamples::select` can serve it like every other stage.
4. Replace the blanket `NoDispatchPlan` return in `unstarted_issue_reason` with a real estimate once the row has a `position`; keep the refusal only for rows `dispatch_plan` genuinely has no position for (e.g. `blocked`, or `queued` with no plan coverage).
5. For not-yet-started `land`: convolve the new `start` distribution with the existing post-dispatch stage chain, per the Phase 1 spec's resampling combinator (`eta/simulate.rs`) — extend it to prepend the new stage rather than building a second combinator.
6. Per the Phase 1 spec's accepted v0 simplification (stage independence): treat the new stage like the other four in the resampling combinator. Modeling correlation between queue position and post-dispatch durations is out of scope for this phase.

### Related open work (heads-up, not a dependency)

#9579 (filed off Phase 2 / PR #9578): `loom-daemon eta backtest --heuristic land-v1` currently scores **zero** land-v1 cases against real history — the promotion backtest gate (operator decision 2 on #9289) can't validate `land-v1` at all right now. This is a Phase 2 backtest-harness bug, not a gap in this phase's start/land-for-unstarted scope, so it isn't absorbed into this issue's Acceptance Criteria — but worth checking whether it's fixed before backtesting this phase's own changes, since the same broken gate would silently swallow this phase's regressions too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Kind::Start` exists and produces real quantiles (not a blanket refusal) for a `loom:issue`-labeled issue that has a `dispatch_plan` position and sufficient `Stage::Ready`-equivalent turnaround history.
- [ ] `land` estimates are produced for not-yet-started `loom:issue` issues (previously always `no_estimate_reason: no_dispatch_plan`) by convolving the new `start` distribution with the existing post-dispatch stage chain.
- [ ] A ready item with a `dispatch_plan` position but insufficient turnaround samples returns `insufficient_samples`, never a fabricated number.
- [ ] A ready item genuinely outside `dispatch_plan`'s coverage (blocked, no position) still returns `no_dispatch_plan` — the refusal narrows, it does not disappear.
- [ ] Every new/changed `eta.estimate` and `eta.outcome` emission still carries the full forensic provenance fields (heuristic id, `version`, full `revision` SHA, `tree_state`) required by the Phase 1 operator decision — no new code path bypasses this.
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon eta::` passes, including new tests for the ready-stage history selection, the ready-queue ingestion path, and the extended resampling combinator.
- [ ] A golden fixture pins `start-v1`'s (and the extended `land-v1`'s not-yet-started path) output over a fixed input, per the Phase 1 rule that a shipped heuristic id is immutable.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/eta/mod.rs` — add the new `Stage` variant and `Kind::Start`.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/labels.rs` — replace/extend `unstarted_issue_reason`'s blanket `NoDispatchPlan` return.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/tracker.rs` — new ready-queue ingestion path; extend the `[Kind::Finish, Kind::Land]` loop to include `Kind::Start` for ready items.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/history.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/eta/grid.rs` — serve the new stage's samples through the existing per-`(repo, stage)` quantile-grid path.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/simulate.rs` — extend the resampling combinator to prepend the new stage for not-yet-started `land` estimates.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/heuristics/land_v1.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/eta/heuristics/finish_v1.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/eta/heuristics/mod.rs` — wire `Kind::Start` through the registry and heuristic dispatch.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/turnaround.rs` — extend `SlotLedger` (or add a sibling) to record per-sample turnaround into the eta journal, not just the metric pair.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/journal.rs` — the write path for the new stage's samples.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/fixtures/` — new golden fixture(s) for `start-v1`.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/tests/`, `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/turnaround_tests.rs` — new/updated tests.
- `defaults/docs/eta.md` — document the `start` kind and the new stage.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: `cargo test -p loom-daemon eta::` and `cargo test -p loom-daemon observability::ops::turnaround` (targeted runs while iterating, not the full suite — see this repo's host guidance on modest local builds).
- [ ] Automated: a golden fixture test pinning `start-v1`'s output (and the extended `land-v1`'s not-yet-started output) over a fixed input, per the Phase 1 immutable-id rule.
- [ ] Manual verification: on a host with `autonomous.eta.enabled` and a real `loom:issue` backlog, confirm `eta.estimate` rows for ready issues carry `kind: "start"` (or a `land` row for an unstarted issue) with real quantiles instead of `no_estimate_reason: "no_dispatch_plan"`, once turnaround history exists.

issues.title: mcp-loom: get_agent_metrics joins raw MCP tool args into a shell string (no server-side schema enforcement)
issues.body:
## Context

Independent security audit (2026-09-26 session). `mcp-loom`'s `get_agent_metrics` tool builds a shell command by **string-joining unvalidated MCP tool arguments**:

- `mcp-loom/src/tools/terminals.ts:527-558` — `args` is assembled from `options.command / role / period / format / issue` with no per-value validation, then:
  `execAsync(\`bash "${scriptPath}" ${args.join(" ")}\`, { cwd: workspacePath })` (`:558`) — the only `exec*` call in mcp-loom.
- `mcp-loom/src/index.ts` — `setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, …)` passes `request.params.arguments` through as `Record<string, unknown>`; the tool's `inputSchema` (enum constraints on `command`/`role`/`period`/`format`, number on `issue`) is **advisory to the client** — the SDK does not enforce it server-side. Any client, or a model emitted an off-enum string (the normal case under prompt injection), breaks the string.

So `role: "builder; touch /tmp/pwn#"` (or any value containing `;`, `$(…)`, backticks, `&&`, newline) escapes into arbitrary shell execution as the user running the MCP server. Combined with Loom's threat model (autonomous agents read untrusted forge text under `--dangerously-skip-permissions` — see `defaults/docs/untrusted-external-content.md`), a forged issue/PR comment directing the agent to call the tool with hostile args is a complete **injection → command execution** chain; see the sibling issue on the missing MCP guard matcher for the hook-coverage half of this chain.

## What changes

1. `terminals.ts`: stop building a shell string. Use `execFile`/`spawn` with an **argument array** — `execFile("bash", [scriptPath, ...validatedArgs])` — so no shell interpretation exists at all (`/bin/bash -c` is unnecessary; `agent-metrics.sh` takes plain flags).
   - If a value must be an array flag, push each element separately; never `.join(" ")`.
2. Validate each option server-side before use (do not rely on `inputSchema`):
   - `command`/`role`/`period`/`format`: explicit allow-lists (the same sets the schema documents); `issue`: integral number ≥ 1.
   - Anything off-allow-list → tool returns `{ success: false, error: … }` naming the invalid argument, no child process spawned.
3. Audit the other mcp-loom tools (`logs.ts`, `ui.ts`, `sweeps.ts`) for the same class: any `child_process` use with a constructed string, and any tool argument that reaches `fs` paths (path traversal via `join(workspacePath, arg)`) — flag paths and validate them as well.

## Out of scope

- Adding a PreToolUse MCP matcher — separate sibling issue (hook wiring lives in `.claude/settings.json` / guard hooks, not in mcp-loom).
- The daemon-side MCP surface (`loom-daemon` MCP tools) — separate codebase, same policy should apply; note for the curator if relevant.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `mcp-loom/src` contains no `shell` string construction: grep for `` `bash `` / `exec(` with template literals returns nothing (add a `package.json` script or test asserting this).
2. Calling `get_agent_metrics` with `role: "x; touch /tmp/mcp-loom-pwn#"` returns a structured error, spawns no child, and creates no file (unit/integration test).
3. Every tool argument reaching the shell or `fs` goes through an allow-list/validator; off-allow-list values never spawn a process (tests per option).
4. Existing documented `agent-metrics.sh` invocations behave byte-identically for valid inputs (compare a full-matrix run before/after).

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->
<!-- loom:points=8 -->

### Verified corrections

- **2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `53a29fd9e`**: every claim above checks out as written — `mcp-loom/src/tools/terminals.ts:558` is the sole `exec*`/`child_process` call site in `mcp-loom/src` (`git grep` across every `.ts` file under `mcp-loom/src` at this sha, matched only here); `mcp-loom/src/index.ts:43-56` passes `request.params.arguments` through as a bare `as Record<string, unknown>` type assertion with no runtime schema check; and the `get_agent_metrics` `inputSchema` (`terminals.ts:831-870`) does declare the `enum` constraints on `command`/`role`/`period`/`format` the issue describes.
- **2026-09-29, additional finding**: no other tool argument reaches a path-join with user input anywhere in `mcp-loom/src` — the only `join(workspacePath, …)` call sites are `mcp-loom/src/shared/config.ts:229,239`, `mcp-loom/src/tools/terminals.ts:523`, and `mcp-loom/src/tools/ui.ts:244`, and all four use hardcoded literal path segments (`.loom/config.json`, `.loom/state.json`, `.loom/scripts/agent-metrics.sh`), never an option/arg value. So the "Out of scope" item 3 audit of `logs.ts`/`ui.ts`/`sweeps.ts` turns up **no additional injection or path-traversal site today** — `logs.ts` is a 31-line schema-only file with no `child_process`/`fs` calls at all. Re-verify if these files grow new tool handlers before relying on this.
- **2026-09-29, confirmed**: `.loom/scripts/agent-metrics.sh` (synced from `defaults/scripts/agent-metrics.sh`, byte-identical in this checkout) is a thin stub that `exec`s `loom-daemon stats <command>` and takes only plain flags (`--role`, `--period`, `--format`, `--issue`, `--by-model`) — supports the proposed `execFile("bash", [scriptPath, ...validatedArgs])` fix with no script-side changes needed.

### Affected Files

- `mcp-loom/src/tools/terminals.ts` - replace the `execAsync(\`bash "${scriptPath}" ${args.join(" ")}\`, …)` call (line 558) with `execFile`/`spawn` passing an argument array; add server-side allow-list validation for `command`/`role`/`period`/`format` (matching the existing `inputSchema` enums) and a numeric-≥1 check for `issue` before any value is used
- `mcp-loom/src/index.ts` - no change expected (the `CallToolRequestSchema` handler at line 43 stays a thin dispatcher); confirm during implementation that no other call site relies on `inputSchema` being enforced upstream
- `mcp-loom/src/tools/logs.ts`, `mcp-loom/src/tools/ui.ts`, `mcp-loom/src/tools/sweeps.ts` - covered by the "Out of scope" audit item; per the Verified corrections above, none currently construct a shell string or join user input into a filesystem path, so no code change is expected here — only add the assertion/test from AC #1 that would catch a future regression

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: unit test for `get_agent_metrics` (or a shared validator helper) asserting `role: "x; touch /tmp/mcp-loom-pwn#"` (and the same for `command`/`period`/`format`) returns a structured `{ success: false, error }`, spawns no child process, and creates no file — this is AC #2
- [ ] Automated tests: one test per option (`command`, `role`, `period`, `format`, `issue`) asserting an off-allow-list value never reaches `execFile`/`spawn` — this is AC #3
- [ ] Static check: a `package.json` script or test asserting `mcp-loom/src` contains no template-literal shell-string construction (grep for `` `bash `` / `` exec(` `` with a template literal) — this is AC #1
- [ ] Manual/regression verification: run the full documented `agent-metrics.sh` invocation matrix (all `command` × `role` × `period` × `format` combinations used by existing docs/tests) before and after, and confirm byte-identical output — this is AC #4

issues.title: No label means "approved, but not yet" — loom:blocked is not a merge gate
issues.body:
## There is no label meaning "approved, but not yet"

Two PRs in `2AMLogic/ufo-integrations` needed to land in a specific order, for a concrete reason: #111 *grew* a set of shared test fakes, #112 *deduplicated* them. Dedupe-before-grow leaves the dedupe having processed a set that immediately grows again.

Two agents agreed that order explicitly. A fleet dispatch agent then authored #112, approved it, and **merged it first** — correctly by its own lights, since it held a verdict and nothing in the repo said otherwise. #111 was left conflicting and #112 deduped the wrong set.

There was no label that would have prevented this.

## `loom:blocked` looks like the answer and is not

This is the trap worth documenting, because it is the obvious first guess:

```
- name: loom:blocked
  description: Implementation blocked, needs help or clarification
```

`defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` **never reads it**. `grep -n "loom:blocked" defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` returns nothing. It is an issue-status label about implementation being stuck, and it gates sweep selection, not merging. A PR carrying it merges exactly as if it did not.

The labels the merge script actually gates on are `loom:operator` and `loom:operator-only`, through the mutual-exclusion guard (`merge-pr.sh:874` — *"A PR can carry BOTH `loom:pr` (approved) and a blocking verdict/hold label"*), which correctly refuses and has no override flag.

## Why `loom:operator` is the wrong tool for ordering

It works — it would have stopped the merge. But it means *"a human must act or rule on this, outside automation"*, and that is false when the truth is "after #111 lands." Using it for sequencing would:

- **poison a signal that currently means something.** An operator scanning for `loom:operator` is looking for things needing their judgement. Ordering holds are not those, and burying the real ones among them makes the label worth less.
- **require a human to clear it.** An ordering hold should clear when its dependency merges, which is a mechanical condition, not a ruling.

## The missing primitive

A label meaning **approved, and must not merge yet** — a hold that is not an escalation:

- refused by `merge-pr.sh` the way `loom:operator` is, with the same no-override treatment, since the point is that an automated merger honours it
- distinguishable from `loom:operator` so operator-attention scans stay clean
- ideally naming what it waits on, so it is clearable by a condition rather than by memory — `loom:after:#111` or a body reference, so a Champion landing #111 can clear it

Even without the auto-clear, a plain `loom:hold` that the merge script refuses would have prevented all three incidents that day.

## Related

- rjwalters/loom#9372 — `merge-pr.sh` deletes a merged parent's branch, which **closes** stacked children instead of retargeting them. Same session, adjacent cause: base-pointer stacking is the natural way to express "this depends on that", and the tooling punishes it at both ends — the child gets closed on merge, and nothing prevents the parent merging first.
- rjwalters/squad#107 — the coordination-side half: decisions negotiated in a chat room are invisible to fleet agents, so they need repo state. This issue is the repo-state side of that: right now there is no correct label to encode it in.

issues.title: role runner: one active instance per (repository, role) for every role, concurrent across repositories (Phase 1; demand-weighting split to #9392)
issues.body:
## Summary

Operator direction (2026-09-28): **the repository is the parallelism boundary. Every role-runner role may have one active instance per repository, not one per daemon.** This started as a Judge request and was widened the same day ("repos are a clean parallelism boundary"). The direction also covers and **rebalance fleet effort between building and reviewing based on demand**. This means how many PRs are waiting, not a fixed timer.

## How it works today (cited from loom-daemon at c6cc067fa)

- Builders come from the work-finder. The default cap is `min(disk, ram, autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrent=3)`, from `work_finder.rs:2250-2256` and `:176`. Each dispatch is a full `/loom:sweep` that carries its own Judge for its own PR.
- Standalone Judge, Doctor, Champion and Curator come from the role runner, which runs one tokio loop per role on a fixed interval: judge 300s, doctor 300s, champion 600s (`role_runner.rs:453-559`).
  - **Each loop awaits each workspace in turn** (`role_runner.rs:3362-3432`).
  - `MissedTickBehavior::Delay` is set at `:3263`.
  - So **Judge is effectively one session per daemon**, walking the host's workspaces serially. robb-studio has 62.
- Admission is already keyed per `(root, role)` (`role_runner.rs:2451-2471`, `InProgress`). The ceiling `autonomous.roleRunner.maxConcurrent` defaults to 7 and counts **all** roles together.
- **Nothing reads demand.** `review_requested` feeds only `pipeline_snapshot` and the health `is_review_stalled` verdict (`health.rs:2036-2041`).
- `autonomous.roleRunner.intervalSecs` is the only interval knob, and it is global. Shortening it only shrinks the gap between serial passes. It raises token spend for every role and adds **no** parallelism.

## Measured now (2026-09-28, 2AMLogic + rjwalters/loom)

| state | count |
|---|---|
| `loom:review-requested` | 28 |
| `loom:reviewing` | **1** |
| `loom:changes-requested` | 19 |
| `loom:pr` (awaiting Champion) | **59** |
| `loom:building` issues | 22 |
| `loom:issue` ready | 106 |

About 30 % of judge ticks failed on robb-studio over the last 31 h. The causes were `ACCOUNT_POOL_EXHAUSTED` and the Codex bridge refusal in #9390, which is mitigated on robb-studio by pinning judge and champion to Claude. Fixing the failures is necessary but not enough: even with zero failures, serial fan-out caps review throughput at about one PR pass per workspace-rotation.

## Proposal

### 1. One active instance per (repository, role), for every role-runner role
- **Unit of parallelism = `(root, role)`.** Every role loop (champion, curator, judge, doctor, auditor, hermit, guide, architect) dispatches workspaces **concurrently** instead of awaiting each one in turn. The existing `(root, role)` in-progress guard (`role_runner.rs:2451-2471`) already ensures at most one instance per repository per role. #9000 names the same serial shape for curator.
- **Different roles in the same repository may run at once.** Judge (`loom:review-requested`), Doctor (`loom:changes-requested`), Champion (`loom:pr`) and Curator (unlabeled issues) act on disjoint label states and already claim with `loom:reviewing` / `loom:treating`. The label state machine arbitrates between them, as it does today between hosts. If a role turns out to need repository exclusivity (e.g. auditor building `main` while champion merges), declare it per role (`exclusiveWith: [...]`) rather than serialising everything.
- **Only dispatch a repository that has work for that role.** Use one cheap query per tick across roots, or `pipeline_snapshot`, for the role's queue label. Width then costs nothing when queues are empty; the host does not spawn 62 × 8 idle agents. Idle-edge roles (hermit, architect) keep their existing idle trigger.
- **Budgets, not one shared ceiling.** Keep a host-wide cap and add `autonomous.roleRunner.roles.<role>.maxConcurrent` per role, so a burst of curator work cannot starve Champion. Admission also respects token-pool headroom, as the work-finder's brake does; the pool, not the loop shape, should be the binding limit.
- Cross-host behaviour is unchanged: host sharding (`role_runner.rs:2977-3000`, #6374) plus claim labels already keep hosts apart.

### 2. Demand-weighted split between building and reviewing
Recompute each work-finder or role-runner tick, all per host:
- `review_debt = review_requested + changes_requested`, and `merge_debt = loom:pr`.
- `judge_width = clamp(ceil(review_debt / k), 1, judge_max)`. Use the same shape for Doctor, and for Champion driven by `merge_debt`.
- **Build back-off (a WIP limit):** once `review_debt + merge_debt > W`, the work-finder stops admitting **new** issue builds. Its freed slots run PR-only sweeps (Judge → Doctor → merge, the #7649 watchdog path) until the debt falls below `W_low`, with hysteresis so it does not oscillate.
- An empty queue hands everything back to builders automatically.
- Start conservative: `k=3`, `judge_max=4`, `W=40`, `W_low=25`. Expose all four as config and log each decision so they can be tuned from SigNoz.

### 3. Champion is the larger backlog
59 approved PRs are waiting to merge, compared with 28 waiting for review. Champion is single-instance at 600s and was also hit by #9390. Per-repository width plus the `merge_debt` weighting in §2 should apply to Champion first. It is the cheapest role and it releases the most finished work.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every role-runner role runs concurrently across repositories, with at most one instance per `(repository, role)`, bounded by a host cap plus per-role budgets.
- [ ] Different roles may run in the same repository at once. Any role that needs repository exclusivity declares it explicitly.
- [ ] A repository with an empty queue for a role is not dispatched for that role.
- [ ] Work-finder admission backs off new builds above a configurable review+merge debt, with hysteresis. Each decision is logged, with the debt it saw.
- [ ] Measured before and after on one host: `loom:reviewing` concurrency, median time in `loom:review-requested` and `loom:pr`, and token spend per merged PR.

Related: #9000 (roles process one workspace at a time), #9249 (parallel judges), #8928 (per-host dispatch concurrency), #8923 (PR latency, closed; it found review was not the bottleneck when the queue was 4 deep), #7649 (review-stall → PR-only sweep), #9390 (Codex bridge refusals).




---

## Curator enrichment (2026-09-28, verified against `origin/main` 42e150430)

### Scope decision: this issue is now Phase 1. Phase 2 is #9392.

The full proposal is too large for one Builder PR. It has two independent subsystems (role-runner loop shape and work-finder admission) and would run to several hundred lines of code plus tests. It is split as follows:

| Phase | Covers | Tracked in |
|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1 (this issue)** | §1: every role-runner role dispatches **concurrently across repositories**, with at most one instance per `(repository, role)`, per-role concurrency budgets under the existing host ceiling, and empty-queue gating | **#9391** |
| Phase 2 | §2 and §3: demand-weighted build back-off (a WIP limit with hysteresis), debt-driven Judge/Doctor/Champion width, token-headroom-aware admission, and the before/after measurement | #9392 (depends on this issue) |

**The Builder on this issue delivers Phase 1 only.** The §2 and §3 text above stays here for context and is out of scope for this PR. The last acceptance bullet in the original list (before/after measurement) and the work-finder back-off bullet move to #9392.

### Citation check (all verified on `origin/main`, no drift)

| Cited | Actual | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `role_runner.rs:453-559` `DEFAULT_ROLES` | `:453-560` | champion 600s, curator/judge/doctor 300s, auditor/hermit 600s, guide 900s. `architect` (3600s) and `concierge` are `interval_default: false` |
| `role_runner.rs:2451-2471` admission | `RoleRunGuard::admit` at `:2451-2472`, `RoleAdmission` enum at `:2396-2411` | The host ceiling and the `(root, role)` check run under **one** lock (see the doc comment at `:2438-2450`), and that atomicity must be kept |
| `role_runner.rs:3263` `MissedTickBehavior::Delay` | `:3263` in `spawn_multi_role_task` (`:3248`) | `:3127` is the test-only single-root `spawn_role_task` |
| `role_runner.rs:3362-3432` serial loop | `for root in roots` at `:3362`, `spawn_blocking(...).await` ending at `:3432` | The `_run_guard` is held in the loop body and dropped at the end of each iteration |
| `role_runner.rs:2234-2266` ceiling | `default_max_concurrent` `:2234`, `resolve_max_concurrent` `:2259-2266` | The default is the count of interval-default roles, which is **7** |
| `role_runner.rs:2977-3000` sharding | `decide_root_tick` (`:2926`), shard gate at `:2977-3000` | Unchanged by this issue |
| `work_finder.rs:176`, `:2250` | `DEFAULT_WORK_FINDER_MAX_CONCURRENT = 3` at `:176`; `resolve_dynamic_max_concurrent` at `:2251-2257` | Phase 2 only |
| `health.rs:2036` | `is_review_stalled` at `:2036-2041` | Phase 2 only |

Additional sites the Builder must touch that the body did not list:
- **`plan_idle_runs`** (`role_runner.rs:2592-2690`) also calls `RoleRunGuard::admit` (`:2644-2690`). Idle-edge runs must count against the same per-role budget.
- The **spawn site** is `daemon_service.rs:1907` (`role_runner::spawn_multi_role_task(...)`). It shares one `InProgressGuard` created at `:1309` across all role loops. The signature can stay unchanged.

### Correction: config key naming

The body proposes `autonomous.roleRunner.roles.<role>.maxConcurrent`. That shape is not possible, because **`autonomous.roleRunner.roles` is already an array**: the interval-cadence allowlist parsed in `read_role_runner_config` (`role_runner.rs:1272`, `:1430`) and documented at `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md:4485`. Use a sibling map key instead, following the existing per-role map precedents `roleModels` (`:1323`) and `onIdleMaxWait` (`:1287`, `:1457-1470`):

```json
"autonomous": { "roleRunner": { "roleMaxConcurrent": { "judge": 3, "champion": 3, "curator": 2 } } }
```

Parse it the same way as those keys: trim and lower-case each role key, soft-fail per entry, and drop zero, negative or non-integer values to the default. Like `maxConcurrent`, it is resolved from each root's own config and hot-applied every tick.

### Implementation guidance (Phase 1)

1. **Concurrent loop shape** (`spawn_multi_role_task`, `:3248-3450`)
   - Replace the per-root `spawn_blocking(...).await` with a `tokio::task::JoinSet` owned by the loop.
   - For each root that `decide_root_tick` admits, spawn the blocking invocation into the set and **move the `RoleRunGuard` into the task**. The `(root, role)` entry is then held for the invocation's real lifetime and released on drop on every exit path, as it is today. `RoleRunGuard` holds only an `Arc<Mutex<..>>` and a `(PathBuf, &'static str)`, so it is `Send`.
   - **Do not await the set at the end of the tick.** A `(root, role)` still running at the next tick is refused by the existing `RoleAdmission::InProgress` path (#4364). That refusal is what enforces one instance per `(repository, role)`.
   - At the top of each tick, and on the drain path, collect finished tasks with `try_join_next()`. Run `feed_pool_exhausted_observer` and `log_outcome_for_root_deduped` there. The four dedup maps (`failing_roots`, `no_token_pool_roots`, `pool_exhausted_roots`, `model_mismatch_roots`) then stay single-owner and need no `Arc<Mutex>`. Return `(root, outcome, elapsed)` from each task.
   - A task that panics must still log the root it was running, as the current `Err(e)` arm does. Keep a `HashMap<tokio::task::Id, PathBuf>`, or `catch_unwind` inside the closure.
   - Keep the `catch_unwind` around `decide_root_tick` (#6201), the drain check (#4090) and the rate-limit check (#4429) exactly as they are.
   - Recommended: pull the per-tick dispatch into a function that takes an injectable `RoleInvocationRunner` factory. Production passes `ScriptRoleInvocationRunner::new`, and tests pass a fake. Without that seam, acceptance criterion 1 cannot be unit-tested. `role_runner.rs` is already about 4,000 lines, so a new submodule `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs` is a reasonable home.
2. **Per-role budget in admission**
   - Extend `RoleRunGuard::admit` (or add `admit_with_role_budget`) to take `role_budget: usize`.
   - Under the **same single lock**, count the in-flight entries whose `.1 == role`. When that count is at or above the budget, return a new `RoleAdmission::RoleBudgetReached { role, active, budget }`.
   - Check order: `InProgress`, then host `CeilingReached`, then `RoleBudgetReached`. Update `into_guard` to match.
   - `try_acquire` stays unbounded for both limits.
   - **Default budget**: `max(1, host_ceiling / 2)`, which is 3 at the default ceiling of 7, clamped to `≤ host_ceiling`. With a default of 1 this issue would change nothing. With a default equal to the host ceiling, one role could take every slot, which is exactly the starvation §1 warns about.
   - The host ceiling (`maxConcurrent`) stays as it is and still counts every role together.
3. **Empty-queue gating**
   - Add `work_queue_labels(role) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]>`. For Phase 1: `judge → ["loom:review-requested"]`, `doctor → ["loom:changes-requested"]`, and **`None` for every other role**. `None` means the role is ungated and dispatched as it is today.
   - **Do not reuse `role_collision::probe_target_for_role`** (`role_collision.rs:177`). Its curator target is `loom:curating`, which is the in-flight marker, not the work queue. Its champion target is `loom:pr`, but Champion also promotes `loom:curated` issues and evaluates proposals, so gating Champion on `loom:pr` alone would starve issue promotion. Gating Champion and Curator correctly needs a multi-label or search-based queue definition. That can follow once there is evidence; per-role budgets already bound them in this issue.
   - Probe with `crate::forge_listing::list_issues_cached_as(...)`, which is ETag-cached so an unchanged queue costs a free `304`. `RestQueueSource::list_queue` at `role_collision.rs:549` shows the call shape. The probe must run on the blocking thread, inside the spawned task and before `invoke_with_collision_probe`.
   - An empty queue returns a new **non-failure** `RoleTickOutcome::QueueEmpty` (`role_runner/outcome.rs`) and spawns no agent. Log it at `debug!`. It must never enter the `failing_roots` fail/recover edge. Handle it in `role_tick_telemetry` like `LoadSkipped`.
   - A listing error **fails open**: dispatch as if the queue were non-empty.
4. **Refusal log volume**
   - With 62 roots, a per-root `WARN` for every `CeilingReached` or `RoleBudgetReached` refusal on every tick is spam.
   - Once a tick hits the host ceiling or the role budget, stop admitting for the rest of that tick. Emit **one** aggregated line per tick per role that names the active count, the limit and how many roots were deferred.
   - The per-`(root, role)` `InProgress` skip stays at `debug!`.
5. **Role exclusivity (`exclusiveWith`)**: no role declares one in Phase 1. Judge, Doctor, Champion and Curator act on disjoint label states and already claim items (`loom:reviewing`, `loom:treating`). Different roles in the same repository therefore run at once by default, and that needs no code: the `InProgressGuard` key is already `(root, role)`. Add the mechanism only when a concrete conflict is observed, and document that decision in the docs.
6. **Unchanged**: host sharding and roster (#6374/#6704), the per-root `enabled` gate (#4377), the per-role config gate (#7947), `onIdleMaxWait` promotion (#7511), per-invocation token-pool selection and the `PoolExhausted` pre-spawn skip feeding the #6614 brake (#7607), and cross-host claim labels.

### Phase 1 acceptance criteria (these replace the original list for this PR)

- [ ] **AC1, concurrent across repositories.** A test drives the per-tick dispatch for one role over 3 enabled roots with a fake runner that blocks on a 3-party barrier or latch. All three invocations are in flight at once. The test must fail (time out) under the old serial `await`.
- [ ] **AC2, one instance per `(repository, role)`.** While root A's judge run is still in flight, the next tick refuses A with `RoleAdmission::InProgress` and does not spawn a second instance. The other roots are still admitted. Existing `test_admit_distinguishes_in_progress_from_ceiling_reached`, `test_admit_refuses_once_ceiling_reached_across_roots`, `decide_root_tick_*` and `shard_dispatch` tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3, different roles in the same repository.** Judge and doctor on the same root are both admitted simultaneously.
- [ ] **AC4, per-role budget.** With `roleMaxConcurrent.judge = 2` and more than 2 roots, the third judge admission returns `RoleBudgetReached`, while a curator admission on another root in the same state is still `Admitted`. The host ceiling is still enforced across all roles combined. Idle-edge admissions (`plan_idle_runs`) count against the same budget.
- [ ] **AC5, budget resolution.** Unit tests cover the `roleMaxConcurrent` map: a valid entry, zero, a negative value, a non-integer, an unknown role, a mixed-case key, the absent-key default of `max(1, ceiling/2)` (3 at ceiling 7), and a budget larger than the ceiling, which is clamped.
- [ ] **AC6, empty-queue gating.** With a stubbed empty `loom:review-requested` listing, judge spawns no agent and records `QueueEmpty`, which is not a failure. A non-empty listing dispatches. A listing **error** dispatches (fail-open). Ungated roles (curator, champion, auditor, hermit, guide) are unaffected by the gate.
- [ ] **AC7, completion bookkeeping preserved.** A finished task still feeds `feed_pool_exhausted_observer` and `log_outcome_for_root_deduped`, so the fail and recover edges still log exactly once. A panicking invocation task logs its root and the loop keeps ticking (#6201).
- [ ] **AC8, log volume.** A tick refused at the ceiling or budget emits one aggregated line per role, not one per root.
- [ ] **AC9, docs.** `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` covers three changes:
  - A new `autonomous.roleRunner.roleMaxConcurrent` row in the config table.
  - The `maxConcurrent` row (`:4487`) and "The other half of the agent budget" section updated to say role loops now dispatch across repositories concurrently, bounded by the host ceiling plus per-role budgets.
  - A note on which roles are queue-gated and that no role declares exclusivity.
- [ ] **AC10.** `cargo test -p loom-daemon` and `cargo clippy -p loom-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

**Out of scope for this PR (tracked in #9392):** work-finder build back-off, debt-driven width, token-headroom admission, the before/after measurement. Also out of scope here: queue-gating Champion and Curator, and an `exclusiveWith` mechanism.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs`: `spawn_multi_role_task` loop shape, `RoleRunGuard::admit` and `RoleAdmission`, `RoleRunnerConfig` and `read_role_runner_config` (`roleMaxConcurrent`), `plan_idle_runs`, the budget resolver
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/outcome.rs`: new `RoleTickOutcome::QueueEmpty`
- `loom-daemon/src/role_tick_telemetry.rs`: handle the new outcome variant
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs`: register the new test module. Existing admission, decide and shard tests must stay green
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs`: **new**, recommended home for the per-tick dispatch, the injectable runner factory and `work_queue_labels`
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests/concurrent_dispatch.rs`: **new**, tests for AC1 through AC8
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`: config table and role-runner budget section
- Reference only, expected unchanged: `loom-daemon/src/daemon_service.rs` (spawn site `:1907`), `loom-daemon/src/role_collision.rs` (probe-call pattern), `loom-daemon/src/forge_listing.rs` (cached listing), `loom-daemon/src/role_shard.rs`

Related: #9000 will largely be resolved by this issue: curator becomes concurrent across workspaces, bounded by its budget. Re-check #9000 after merge.

issues.title: flake: dashboard redaction.test.ts asserts publicText lacks "214" (lines_added) but ingestedAt millis can be .214
issues.body:
## Problem

`dashboard/test/redaction.test.ts:1027`, in the `sweep.outcome` case of "GET /public/history vs GET /api/history — end-to-end redaction", asserts:

```ts
expect(publicText).not.toContain("214"); // lines_added
```

`publicText` is the whole response body, and it includes real wall-clock timestamps such as `ingestedAt`. Whenever a timestamp's milliseconds read `.214`, the assertion fails even though nothing leaked. With several timestamps in the response, the odds are a few in a thousand per run.

## Observed

On merge train #9020 (2026-09-26), the `Dashboard Tests` job failed on `ingestedAt …05:54:56.214Z`. The train touched no dashboard files. Re-running the job passed.

## Fix

Assert on the parsed field rather than on a substring of the whole body. For example, parse the JSON and check that no record has `lines_added`, or match a key-anchored pattern like `/"lines_added"\s*:/` or `/:\s*214[,}]/`. Alternatively, freeze the clock in this test (`vi.useFakeTimers()` / a fixed `now`) so timestamps are deterministic. Check the other bare-number assertions in the same block too (`4703`, `4710`, `48213`, `6120`) and anchor them the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The redaction assertions can't match timestamp digits (anchored patterns, or a frozen clock).
- [ ] The test still fails if `lines_added` (or the other private fields) leaks into `/public/history`.

issues.title: tracing phase 2: stitch CI runs into the issue's story trace (#9037)
issues.body:
## Phase 2 of #9037: stitch CI runs into the issue's story trace

After #9068 (PR #9084), every issue has a deterministic D32 v1 story trace (`story_context(repo_id, issue)`), and issue sweeps join it. CI runs still land only in their own per-run trace (`ci_telemetry/records.rs::run_context`, keyed on `(repo, run_id, attempt)`). So the waterfall jumps from the Builder straight to nothing.

## Design (per #9037 phase 2 + harness-ops `docs/story-trace.md` D32)

- A CI run belongs to story N when **exactly one** loom-managed issue is resolved for it. The run's `pull_requests[]` gives the PR; the PR's closing references (the D32 rule: exactly one closed issue) give the issue. The fallback is `head_branch == feature/issue-N`. If there are zero or several candidates, the run is **not** stitched; that is counted and logged, and never guessed.
- For a stitched run, emit an **additional** `loom.ci.run` span into the story trace, parented to the story root span (`story_context(repo_id, N)`). It gets a deterministic span id derived from `(repo_id, run_id, attempt)` so re-polls are idempotent. Its job spans are children of it.
- The existing per-run CI trace stays unchanged (same ids; the `derived_ci_ids_are_unchanged_by_the_shared_derivation` pin must still pass). The two are **linked** both ways, so existing CI saved views keep working.
- `repo_id` comes from the #9068 resolver cache (`telemetry/repo_identity.rs`). An unresolvable repo means no stitching, with no name-derived fallback.
- Attributes: `loom.story`, `loom.story.key_version=v1`, `loom.issue`, `loom.pr_number`, plus the existing CI attributes. Everything stays within the telemetry allowlist.
- Single emitter: the D32 table allows either the harness-ops CI poller (harness-ops#193, `loom:operator-decision`, not built) or loom's poller (#8824) to emit `ci.run`. This issue makes **loom's poller the story emitter**, and harness-ops#193 must not also stitch, to avoid duplicate rows (SigNoz doesn't dedup). Note this on harness-ops#193.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A run on `feature/issue-N` or with a PR closing exactly #N produces a story-trace span with trace id = `story_context(repo_id, N).trace_id`, parent = the story root span id.
- [ ] Re-polling the same run produces identical span ids (idempotent).
- [ ] Ambiguous or unresolvable runs are not stitched; a test asserts no span is created.
- [ ] Per-run CI trace ids are unchanged (existing pins pass); links are present in both directions.
- [ ] Tests use the D32 vectors fixture from #9068.

Depends on #9068 / PR #9084. Phase 3 (the story root, intake, dwell, review-wait and merge spans) is owned by the harness-ops storyline reconciler (harness-ops#319, in progress), not loom.

issues.title: Telemetry mega PR A follow-ups: OpenCode open-row pruning, trace-join edge cases, role-tick usage join
issues.body:
## Context

These are non-blocking findings from the Judge review of PR #9008 (telemetry mega PR A: #8908, #8931, #8965, #8966), plus one scope gap that PR left out on purpose.

## Items

1. **OpenCode open rows that are deleted** (`observability/ops/quota/opencode.rs`, `StoreCursor::advance`). An open rowid whose row is later deleted, for example by a session deletion, stays in `open` until the 6 h age bound. Until then it holds the read floor low. Every open rowid is always inside the read range, so an open key missing from the returned rows can be dropped right away.
2. **Join index cap** (`observability/runtime_usage/join.rs`, `entries()`). `take(MAX_ENTRIES)` reads at most 1024 files. Past that, a second matching entry could go unseen and an ambiguous session could be joined. When the cap is hit, return "ambiguous" (no join).
3. **Join entries that never close** (daemon crash, or no terminal record written). Such an entry keeps matching every session of that issue for 7 d, so re-dispatches of the issue come out ambiguous and stay unjoined. This fails safe, but the joins are lost. Close orphaned entries during restart reconciliation.
4. **`record_codex` over-count** (`observability/ops/pool_marks.rs`). When the account is already `ReauthRequired`, `health.rs` writes no new hold for a later `RECOVERABLE`, yet a `transient` point is still emitted.
5. **Scope gap from #8908.** Role-tick executions get no `loom.runtime.usage` span and no `session.summary` trace join (only sweeps do). Subagent transcripts whose head names no issue also stay unjoined.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each item is fixed with a test, or closed with a rationale.

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->
<!-- loom:points=5 -->

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/quota/opencode.rs` - item 1: `StoreCursor::advance` should drop an `open` rowid immediately once its backing row is confirmed deleted, rather than waiting out the 6h age bound.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/runtime_usage/join.rs` - item 2: `entries()`'s `.take(MAX_ENTRIES)` (1024) silently truncates; when the cap is hit, the join should report "ambiguous" instead of risking a missed second match. Item 3: an entry with no terminal record should be closed during restart reconciliation instead of persisting for the full 7d window.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/pool_marks.rs` - item 4: `record_codex` emits a `transient` point even when `health.rs` wrote no new hold because the account is already `ReauthRequired`; the over-count should be suppressed in that case.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/runtime_usage.rs` - item 5: role-tick executions (Judge/Champion/Doctor running outside a sweep) currently emit no `loom.runtime.usage` span and get no `session.summary` trace join; only sweeps do today. Also: subagent transcripts whose head names no issue stay unjoined.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Item 1: unit test in `opencode.rs` - an open rowid whose backing row is deleted mid-window is excluded from the next `advance()` call's returned rows, not just after the 6h bound.
- [ ] Item 2: unit test in `join.rs` - construct >1024 candidate entries so the cap is hit and assert the join result is "ambiguous" rather than an incorrect single match.
- [ ] Item 3: integration/reconciliation test - an entry with no terminal record present at restart is closed by reconciliation rather than surviving the full 7d window.
- [ ] Item 4: unit test in `pool_marks.rs` - with the account already `ReauthRequired`, a later `RECOVERABLE` classification does not emit a `transient` over-count point.
- [ ] Item 5: integration test - a role-tick execution (Judge/Champion/Doctor, non-sweep) produces a `loom.runtime.usage` span and joins to a `session.summary` record; a subagent transcript with no issue in its head is exercised as the documented unjoined case.
- [ ] Per the issue's own acceptance criteria, any item may instead be closed with a written rationale in lieu of a code fix + test.

issues.title: Telemetry record kinds serialize through four shared registration sites, so concurrent observability PRs conflict pairwise
issues.body:
## Problem

Adding a telemetry record kind requires editing the same four files every time, at adjacent lines. Any two concurrent PRs that each add a kind therefore conflict with each other — not because they disagree, but because git cannot auto-merge two insertions into the same enum, the same `pub mod` block, and the same match arm list.

This is not hypothetical. On 2026-09-25, **#8915** (`ci.job` log capture, merged 16:00Z) and **#8909** (`metric.points`, #8860 phase 1) collided. They share six files:

```
defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md               <- CONFLICT
loom-daemon/src/observability/otlp/mapping.rs   <- CONFLICT
loom-daemon/src/telemetry/envelope.rs           <- CONFLICT
loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs                <- CONFLICT
defaults/docs/observability.md                  (auto-merged)
defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml    (auto-merged)
```

The colliding edits are structurally identical in shape. #8909 adds:

```rust
pub mod ops;
pub use ops::MetricPointsRecord;
    #[serde(rename = "metric.points")]
    MetricPoints(MetricPointsRecord),
                TelemetryRecord::MetricPoints(_) => 10,
```

#8915 adds `pub mod logs;` plus its own registrations in the same block and the same match. Each PR is individually clean; the pair is unmergeable. #8909 went from green to `CONFLICTING` roughly 15 minutes after #8915 merged, and a peer host spent a rebase cycle on it.

Note the `=> 10` arm in particular: both PRs need "the next number" from one hand-maintained sequence, so that line conflicts by construction.

## Why it matters now

Six observability work streams are concurrently open or queued, and most of them add a record kind or a signal name: **#8909**, **#8915** (landed), **#8907**, **#8908**, **#8692**, **#8903**. They will collide pairwise, serially, for as long as this burst lasts — each collision costing one rebase and, if a verdict was already rendered, a re-review under the verdict-SHA staleness rule.

Measured context: across the last 40 merged PRs (2026-09-23 22:18Z → 2026-09-25 16:11Z), `loom:merge-conflict` was applied **zero** times and only 8/40 PRs were force-pushed at all. Conflicts are *not* a general problem in this repo — this is localised contention in one narrow set of registration sites during a topical burst.

## Proposal

Reduce the number of shared lines a new record kind must touch. Options, roughly in increasing cost:

1. **Split the registration sites by kind family.** #8909 already established the good half of this pattern — `telemetry/ops.rs`, `observability/ops/`, `otlp/mapping/ops.rs` are new sibling modules, not edits to over-threshold files. What remains centralised is the enum variant, the `pub mod` / `pub use` lines, the serde rename, and the ordering arm. A macro or a registry that takes one declaration per kind would collapse four edit sites to one.
2. **Make the ordering arm derivable** rather than a hand-assigned integer, so two PRs never contend for the same number.
3. **Give `telemetry-schema.md` a per-kind section file** (or a generated table) so the doc stops being a single append-point table.

At minimum, document the contention so concurrent authors sequence deliberately instead of discovering it at merge time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding a new telemetry record kind touches at most one shared line, or none.
- [ ] Two independent branches each adding a record kind merge cleanly in a test (add a regression test or a documented manual check).
- [ ] The per-kind ordering value is no longer a hand-assigned literal that two PRs can both claim.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` no longer requires two concurrent PRs to append to the same table rows.

## Notes

Filed from a cross-repo triage pass, not from a Builder run. The conflict described above was resolved by a peer session on `host-75acf4b9` before this issue was filed — #8909 is mergeable again. The structural point stands independently of that one incident.
