issues.title: feat(dashboard): expose dedicated org-wide ranked ready dispatch queue view (/dashboard/queue)
issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Original Issue

### Problem Statement
Operators currently lack a dedicated web URL on `dashboard.2amlogic.com` to inspect the full org-wide candidate queue ranked strictly by Loom's dispatch comparator (`work_finder::candidate_cmp`).

### Proposed Solution
Implement a dedicated view and hard URL `https://dashboard.2amlogic.com/#/queue` (backed by `GET /api/v1/queue/ranked`).

### Key Features
1. **Ranked Candidate Feed:**
   - Displays all unblocked `loom:issue` candidates across all allowlisted org repos (`2AMLogic/*`, `rjwalters/loom`).
   - Strict comparator ordering:
     1. Tier 1 (`tier:goal-advancing`) -> Tier 2 (`tier:goal-supporting`) -> Tier 3 (`tier:maintenance`).
     2. High priority / urgent flags (`priority:high`).
     3. Curated status (`loom:curated`).
     4. Creation timestamp.
2. **Interactive Controls:**
   - Filter by Org / Repo.
   - Filter by Tier.
   - View skip / defer reason annotations.
   - Live auto-refresh.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hard URL `https://dashboard.2amlogic.com/#/queue` renders the ranked org-wide candidate queue.
- [ ] API endpoint `GET /api/v1/queue/ranked` returns structured JSON ordered by dispatch priority.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-27, verified against `main` @ `7e0a29b0d`)

### The requested `#/queue` view and its data path already exist (Issue #8852)

This is not a greenfield feature. As of `7e0a29b0d`:

- `dashboard/web/src/router.ts` already parses `#/queue` as a first-class route (`parseRoute`), and `dashboard/web/src/app.ts:283` already renders it via `workQueueView()` (`dashboard/web/src/views/workQueue.ts`).
- `workQueueView` already merges **every reporting host's** queue into one page — Running / Ready / Blocked lists, one row per `repo#issue`, each showing repo, host, phase, waiting time, and disposition/reason, folded by `mergeFleetQueue` (`dashboard/web/src/workQueue.ts`). This is the "org-wide" aggregation the issue asks for, in the only sense that's coherent given the per-host-daemon model (see "What 'org-wide' can mean" below).
- The data path end to end: `loom-daemon`'s work finder computes dispatch order via `work_finder::candidate_cmp` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs:609-627`), records one `ReadyQueueRow` per ready issue per tick (`loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs`), which is (a) rendered locally, single-host, by CLI `loom-daemon queue` (`loom-daemon/src/cli/ready_queue_cmd.rs`), and (b) pushed as `queue.snapshot` telemetry (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/queue_snapshot.rs`) to the dashboard Worker, where it's ingested/stored/redacted by `dashboard/src/queueState.ts` and served via the existing `GET /api/fleet-state` (authenticated) and `GET /public/fleet-state` (redacted, no repo-identifying fields on private rows) endpoints — the same endpoints `dashboard/web` already polls for every other panel.
- **No new `GET /api/v1/queue/ranked` endpoint should be built.** `queueState.ts`'s doc comment and `QueueSnapshotRecord`/`QueueRow` (`dashboard/web/src/queueTypes.ts`) already carry every field the issue asks for (rank, tier, urgent, disposition, reason, created_at). Adding a parallel versioned REST surface would duplicate the Durable-Object aggregation `#8852` phase 3 already built and give the dashboard two sources of truth for the same data.

### Correction: the issue's stated comparator does not match the real dispatch order

The filed acceptance criteria assert ordering by `tier:goal-advancing` -> `tier:goal-supporting` -> `tier:maintenance`, then `priority:high`, then `loom:curated`, then creation time. **This is not how the daemon orders dispatch candidates**, verified against `main` @ `7e0a29b0d`:

```
loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs:608-627 (candidate_cmp) and
loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs:1-8 (module doc):

  "The order is the daemon's own dispatch comparator, crate::work_finder::candidate_cmp:
   workspace priority, then loom:urgent, then oldest createdAt, then issue number.
   tier:* labels are carried as information only; they do not affect dispatch order."
```

The real total order is **(workspace priority ascending, `loom:urgent` first, oldest `createdAt` first, issue number)** — `workspace_priority` is a per-workspace daemon *config* value (`.loom/config.json`'s `terminals`/workspace priority), not derived from an issue's `tier:*` label. `tier:*` labels are informational-only (see `dashboard/web/src/views/workQueue.ts`'s `flags()`, which renders the tier badge with the tooltip "Informational: the daemon does not order by tier"). `priority:high` is not a recognized ordering input at all (the real urgency signal is the `loom:urgent` label), and `loom:curated` plays no role in dispatch ordering either.

**Acceptance criteria below are rewritten against the verified behavior, not the filer's assumption.** A Builder should not attempt to make the queue sort by tier/`priority:high`/`loom:curated` — that would contradict the daemon's actual dispatch semantics and mislead operators about why an issue is (or isn't) about to be picked up.

### What "org-wide" can mean here, and what it can't (scope guard)

Given the per-host daemon + fleet model, an "org-wide ranked queue" can only be **the merge of every host currently reporting queue telemetry** — exactly what `mergeFleetQueue` already does today. It is bounded by which hosts are online, have their work finder enabled, and have ticked recently (a host's rows go stale/offline per `QUEUE_STALE_AFTER_SEC`/`QUEUE_OFFLINE_AFTER_SEC` in `dashboard/web/src/workQueue.ts`).

**Explicitly out of scope for this PR** (name as a follow-up if ever wanted, do not build it here): an independent, host-agnostic recomputation of the ready queue by the dashboard Worker itself querying the forge directly. That would duplicate the daemon's own skip-label/admission/quarantine logic in a second codebase and could disagree with what actually dispatches — the daemon's own per-tick export is the only place `candidate_cmp` is evaluated, and that must stay true.

### The real, buildable gaps

Given the above, the genuinely missing pieces — the actual scope of this issue — are:

1. **No visible dispatch-rank column in the merged fleet view.** `hostQueuePanel` (host-detail page) already shows `rankText(row)`; `workQueueView`'s merged Running/Ready/Blocked lists (the `#/queue` page) do not surface `QueueRow.rank` at all today.
2. **No filter controls on `#/queue`.** `workQueueView` renders the full merged list unconditionally — no repo/org or tier filter, contrary to the "Interactive Controls" the issue asks for.
3. **No persistent nav entry.** Unlike Charts/Tokens/Spend/Feed (`dashboard/web/src/panels.ts`'s `PANEL_MOUNTERS`), `#/queue` has no top-level nav link — it's reachable only via the "All queued, running and blocked issues →" link inside `workQueueSummarySection` on the overview page. `https://dashboard.2amlogic.com/#/queue` already works as a hard URL today (confirmed by reading `router.ts`/`app.ts`); it's just not discoverable from primary nav.
4. **"Live auto-refresh"** — verify against current polling behavior in `dashboard/web/src/app.ts` before treating this as a gap; `#/queue` is "a view over the polled snapshot, like `overview`/`host`, not a self-fetching panel" per `router.ts`'s own doc comment, so it already refreshes whenever the app's existing poll loop does. Not traced further by the Curator — confirm the poll interval is reasonable for a queue view (existing behavior, no separate polling to add) rather than building new refresh logic.
5. **"View skip / defer reason annotations"** — already implemented: `reasonCell`/`reasonText` in `dashboard/web/src/views/workQueue.ts` already render the daemon's disposition + reason + detail (park label / open-PR link) per row. No new work needed here; verify in the test plan rather than re-implementing.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `#/queue`'s merged Ready list (and Running/Blocked, where a rank exists) displays each row's dispatch rank/position (`QueueRow.rank`, reusing the existing `rankText()` convention — "–" for unranked/labelled-blocked rows), not only in the per-host detail panel.
- [ ] `#/queue` gains client-side filter controls for **repo** and **tier**, filtering the already-merged `FleetQueueItem[]` — no new network request per filter change, consistent with the "view over the polled snapshot" architecture `router.ts` documents.
- [ ] A persistent link to `#/queue` is added to the dashboard's primary navigation (alongside Charts/Tokens/Spend/Feed), so the queue view no longer depends on first visiting the overview page.
- [ ] No new backend/API endpoint is introduced. The feature is built entirely on the existing `GET /api/fleet-state` / `GET /public/fleet-state` payloads already fetched into `FleetView` (do **not** add `GET /api/v1/queue/ranked`).
- [ ] The issue's/PR's description of dispatch ordering matches verified behavior: `workspace_priority` (config), then `loom:urgent`, then oldest `createdAt`, then issue number — not `tier:*`/`priority:high`/`loom:curated`.
- [ ] New/changed logic (rank column, filter state/predicate) has unit tests added to `dashboard/web/test/workQueue.test.ts` following the existing patterns there (e.g. the `mergeFleetQueue`/`workQueueSummarySection` describe blocks), and `dashboard/web/test/router.test.ts` if nav/route wiring changes.
- [ ] `cd dashboard/web && npm run check` (typecheck + `vitest run`) passes.

### Affected Files (starting point — verify completeness before dispatch, per "Verify enumerations")

- `dashboard/web/src/views/workQueue.ts` — add rank column to merged lists; wire filter UI.
- `dashboard/web/src/workQueue.ts` — pure filter-predicate helper(s) alongside `mergeFleetQueue`/`compareItems`, unit-testable without DOM.
- `dashboard/web/src/router.ts` / `dashboard/web/src/app.ts` — only if nav wiring requires a route-level change beyond the existing `#/queue` parse (likely just a template/nav-markup change, not a new `Route` variant).
- `dashboard/web/test/workQueue.test.ts` — new tests for rank display and filtering.
- `dashboard/web/test/router.test.ts` — only if nav wiring touches routing.
- No `loom-daemon/*` changes expected — the daemon side of this data (comparator, `ReadyQueueRow`, `queue.snapshot` telemetry) already exists and is out of scope.

### Overlap Risk With Concurrently Curated Issues

- **#9029** (dashboard timeline/saturation panel, curated in parallel): likely touches `dashboard/web/src/app.ts` (panel/mount registration) and possibly `dashboard/web/src/panels.ts`/`router.ts` if it adds a new self-fetching panel route the way Charts/Tokens/Spend/Feed work. This issue's nav-link addition touches the same files for a different reason (adding a plain view route to nav, not a new panel). Not traced whether the two land in literally the same lines — flagged as a coordination/rebase risk on `app.ts` (and possibly `router.ts`), not a hard blocker; whichever PR merges first, the other rebases.
- **#9034** (host-class refusal) is adding a new `QueueDisposition` variant to `loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs` (`ALL`, `as_str()`, `reason()`, `state()`) and touches every exhaustive match over it, per its own Affected Files list (`loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/queue.rs`, `queue_blocked.rs`, `telemetry/queue_snapshot.rs`). On the dashboard side, an unrecognized disposition already degrades gracefully today — `dashboard/src/queueState.ts`'s `normalizeRow` maps any unknown `state` value to `"unknown"` (`ROW_STATES.find(...) ?? "unknown"`), and the TS `QueueRowState` union already includes `"unknown"` — so #9034 landing first or second should not break this issue's Builder. No code coordination is structurally required, but avoid hand-editing `dashboard/src/queueState.ts`'s disposition/state handling in this PR; if it needs touching at all, keep the diff additive.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Unit tests: rank-column rendering for a `QueueRow` with `rank > 0` and with `rank === 0` (unranked), extending `dashboard/web/test/workQueue.test.ts`.
- [ ] Unit tests: filter predicate(s) — filtering by repo, by tier, and the "no filter" (show-all) default — as pure-function tests over `FleetQueueItem[]`, not DOM tests.

issues.title: cleanup-branches.sh: drop the dead extract-and-eval of merge-pr.sh's _maybe_delete_local_branch helpers; call loom-daemon merge-pr delete-branch directly
issues.body:
## Problem

`defaults/scripts/cleanup-branches.sh` reuses `merge-pr.sh`'s `_maybe_delete_local_branch` for its `pr-*` review-branch pass. It `awk`-extracts the function body out of `merge-pr.sh` and `eval`s it, alongside:

- a `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/branch-landed.sh"`, plus a hand-written fail-closed `branch_landed()` shim for a partially-resynced `.loom/`;
- the extracted transitive helpers `_primary_worktree_path`, `_is_primary_worktree_path`, and `_find_worktree_by_branch`, plus fallback shims for each.

The #8191 local-branch-cleanup slice turned `_maybe_delete_local_branch` into a thin call to `loom-daemon merge-pr delete-branch`, which is the same `worktree_cli::branch_delete` rule `worktree.sh remove` uses. After that slice, **none of the sourced/extracted helpers above is called by the extracted body.** They are dead weight in the portable-shell pool. The extract-and-`eval` contraption also exists only to avoid a second implementation. That goal is now met more directly by calling the subcommand itself.

That slice intentionally left `cleanup-branches.sh` unchanged. Its retained suite `test-cleanup-branches-pr-review-branch.sh` asserts on that wiring's source text in 9 places, and changing it would have widened the slice beyond the `merge-pr.sh` port.

## Suggested fix

- Replace the extract/`eval` block with a direct `loom-daemon merge-pr delete-branch --repo-root … --branch … --expected-head-sha … [--default-branch …]` call. Replay its `LEVEL<TAB>message` stdout through the script's own `info`/`warning`/`success`, as `merge-pr.sh` does. Or, better, add a small shared shell helper both callers use.
- Drop the `branch-landed.sh` sourcing, the `branch_landed()` shim, and the dep-helper extraction list.
- Retire the source-text assertions in `test-cleanup-branches-pr-review-branch.sh` under the three-part test in `defaults/docs/verification-recipes.md` §6, with the suite's behavioural cases as successors. Those cases already run against the pinned daemon.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cleanup-branches.sh` no longer extracts or `eval`s any function from `merge-pr.sh`.
- [ ] `test-cleanup-branches-pr-review-branch.sh`'s behavioural cases pass unchanged. Any retired source-text assertion is recorded via `retired()` with a named successor.
- [ ] The portable-shell line count drops, and nothing in the file-size / shell-budget ratchets grows.

Found while building the #8191 local-branch-cleanup slice.

issues.title: test-loom-daemon-update.sh scenario 64: pipefail + `grep -q` SIGPIPE race turns a passing --help assertion into a CI failure
issues.body:
Surfaced while judging PR #9137 (issue #8923). The job `Native Port Suites (daemon lifecycle, watchdog, spawn-claude)` failed at head `3ae21236` on:

```
✗ --help documents --drain / --timeout / --force-after-timeout / --restart-now
```

(run 36273670203, job 108492391307). It is a harness defect, not a behavioural one, and it will recur on unrelated PRs.

## Mechanism

`defaults/scripts/tests/test-loom-daemon-update.sh` sets `set -uo pipefail` (line 25). Scenario 64 (~line 3802) asserts via four chained pipelines:

```bash
help64_out=$(bash "$UPDATE_SCRIPT" --help 2>/dev/null)
if echo "$help64_out" | grep -q -- '--drain' && echo "$help64_out" | grep -q -- '--timeout' \
    && echo "$help64_out" | grep -q -- '--force-after-timeout' \
    && echo "$help64_out" | grep -q -- '--restart-now'; then
```

`grep -q` exits the instant it matches, closing the pipe. `--help` output is **33,024 bytes** — just past GNU grep's 32 KiB initial read buffer — so `grep` can match-and-exit while `echo` still has bytes to write. `echo` then takes `EPIPE`, and `pipefail` promotes that write error to the pipeline's status, so the `if` takes the `else` branch **even though every pattern matched**.

The failing run's own log carries the proof:

```
defaults/scripts/tests/test-loom-daemon-update.sh: line 3806: echo: write error: Broken pipe
✗ --help documents --drain / --timeout / --force-after-timeout / --restart-now
```

Line 3806 is the `--restart-now` leg. A broken pipe there is only reachable because that `grep -q` matched and exited early — an *unmatched* `grep -q` reads to EOF and never closes the pipe. So the assertion's content check succeeded and the test reported failure anyway.

## Why it is unattributable to the PR that tripped it

`defaults/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh` and `defaults/scripts/tests/test-loom-daemon-update.sh` are byte-identical between `5344bfb6` (where this job passed) and `3ae21236` (where it failed):

```
git diff 5344bfb6 3ae21236 -- defaults/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh \
    defaults/scripts/tests/test-loom-daemon-update.sh   # empty
```

and no `main` commit pulled in by that PR's rebase touched either path.

## Suggested fix

Stop putting a large payload through a pipe into an early-exiting reader. Use a herestring (no pipe, no SIGPIPE):

```bash
if grep -q -- '--drain' <<<"$help64_out" && grep -q -- '--timeout' <<<"$help64_out" \
    && grep -q -- '--force-after-timeout' <<<"$help64_out" \
    && grep -q -- '--restart-now' <<<"$help64_out"; then
```

Then audit the rest of this suite (and sibling suites) for the same `echo "$big" | grep -q` shape — this is the same mechanism class as #7285 and #7540, and scenario 63's own history (#7201) shows the neighbouring `--help documents --check / --dry-run / --no-restart` assertion already flaked once for a different reason. Per #7789 ("fix the mechanisms, not the instances"), a repo-wide sweep for `| grep -q` under `pipefail` is worth more than patching this one line.

issues.title: role runner / work finder: demand-weighted build/review allocation (Phase 2 of #9391)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

## Summary

Phase 2 of #9391, split out during curation. #9391 now covers **Phase 1 only**: every role-runner role dispatches concurrently across repositories, with at most one instance per `(repository, role)`, per-role budgets, and empty-queue gating. This issue carries the **demand-weighted** half of the operator's 2026-09-28 direction, #9391 §2 and §3: shift fleet effort between building and reviewing based on how many PRs are waiting, not on a fixed timer.

**Depends on #9391 (Phase 1) merging.** Width only has something to weight once role loops can run more than one repository at a time.

## Problem

Nothing in the daemon reads review or merge demand when it admits work. `RepoPipelineSnapshot::review_requested` / `changes_requested` / the `loom:pr` count (`loom-daemon/src/pipeline_snapshot.rs:49-75`, `:605-640`) feed only the `health` queue section and `is_review_stalled` (`loom-daemon/src/health.rs:2036`). The work-finder keeps admitting new issue builds up to `min(disk, ram, autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrent)` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs:176`, `:2251`), however deep the review and merge queues get. The 2026-09-28 measurement in #9391 found 28 PRs in `loom:review-requested`, 59 in `loom:pr` and 106 issues ready, so builders were piling up finished work faster than it could be reviewed or merged.

## Proposal (from #9391 §2/§3)

Recompute each work-finder or role-runner tick, per host:

- `review_debt = review_requested + changes_requested` and `merge_debt = loom:pr`.
- **Role width:** `judge_width = clamp(ceil(review_debt / k), 1, judge_max)`. Doctor uses the same shape on `changes_requested`, and Champion uses it on `merge_debt`. This width **replaces the static Phase 1 per-role budget as the effective budget**, capped by the Phase 1 budget.
- **Build back-off (WIP limit):** once `review_debt + merge_debt > W`, the work-finder stops admitting **new** issue builds. Its freed slots run PR-only sweeps (Judge → Doctor → merge, the #7649 path) until the debt falls below `W_low`. Hysteresis prevents oscillation. When the queue is empty, every slot goes back to builders.
- Champion goes first (§3). It is the cheapest role and it releases the most finished work.
- Conservative defaults: `k=3`, `judge_max=4`, `W=40`, `W_low=25`. Expose all four as config keys under `autonomous.workFinder.*` / `autonomous.roleRunner.*`. Log every back-off and width decision along with the debt it saw, so the values can be tuned from SigNoz.
- Optional: make role admission aware of token-pool headroom, so the pool rather than loop shape is the binding limit. Phase 1 only keeps the existing per-invocation pool selection and the #6614 empty-pool brake.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Work-finder admission stops admitting new issue builds above a configurable `review_debt + merge_debt` threshold `W` and resumes below `W_low`. Unit tests cover the hysteresis edges: exactly `W`, between `W_low` and `W` on both the rising and falling path, and exactly `W_low`.
- [ ] While backed off, freed slots dispatch PR-only sweeps rather than sitting idle. This is tested with a stubbed pipeline snapshot.
- [ ] Judge, Doctor and Champion effective width follows `clamp(ceil(debt/k), 1, max)`, bounded by the Phase 1 per-role budget. Unit tested.
- [ ] Each decision logs one line with the debt observed, the threshold, and the resulting admission or width.
- [ ] An unobserved debt axis (a `None` snapshot field) never triggers back-off. It fails open to today's behaviour, matching `is_review_stalled`'s "cannot tell" discipline.
- [ ] Every new key is documented in `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`'s config table.
- [ ] Before/after measurement on one host: `loom:reviewing` concurrency, median time in `loom:review-requested` and `loom:pr`, and token spend per merged PR (carried over from #9391's acceptance).

## Affected files (expected)

- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs`: admission back-off
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs`: demand-driven effective width
- `loom-daemon/src/pipeline_snapshot.rs`: debt inputs, reused rather than re-queried
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`

Related: #9391 (Phase 1, prerequisite), #7649, #8928, #9249, #8923.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-28, verified against `origin/main` `23afd5c0d`, which includes #9403 = #9391 Phase 1)

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->
<!-- loom:points=8 -->

### Scope decision: this issue is now **Phase 2a only**

The original body mixed three deliverables. They are now separated:

| Part | Where | Delivered by |
|---|---|---|
| **2a: demand ledger, demand-weighted Judge/Doctor width, Champion-first ceiling reservation** | **this issue (#9392)** | **this sweep's Builder** |
| 2b: work-finder build back-off (WIP limit, `W`/`W_low` hysteresis) and PR-only work in the freed slots | #9410 (filed at `loom:triage`, depends on this issue's ledger) | a later sweep |
| Before/after measurement | the post-merge operational checklist at the bottom of this issue | an operator/Champion step after merge, **not** a build AC |

**Why 2a goes first.** Phase 1 left the role-runner host ceiling heavily over-subscribed, and nothing on it prefers PR work. The facts, measured on `23afd5c0d`:
- `default_max_concurrent()` = number of interval-default roles = **7** (`role_runner.rs:2244`: `interval_default_roles().len()`; `DEFAULT_ROLES` at `:453` lists champion, curator, judge, doctor, auditor, hermit, guide with `interval_default: true`).
- The default per-role budget is `ceiling/2` = **3** (`concurrent_dispatch.rs:104`).
- Only judge and doctor are queue-gated (`work_queue_labels`, `concurrent_dispatch.rs:64-70`). Champion, curator, auditor, hermit and guide are dispatched to every registered repo every tick, up to budget 3 each, which is 15 wanted slots against a ceiling of 7.

So on a many-repo host, the 7 slots go to whichever role loop ticks first. With 28 `loom:review-requested` and 59 `loom:pr` PRs waiting, curator, auditor, hermit and guide still compete on equal terms with judge and champion. Reserving ceiling slots for the PR roles in proportion to their debt, Champion first, is the change in this code that most directly drains those two queues. It stays inside `role_runner/` and needs no new dispatch type.

2b is not the simpler part. The work-finder has no PR-only dispatch path today: `grep -n PrSet loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` returns no lines, and `SweepTarget::PrSet` is only produced by `sweep_registry/` (the #7649 watchdog handoff). "Freed slots run PR-only sweeps" therefore needs a new candidate source, which is why it was split out.

### Verified citations (as of `23afd5c0d`)

| Original citation | Status |
|---|---|
| `pipeline_snapshot.rs:49-75` fields | Struct at `:49`. `review_requested` `:62`, `changes_requested` `:64`, `approved` (the `loom:pr` count) **`:77`**. |
| `pipeline_snapshot.rs:605-640` | The `gh pr list` calls sit at `:590-640` (review-requested at `:597`, `loom:pr` at `:635`). **These are uncached GraphQL `gh pr list` subprocesses**, used only by the CLI `status --pipeline` and `serve.rs:480`. See "Data path" below: the dispatcher must not call them. |
| `health.rs:2036` `is_review_stalled` | Correct: `:2036`. Returns `false` unless both axes are `Some` (the fail-open discipline to copy). |
| `work_finder.rs:176`, `:2251` | `:176` is `DEFAULT_WORK_FINDER_MAX_CONCURRENT = 3`. `resolve_dynamic_max_concurrent` is at **`:2250`**. Its per-tick call in the production loop (`spawn_multi_work_finder_task`, `:2708`) is at **`:2894`**. These now belong to #9410, not to this issue. |
| `role_runner.rs` "demand-driven effective width" | Phase 1 put the budget path in **`role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs`**, not in `role_runner.rs`. See the next section. |

### Where 2a plugs into the Phase 1 budget path

Traced by reading the code at `23afd5c0d`. Nothing was executed.

1. `spawn_multi_role_task` (`role_runner.rs:3308`) builds one `RoleDispatcher` per role (`:3328`). Each interval it calls `dispatcher.dispatch_tick(roots, &in_progress)` (`:3394`). After a `QueueEmpty` run it calls `resume_after_queue_empty` (`:3351`).
2. `RoleDispatcher::walk` (`concurrent_dispatch.rs:520`) calls `decide` for each root, rotating from the round-robin cursor (`rotation_start`, `:507`). It **stops at the first `Refused`**, because every limit is host-wide, and keeps the remaining roots in `pending`.
3. The production `decide` is `decide_root_tick_detailed` (`role_runner.rs:3012`). It ends in `concurrent_dispatch::admit_root_tick` (`role_runner.rs:3157` calls `concurrent_dispatch.rs:189`).
4. `admit_root_tick` resolves `ceiling = resolve_max_concurrent(config)` and `budget = resolve_role_max_concurrent(&read_role_max_concurrent(root), role, ceiling)` (**`concurrent_dispatch.rs:196-197`**). It then calls `RoleRunGuard::admit_with_role_budget` (`role_runner.rs:2486`), which checks `InProgress`, then `CeilingReached`, then `RoleBudgetReached` under **one lock** (`:2493-2514`).

**Plug point.** `admit_root_tick`, between computing `budget` (`:197`) and calling the admission:
- Replace `budget` with `demand::effective_budget(role, budget, &host_debt, &cfg)` for **judge and doctor**.
- Pass the Champion-first reservation into a new admission variant. That variant takes the reservation **inside the same lock**, so the count the decision is made against is the count the insert lands in (the #6102 race argument in `admit`'s doc comment, `role_runner.rs:2460-2465`).
- Leave the `walk` stop-at-first-refusal logic as it is. A reservation refusal is host-wide too.

**Other admission sites that must stay consistent.** `RoleAdmission` is matched exhaustively at `role_runner.rs:2438` (`into_guard`), `:2738` (idle-edge admission, which calls `admit_with_role_budget` at `:2706`) and `:3249` (the single-workspace loop). If you add a variant, handle all three.
- Idle-edge runs **keep the Phase 1 budget** and do not take the demand path. That keeps this PR's blast radius to the interval loop.
- The idle-edge site must still compile against the new variant. Treat it as a refusal and log it at `debug!`.

### Data path: the dispatcher reads a ledger fed by listings it already makes (no new per-tick forge query)

The constraint: nothing may add a forge query per tick per repo. `pipeline_snapshot::GhPipelineSource` is ruled out, because every field is an uncached GraphQL `gh pr list` (`pipeline_snapshot.rs:590-640`).

What already exists (verified by reading, `23afd5c0d`):
- `forge_listing::list_issues_cached_as` (`forge_listing.rs:97`) is the ETag-cached REST listing. An unchanged listing costs a free `304` (module doc `:10-17`). The cache is keyed by resolved repo + credential + URL, so **every caller listing the same label shares one entry** (`:176`, `store::daemon_cache_key`).
- The Phase 1 queue gate `forge_queue_probe` (`concurrent_dispatch.rs:286`) already lists `loom:review-requested` (judge) and `loom:changes-requested` (doctor) **once per admitted run**, inside the spawned blocking task, not in the synchronous walk (`run_gated`, `:313-333`). It currently throws the rows away and keeps only `!rows.is_empty()` (`:302`).
- Nothing lists `loom:pr` per run by default. `role_collision`'s champion probe lists it (`role_collision.rs:180`, `:550`), but only when collision detection is on, and that defaults to `false` (`resolve_detection_enabled`, `role_collision.rs:352-365`, falling through to `sweep_registry::resolve_collision_detection`, env > config > false).

**Specified data path.** Add a process-global **demand ledger** in a new module `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/demand.rs`:
- It maps `(root, axis)` to `(count, observed_at: Instant)`, where `axis ∈ {Review = loom:review-requested, Changes = loom:changes-requested, Merge = loom:pr}`. `count` is the number of **open PR rows** (`RestIssue::is_pull_request`) in the listing.
- **Judge and doctor.** `forge_queue_probe` records the PR-row count of the listing it already makes. You can change `QueueProbe` to return a count, or record inside the probe. Either way, **no new call**.
- **Champion.** `run_gated` makes **one** extra `list_issues_cached_as` call for `loom:pr`, with caller `"role_demand"`, and records it. This call is **count-only and never gates** Champion. Champion stays ungated because it also promotes `loom:curated` issues (`concurrent_dispatch.rs:58-62`). The cost is one ETag request per *admitted champion run*, a free `304` when nothing changed. It is not per tick per repo.
- **Reads.** `admit_root_tick` reads a host aggregate from the ledger, which is a mutex read with no I/O. For each axis it takes the sum over entries younger than `staleSecs`, plus the number of roots with a nonzero fresh count. An axis with no fresh entry is **`None` (unobserved)**.
- A failed listing records nothing, so that root's entry ages out. An error never reads as `0`.
- The listing is single-page (`PER_PAGE = 100`, `forge_listing.rs:42`), so a per-root count saturates at 100. That is acceptable, and matches the existing truncation warning.
- #9410 (2b) reads the same ledger. That is the reason it lives in its own module rather than inside `RoleDispatcher`.

Staleness caveat (inferred, not measured). An entry refreshes only when its role runs in that root. Empty judge/doctor queues refresh quickly: a `QueueEmpty` run triggers `resume_after_queue_empty` within the same interval. Deep queues refresh once per admitted run. `staleSecs` bounds how long a stale count can steer admission.

### Width and reservation rules (the spec for 2a)

For role `r` with debt axis `d(r)` (judge → Review, doctor → Changes, champion → Merge):

- **Correction to the original.** Judge's width uses `review_requested` **only**, not `review_requested + changes_requested`. A `loom:changes-requested` PR is Doctor's work until Doctor returns it to review.
- `width(r) = clamp(ceil(debt/k), 1, min(max, phase1_budget(r)))` when the axis is observed. When it is unobserved, `width(r) = phase1_budget(r)`, which is exactly Phase 1 behaviour.
- **Effective budget.**
  - Judge and doctor: `width(r)`. They are queue-gated, so this only changes how many *non-empty* repos are served at once.
  - **Champion: unchanged Phase 1 budget.** It is ungated and has non-PR work (promotion), so demand must never throttle it. Its width feeds only the reservation.
- **Reservation (Champion-first).**
  - Each PR role reserves `want(p) = min(width(p), roots_with_nonzero_debt(p))` ceiling slots. `want` is `0` when the axis is unobserved or its debt is 0. A role cannot use more slots than it has distinct repos with debt, because Phase 1 allows one instance per `(repo, role)`.
  - Priority order is **champion > judge > doctor > every other role**.
  - When role `r` is admitted, compute `reserved(r) = min( Σ_{p higher-priority than r} max(0, want(p) − active(p)), ceiling − nonPrFloor )` under the admission lock. Admit only if `active_total + reserved(r) < ceiling`.
  - For every non-PR role (curator, auditor, hermit, guide, architect, ...) the sum is over all three PR roles.
  - Champion's `reserved` is always 0.
- `nonPrFloor` stops non-PR roles from being starved entirely.
- **Correction to the original defaults.** At the default ceiling of 7, Phase 1's default budget is 3, so `max = 4` binds only where `roleMaxConcurrent` is configured to 4 or more. That is intended: demand never raises a role above its Phase 1 budget.

### Config keys (all under `autonomous.roleRunner.demandWidth`, resolved per root and applied live, like `roleMaxConcurrent`)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` restores exactly Phase 1 admission (no ledger reads, no reservation, no extra champion listing) |
| `perRun` (`k`) | `3` | debt items per role run in the width formula |
| `max` | `4` | upper clamp on judge, doctor and champion width (still capped by the Phase 1 budget) |
| `reserve` | `true` | Champion-first ceiling reservation. `false` keeps the width but reserves nothing. |
| `nonPrFloor` | `1` | ceiling slots the reservation always leaves for non-PR roles |
| `staleSecs` | `1800` | ledger entries older than this are unobserved |

Invalid values (zero, negative, non-integer) drop to the default per key, which is the `parse_role_max_concurrent` discipline (`concurrent_dispatch.rs:79-96`). Use no env vars, matching `roleMaxConcurrent` (config only).

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `role_runner/demand.rs` ledger:
  - [ ] Recording and aggregation are unit tested: sum, roots-with-debt, staleness expiry (an entry older than `staleSecs` makes the axis `None`), and a failed listing records nothing.
  - [ ] Only PR rows are counted.
- [ ] Judge and doctor feed the ledger from the existing `forge_queue_probe` listing. A test with a stub probe or runner shows **no additional listing call** for those roles.
- [ ] Champion's admitted run records `loom:pr` exactly once per run. A test counts the calls. Champion is **never** gated by that count: an empty `loom:pr` listing still invokes the runner.
- [ ] `width()` pure-function tests:
  - [ ] debt `0` → 1.
  - [ ] debt `k` → 1.
  - [ ] debt `k+1` → 2.
  - [ ] a large debt clamps to `min(max, phase1_budget)`.
  - [ ] unobserved (`None`) → `phase1_budget`.
- [ ] Judge and doctor admission uses `width` as the effective budget, and refusals report it. A `RoleDispatcher::with_decide` / `admit_root_tick` test with an injected ledger shows judge refused at `width` while the Phase 1 budget still has room. Champion's budget is unchanged by any debt value.
- [ ] Champion-first reservation (lock-level tests on the new admission fn, with a stubbed ledger):
  - [ ] With merge debt spread over ≥2 roots and `active_total = ceiling − 1`, a curator admission is refused with the new reservation variant while a champion admission succeeds.
  - [ ] Reservation never exceeds `ceiling − nonPrFloor`.
  - [ ] `want(p)` counts only roots with nonzero debt.
  - [ ] Reservation is 0 when every axis is unobserved.
- [ ] `demandWidth.enabled: false` gives byte-identical Phase 1 admission. The existing `role_runner/tests/concurrent_dispatch.rs` tests pass unchanged, and a new test asserts no ledger or champion listing call.
- [ ] Logging:
  - [ ] One INFO line when a role's `(effective width, reservation)` **changes**, naming the observed debt, `k`, `max`, the Phase 1 budget and the result. It is edge-triggered, not per tick per root.
  - [ ] The tick's existing single refusal summary line (`refusal_summary_line`, `concurrent_dispatch.rs:224`) gets a reservation case that names the reserved count and which PR roles it is held for.
- [ ] Every exhaustive `RoleAdmission` match compiles and behaves: `role_runner.rs:2438`, `:2738` (idle edge, which keeps the Phase 1 budget), `:3249`.
- [ ] All six keys are documented in `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`: the config table next to `roleMaxConcurrent` (`:4548`), the summary table (`:7496`), and one paragraph in the "Concurrent across repositories" section (`:3663` onward).
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon` and `cargo clippy -p loom-daemon -- -D warnings` pass.

### Implementation Guidance

- Keep the formula and reservation arithmetic as **pure functions** in `demand.rs` (inputs: debts, actives, config). Keep the one-lock part in `role_runner.rs` as a sibling of `admit_with_role_budget` (for example `admit_with_demand(set, root, role, ceiling, budget, &ReservationPlan)`), so existing callers are untouched.
- `active(p)` per role must be counted **inside the admission lock** from the `InProgressGuard` set. The same set already gives `role_active` at `role_runner.rs:2503`.
- Do **not** probe the forge in `admit_root_tick`. It runs in the synchronous walk (see the module doc, `concurrent_dispatch.rs:36-43`).
- Declare the module next to `pub mod concurrent_dispatch;` (`role_runner.rs:3921`). Put tests at `role_runner/tests/demand.rs`, following the `#[path = "tests/concurrent_dispatch.rs"]` pattern at `concurrent_dispatch.rs:655-658`.
- Out of scope: build back-off and PR-only sweeps (#9410), token-pool-aware admission (#9391 §2, optional), and changes to `pipeline_snapshot.rs` or `health.rs`, which stay read-only references for semantics.

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/demand.rs` (**new**): ledger, aggregation, `width`/`want`/reservation pure functions, `demandWidth` config parse
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests/demand.rs` (**new**): unit tests for the above
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs`: `forge_queue_probe`/`QueueProbe` record counts; `run_gated` champion `loom:pr` count-only listing; `admit_root_tick` effective budget and reservation; `LimitRefusal` reservation case and `refusal_summary_line`
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests/concurrent_dispatch.rs`: dispatcher-level tests (injected ledger, `enabled:false` parity)
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs`: `mod demand;`, the new admission fn and `RoleAdmission` variant, exhaustive-match arms at `:2438`, `:2738`, `:3249`
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`: the six keys and one section paragraph

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: the new `role_runner/tests/demand.rs` plus additions to `role_runner/tests/concurrent_dispatch.rs`, as listed in the ACs. No test may touch the network. Use the stub `QueueProbe`, `RunnerFactory` and an injected ledger.
- [ ] Edge cases: every axis unobserved; one axis stale and others fresh; ceiling 1 (reservation capped by `nonPrFloor`, so champion and curator can still each run); `roleMaxConcurrent` below `max`; a root with debt that leaves the registry.
- [ ] Manual (optional, local): run `loom-daemon` on a host with PR debt, grep the role-runner log for the new width/reservation INFO lines, and check that no new `role_demand` caller appears in `forge_call_stats` more often than champion runs are admitted.

### Post-merge operational follow-up (NOT a build AC; do not block the PR on it)

- [ ] On one host, for about 24h before and after deploy, measure `loom:reviewing` concurrency, median time in `loom:review-requested` and in `loom:pr`, and token spend per merged PR. Carried from #9391's acceptance. Record the result as a comment here. If it shows the defaults need tuning, file it as a separate issue.

### Dependencies

- #9391 Phase 1: **merged** (#9403, on `origin/main` at `23afd5c0d`). No open blockers.
- #9410 (2b) depends on **this** issue, not the other way round.

issues.title: ETA phase 2: backfill + leak-free backtest harness (eta backfill, eta backtest)
issues.body:
Phase 2 of #9289 (ETA as a Loom primitive). Plan: Curator comment https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5867874254, operator decisions https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5869738711. **Depends on #9289 Phase 1** (core, heuristic registry, explanation schema, journal); do not start before it merges.

### Scope
- `loom-daemon eta backfill`: populate the stage-sample journal from `pr-latency` history (and any other local history), so heuristics have a baseline on day one.
- `loom-daemon eta backtest --heuristic <id> [--since] [--repo]`: replay past issues. At sampled moments `t`, compute the estimate using **only samples observed before `t`** (no leakage), then score it against the real outcome. Output (JSON + table): mean pinball loss, p25–p75 coverage and bias per kind/repo/horizon bucket. Also add a paired comparison of two heuristic ids on the identical replay set.
- This backtest is the **first gate for promoting a heuristic** (operator decision 2).

### Acceptance
- A leakage test: a fixture where future samples would change the answer, and the backtest must not see them.
- Golden backtest report on a fixture history.
- A paired-comparison test.
---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main`)

### Dependency status
Confirmed: #9289 Phase 1 merged (closed via PR #9355, `feat(eta): tracker, eager stage journal, eta.estimate/eta.outcome`, merged 2026-09-28T15:36:25Z). `loom-daemon/src/eta/{config,emit,explanation,grid,heuristics,history,journal,labels,score,simulate}.rs` all exist on `origin/main` as of this check, including `heuristics::{finish_v1, land_v1}` and `history::StageSamples::select`/`select_at` — the leak-free-replay primitive `eta/mod.rs`'s own doc comment says "the backtest in #9325 depends on this." This issue is unblocked; there is no `## Dependencies` checklist item left open.

There is no `loom-daemon eta backfill`/`eta backtest` CLI yet (verified: no `cli/eta_*` files, no `"eta"` subcommand registered) — this issue is genuinely the next increment, not already partially done.

### Related open work (absorbed/disregarded)
- **#9343** (ETA history must be fleet-global): disregarded for this issue's own scope. It explicitly names this issue ("Backtests would inherit all of this. (#9325)") as a *consumer* of the host-local-history limitation, not a redefinition of this issue's spec — `eta/mod.rs` already documents the same limitation inline. Phase 2 backtests against local history as designed; fleet-global history is separate follow-on work.
- **#9311** (dispatch_plan `held_until`): disregarded — separate `work_finder`/dispatch-plan scope (time-boxed hold expiry for the scheduler), not part of the backfill/backtest harness this issue delivers.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/cli/eta_cmd.rs` (new) — `loom-daemon eta backfill` and `loom-daemon eta backtest --heuristic <id> [--since] [--repo]` subcommands, modeled on the existing `cli/pr_latency_cmd.rs` + `cli/pr_latency_render.rs` split (parse/report separation).
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/mod.rs` — register the new `eta_cmd` module and CLI subcommand, alongside the existing `pr_latency_cmd`/`pr_latency_render` registration.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/journal.rs` — read path for `backfill`: populate `eta-stage-samples.jsonl` rows from `pr_latency::{PrHistory, PrEvent}` (`loom_daemon::pr_latency`, used today by `cli/pr_latency_cmd.rs`) for a baseline on day one.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/history.rs` — `StageSamples::select`/`select_at` is the as-of-`t` sample selection the backtest must call at each replay instant; no leakage is possible only if the backtest goes through this, not a hand-rolled filter.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/score.rs` — `OutcomeKind`/pinball-loss scoring machinery the backtest report aggregates (mean pinball loss, p25–p75 coverage, bias) per kind/repo/horizon bucket.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/simulate.rs` — `run_explanation`, used to recompute a heuristic's quantiles at each replayed instant from the as-of-`t` history.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/fixtures/` (new fixture) — a golden backtest report fixture and a leakage-test fixture (a case where a future sample would change the answer if selection leaked).

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: leakage test — a fixture where a sample observed at/after replay instant `t` would change the estimate; assert the backtest's result is identical whether or not that future sample exists in the underlying journal.
- [ ] Automated: golden backtest report — fixed fixture history (can extend `eta/fixtures/history-a.jsonl` or add a new one) → stable mean pinball loss / coverage / bias output, pinned like the existing `explanation-golden.json`.
- [ ] Automated: paired comparison of two heuristic ids (e.g. a real one vs. a synthetic worse one) on the identical replay set, asserting the comparison correctly ranks them.
- [ ] Manual: run `loom-daemon eta backfill` against a real `.loom/logs/` history and confirm the stage-sample journal gains rows; run `loom-daemon eta backtest --heuristic finish-v1` and sanity-check the printed report.

issues.title: Investigate daemon dispatch superseding a freshly renewed in-session sweep lease
issues.body:
## Observed collision

During the operator-requested in-session sweep of #8787 on 2026-09-24, the session published a lease before curation and renewed it successfully. A second host subsequently published a daemon sweep lease and claimed the same issue after promotion to `loom:issue`.

Forge evidence:

- In-session lease comment [5822662982](https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/8787#issuecomment-5822662982), host `host-d9142cf3`, sweep `sweep-20260924T213744Z-76692-1b436e14`: created **21:37:54Z**, renewed **21:42:08Z**.
- Peer daemon lease comment [5822727954](https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/8787#issuecomment-5822727954), host `host-f4fe7748`, sweep `sweep-issue-8787-1790286133`: created/updated **21:42:16Z**, only eight seconds after the earlier lease renewal.
- The in-session `sweep-lease-fence.sh check 8787 --host host-d9142cf3` returned **ABORT: SUPERSEDED** because the peer lease was newest. The session immediately stopped its Builder and renewal, preserved the clean worktree, and did not push/open a PR or alter the peer's claim.

The documented claim-then-verify-order contract says a later dispatcher should yield to the earlier live lease. The fresh in-session lease was inside the default 15-minute TTL. This is a verified ownership collision, **not yet a diagnosed source defect**: the peer's actual binary version/configuration, comment visibility and dispatch path must be checked before deciding whether code, installation drift or transient forge behavior caused it.

## Expected behavior

A live in-session lease protects the issue across curation → promotion → Builder startup, even before/while the `loom:building` label changes. A later daemon dispatcher must not leave two active owners; it should observe/yield to the existing live owner before spawning work. The in-session pre-push fence remains fail closed and must not be bypassed to paper over this collision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reconstruct the peer dispatch's version, path, pre-claim/claim-order checks and redacted relevant diagnostics for the observed timestamps; identify the actual cause.
- [ ] Add a regression covering a pre-published in-session lease, fresh renewal, `loom:curating` → `loom:issue` → `loom:building` transition, and racing daemon dispatch. The later dispatcher yields before builder/worktree access and leaves the winning claim intact.
- [ ] Cover stale/yielded leases, forge read failures and concurrent promotion without weakening existing exclusion/fence behavior or treating timestamps embedded in prose as liveness.
- [ ] If cause is installation/version drift rather than current source, document and apply the supported corrective update and provide post-update evidence instead of an unrelated speculative patch.

## Starting points

`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/guards.rs`, `sweep_registry/private_dispatch.rs`, dispatch claim ordering, and `defaults/scripts/sweep-lease-{publish,renew,fence}.sh`. Related #6287/#6320/#6485; #8553 concerns local worktree locking, not this cross-host admission/lease race.

Keep new executable logic in Rust and preserve shell budget, credential and no-daemon-state-write requirements. No production secrets in evidence.

issues.title: loom-daemon: 4 pre-existing test failures on this macOS host, unrelated to any single PR (found via #8191 sweep's post-wave build gate)
issues.body:
While running `/loom:sweep 8191`'s post-wave integration gate (`bash .loom/scripts/build-gate.sh`) against `main` at `68d8b794` (right after merging PR #9182, a `#8191` slice), the full `loom-daemon` test suite reported 4 failures out of 9570 tests. None are in a module PR #9182 touched (`merge_pr/worktrees.rs` and friends) — all 4 also reproduce **individually**, single-threaded (`cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib <name> -- --test-threads=1 --exact`), so this is not cross-test contention within one run.

## Failures

1. `worktree_ops::cargo_target::provision::tests::an_unredirected_host_is_a_no_op_even_when_enabled`
   ```
   panicked at loom-daemon/src/worktree_ops/cargo_target/provision/tests.rs:117:5:
   got Provisioned("/var/folders/.../repo/.loom/worktrees/issue-705/target/wt/issue-705")
   ```
   Expected a no-op; got an actual provision decision. Looks like a host-state heuristic (whatever "unredirected" checks) that doesn't hold on this host.

2. `native_tools::provision::state::tests::every_guarded_runtime_pins_tmpdir_into_a_short_reclaimable_path`
   ```
   panicked at loom-daemon/src/native_tools/provision/state_tests.rs:208:9:
   pi pinned TMPDIR /var/folders/.../pinned-tmp/<uuid> is too long for a Unix socket path
   ```
   `/var/folders/...` (macOS's real `$TMPDIR`) is long enough to blow the Unix-socket-path length assumption the test bakes in. This looks like a macOS-specific path-length issue — CI likely runs on Linux with a short `/tmp`, so it wouldn't see this.

3. `ipc::tests::dispatch_sweep_nonblocking_burst_acks_well_under_the_client_deadline`
   ```
   panicked at loom-daemon/src/ipc/tests.rs:1975:5:
   burst of 10 concurrent dispatch_sweep calls took 5.7785s — looks serialized behind the registry mutex (serialized bound ~7s)
   ```

4. `sweep_registry::dispatch::tests::concurrent_issue_dispatches_do_not_serialize_on_the_account_selection_poll`
   ```
   panicked at loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch/tests.rs:3093:5:
   burst of 10 concurrent dispatches took 5.230986792s (poll_delay=700ms) — looks serialized behind the registry mutex (serialized bound ~7s), not concurrent
   ```

(3) and (4) are timing-bound assertions on wall-clock concurrency; on a loaded host (this one had several concurrent `cargo build`/`cargo test` invocations running from the same sweep's Builder/Doctor/build-gate passes) they can plausibly cross the bound even without a real regression. (1) and (2) look like genuine host-environment assumptions (macOS `TMPDIR` shape, some "unredirected host" detection) rather than load-sensitivity.

## Why filing rather than fixing inline

This surfaced as a side-effect of `/loom:sweep 8191`'s post-wave `buildGate` check, which is scoped to catching cross-PR integration breaks — not general test-suite maintenance. None of the 4 failing modules were touched by the PR that triggered the gate (#9182), so treating this as a "red main caused by this sweep" and halting would be wrong; recording it as a follow-up for someone to triage (fix the assumption, mark host-conditional, or convert (3)/(4) to a looser/relative bound) is the correct scope.

## Suggested triage

- (1), (2): confirm whether these are meant to be Linux-only (CI-only) assumptions; if so, gate them behind a host check or `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, or fix the assumption so it holds on macOS too.
- (3), (4): consider whether the timing bound is too tight for a loaded dev host, or whether these should use a relative/statistical bound instead of an absolute wall-clock one.

Not investigated further — reporting as found, per the standard "file the follow-up, don't block on it" convention.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `83abe1f97`)

### Problem Statement
`cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib` is not green on a macOS dev/sweep host even with no regression in flight, so every post-wave `buildGate` run reports noise that Builders and sweeps must each re-diagnose. The four failures fall into two different classes and should be fixed separately, not as one "flaky tests" item:

| # | Test | Class |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `worktree_ops::cargo_target::provision::tests::an_unredirected_host_is_a_no_op_even_when_enabled` | deterministic, macOS-only (reproduced in isolation, twice) |
| 2 | `native_tools::provision::state::tests::every_guarded_runtime_pins_tmpdir_into_a_short_reclaimable_path` | deterministic on macOS when the ambient `$TMPDIR` is long; did **not** reproduce in the second corroborating run |
| 3 | `ipc::tests::dispatch_sweep_nonblocking_burst_acks_well_under_the_client_deadline` | wall-clock bound, load-sensitive |
| 4 | `sweep_registry::dispatch::tests::concurrent_issue_dispatches_do_not_serialize_on_the_account_selection_poll` | wall-clock bound, load-sensitive (reproduced at 4.1s even with 3 tests selected, so not purely intra-run contention) |

The comment also reports a fifth, host-load-only flake (`sweep_registry::reaper::container_stop::cancel_latency_tests::stalled_docker_discovery_delays_neither_sigterm_nor_unrelated_reads`) that passed on isolated re-run; include it in the timing-bound class (3/4) rather than filing separately.

### Suspected Cause (unverified — read from source, not run)
- **(1)** `provision.rs:164-167` compares `realish(root)` against `realish(worktree_path)` with `starts_with`; the test builds `root = <worktree>/target`, which does not exist yet. If `realish` canonicalizes only paths that exist, the worktree side resolves `/var/folders/…` → `/private/var/folders/…` while the not-yet-created `target` side stays `/var/folders/…`, so the `starts_with` containment check misses and the code falls through to `Provisioned`. That would also be a **production** bug on any macOS worktree under a symlinked prefix, not only a test artefact. Not stepped through; refute or confirm by printing both `realish` results on macOS.
- **(2)** `state_tests.rs:208-211` asserts `tmpdir.len() < 90` on `pinned_base.join(uuid)`, where `pinned_base` is under `tempfile::tempdir()` (i.e. the ambient macOS `$TMPDIR`, ~50 chars before the uuid). The fix may be in the test (root the pinned base under a short fixed prefix) or in the product (if the real pinned base can also exceed the socket limit on macOS, the test is correctly failing — check `NATIVE_PINNED_TMPDIR_BASE_ENV`'s production default first).
- **(3)/(4)** absolute wall-clock "serialized bound ~7s" assertions; measured 4.1–7.5s on a loaded host. Plausibly bound-too-tight, but the isolated 4.1s run means a real serialization regression cannot be ruled out without a relative comparison.

A measured refutation of any of these (e.g. "(1) is fine, the test fixture is wrong") is a complete, successful outcome for this issue.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] (1) On macOS, `an_unredirected_host_is_a_no_op_even_when_enabled` passes; if the cause is the canonicalization mismatch, `realish` (or the containment check) is fixed in product code and a regression test covers a not-yet-existing child of a symlinked worktree prefix.
- [ ] (2) `every_guarded_runtime_pins_tmpdir_into_a_short_reclaimable_path` passes on macOS with the default long `$TMPDIR`, without weakening the `< 90` socket-path assertion on the real pinned-base default.
- [ ] (3)/(4) replaced by a relative or statistical bound (e.g. burst elapsed vs. a serial baseline measured in the same test) so they neither flake under load nor lose the "not serialized behind the registry mutex" guarantee; a deliberately-serialized stub must still make them fail.
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib` completes with 0 failures on a macOS host, run twice, once while another `cargo build` is running.

## Affected Files
- `loom-daemon/src/worktree_ops/cargo_target/provision.rs` — `realish`/containment check (~L164) if the cause is confirmed in product code
- `loom-daemon/src/worktree_ops/cargo_target/provision/tests.rs` — test 1 (~L110) and a new symlinked-prefix regression test
- `loom-daemon/src/native_tools/provision/state_tests.rs` — test 2 (~L185-211)
- `loom-daemon/src/ipc/tests.rs` — test 3 (~L1936-1981)
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch/tests.rs` — test 4 (~L3093)
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper/container_stop.rs` (cancel-latency test) — only if the fifth flake is folded in

All six paths confirmed present on `origin/main` @ `83abe1f97` via `git ls-tree`.

## Test Plan
- [ ] Manual verification: on macOS, `cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib <name> -- --test-threads=1 --exact` for each of the four names, before and after.
- [ ] Automated tests: new symlinked-prefix regression test for (1); relative-bound tests for (3)/(4) with a negative control that fails under an injected serialization.
- [ ] Edge cases: run the full lib suite under load (concurrent `cargo build`); run on Linux CI to confirm no regression there.

## Notes
- Related open work: PR #9457 (ci-telemetry job dependency wait) surfaced only because it cross-references #9194 in passing; it touches none of these modules — disregarded as out of scope.
- Suggest a `routine` tier despite the timing tests: (1) may turn out to be a real product bug that tests would catch, and each fix is small and independently verifiable.

issues.title: Guard telemetry: force-op:detached blocks own-branch worktree resync via -C "$VAR" (31 events)
issues.body:
## What I Observed

`.loom/logs/guard-decisions.log` on this host (loom-worker) shows 31
`force-op:detached` ASK events since 2026-08-22 — an ASK tier means no
human answers it in a headless run, so each one fully stalls the command.
No open issue currently tracks this pattern (`check-duplicate.sh` returned
"No duplicates found").

## Representative Examples

Nearly all instances share one shape — a Builder/Doctor resyncing its own
feature branch inside its own managed worktree, using a shell variable for
the `-C`/cwd argument rather than a literal `cd`:

```bash
WORKTREE_ABS="$(cd .loom/worktrees/issue-9133 && pwd)"
git -C "$WORKTREE_ABS" fetch origin feature/issue-9133
git -C "$WORKTREE_ABS" reset --hard origin/feature/issue-9133
git -C "$WORKTREE_ABS" branch --set-upstream-to=origin/feature/issue-9133
git -C "$WORKTREE_ABS" rev-parse HEAD
```

and the `push` sibling:

```bash
cd .loom/worktrees/issue-8875 && git push --force-with-lease
```

Most recent instances: 2026-09-27T14:18:18Z (`issue-8875`), 2026-09-27T16:51:53Z
(`issue-9133`), 2026-09-25T18:01:57Z (`pr-8823`) — this is an active,
currently-recurring pattern, not a stale/historical one.

## Guard-Decision Telemetry Review Classification (role standing policy, #3898)

**Allowlist / refine.** `defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh` already
has a dedicated safe-shape allowlist for exactly this operation (#7530,
#5772): a `git reset --hard` whose target resolves to `origin/main`,
`origin/<default-branch>`, or the worktree's OWN tracked branch, inside a
Loom-managed worktree, is meant to be treated as safe (`_fdetached_safe=true`
at guard-destructive-generic.sh:9195-9217) — "a strict subset of the
force-push power that same agent already holds over that same branch via its
own PR."

That allowlist depends on resolving `_fcwd` (from a `-C` flag or `cd`) to an
absolute path via `_fcwdabs=$(normalize_abs_path "$_fcwd")` and then checking
`_in_any_managed_worktree "$_fcwdabs"` and `_managed_worktree_branch
"$_fcwdabs"`. When `-C` receives a shell variable populated by command
substitution (`-C "$WORKTREE_ABS"` where `WORKTREE_ABS="$(cd ... && pwd)"`)
rather than a literal path, the guard's static command parser cannot resolve
`$WORKTREE_ABS` to a path at all, so `_fcwdabs` stays empty,
`_in_any_managed_worktree ""` returns false, and the command falls through to
`force-op:detached` even though the reset target is provably the worktree's
own branch. This is the same root-cause class already identified for
`rm-scope-unresolved-var` (#9304) and `worktree-write-confinement-unresolved-var`
(#8755) — a guard's same-command resolution fast path not covering a
`VAR="$(cd <literal-relative-worktree-path> && pwd)"` assignment immediately
preceding its use — just manifesting in the force-op guard path instead.

Proposed refinement: extend the existing same-command resolution fast path so
that when `-C "$VAR"` (or a preceding bare `cd "$VAR"`) is used, and `$VAR`
was assigned in the same command block via `VAR="$(cd <literal-path> && pwd)"`
or `VAR="$(realpath <literal-path>)"` where `<literal-path>` is itself a
literal (no further expansion) — resolve `$VAR` to that literal path before
running the existing `_fdetached_safe` checks, rather than treating it as
unresolved. This does not touch the fail-closed default for genuinely
unresolvable targets (e.g. a value read from network output or an argument
handed in from outside the command).

## Impact

Headless (non-interactive) contexts have no human to satisfy the ASK, so each
occurrence blocks a Builder/Doctor from resyncing its own worktree to its own
already-pushed branch after an upstream rebase/force-push — exactly the
routine, in-scope, own-branch operation the existing #7530 allowlist was
built to cover, just defeated by the variable-cwd shape.

## Environment

- Host: loom-worker (AWS dispatch worker), `uname -sr`: Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws
- Commit audited: 680f612c0bf19ae534af2f3dc206150f116b417c
- Log window: 2026-08-22 through 2026-09-27 (31 events)

---
Discovered during main branch audit — Guard-Decision Telemetry Review (standing policy, #3898).

<!-- loom:premise-check exists=yes deliberate=yes reversal=no verdict=clear -->
premise-evidence: defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh:9168-9194 — the existing comment block documents the #7530/#5772 own-branch worktree-resync allowlist and its "fail toward asking" default for anything it cannot prove safe.
premise-extends: this proposes widening the existing same-command resolution fast path to one additional well-defined, literal-only shape (`VAR="$(cd <literal-path> && pwd)"` used as `-C "$VAR"`); it does not touch or weaken the fail-closed default for genuinely unresolvable targets, so it extends rather than reverses the #7530 design decision.

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->
<!-- loom:points=5 -->

### Verification against `origin/main`

Fetched and inspected `origin/main` @ `680f612c0` (2026-09-28). All code
references in the issue body check out, with exact current line numbers:

- `defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh:9195-9217` — the
  `_fdetached_safe` block (matches the issue's citation exactly).
- `defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh:9168-9194` — the preceding
  comment block documenting the #7530/#5772 own-branch worktree-resync
  allowlist and its fail-toward-asking default (matches the issue's
  `premise-evidence` citation exactly).
- `_fcwdabs=$(normalize_abs_path "$_fcwd")` is at line 9197; `_in_any_managed_worktree`
  is defined at line 1219; `_managed_worktree_branch` is defined at line 1253;
  `normalize_abs_path` is defined at line 7949 — all as named in the issue.

Traced the resolution path the fix needs to extend
(`git show origin/main:defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh`,
`parse_force_ops()` at line 4121):

- The `-C` argument resolution at lines 4311-4322 already calls
  `resolve_var()` (the shared `_VARRESOLVE_AWK` helper, line 2088) on a
  bare `$VAR`/`${VAR}` token — but `resolve_var()` only substitutes when
  `varmap[vname]` is a **literal** value. `record_assign()` (line 2163)
  stores whatever text follows `NAME=` verbatim (quote-stripped only) — for
  `WORKTREE_ABS="$(cd .loom/worktrees/issue-9133 && pwd)"` that is the
  literal string `$(cd .loom/worktrees/issue-9133 && pwd)`, which still
  starts with `$`, so `resolve_var()`'s own guard
  (`if (vv == "" || substr(vv, 1, 1) == "$") return tok`, line 2105) bails
  and returns the token unresolved — confirming the issue's root-cause
  claim.
- **There is already a narrower fast path for a related but distinct
  shape**: `#6724`'s `cd_proven`/`curcwd` tracking (lines 4244-4270) resolves
  `NAME=$(pwd)` / `` NAME=`pwd` `` **only when a separate, same-command,
  earlier `cd <literal-path>` segment already proved `curcwd`** — i.e. the
  two-statement form `cd <literal> && WORKTREE_ABS=$(pwd) && …`. It does
  **not** cover this issue's shape, where the `cd` and `pwd` are both
  *inside* the single assignment's own command substitution
  (`WORKTREE_ABS="$(cd <literal> && pwd)"`), so the existing #6724 path
  never even runs the `cd_proven` scan against it — this is a genuinely
  distinct, still-unhandled shape, not a duplicate of #6724's fix.
- **The closest existing precedent for the shape this issue actually asks
  for is #7532's `extract_cat_file()` / `match_cat_assignword()`** pair
  (lines 4128-4209): a narrow, textual, single-token recognizer for
  `NAME=$(cat <file>)` tried *before* the generic assignment scan, which
  extracts the literal argument and resolves it without ever touching the
  general `$(...)`-substitution case. The proposed fix should mirror this
  exact pattern for `$(cd <literal-path> && pwd)` / `` `cd <literal-path> && pwd` `` and
  the `$(realpath <literal-path>)` variant the issue also names, rather than
  attempting to special-case it inside `record_assign()`/`resolve_var()`
  (which are shared with `extract_write_targets()` and must stay generic).
- Downstream, the extracted literal path still passes through the *same*
  `normalize_abs_path()` call (line 9197) and the *same* `_in_any_managed_worktree`
  / `_managed_worktree_branch` safety checks (lines 9202-9217) that already
  gate the literal-`-C`-argument case today — the fix only widens *where a
  literal cwd string can be extracted from*, not the safe-shape predicate
  itself. This is what keeps the blast radius bounded despite guard-hook
  fail-closed stakes: a resolution bug here degrades to "stays unresolved,
  keeps asking" (the current, safe status quo) rather than to a new class of
  false-allow, unless the extracted literal is both wrong *and* happens to
  coincidentally satisfy the unchanged downstream managed-worktree/branch
  match — a narrow compound failure, not a direct weakening of the fail-closed
  default.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `parse_force_ops()` in `defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh`
      recognizes the literal-only shape `NAME="$(cd <literal-path> && pwd)"`
      (and the unquoted / backtick variants: `` NAME=`cd <literal-path> && pwd` ``,
      `NAME=$(cd <literal-path> && pwd)`) immediately preceding a `-C "$NAME"`
      or `cd "$NAME"` use in the same command, and resolves `$NAME` to
      `<literal-path>` (joined against the tracked `curcwd` the same way a
      literal `cd <literal-path>` argument already is, per lines 4285-4303) —
      not to the unresolved raw substitution text.
- [ ] The same recognizer also covers `NAME="$(realpath <literal-path>)"` (the
      other case named in the issue body), extracting `<literal-path>` the
      same way.
- [ ] `<literal-path>` must itself be a literal with no further `$` expansion
      or embedded quote characters — mirror `extract_cat_file()`'s own
      literal-only contract (line 4128-4147) exactly; any shape with a nested
      variable, command substitution, or unresolvable segment inside
      `<literal-path>` falls through unresolved (fail closed), matching the
      existing behavior for every currently-unresolvable shape.
- [ ] With the fix applied, the exact reproduction from the issue body —
      `WORKTREE_ABS="$(cd .loom/worktrees/issue-N && pwd)"` followed by
      `git -C "$WORKTREE_ABS" reset --hard origin/feature/issue-N` inside that
      worktree, on that worktree's own tracked branch — resolves
      `_fdetached_safe=true` and does **not** call `ask … "force-op:detached"`.
- [ ] A reset whose target does **not** match the worktree's own branch (e.g.
      `origin/feature/issue-M` for a different issue M, or a protected
      branch), or whose `-C "$VAR"` cwd resolves outside any managed
      worktree, still asks exactly as before — i.e. the fix does not touch
      `_fdetached_safe`'s own safe-shape predicate (lines 9198-9217), only the
      upstream cwd-argument resolution feeding into it.
- [ ] `git -C "$VAR" push --force-with-lease` (the `push` sibling shape named
      in the issue body) is unaffected by this fix's own-branch-reset scope —
      confirm in the test plan that it still asks as `force-op:all`/`force-op:protected`
      (its existing, unrelated code path), so this refinement is not
      mistakenly read as also softening force-push handling.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh` — extend `parse_force_ops()`'s
  same-command assignment-scanning loop (the `while ((_alen =
  next_assignword_len(seg)) > 0)` block, lines 4244-4271) with a new
  literal-recognizer function (sibling to `extract_cat_file()` /
  `match_cat_assignword()`, lines 4128-4209) for the `$(cd <literal> && pwd)`
  / `` `cd <literal> && pwd` `` / `$(realpath <literal>)` shapes, storing the
  resolved literal directly into `varmap[NAME]` (bypassing
  `record_assign()`'s verbatim-text storage for exactly this recognized
  shape, the same way the existing `#6724` `cd_proven`/`$(pwd)` branch and
  `#7532` `extract_cat_file()` branch already do at lines 4258-4267).
  Verified present on `origin/main` @ `680f612c0`, 2026-09-28.
- `defaults/hooks/tests/` (or wherever the existing `force-op:detached` /
  #7530 / #5772 allowlist regression tests live — locate via `grep -rl
  "force-op:detached" defaults/hooks/tests/` in the worktree at build time,
  since this curation pass did not enumerate the test directory tree) — add
  new cases for the `-C "$VAR"` compound-assignment shape. **Not
  independently verified against `origin/main` in this pass** — the Builder
  must confirm the actual test file path(s) before writing new cases; treat
  this bullet as a pointer, not a promise of an exact path.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Add a regression test reproducing the issue's exact first example:
      `WORKTREE_ABS="$(cd .loom/worktrees/issue-N && pwd)"; git -C

      Loom-managed worktree on its own tracked branch — asserts no `ask` /
      `force-op:detached` fires (mirrors the existing #7530/#5772 literal-`-C`
      test case, just with the variable-cwd shape).
- [ ] Add a negative-control test: same shape but the reset target is
      `origin/feature/issue-<other>` (a different worktree's branch) — asserts
      the command still asks `force-op:detached` (proves the fix does not
      loosen the safe-shape predicate itself, only the cwd resolution feeding
      it).
- [ ] Add a negative-control test: `-C "$VAR"` where `$VAR`'s assignment is
      NOT a literal-only `$(cd <literal> && pwd)`/`realpath` shape (e.g. `VAR="$(some_dynamic_command)"`,
      or the path argument itself contains a nested `$OTHER`) — asserts the
      command still asks (fail-closed unchanged for genuinely unresolvable
      values).
- [ ] Add a test for the `$(realpath <literal-path>)` variant named in the

- [ ] Add a test confirming `git -C "$VAR" push --force-with-lease` (the

- [ ] Run the full guard-hook test suite locally (`defaults/hooks/tests/…`,

issues.title: docs: autonomous.ciTelemetry.* is missing from daemon-reference.md's canonical autonomous knob table
issues.body:
## What

`.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` §"Daemon configuration" carries the canonical
`autonomous.*` knob table — every key, its env override, its default, and
whether it is **restart required**. #8847 (#8824) adds a whole new
`autonomous.ciTelemetry` block and does not touch that file, so the new
keys are absent from the one table an operator scans to answer "what can I set,
and does editing it take effect without a restart?".

`defaults/docs/ci-observability.md`'s phase-1 section documents the keys well —
but that is the *subsystem* page. The daemon-reference table is the *index*, and
an index that silently omits a subsystem is worse than one that never claimed to
be complete.

## Change

Two edits to `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (the `.loom/docs/` copy is a
symlink, so parity is automatic):

1. Add `"ciTelemetry"` to the big illustrative `autonomous` JSON block:

```json
    "ciTelemetry": {
      "enabled": true,
      "org": "2amlogic",
      "intervalSecs": 120,
      "excludedRepos": [],
      "logCaptureEnabled": false,
      "logCaptureMaxBytes": 5242880,
      "logCaptureExcludedRepos": []
    }
```

2. Add rows to the `| Config key | Env override | Default | Notes |` table,
   matching the shape #8847 actually shipped (re-read it rather than trusting
   the text below — `intervalSecs` semantics and the exclusion rules in
   particular):

| Config key | Env override | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autonomous.ciTelemetry.enabled` | `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` | `false` | Periodic GitHub Actions run/job capture. Read-only observer: it can never change a dispatch, claim, or merge decision. **Restart required** — resolved once before the task is spawned. See [`ci-observability.md`](ci-observability.md) |
| `autonomous.ciTelemetry.org` | `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_ORG` | `2amlogic` | The org whose repos are auto-discovered and polled. Empty → default. **Restart required** |
| `autonomous.ciTelemetry.intervalSecs` | `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL_SECS` | `120` | Poll cadence. Zero/invalid → default. **Restart required** |
| `autonomous.ciTelemetry.excludedRepos` | *(config only)* | `[]` | **Log-capture-only** exclusions (phase 2, #8825); each entry needs `repo` **and** a non-empty `reason`. Run/job records and duration metrics are never excludable (#8827's standing policy) |
| `autonomous.ciTelemetry.logCaptureEnabled` | `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_LOG_CAPTURE_ENABLED` | `false` | Phase 2 (#8825) gate. Phase 1 refuses to honour it — no code path downloads a job log |
| `autonomous.ciTelemetry.logCaptureMaxBytes` | `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_LOG_CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES` | `5242880` (5 MiB) | Per-job cap on captured log text. **Restart required** |
| `autonomous.ciTelemetry.logCaptureExcludedRepos` | *(config only)* | `[]` | Repos excluded from **log capture only** — their `ci.run`/`ci.job` records and duration metrics are still captured unconditionally, same admission rule (`repo` + non-empty `reason`) as `excludedRepos`. Distinct key from `excludedRepos` deliberately: excluding a repo there would also drop its metrics, which the ci-observability policy forbids. **Restart required** |

> **Curator note (verified 2026-09-25 against `origin/main` @ merged PR #8847, `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/mod.rs`)**: the issue's original draft table above listed five keys; the shipped `CiTelemetryConfig`/`read_config()` actually expose seven — `logCaptureMaxBytes` and `logCaptureExcludedRepos` were missing from the draft and are added here. All seven are resolved once in `spawn_task()` before the poll loop starts (never re-read per tick), so all seven are **Restart required** — confirmed by reading `spawn_task()` directly, not inferred.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every key `ci_telemetry`'s config resolver actually reads appears in the
   daemon-reference table, with the env-var name and default **read off the
   code**, not copied from this issue.
2. Each row states restart-required vs. re-read-per-tick truthfully — check
   where the value is resolved (bring-up vs. inside the loop) before writing it
   down. A wrong "restart required" is worse than an absent row.
3. `scripts/check-docs-defaults-parity.sh`, `check-doc-anchors.sh`,
   `check-doc-tocs.sh` and `check-markdown-token-budget.sh` pass.

## Why this is its own issue

#8847 is already Judge-approved; re-opening review on it for a docs row would
cost more than it saves. This is a self-contained docs-only change.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8824 / its implementing PR #8847: merged (PR #8847 merged 2026-09-25; #8824 closed). `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/mod.rs` now exists on `origin/main`, confirmed via `git show origin/main:loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/mod.rs`.

Dependency resolved — this issue is unblocked.

## Affected Files

- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (`.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` is a symlink to this file, per the issue's own "Change" section) — add `ciTelemetry` to the illustrative `autonomous` JSON block and the new rows to the `autonomous.*` knob table (seven keys total — see Curator note above)
- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/mod.rs` (merged via PR #8847) — reference only; source of truth for the env-var names, defaults, and restart-required-vs-re-read-per-tick behavior the new table rows must match

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: `scripts/check-docs-defaults-parity.sh`, `scripts/check-doc-anchors.sh`, `scripts/check-doc-tocs.sh`, `scripts/check-markdown-token-budget.sh` all pass (AC3)
- [ ] Manual verification: each of the seven new table rows' env-var name and default is read directly from `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/mod.rs` on the build base, not copied from this issue's draft table (AC1)
- [ ] Manual verification: for each new row, confirm whether the value is resolved at daemon bring-up (restart required) or re-read inside the poll loop, before writing "Restart required" (AC2)

<!-- loom:complexity=mechanical -->

**Why `mechanical`, not `routine`**: this is a docs-only addition to an existing table, following the exact row shape already established by every other `autonomous.*` block in the same file — a mistake (a wrong env-var name, a wrong default, a wrong restart-required claim) is obvious just by diffing the new rows against the shipped code, per AC1/AC2's own instruction to re-read rather than trust the draft.
