issues.title: release: Linux build legs fail to link (__isoc23_sscanf) since v0.19.397 — rust-cache restores ubuntu-24.04 objects onto the ubuntu-22.04 pin
issues.body:
## Problem

Every **Build and Release** run since v0.19.397 (2026-09-26 05:09 UTC) has failed on both Linux legs, so **no release after v0.19.396 has been promoted to Latest**. `loom-daemon-update.sh` resolves `releases/latest`, so the fleet can't pick up anything merged since then (#8996, #9009, …).

| Release | Result |
|---|---|
| v0.19.396 (04:30) | success, 10 assets, Latest |
| v0.19.397 → v0.19.401 | failure: `Build loom-daemon (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)` and `(aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu)`; `Promote the Release to Latest` skipped; 2 assets |

Link errors (run 36227540696):

```
rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: __isoc23_sscanf
rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: __isoc23_strtol
error: linking with `cc` failed: exit status: 1
error: linking with `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc` failed: exit status: 1
```

## Cause

`__isoc23_*` are glibc ≥ 2.38 symbols. They come from C objects compiled on a newer-glibc host being linked on ubuntu-22.04 (glibc 2.35).

- **#8899** (landed via merge train #8996, `7ceec3dc`, about 05:07 UTC) pinned the Linux build legs from `ubuntu-latest` (24.04, glibc 2.39) to `ubuntu-22.04`, as #8842 decided.
- The `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` step in `.github/workflows/release.yml` is keyed only on `${{ matrix.target }}`. rust-cache's automatic key includes `runner.os` (`Linux`) but not the image version. The 22.04 runners therefore **restore the target dir built on 24.04**, including build-script C objects compiled against glibc 2.39, and the link fails.

The first failing release immediately follows the #8996 merge, and every later one fails the same way.

## Fix

Add the runner image to the rust-cache key, e.g. `key: ${{ matrix.target }}-${{ matrix.os }}`, so a 22.04 leg never restores a 24.04 cache. The first run after the fix is a cold build. After that it's cached per image. The "Verify build host glibc floor" step stays as the runtime guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The next Build and Release run after the fix passes both Linux legs and promotes its release to Latest (`gh release list` shows it as Latest with the full asset count).
- [ ] `loom-daemon-update.sh --dry-run` on an up-to-date host resolves that new release.

Found while updating an operator host's daemon (it stayed on v0.19.396 because nothing newer was Latest).

issues.title: [Epic #9429] story-points: points-landed-per-day throughput query and rollup
issues.body:
Parent epic: filed separately (Fibonacci story points — size-weighted throughput). Depends on: phase 3 (points on telemetry).

## Goal

The number this epic exists for: **story points landed per day**, queryable in SigNoz, retention-safe, defined once.

## Work

- [ ] Add a canonical question set under `defaults/observability/` (sibling to `cycle-time-questions.md`, same discipline: definitions fixed once, every question a committed SQL statement): points landed per day and per ISO-week (successful ships only — a failed sweep lands nothing, following the existing `ship` definition), trend over months, per-repo split
- [ ] Backend-neutral rollup + per-backend extraction, following the `loom_analytics.ship_cycle_time` pattern — raw log retention is ~7 days, so the trend question is unanswerable from raw logs; that is exactly why CT6 needed the rollup
- [ ] The join: `sweep.outcome` rows → `loom.story_points`; sweeps without points are reported as a data-gap count (CT7 discipline: missing is not zero)
- [ ] Contract tests mirroring `loom-daemon/tests/cycle_time_artifacts.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A committed query answers "points landed per day" for any window since the rollup's existence
- [ ] The answer separates successful landings from failed sweeps
- [ ] Re-running the rollup over an already-ingested window is idempotent, with a CT8-style reconciliation against raw records
- [ ] A short ops note says where to read the number for capacity tuning ("the pipeline lands N points/day — do we need another Judge?")

---

## Curator technical guidance (2026-09-29)

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->
<!-- loom:points=3 -->

### Verified corrections

- **2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main`** (`git fetch origin --quiet`; every path below confirmed via `git ls-tree -r origin/main --name-only`): the epic's sibling phases (#9430 rubric, #9431 `points:*` labels, #9432 `loom.story_points` telemetry) all merged, and in the same window a related-but-distinct epic (**#9446/#9466, "sweep_facts"**) landed the retention-safe rollup infrastructure this issue's `## Work` section describes wanting to build from scratch. That infrastructure is **not** the `loom_analytics.ship_cycle_time` ClickHouse pattern this issue names — it's a newer, D1-based generalization of the same idea (`defaults/observability/sweep-facts/`), and it already answers a closely related question:
  - `sweep-facts-questions.md` SF2 — *"How much work lands per day?"* — is explicitly annotated `(#9466, consumed by #9433)`: the sweep-facts author already treated this issue as SF2's downstream consumer.
  - SF2 sums **LSI** (landed-size index: a continuous measurement derived from `hw_lines`/`hw_files`/tokens, see `landed-size.sql`), **not** the Curator-assigned `points:*` label. `sweep_facts` (the D1 table `sweep-facts-rollup.sql` creates) has **no `story_points` column today** — `grep -n story_points defaults/observability/sweep-facts/*.sql` returns no matches as of this commit.
  - `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` §`story_points` (~line 725) states outright: *"With it on the record, 'story points landed per day' (#9433) ... is a `GROUP BY` over this journal instead of a join against the forge."* — the schema doc already anticipated this issue would be built as a `sweep_facts` extension, not a parallel rollup.

**Recommendation — supersedes the literal `## Work` bullets above, which pre-date this infrastructure**: extend `sweep_facts` rather than building a second `loom_analytics`-style pipeline.

1. Add a `story_points INTEGER` column to `sweep_facts` (`sweep-facts-rollup.sql`'s `CREATE TABLE`), populated by `json_extract(r.payload, '$.story_points')` in the `INSERT OR REPLACE` — the same pattern every other optional numeric column there already follows (e.g. `doctor_cycles`, line ~150). The table's key/grain is unchanged, so idempotence (`INSERT OR REPLACE` on `(repo, issue, sweep_id)`) and SF7's existing reconciliation cover the new column with no extra work.
2. Mirror the column in both ClickHouse extraction views, reading the numeric OTLP attribute `loom.story_points` (name confirmed in `telemetry-schema.md`'s `story_points` section): `toInt64OrNull(LogAttributes['loom.story_points'])` in `sweep-facts-extract-clickstack.sql` (next to `tokens_in`, ~line 65), and the number-map-then-string-map fallback `sweep-facts-extract-signoz.sql`'s other numeric columns already use (mirror `doctor_cycles`'s handling there).
3. Add a new committed question (`SF8`) to `sweep-facts-queries.sql` / `sweep-facts-questions.md`: points landed per day and per ISO week, **landed sweeps only** (reuse `landed-size.sql`'s `landings` CTE predicate: `disposition = 'landed'`, or the documented pre-#9441 fallback). Per the operator's comment on this issue (2026-09-29, "turian"), report:
   - `landings` (issue count) — turian: "report issue count alongside," since count alone explains most of the daily variance (measured R² 0.83 by count, 0.94 with points, over a 34-day window).
   - a **data-gap count**: landed sweeps whose `story_points` is `NULL` — CT7/SF4 discipline, "missing is not zero." This is the literal `sweep.outcome → loom.story_points` join the original `## Work` bullet asks for.
   - **Do NOT `sum(story_points)` directly.** turian's comment (backed by the story-points experiment's measured data) states raw Fibonacci labels are ordinal, not a unit: the pre-registered ±30% additivity test failed on all three measured axes (tokens 1 : 1.3 : 2.2 : 3.4 : 5.1 : 8.2; lines 1 : 8.5 : 21 : 47 : 82 : 197). Report the **measured point value per bucket** instead, joining each landing's *assigned* `story_points` (cast to the `TEXT` size-class key) against `landed-size.sql`'s existing `measured_points(size_class, measured_point_tokens, measured_point_lines)` CTE — the same table SF2/`landed-size.sql` already use for the *actual* (LSI-derived) class, applied here to the *forecast* (Curator-assigned) class instead. If a raw label sum is reported at all, name it plainly as non-additive (e.g. `labels_summed_ordinal_do_not_use_as_size`), never as "points landed."
   - Cross-reference SF2's `lsi_landed` rather than recomputing LSI — SF8 adds the forecast/label side, SF2 already has the actual/measured side.
4. Extend `loom-daemon/tests/sweep_facts_artifacts.rs`: add `story_points` everywhere the test asserts column parity across `sweep_facts`'s `CREATE TABLE`, its `INSERT OR REPLACE` list, and both extraction views' output columns; add `"SF8"` to `QUESTION_IDS`. This is the "contract tests mirroring `cycle_time_artifacts.rs`" the original `## Work` asks for — it already exists as `sweep_facts_artifacts.rs` (same author, same shape); this issue extends it rather than writing a new one.
5. Short ops note: extend `sweep-facts-questions.md`'s existing prose/table (do not create a new file — ratchet discipline) with where to read the number for capacity tuning, e.g. beside SF2's row, since capacity tuning reads SF2 (data-driven headline) and SF8 (coverage / forecast-vs-actual) together.

### Dependency status (verified 2026-09-29 against `origin/main`)

All three sibling phases are closed and merged, no blocker remains: #9430 (rubric), #9431 (`points:*` labels — confirmed live: `gh label list --search "points:"` returns `points:1/2/3/5/8/13`), #9432 (`loom.story_points` on telemetry — confirmed: `loom-daemon/src/story_points.rs`, `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` §`story_points`).

### Operator context (not contested by this curation pass)

This issue carries `loom:building` from an operator-directed claim (see this issue's own 2026-09-29 comment, "Operator-directed build... Claiming #9433 as Builder"), and a fleet lease (`sweep-issue-9433-1790721183`) was active as of this curation pass. This curation is applied per explicit dispatch instructions and does not reclaim the Builder claim. **Because the finding above changes the intended implementation approach**, whoever is driving the active Builder sweep should read this section before finishing: following the literal original `## Work` bullets (a new `loom_analytics`-pattern ClickHouse pipeline) would duplicate infrastructure `sweep_facts` already provides and risks the ordinal-label-sum pitfall described above, which could pass tests/review while shipping a misleading "points landed" number.

### Acceptance criteria (refined, additive to the original)

- [ ] `sweep_facts.story_points` exists, sourced from `loom.story_points`, `NULL` when the sweep's issue carried no (or more than one, or an out-of-vocabulary) `points:*` label — never `0` (mirrors `telemetry-schema.md`'s own absent-vs-zero contract for this exact field).
- [ ] A committed query (`SF8` in `sweep-facts-queries.sql`) answers "points landed per day" and "per ISO week" for any window since `story_points` began being captured, using the bound `{since}`/`{until}` window pattern the other SF queries already use — no hand-edited date literal.
- [ ] The answer counts **landed** sweeps only (`disposition = 'landed'`, or the documented pre-#9441 fallback); a failed or non-landed sweep contributes to neither the points sum nor the landings count.
- [ ] Landed sweeps with no `story_points` are reported as an explicit data-gap count, separate from (never folded into) the points sum.
- [ ] "Points landed" is reported via the **measured point value per bucket**, not a raw sum of Fibonacci labels — see the "Do NOT `sum(story_points)` directly" guidance above and turian's comment on this issue for the measured non-additivity data this requirement is based on.
- [ ] Re-running `sweep-facts-rollup.sql` over an already-ingested window stays idempotent (structurally true via `INSERT OR REPLACE` on `(repo, issue, sweep_id)` — verify the new column doesn't change that); SF7's existing reconciliation query covers the new column with no separate CT8-style query needed, since SF7 already reconciles the whole `sweep_facts` row and this issue only adds a column to it.
- [ ] `loom-daemon/tests/sweep_facts_artifacts.rs` is extended to cover the new column and `SF8` the same way it covers SF1–SF7 today (static contract, no live backend required).
- [ ] A short ops note (extending `sweep-facts-questions.md`, not a new file) states where to read the number for capacity tuning.

### Affected files (verified present on `origin/main`, 2026-09-29)

- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-rollup.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-queries.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-questions.md`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-extract-clickstack.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-extract-signoz.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/landed-size.sql` (read-only reference for the `measured_points` join — no change expected unless the join needs a new view)
- `loom-daemon/tests/sweep_facts_artifacts.rs`

### Test plan

- `cargo test -p loom-daemon --test sweep_facts_artifacts` (static contract; extend it, then run it).
- Local SQLite syntax-check of the extended `sweep-facts-rollup.sql` / `sweep-facts-queries.sql` (and `landed-size.sql` if the join needs a helper view) against an empty schema (`sqlite3 :memory: < file.sql`) — the same no-op-safe check `story-points-evidence.md` used for the original SP1–SP4 file.
- No live D1/ClickHouse execution is required for this issue — mirrors the "contract-checked, not yet executed live" status the sibling `sweep-facts` artifacts already carry (`sweep-facts-questions.md` §Verification status). Do not block on Cloudflare/SigNoz credentials.

issues.title: [Epic #9429] story-points: carry loom.story_points onto sweep telemetry
issues.body:
Parent epic: #9429. Depends on: phase 2's `points:*` labels.

## Goal

Carry the assigned points through telemetry so every backend query can join assigned estimate to actual cost without leaving SigNoz: emit `loom.story_points` on sweep records.

## Work

- [ ] At sweep dispatch, when the sweep is bound to an issue, read the issue's `points:*` label from the issue data the dispatch path already resolves (the forge listing/view already carries the labels connection — do not add a second fetch); where a new labels-connection query is introduced, cap `labels(first:)` at the points vocabulary size (~6) so the extra cost stays flat as label count grows
- [ ] Emit `loom.story_points` as a numeric attribute on `sweep.started` and `sweep.outcome`
- [ ] Additive schema change per `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` conventions; **absent vs. measured zero**: omit the attribute entirely when the issue carries no `points:*` label (pre-epic issues, operator-filed issues) — never emit 0
- [ ] Daemon-side guard enforcing **one `points:*` label per issue**: zero → attribute absent; one → attribute emitted; more than one → log loudly and omit, never guess which one wins
- [ ] Contract tests for the label handling: label present / absent / multiple — the multiple case must be surfaced, never silently resolved
- [ ] Update the telemetry schema doc

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A sweep of an issue carrying one `points:*` label produces `sweep.outcome` records with `loom.story_points`
- [ ] A sweep of an issue without a points label produces records with no such attribute (absent, not 0)
- [ ] Multiple points labels are logged and resolve to no attribute, never to a guess

issues.title: Stale-verdict clearing does not disarm GitHub auto-merge — unreviewed heads merge (#8694)
issues.body:
## Problem
When the stale-verdict guard clears `loom:pr` because the head SHA moved (`loom:verdict-stale` comment), it does not disable GitHub's native auto-merge if one was armed earlier (e.g. by `merge-pr.sh --auto`). The armed auto-merge then fires as soon as the ruleset's required checks pass on the *new, unreviewed* head.

## Observed 2026-09-25
- #8694 merged as `528f2971` at 12:34:07Z, 3 minutes after a Doctor rebase force-push, still labeled `loom:review-requested`, with no approval at the merged head (auto-squash armed 09-22).
- #8847 and #8843 merged at 12:06-12:07Z about 2 minutes after `gh pr update-branch` moved their heads and the stale-verdict notice cleared `loom:pr`.
- It also bypasses the #8248 required-check-freshness guard, which only runs inside `merge-pr.sh`.

## Fix
Wherever a verdict is invalidated for a head move (stale-verdict clearing, `loom:changes-requested`, `loom:operator`, `loom:blocked`), also call `disablePullRequestAutoMerge` and record it in the comment. Add a test for this.

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

issues.title: Observability: real-time token burn for Codex, OpenCode (GLM) and Kimi stores (#8857 phase 2)
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 of #8857. Phase 1 exports real-time token burn (`loom.llm.tokens.*` and `loom.llm.requests` delta counters, `provider`/`model` labels) for **Claude only**, via a host-wide interval sampler over `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/projects/**.jsonl`. The sampler attributes each API message (`message.id`) to its first record's timestamp and counts it once.

The other subscription runtimes need the same interval reader. Their existing readers answer a different question: they return a *session's* total for a session **created** in a window (`codex_usage::fold_rollout` filters on `session_meta.timestamp`, and `SessionFilter` matches nothing when empty). So they cannot be reused as they are for time-bucketed burn. Reusing them would double-count long sessions and drop sessions that started before the window.

## Proposal

For each store, add a per-event, host-wide interval fold that feeds the same `ops::quota` burn emitter with `provider` set to the store's provider:

- **Codex** (`~/.codex` and pooled `~/.loom/codex-profiles/*`): attribute each `token_count` event's delta (`Counters::delta`) to that line's own timestamp. One request = one `token_count` event with a non-null `info`.
- **OpenCode** (ZAI/GLM trials): per-message rows in its SQLite store, attributed by message time.
- **Kimi**: `wire.jsonl` usage events.
- **Pi**: blocked on #8594's schema capture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each store, a fixture test shows that a session spanning two windows is split between them with no double count.
- [ ] `provider` label values match `tokens.snapshot`'s vocabulary (`claude`, `codex`) or the API-key pool's provider directory name (e.g. `zai`, `kimi`).
- [ ] With no OTLP exporter configured, no store is read.

---

## Curator enrichment (sweep, 2026-09-25)

### On-disk formats verified on a real host (no credential files opened)

- **OpenCode (GLM / Z.ai):** the default XDG store `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is live on this host, *not* only `~/.loom/opt/opencode-<ver>/xdg/...` (the only place `opencode_usage::discover_opencode_dbs` looks). Per-request usage is in table **`message`** (one assistant row per API step; 36k `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3-flash` rows here): `data` JSON carries `role`, `providerID`, `modelID`, `tokens.{input,output,reasoning,cache.read,cache.write}` and `time.{created,completed}` (ms). Rows are written at creation with zero tokens and **updated in place** on completion (`time_updated` column bumps), so the incremental key is completion time, not append offset. Error rows (e.g. the 429 "Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted") carry all-zero tokens.
- **Codex:** `sessions/<Y>/<M>/<D>/rollout-*.jsonl`; each line has its own `timestamp`; `event_msg/token_count.info.total_token_usage` is cumulative per file and each event is written twice, so a per-file (offset, previous counters, current `turn_context.model`) cursor yields per-event deltas.
- **Kimi:** `~/.kimi-code/sessions/wd_*/session_*/agents/*/wire.jsonl`, append-only; `usage.record` events carry per-request `usage` and `time` (ms); only `usageScope:"turn"` observed. `llm.request` resolves the model alias.

### Plan

1. One shared incremental seam under `observability/ops/burn/`: a per-file **tail cursor** (byte offset, complete lines only, reset on truncation / inode change, files keyed by canonical path so symlinked profile `sessions/` dirs count once) plus a per-provider **event ledger**. Each store decodes new lines/rows into `(timestamp, model, usage)` events; the sampler drains events at or before the window end into the window, holding later ones.
2. Claude moves onto the same seam (fixes #8941 items 2 and 3): message ids are remembered across samples, and a later streamed chunk contributes only its increment.
3. Burn intervals are exported with an explicit end time (window end) so consecutive intervals abut exactly.
4. `provider` labels: `claude`, `codex`, `kimi`, and for OpenCode the pool namespace (`zai-coding-plan` → `zai`), else OpenCode's own provider id.
5. No store read when no OTLP exporter (unchanged `record()` early return).

### Acceptance criteria (added)

- [ ] Per store, a fixture test: a session appended across two samples is split between the windows with no double count (Codex duplicate `token_count` events count once; Claude streamed chunks count once).
- [ ] Truncated/replaced file resets its cursor without re-counting; symlinked session dirs counted once.
- [ ] OpenCode reader issues exactly one query naming `message` only (pinned by a test).
- [ ] #8941 items 1–5 closed or explicitly deferred with a comment on #8941.

issues.title: ETA phase 5: shadow mode + promotion switch (backtest-gated), land-v2 with censoring
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Phase 5 of #9289 (ETA as a Loom primitive). Plan: Curator comment https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5867874254, operator decisions https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5869738711. **Depends on #9289 Phase 1** (core, heuristic registry, explanation schema, journal); do not start before it merges.

### Scope
- Every registered heuristic is computed and logged; one is `current` (config).
- Promotion rule (operator decision 2): the candidate must beat `current` on the phase-2 **backtest** pinball loss per kind, then must not be worse **live** (paired pinball, ≥50 pairs, coverage within [40%, 60%]). Only then flip the config.
- `land-v2`: path bootstrap with Kaplan–Meier handling of censored (still-open) samples, the v0 limitation the Curator named.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Curated against `origin/main` (2026-09-30). Phases 1–3 have all merged: #9289 (Phase 1, core), #9325 (Phase 2, `eta backfill`/`eta backtest`, PR #9578), #9326 (Phase 3, `start-v1`/`land` for unstarted issues, PR #9701) — this phase is unblocked.

### Problem Statement

Today `loom-daemon` computes and emits an estimate using only the single `current` heuristic per kind (`Registry::current`, `loom-daemon/src/eta/mod.rs:539`, called from `tracker.rs:1168` with one heuristic, not the full registry). There is no mechanism to:
1. Run a **candidate** heuristic silently alongside `current` ("shadow mode") and accumulate paired live scores.
2. **Promote** a candidate to `current` once it clears both gates from the operator's decision 2 on #9289 — backtest-first, then live — and record that decision auditable.
3. Score `land-v2`, a Kaplan–Meier-censored heuristic that the design doc named as the `-v2` follow-up to `land-v1`'s "ignore right-censoring" limitation (`land-v1`'s doc comment / #9289 Curator comment §3.2).

### Current code state (verified against `origin/main`)

- `EtaConfig` (`loom-daemon/src/eta/config.rs`) already has `current_start` / `current_finish` / `current_land` fields read from `autonomous.eta.current.<kind>` — the config surface the promotion switch needs to flip already exists; nothing new to add there for the switch itself.
- `Registry` (`loom-daemon/src/eta/mod.rs:495`) holds three built-in heuristics (`StartV1`, `FinishV1`, `LandV1`) and exposes `ids()`, `get(id)`, and `current(kind, configured)`. There is no notion of "every registered heuristic for a kind" vs. "the current one" — `Registry` has no `for_kind(kind) -> Vec<&dyn Heuristic>`-style accessor yet, and the tracker never calls more than one heuristic per emission.
- `backtest::compare` (`loom-daemon/src/eta/backtest.rs:418`) already exists and returns a winner between two heuristics by mean pinball loss on the identical replay set — this is the **backtest gate**, already shipped by Phase 2/#9578, and the CLI already exposes it as `eta backtest --heuristic <id> --compare <other>` (`loom-daemon/src/cli/eta_cmd.rs:161,218`). Phase 5 consumes this, it does not reimplement it.
- `OutcomeKind`/scoring (`loom-daemon/src/eta/score.rs`) already computes pinball loss, coverage (`covered`/`below_p25`/`above_p75`) per estimate/outcome pair — the primitive the **live** gate's paired comparison needs also already exists; what's missing is running it for a second (candidate) heuristic per subject and pairing the two series.
- No shadow-mode, promotion-switch, or KM/censoring code exists anywhere under `loom-daemon/src/eta/` as of this curation pass (`rg -n "shadow|promot|censor|kaplan" loom-daemon/src/eta/` returns no hits outside doc comments already quoted above).

### Suspected cause (unverified) — land backtest gate has zero cases today

Not a defect in *this* issue's scope, but load-bearing for the **land** kind's promotion path specifically: #9579 (open, `loom:triage` as of this curation) reports that `eta backtest --heuristic land-v1` scores **zero** replay cases on every host, because `cases_from_record` only derives a `land` case from a `sweep.outcome` record ending in an in-sweep `merge` phase, and the fleet's PRs are merged out-of-sweep by Champion. This means the phase-2 backtest gate is currently **unevaluable for `land`** candidates (including `land-v2` from this issue) — not because a candidate estimates badly, but because there is nothing to score it against yet. `start` and `finish` are unaffected (the `finish-v1` backtest already scores 123 cases per #9579's own repro).

This does not block building the shadow-mode/promotion-switch mechanism itself (it can and should be built and tested with synthetic/fixture backtest results for all three kinds, exactly as `backtest-golden.json` already does for Phase 2). It does mean that in practice, until #9579 lands, `land-v2` cannot clear the backtest gate on real fleet data and the promotion switch will correctly refuse to flip `current_land` — which is the safe behavior, not a bug in this issue. Builder: verify #9579's status before relying on real (non-fixture) `land` backtest numbers for any manual promotion decision on this issue's PR.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Registry` (or an equivalent accessor) can enumerate every registered heuristic for a given `Kind`, not just `current` — the shadow-mode input.
- [ ] The tracker computes and logs an `eta.estimate` for every registered heuristic per kind per tracked subject (not only `current`); only `current`'s estimate is the primary/enqueued one used by existing consumers (loom-ui snapshot, dry-run logging), so this is additive, not a behavior change to the existing single-heuristic path.
- [ ] A live paired-scoring mechanism accumulates `(current, candidate)` score pairs per kind as `eta.outcome`s resolve, and reports: pair count, paired mean pinball loss for each side, and p25–p75 coverage for the candidate.
- [ ] The promotion switch flips `autonomous.eta.current.<kind>` (persisted config, not just in-memory) **only** when, in order: (1) the candidate beats `current` on `backtest::compare`'s phase-2 backtest pinball loss for that kind, **and** (2) the live paired comparison has ≥50 pairs, the candidate is not worse (paired pinball loss), and coverage is within [40%, 60%]. Either gate failing leaves `current` unchanged.
- [ ] The promotion decision itself is recorded (a dated log line / event / config-change record sufficient for an operator to see *why* a switch happened, with the backtest and live numbers that justified it) — this is what makes an automatic config mutation auditable, per the general Loom principle that autonomous state changes must be explainable, not just effective.
- [ ] `land-v2` is implemented as a new `Heuristic` registered alongside `land-v1`: `land-v1`'s stage-duration grids gain Kaplan–Meier survival-curve handling for still-open (censored) samples in place of `land-v1`'s "ignore right-censoring" simplification (§3.2 of the #9289 design comment), and is scored through the same backtest/shadow/live pipeline as any other candidate — it does not get to bypass the promotion gate.
- [ ] Hermetic tests cover: shadow computation running all registered heuristics without changing `current`'s emitted primary estimate; the promotion switch correctly gating on both backtest-then-live in order (a fixture where only one gate passes must not promote); config persistence of a flip; and `land-v2`'s KM estimator against a fixture with a mix of censored and observed samples (a positive control showing censoring changes the estimate — mirrors #9579's own leakage-test discipline).
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib -- eta::` green against a freshly built daemon (per the #9651 lesson already referenced across this repo's `.loom/config.json`/CI: stale local builds silently pass tests against old behavior).

## Implementation Guidance

- **Shadow computation**: extend `Registry` with a `for_kind(kind: Kind) -> impl Iterator<Item = &dyn Heuristic>` (or similar), and change the tracker's single `ctx.registry.current(kind, configured)` call site (`tracker.rs:1168`) to loop over `for_kind(kind)`, computing an `Explanation` for each, emitting `eta.estimate` for all, but only feeding `current`'s result into whatever downstream consumer currently expects exactly one estimate per subject/kind (check `emit.rs`/`tracker_ready.rs` for that assumption before changing the emission shape).
- **Live paired scoring**: reuse `score.rs`'s existing pinball/coverage primitives per-heuristic; the new piece is pairing two heuristics' scores against the *same* outcome and accumulating a running count — this likely wants its own small module (e.g. `loom-daemon/src/eta/shadow.rs`) rather than growing `score.rs`, since `score.rs` today scores one heuristic against one outcome with no notion of a second heuristic.
- **Promotion switch persistence**: `EtaConfig` is read via `config_resolver::resolve_effective_config` (env > config > default); flipping `current_land` etc. means writing to the persisted `autonomous.eta.current.<kind>` config key, not just the in-memory `EtaConfig` struct — follow whatever the repo's existing config-mutation pattern is for autonomous daemon state changes (grep for another `autonomous.*` block that self-modifies, if one exists, before inventing a new persistence path).
- **`land-v2` / Kaplan–Meier**: lives beside `heuristics/land_v1.rs` as `heuristics/land_v2.rs`, registered in `Registry::builtin()` (`mod.rs`) and `heuristics/mod.rs`. The KM estimator replaces `land-v1`'s plain empirical quantile grid (`grid.rs`) for stages with censored (still-open) samples; `pr_latency::stats` is the sibling module `grid.rs` already borrows `nearest_rank` from — check it for an existing survival/censoring primitive before writing one from scratch.
- **#9579 interaction**: do not silently work around #9579 inside this issue's scope (e.g. by loosening the backtest gate for `land`) — that would defeat the gate's purpose. If #9579 is still open when this is built, ship the mechanism and let the gate correctly refuse to promote `land-v2` on real data until #9579 lands; use fixtures for the mechanism's own tests.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/eta/mod.rs` — `Registry`: add a per-kind enumeration accessor; `heuristics::` module registration for `land-v2`.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/heuristics/mod.rs`, new `loom-daemon/src/eta/heuristics/land_v2.rs` — the KM-censored heuristic implementation.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/tracker.rs` — shadow computation: loop over every registered heuristic per kind instead of only `current` (currently single-heuristic at `tracker.rs:1168`).
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/config.rs` — read side is already there (`current_start`/`current_finish`/`current_land`); needs the write/persistence path for the promotion switch.

issues.title: verdict-staleness-guard.sh drops Judge verdicts on tree-identical re-date commits — the daemon path's #9124 tree-unchanged exemption was never ported
issues.body:
## Summary

`defaults/scripts/verdict-staleness-guard.sh` (#5686) invalidates a Judge verdict on **any** head move, including a **tree-identical** one. #9490/#9124 taught the daemon's verdict-invalidation pass (`loom-daemon/src/claim_reconciliation/verdict_invalidation.rs::tree_unchanged`) to skip invalidation when `compare/{marker}...{head}` reports `files: []`. The shell guard never got that exemption, so the two mechanisms disagree (ci-principles.md rule 4: one mechanism per behaviour).

## Observed (2026-09-30)

PR #9541: verdict anchored at `490fb81a8`, a no-op re-date commit pushed to `42ea7263a` (same tree; `gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/compare/490fb81a8…42ea7263a` → `files=0`). At 00:27:25Z `loom-fleet-dispatch` posted `<!-- loom:verdict-stale from=490fb81… to=42ea726… -->` "*Automated by verdict-staleness-guard.sh (#5686)*", removed `loom:pr`, and added `loom:review-requested`. The running daemon (0.19.517, c12dd5a) already contains #9490, so this came from the shell path. #9483 lost its verdict the same way.

## Why it matters

It re-arms the stale-check treadmill (#8248). Every re-date, whether the automated #8508 commit or an operator's no-op push under the documented "push any commit" release, now also costs a full Judge cycle. By the time Judge re-approves, `main` has usually moved again. This is part of why ~13 PRs ended on `stale-check-hold (remedy exhausted)` and needed a human.

## Fix direction

Make the shell guard ask the same question as the daemon, in one place. Either:
1. Have `verdict-staleness-guard.sh` delegate the decision to a `loom-daemon` subcommand that reuses `tree_unchanged` (preferred per the language policy: new logic lives in `loom-daemon`, not shell); or
2. Retire the shell guard's invalidation arm if the daemon pass fully covers its callers (`post-verdict.sh` and the role prompts that invoke it). Audit the callers first.

In both cases keep the fail-closed behaviour: if the comparison can't be made, invalidate as today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A tree-identical head move (e.g. a `chore: re-date required checks …` commit, or any empty commit) does **not** remove `loom:pr` via either path; a head move that changes the tree still does (tests for both).
- [ ] A failed or unparseable compare still invalidates (fail closed), matching `tree_unchanged`'s `None` arm.
- [ ] Only one implementation of the "did the reviewed tree change" decision remains, or the two share one daemon subcommand.

## Curator notes (2026-09-29, verified against `main` @ `091869563`)

- `defaults/scripts/verdict-staleness-guard.sh`'s Step 4 FRESH/STALE decision is a pure string comparison of the marker SHA against the PR's current `headRefOid` (`if [[ "${HEAD_SHA:0:${#MARKER_SHA}}" == "$MARKER_SHA" ]]`) — there is no `gh api .../compare/...` call anywhere in the script (`grep -n "compare" defaults/scripts/verdict-staleness-guard.sh` → 0 hits outside comments/prose). So this is not a divergent copy of the daemon logic; the shell guard never had a tree-comparison arm at all.
- `loom-daemon/src/claim_reconciliation/verdict_invalidation.rs::tree_unchanged` (lines 160-178) calls `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{marker_sha}...{head_sha}` and returns `Some(true)` on `files: []`; `handle_invalidate` (lines 63-91), gated by `verdict_tree_carveout_enabled()` (env `LOOM_VERDICT_TREE_CARVEOUT`, default on), re-anchors instead of clearing when that holds.
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`'s "Agent-side fast paths" section (~line 2867) currently describes the shell guard and the daemon pass as sharing behavior via the same guard script — that description is inaccurate today and needs correcting alongside whichever fix direction is taken.

### Callers of the shell guard (per fix option 2's "audit the callers first")

All confirmed present on `main` as of this curation:

| Caller | Invocation |
|---|---|
| `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/judge.md` (x2) / `defaults/.agents/skills/loom-judge/SKILL.md` (x2) | `--clear --anchor` (Stale-Verdict Sweep, step 0 of every Judge pass) |
| `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/doctor.md` / `defaults/.agents/skills/loom-doctor/SKILL.md` | `--clear` (Stale-Verdict Check, before claiming) |
| `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md` | `--clear` (Verdict-State Janitor Part 2, before the merge-safety criteria) |
| `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/sweep-mode-c-lifecycle.md` | `--clear` (Mode C pre-merge check) |

**Constraint on option 2** (retiring the shell guard's invalidation arm): `defaults/scripts/check-cas-recheck-consistency.sh` (check #5) CI-enforces that `champion-pr-merge.md` and `doctor.md` each still invoke `verdict-staleness-guard.sh` — removing those call sites without updating this consistency check fails CI. `defaults/scripts/tests/test-verdict-staleness-guard.sh` and `test-post-verdict.sh`'s T13 cross-check also pin the guard's marker-regex format; either fix direction must keep those in sync.

This tips the balance slightly toward **option 1** (delegate to a new `loom-daemon` subcommand reusing `tree_unchanged`): it changes zero caller call sites, matches the shell-language-policy (new logic is a daemon subcommand, not shell), and avoids touching `check-cas-recheck-consistency.sh`'s caller-presence assertions. Not a mandate — flagged as guidance, not a requirement; the Builder should confirm which option is cheaper once actually scoping the diff. (Whether the daemon's own `reconcile_pr_verdicts` pass already runs synchronously enough to cover what the shell guard's callers need is not traced here — flag as unverified if load-bearing.)

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/verdict-staleness-guard.sh` — Step 4 FRESH/STALE decision; needs the tree-comparison exemption (or a call into a new daemon subcommand exposing it).
- `loom-daemon/src/claim_reconciliation/verdict_invalidation.rs` — existing `tree_unchanged` / `reanchor_tree_unchanged_verdict` / `verdict_tree_carveout_enabled`; the logic to reuse, plus a possible new thin CLI entry point if option 1 is taken.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-verdict-staleness-guard.sh` — add coverage for a tree-identical head move not clearing the verdict, and a tree-changed move still clearing it.
- `defaults/scripts/check-cas-recheck-consistency.sh` — update only if option 2 removes a caller's invocation.
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (~line 2867, "Agent-side fast paths") — correct the "share the guard script" description once the two paths actually agree.

All five paths verified present on `origin/main` at curation time (2026-09-29, commit `091869563`).

## Test Plan

- [ ] Unit test in `test-verdict-staleness-guard.sh`: stub `gh api .../compare/A...B` to return `{"files": []}`; verify the guard does not invalidate the verdict (FRESH or equivalent), matching AC1.
- [ ] Unit test: stub the same compare call to return a non-empty `files` array; verify the guard still reports STALE and clears as today (the "still invalidate on a real change" half of AC1).
- [ ] Unit test: stub the compare call to fail (non-zero exit / malformed JSON); verify the guard still invalidates (fail-closed, matching `tree_unchanged`'s `None` arm and AC2).
- [ ] `./.loom/scripts/tests/test-verdict-staleness-guard.sh` and `./.loom/scripts/tests/test-post-verdict.sh` (T13 cross-check) both still pass.
- [ ] `./defaults/scripts/check-cas-recheck-consistency.sh` still passes (or is updated in the same PR if a caller invocation changes).
- [ ] Optional live check: re-run `./.loom/scripts/verdict-staleness-guard.sh <PR>` against a PR with a known tree-identical re-date commit (e.g. re-check the #9541/#9483 history cited above) and confirm it no longer reports STALE.

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->
<!-- loom:points=3 -->

**Complexity rationale**: `routine` — the fix ports an already-proven, already-tested comparison (`tree_unchanged`, landed under #9124) into or behind the shell guard; a mistake here is directly observable in the new unit tests (a verdict wrongly kept or wrongly cleared), not a subtle judgement call. `complex` would overstate a porting/wiring task with reference logic already reviewed.

**Points rationale**: `3` — one shell script's Step 4 (or a thin new daemon CLI verb it calls), 2-3 new/adjusted unit tests, and a doc correction; roughly 100-150 hand-written lines across 3-4 files, below the `points:5` median (~610 lines/6 files) but above `points:2`'s ~110 lines/2 files given the daemon-subcommand plumbing option 1 may require.

issues.title: worktree.sh --json: the "preserve existing work" path exits 0 with empty stdout, emitting no JSON document
issues.body:
## What happens

`defaults/scripts/worktree.sh --json <N>` exits **0 with completely empty
stdout** when the worktree already exists and carries real work (commits ahead
or uncommitted changes). No JSON document is emitted at all.

The `--json` contract everywhere else in the script is "exactly one JSON
document on fd 3" — there are ~15 `>&3` emit sites covering every other
outcome, including the failure ones (`worktree-lock-timeout`,
`branch-already-landed`, `corrupted-git-identity`, "Directory exists but is not
a registered worktree", …). The "preserve existing work" branch is the gap:

`defaults/scripts/worktree.sh` (≈line 1543 on `main` today):

```bash
if [[ "$local_commits_ahead" -gt 0 || -n "$local_uncommitted" ]]; then
    write_loom_sentinel "$WORKTREE_PATH"
    if [[ "$JSON_OUTPUT" != "true" ]]; then
        print_info "Worktree is registered with git"
        ...
        print_info "To use this worktree: cd $WORKTREE_PATH"
    fi
    exit 0
fi
```

The whole human-readable block is inside the `!= "true"` guard, and there is no
`else` writing a document to `>&3`. This is the **most common** outcome for a
`--json` caller in practice: re-entering an existing builder worktree that has
work in it.

## Why it matters

A programmatic caller cannot distinguish this from a truncated pipe, a crashed
child, or a daemon that died before writing. Exit 0 says "success", and the
sibling *sparse* fast path a few lines above (line ≈1488/1507) *does* emit
`{"success": true, "worktreePath": …, "branchName": …, "issueNumber": …,
"sparse": …, "cone": …}` for what is the same "worktree already exists" answer —
so the shape a caller would parse already exists and is already spelled out
twice in the file.

## Reproduction

Verified on a scratch repo (bare `origin` + clone + `.loom/scripts/`):

1. `worktree.sh <N>` to create the worktree.
2. Leave an uncommitted change in it (or a commit ahead of the base).
3. `worktree.sh --json <N> 2>/dev/null | wc -c` → **0**, `$? == 0`.

## Scope / provenance

Found while porting the upstream-tracking correction in #8195 slice 9
(PR #9110). **Pre-existing and out of that slice's scope** — the port was
verified byte-identical against `origin/main`'s pre-port `worktree.sh` on the
exact same fixture, so this is not a regression introduced there. Filed
separately rather than fixed inline because it is a *contract* change to
`--json` output, not a refactor, and it wants its own retained-suite coverage.

## Suggested fix

Add the missing `>&3` emit to the preserve branch, mirroring the sparse fast
path's key set (the `sparse: false, cone: []` variant), and extend
`defaults/scripts/tests/test-worktree-json-purity.sh` with a case that asserts
the preserve path emits exactly one parseable document — not merely that stdout
is *pure*, which an empty stdout trivially satisfies. That last point is worth
checking against the whole suite: a purity assertion that passes on empty output
cannot tell "clean" from "absent", so there may be sibling paths with the same
gap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `worktree.sh --json <N>` on an existing worktree with work emits exactly
      one JSON document, key-compatible with the sparse fast path's
      `{"success": true, "worktreePath", "branchName", "issueNumber", "sparse",
      "cone"}`.
- [ ] Exit code is unchanged (0) — this is an output gap, not a status one.
- [ ] Human (non-`--json`) output is byte-identical to before.
- [ ] `test-worktree-json-purity.sh` gains a case asserting the document is
      *present and parseable*, not only that stdout is pure; and the audit of
      whether any other `exit 0` path shares this gap is recorded in the suite or
      the issue.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29)

Verified against `origin/main` (`git fetch origin` performed this pass): the
preserve-branch at `defaults/scripts/worktree.sh` lines ~1594-1600 (line
numbers have shifted slightly from the issue's original ~1543 due to
unrelated intervening changes, but the code shape is unchanged) still has no
`>&3` emit inside the `$JSON_OUTPUT == "true"` case — confirmed by reading
the block directly. The sparse fast path's comparison emit is at line 2073
today (`echo '{"success": true, "worktreePath": ..., "sparse": ..., "cone":
...}' >&3`), matching what the issue describes.

Also confirmed while reading the surrounding code: the sibling "stale
worktree reset" branch (the `else` arm just below the preserve branch, all
three of its `exit 0` paths) has the same gap — none of them write to fd 3
in `--json` mode either. This corroborates the issue's own note that other
exit-0 paths may share the defect; scoping that audit explicitly below.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/worktree.sh` — add the missing `>&3` JSON emit to the
  "preserve existing work" branch (~line 1594), mirroring the sparse fast
  path's key set at line 2073 (`success", "worktreePath", "branchName",
  "issueNumber", "sparse", "cone"`). While in this area, also audit the three
  `exit 0` paths in the adjacent "stale worktree reset" `else` branch
  (~lines 1610-1650) for the same missing-emit gap and fix any that are
  missing it, per the issue's own "Suggested fix" note — this is the same
  file and the same contract, so it belongs in the same PR rather than a
  follow-up issue.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-worktree-json-purity.sh` — add a case for the
  preserve-path (existing worktree with uncommitted changes or commits
  ahead) asserting the emitted document is present and parseable (exactly
  one JSON object, `jq -e .success == true`), not merely that stdout is
  pure — an empty stdout trivially satisfies pure-but-not-present. Add
  matching cases for any stale-reset paths fixed above.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: extend `test-worktree-json-purity.sh` with the
      preserve-path case described above (and any stale-reset cases needed).
      Run `defaults/scripts/tests/test-worktree-json-purity.sh` directly.
- [ ] Manual verification: reproduce the issue's own repro steps — create a
      worktree, leave an uncommitted change, run
      `worktree.sh --json <N> 2>/dev/null | wc -c` — confirm nonzero output
      and `... | jq -e .success` succeeds.
- [ ] Regression: confirm non-`--json` (human-readable) output is
      byte-identical to before for both the preserve and stale-reset paths.

issues.title: flake: private_workspace_docker adapter_chain_pushes_private_branch fixture SIGTERMed (exit 143) in Codex Adapter Smoke
issues.body:
## Flake

`private_workspace_docker::dispatch::adapter_chain_pushes_private_branch_and_preserves_host_logs_and_work` failed in **Codex Adapter Smoke (mocked)**, step "Verify account-private clones and exclusive jobs with Docker fixtures".

- Job: https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/actions/runs/36237581261/job/108404428136 (attempt 4 of run 36237581261, PR #9052)
- Location: `loom-daemon/tests/private_workspace_docker/dispatch.rs:322:18`, `fixture command failed (exit status: 143): spawn-worker: runtime=codex (from env (LOOM_RUNTIME))`
- Exit 143 means the fixture process was SIGTERMed, which is consistent with a timeout or a kill racing the fixture rather than a logic failure.
- Attempts 1–3 of the **same** run replayed the identical test-merge commit and passed. #9052 does not touch this area. So this is non-deterministic.

## Ask

Find where the SIGTERM comes from: an internal timeout in the fixture or the adapter chain, or Docker being slow on the runner. Then fix the root cause. Per `.config/nextest.toml` / ci-principles, do **not** add retries.

Related: #9065 (CI wall time); every flaky re-run costs about 8.5 minutes and can make merges lose the freshness race.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Original problem statement, reproduction link, and ask are already clear. Pulled the actual failed-attempt log (job `108404428136`, confirmed via `gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/actions/jobs/108404428136` to be **`run_attempt: 3`**, not "attempt 4" as the issue states — a minor correction, not material) and traced the failure mechanism further. Adding required sections plus concrete diagnostic evidence.

### What the log actually shows (measured, job `108404428136`, 2026-09-26T12:34:12–14Z)

Fetched via `gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/actions/jobs/108404428136/logs --allow-escape-sequences`. Timeline for the failing test:

```
12:34:12Z  spawn-codex: re-exec at nice -n 10 (issue #4233)
12:34:12Z  spawn-codex: profile is session-managed — dispatching headlessly via
           docker exec loom-codex-session-test-...-a (issue #6926)
12:34:12Z  spawn-codex: hooks=not-ready ... reason="the installed managed-hook
           entry points at a different bridge than this workspace's"
12:34:12Z  Switched to a new branch 'feature/issue-8786'
12:34:12Z   * [new branch] feature/issue-8786 -> feature/issue-8786   (git push succeeded)
12:34:14Z  # LOOM_CLI_START runtime=codex
12:34:14Z  session id: 12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc
12:34:14Z  # LOOM_TERMINAL_RESULT v=2 ... category=RECOVERABLE exit_code=143
12:34:14Z  panicked: fixture command failed (exit status: 143)
```

So the git push to the fixture registry succeeds; the failure happens **inside the `docker exec` dispatch into the already-running session container**, within ~2 seconds of `LOOM_CLI_START`. This rules out: nextest's `slow-timeout` (this step runs plain `cargo test`, not `cargo nextest`, per `.github/workflows/ci.yml` "Verify account-private clones and exclusive jobs with Docker fixtures" — confirmed 2026-09-28), the job's `timeout-minutes: 30` (job completed in ~4 minutes total), and the test's own intentional `libc::kill(-(pid as i32), SIGTERM)` at `loom-daemon/tests/private_workspace_docker/dispatch.rs:387` (that kill targets a *different*, later-spawned child in the same test — `retained_command`, not the `mutate` command that failed here).

### Suspected cause (unverified)

`spawn-codex.sh`'s session-managed path (`defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh:986-1010`, issue #6926) dispatches via `loom-daemon session-exec host --container "$CODEX_SESSION_CONTAINER" --owner-pid "$PPID"`. `loom-daemon/src/session_exec/host.rs` implements an **owner-liveness self-kill**: `run()` resolves `owner::Owner::new(args.owner_pid.unwrap_or(parent))` and both `probe()` (line ~57-65) and the main dispatch loop (`child.kill()` at line ~208) tear down the docker-exec'd child if `libc::getppid() != parent` or a signal flag is set, polling on a short interval with a 3s ceiling in `probe()`.

Not traced further: which of the three self-kill triggers (`getppid() != parent`, the `SIGNAL` atomic, or the 3s probe ceiling) actually fired here — that needs either added trace logging in `host.rs`'s `run()`/`probe()` or a local reproduction, neither of which this curation pass did. The `exec nice -n 10 "$0" "$@"` re-exec (`spawn-codex.sh:315`) replaces the process image in place (bash `exec` + `nice`'s own `execve`), so it does not by itself change the PID/PPID chain — ruled out as a direct cause, but the multi-hop exec chain (spawn-worker.sh → spawn-codex.sh → nice re-exec → `loom-daemon session-exec host`) is exactly the kind of chain where a transient reparenting or a slow `ps`-based ancestry check (`host.rs` line ~93, shelling out to `ps -o ppid=`) could race under CI runner load, which is consistent with this reproducing under `--test-threads` contention / Docker load but not in 3 other attempts of the identical commit.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause of the exit-143 SIGTERM identified with evidence (trace logging output or a local reproduction), not just a hypothesis
- [ ] Fix applied so the specific mechanism no longer fires spuriously (e.g. widen the liveness check's tolerance, fix a `ps`-ancestry race, or address whatever the trace/repro reveals)
- [ ] No retry/quarantine added — per the issue's own ask and `.loom/docs/ci-principles.md`, a flaky test gets root-caused, not papered over
- [ ] `adapter_chain_pushes_private_branch_and_preserves_host_logs_and_work` (and the sibling `private_clones_contain_writes_reuse_and_serialize_all_job_kinds`, which uses the same session-exec dispatch path) run green across several consecutive CI attempts post-fix

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/session_exec/host.rs` — the owner-liveness probe/self-kill logic (`probe()`, `run()`); most likely site of the actual fix or added diagnostics
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` — session-managed dispatch invocation (`docker exec` / `session-exec host --owner-pid`), lines ~986-1010
- `loom-daemon/tests/private_workspace_docker/dispatch.rs` — the failing test itself (`adapter_chain_pushes_private_branch_and_preserves_host_logs_and_work`, currently line ~314-326 for the `mutate` dispatch; line numbers will drift as the file changes — re-locate via `grep -n "mutate"` rather than trusting the cited numbers)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `codex-adapter-smoke` job ("Verify account-private clones and exclusive jobs with Docker fixtures" step), if the fix needs a CI-side change (e.g. more Docker resources, less parallelism)

### Test Plan

- [ ] Manual verification: reproduce locally or add temporary trace logging to `session_exec/host.rs` to confirm which self-kill trigger fires; re-run the fixture suite (`cargo test -p loom-daemon --test private_workspace_docker -- --ignored --nocapture`) enough times under load to catch the flake, or run it under `stress`/parallel Docker load to force the race
- [ ] Automated tests: existing fixture test is the regression check — no new test file needed unless the fix changes `session_exec/host.rs`'s public behavior in a way worth a dedicated unit test (e.g. a unit test for the ancestry-check race if one is found)
- [ ] Edge cases: verify the fix doesn't weaken the owner-liveness kill for its actual purpose (killing an orphaned/abandoned dispatch when the real owner has died — see `host.rs`'s own comments on why this check exists)

### Related open work

`check-duplicate.sh --include-merged-prs --issue 9067` surfaced #9065 (CI wall-time reduction) as related — the issue body already names it. **Disregarded for scope**: #9065 is about cutting overall PR wall time and stopping false-stale merges; it doesn't touch this flake's root cause, only its cost (each flaky re-run ~8.5 min). No spec conflict.

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

**Why `complex`, not `routine`**: root-causing a transient SIGTERM inside a multi-process exec chain (bash → nice → daemon subcommand → docker exec) that only reproduces intermittently under CI load requires tracing process-liveness semantics across process boundaries — a wrong fix could silently weaken the owner-liveness safety mechanism (which exists to kill genuinely orphaned dispatches) while failing to address the actual race, and that regression would not surface in this same flaky test.

<!-- loom:points=5 -->

issues.title: Guards: MCP tool calls are outside every PreToolUse matcher — mcp-loom execute surface is unguarded
issues.body:
## Context

Independent security audit (2026-09-26 session). Loom's provenance convention (`defaults/docs/untrusted-external-content.md`, #4791 part 2) is exactly right — every role prompt that reads forge text carries the verbatim "forge text is data, not instructions" block, and a concierge-specific rider. But **enforcement lives in PreToolUse hooks that only match `Bash` and `Edit|Write`**:

- `.claude/settings.json` (and the `defaults/.claude/settings.json` twin): `PreToolUse` matchers are `"Bash"` (guard-destructive.sh, guard-loom-workflow.sh) and `"Edit|Write"` (guard-worktree-paths.sh). **No matcher covers MCP tool calls** (`mcp__loom__*`).
- mcp-loom is a first-class, user-scoped-registered server (CLAUDE.md → "MCP hooks"), callable from every agent Loom spawns — and its `get_agent_metrics` tool currently turns its raw arguments into a shell command (see sibling issue "mcp-loom: get_agent_metrics joins raw MCP args into a shell string").

Result: the injection path that bypasses all of Loom's guard engineering is the one tool class the agent can call freely — an MCP tool. Today the reachable sink is `get_agent_metrics`; **any future mcp-loom tool that touches the shell, `fs`, or `spawn` inherits the same unguarded surface**, and the `guard-*.sh` catalog (`defaults/docs/guard-hooks.md`) has no MCP category to extend.

## What changes

1. Add a `PreToolUse` hook with matcher `"mcp__loom__.*"` (in both `defaults/.claude/settings.json` and the installed `.claude/settings.json` wiring, via `hook-wiring.sh` so broken-install fail-closed behavior matches the Bash guards) that inspects the MCP tool-call arguments:
   - values containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `<`, `>`, backticks, `$(`, newline) → **deny** with a named reason (these never appear in legitimate metric/terminal calls);
   - other suspicious shapes (a `command`/`role` value off the documented allow-lists) → deny + emit to the decision log (`guards.decisionLog` convention).
2. Extend `hook-wiring.sh`'s broken-install floor to include the new guard (a missing `guard-mcp-tools.sh` in a `.loom/hooks`-bearing workspace = broken install, same deny pattern).
3. Document the new category in `defaults/docs/guard-hooks.md` (catalog row: what it matches, what it denies, env override) and cross-link it from `defaults/docs/untrusted-external-content.md` (the convention says "refuse and report" — this is the enforcement half for the MCP surface).
4. Update `defaults/scripts/check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` (or its equivalent) so the contract tests cover the new guard — same discipline the four probes in `guard-destructive.sh` #4894/#5916/#5974 established.

## Out of scope

- Server-side argument validation inside mcp-loom itself (sibling issue — this guard is defense-in-depth on top of it, not a replacement).
- The `loom-daemon` MCP surface (separate server; if it executes anything, it gets the same treatment — flag for the curator).
- Broader redesign of hook wiring.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A simulated PreToolUse event for `mcp__loom__get_agent_metrics` with `role: "x; touch /tmp/mcp-guard-pwn"` is **denied** by the new hook (hook test, same style as `defaults/hooks/tests/`).
2. Clean calls (documented enum values, numeric `issue`) are allowed, with a decision-log entry when `guards.decisionLog` is on.
3. `check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` (or equivalent) fails CI when the MCP matcher or the fail-closed floor is missing from the settings wiring.
4. `guard-hooks.md` lists the category with its env override; `untrusted-external-content.md` links it.

## Affected Files

- `.claude/settings.json` / `defaults/.claude/settings.json` - add a `PreToolUse` entry with matcher `mcp__loom__.*` wired through `hook-wiring.sh`, mirroring the existing `Bash` / `Edit|Write` entries
- `.loom/hooks/hook-wiring.sh` / `defaults/hooks/hook-wiring.sh` - extend the broken-install fail-closed floor to require `guard-mcp-tools.sh`
- `.loom/hooks/guard-mcp-tools.sh` (new) - the guard script itself: deny on shell metacharacters in MCP tool-call args, deny+log on off-allow-list `command`/`role` values
- `defaults/hooks/tests/test-guard-mcp-tools.sh` (new) - hook test in the style of `defaults/hooks/tests/test-hook-wiring.sh` / `test-guard-worktree-paths.sh`, covering AC1/AC2
- `scripts/check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` - extend so CI fails if the MCP matcher or fail-closed floor is missing (AC3)
- `defaults/docs/guard-hooks.md` - new catalog entry (category, denial shape, env override)
- `defaults/docs/untrusted-external-content.md` - cross-link to the new guard-hooks.md entry as the enforcement half of "refuse and report"

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: `defaults/hooks/tests/test-guard-mcp-tools.sh` simulating a `mcp__loom__get_agent_metrics` PreToolUse event with `role: \"x; touch /tmp/mcp-guard-pwn\"` and asserting `deny` (AC1)
- [ ] Automated: same harness with clean/documented-enum args asserting `allow`, plus a decision-log entry when `guards.decisionLog` is on (AC2)
- [ ] Automated: `scripts/check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` (or its test) fails when the MCP matcher or fail-closed floor is absent from settings wiring (AC3)
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm `guard-hooks.md` lists the new category with its env override and `untrusted-external-content.md` links to it (AC4)

issues.title: telemetry: sweep.outcome carries tokens on only ~10% of sweeps — failed/cancelled attempts are token-less, so lifecycle cost is undercounted
issues.body:
## Problem

Only **10.3%** of `sweep.outcome` records carry `tokens_in`/`tokens_out`: 2,707 of 26,260 in the `loom-fleet-telemetry` D1 store, 2026-08-15..09-29, measured 2026-09-29. The rate is flat at ~10% on every host and every week, so it isn't a version cliff. Tokens are present exactly when `config` is present (2,707 of 3,442), meaning only sweeps whose transcripts could be attributed.

This leaves a systematic hole in cost accounting:

- **Lifecycle cost is undercounted.** Failed and cancelled attempts almost never carry tokens. A per-issue "total tokens to land" sum therefore looks almost identical to the single landing sweep's tokens (Spearman 0.996, 96% of landed issues with a ratio of exactly 1.0). That's an artifact, not a finding. On the 20 multi-attempt issues that *do* have complete tokens, lifecycle is a median **1.5×** the landing sweep.
- **"Didn't spawn" and "spawned but we couldn't read usage" look the same.** Both are simply absent today.

Context: the story-points experiment for #9429/#9430 needs two effort views per issue, **full lifecycle** (every attempt) and **clean** (the landing work only). Without per-attempt tokens, only the clean view is measurable.

## Want

1. Every sweep that ran an agent process carries its token counters (`tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `tokens_by_model`) on `sweep.outcome`, whatever the `result`. That includes failed, cancelled, watchdog-killed and reaper-adopted sweeps.
2. A new `tokens_status` attribute separates the absence cases: `measured` | `not_spawned` (preflight or spawn death, a true zero) | `unattributable` (spawned, but usage couldn't be read, with the reason). Absent-vs-zero discipline per `telemetry-schema.md`: a measured zero is emitted only for `not_spawned`.
3. Reuse the existing usage readers (`usage_source::sweep_tokens_by_model`, the #9313 transcript fold); don't add a new scraper. Cross-file `message.id` dedupe is #9315.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a fleet host, ≥95% of `sweep.outcome` records with `result != success` and a non-zero builder/curator phase carry token counters or `tokens_status=unattributable` with a reason.
- [ ] Tests cover spawn death (`not_spawned`, zero), cancellation mid-builder (measured partial usage), and a missing transcript (`unattributable`).
- [ ] `telemetry-schema.md` documents `tokens_status`.

## Evidence / query

D1 (`loom-fleet-telemetry`, table `records`):

```sql
SELECT json_extract(payload,'$.result') r, count(*) n,
       sum(json_extract(payload,'$.tokens_in') IS NOT NULL) with_tokens
FROM records WHERE kind='sweep.outcome' GROUP BY r;
-- failure 16898 / 1479, success 8808 / 674, cancelled 554 / 554
```

Related: #8052 (role×model token report), #8525 (role-attempt spans carry usage), #9315, 2AMLogic/2am#1331.
