issues.title: resync pipeline correctness batch: staging credential exclusions, stamp convergence, local-fix guard, land allowlist, staging HEAD, unknown-version refusal (consolidates 6 siblings)
issues.body:
## Summary #9046 removed the leaked token-pool copy (`a9da48c2`) and added `.loom/tokens.*/` / `.loom/tokens-*/` to the managed `.gitignore` list. The **credential class** that the resync staging guards are built from was not widened, and the fallback staging recipe is still exclusion-based. Together those leave the same leak open in any repo whose `.gitignore` predates #9046, and in any future secret path nobody has listed yet. This is the second incident of this shape after #7818. ## Evidence (as of `origin/main`) 1. **The leak commit fits the exclusion-based recipe.** `a9da48c2` ("chore: resync installed Loom surfaces", 27 files) contains a real resync surface (`.loom/install-metadata.json`) **plus the entire sibling directory** `.loom/tokens.shadow-disabled-20260926T021559Z/`: 21 `.token` files, `.ranking`, `.ranking.classes.json`, `.rotation_cursor`, `.bad_tokens`. That is the footprint of `git add -A` with an exclusion list, not of the scoped `RESYNC_PATHS` add that `land-resync-commit.sh:485` performs. 2. **`CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` still lists only exact paths.** `loom-daemon/src/init/post_init.rs:350` has `.loom/claude-config/`, `.loom/tokens/`, `.loom/accounts.env`, `.loom/api-keys/`, `.loom/gh-config/`, `.loom/gh-config-by-owner/`. The sibling patterns were added to the separate gitignore list (`post_init.rs:250-251`) only. Its shell copy, `land-resync-commit.sh:310` `LOOM_CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS`, is identical, so `is_credential_leak_path` does not recognize `.loom/tokens.shadow-disabled-/x.token`. 3. **The printed fallback recipe is unchanged.** `defaults/scripts/resync-installed.sh:2803` still prints `git add -A -- . ':!.loom/claude-config' ':!.loom/tokens' …`. The pathspec `:!.loom/tokens` excludes that directory, not `.loom/tokens.shadow-disabled-*`. 4. **Consumer repos lag.** The widened `.gitignore` reaches a consumer only on re-init. rjwalters/llm-monitor (public, receives resync commits) had only `.loom/tokens/` ignored until rjwalters/llm-monitor#217 added the sibling rules outside the managed block. ## Proposed fix - **Stage an allowlist, never an exclusion list.** Replace the `git add -A -- . ':!…'` fallback with the scoped `git add -- "${resync_paths[@]}"` form that `resync-installed.sh:2768` already prints. The resync knows exactly which files it wrote. - **Widen the credential class** (`CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` and `LOOM_CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS`, keeping the machine-checked copy in sync) to include `.loom/tokens.*/` and `.loom/tokens-*/`. Better still, match any `.loom/tokens*` path segment. - **Add a content check, not just a path check:** refuse to land a resync commit whose staged diff adds a line matching a known secret shape (`sk-ant-oat01-…`, `ghs_…`, provider API-key formats). Path lists are how both incidents slipped through; a new secret location will always be one nobody listed yet. - **Consider having resync refresh the managed `.gitignore` block**, so a security rule does not wait for a re-init to reach consumers. ## Still unknown Which process produced `a9da48c2`. Its author identity is a Loom session account, and the automated lander stages only `RESYNC_PATHS`, so it was likely an agent following the printed fallback recipe or running `git add -A` directly. Not verified. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-30, verified against `origin/main` @ `aa20fc045`) **Consolidated**: #9174, #9178, #9345, #9550, #9613 are absorbed below, bodies quoted verbatim (gate checks passed for each: `loom:triage`/unlabeled only, no parent, `loom-daemon forge check-open-pr` exit 1). These are six sibling defects in one resync pipeline; filed separately they cost six full Curator→Builder→CI→Judge cycles for ~2–3 files of combined diff. One right-sized PR with a per-item AC checklist replaces them. ### Consolidated scope (one PR) | # | Fix | Size | |---|-----|------| | #9141 (this issue) | Widen the credential exclusion class + de-exclusionize the fallback staging recipe | small | | #9174 | Stamp `loom_commit` as a full SHA so `install-metadata.json` converges across hosts | tiny | | #9178 | Fix the local-fix guard's "not a resync" predicate (install-commit case is permanently true) | small | | #9345 | Add `.agents/skills/*` + `.gitignore` to `land-resync-commit.sh`'s allowlist | tiny | | #9550 | `--output` staging resolves the *invoking worktree's* HEAD, not the primary checkout's | small | | #9613 | Refuse (or warn loudly + skip restamp) when the resolved source has no version/commit metadata | small | ### Affected Files (verified present on `origin/main` @ `aa20fc045`) - `defaults/scripts/resync-installed.sh` (#9141, #9174, #9178, #9550, #9613) - `defaults/scripts/land-resync-commit.sh` (#9345) - Their test files, where present (Builder confirms; the byte-identical `.loom/scripts/` copies follow the resync rules) ### Acceptance criteria (merged; per-item, nothing dropped) - [ ] **#9141**: the credential class covering `.loom/tokens.*/` / `.loom/tokens-*/` (and any sibling token-pool copy path) is enforced in the staging guard itself, not only `.gitignore`; a copy at an unlisted path cannot be staged. Order-of-work note: land this item's diff first within the PR — it is the security-relevant one. - [ ] **#9174**: `loom_commit` is a full 40-hex SHA; two hosts resyncing the same source commit produce byte-identical `install-metadata.json`. - [ ] **#9178**: a file whose last change was the original install commit is no longer treated as hand-edited; the guard fires only on real local divergence (post-install non-resync edits). - [ ] **#9345**: `land-resync-commit.sh` accepts resync output touching `.agents/skills/*` and `.gitignore`; the reproduce case from #9345 (resync → dry-run land) succeeds. - [ ] **#9550**: `--output ` invoked from a linked worktree stages at that worktree's HEAD; the staged commit fast-forwards onto the feature branch. - [ ] **#9613**: a source without `package.json`/git metadata is refused with a clear error (or skips the restamp with a loud warning) — `unknown` stamps never reach a tracked `install-metadata.json`. **Points**: 5 (~3–5 h combined, 2–3 files, one PR). ## Consolidated from #9174 >
Original body of #9174 (verbatim)
> `resync-installed.sh`'s `restamp_metadata()` writes `loom_commit` as an **abbreviated** SHA. Git auto-sizes that abbreviation per repository and per git version when `core.abbrev` is unset, so two hosts resyncing from the *same* Loom source commit write *different strings* — and `.loom/install-metadata.json` is tracked, so the file never converges and every resync on every managed repo produces a spurious one-line diff that flips back and forth between hosts. > > ### Measured > > Both hosts resynced `rjwalters/llm-monitor` to `loom_version 0.19.436` from Loom source commit `64a3258048cc…`: > > | host | git | stamped `loom_commit` | > |---|---|---| > | loom-worker-1 | 2.43.0 | `64a325804` (9 hex) | > | robb-pro | 2.54.0 | `64a32580` (8 hex) | > > `core.abbrev` is unset on both. The resulting diff, seen for real while reconciling the two checkouts: > > ```diff > - "loom_commit": "64a325804", > + "loom_commit": "64a32580", > ``` > > That was the *only* difference between the two hosts' resync output — 102 files updated on each, byte-identical except this. So the practical effect is that each scheduled resync pass on a host whose abbreviation length differs from whoever pushed last sees a dirty tree, commits it, and pushes a no-op churn commit; the next host reverses it. > > ### Why it is worth fixing rather than ignoring > > - It manufactures commit churn on **every** fleet repo, indefinitely, and those commits are indistinguishable from real surface updates in `git log`. > - It makes "is this host's surface current?" un-answerable by comparing the file, which is what the field exists for. > - An abbreviated SHA is also ambiguity-prone by construction, and it is contrary to house policy elsewhere: 2AMLogic's provenance contract (`docs/provenance.md`, harness-ops D33) requires **full 40-hex SHAs**, with `unknown` spelled out rather than omitted. > > ### Suggested fix > > Stamp the full 40-hex SHA — `git rev-parse HEAD`, not `--short`. Readers that want a short form can abbreviate at display time. > > If a short form is wanted in the file for human readability, it must be pinned to a fixed width (`git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD`) so it is host-independent — but the full SHA is the better answer, and matches the provenance contract. > > Either way a one-time re-stamp will produce one final diff per repo as hosts converge on the new format. > > ### Found via > > Unblocking `llm-monitor` on loom-worker-1, whose scheduled resync had been aborting for eleven days for an unrelated reason (a `rebase --abort` leaving 396 staged paths in the index, so each pass re-attempted the rebase against the previous pass's debris). Once that was cleared and the resync ran clean on two hosts independently, this was the only disagreement left between them. >
## Consolidated from #9178 >
Original body of #9178 (verbatim)
> `resync-installed.sh`'s local-fix guard blocks files that provably have no local fix, and the block is **self-perpetuating** — it can never clear on its own. > > ### The condition it tests > > The guard refuses to overwrite an installed copy when both hold: > > 1. the installed copy has line(s) not present in the new source, **and** > 2. the copy's last change was **not** a routine resync. > > Condition 2 is intended to mean "somebody hand-edited this". It does not. It is also true for **any file that has not been touched since the original `Install Loom …` commit** — because an install commit is not a resync commit. Condition 1 then becomes true on its own as upstream drifts and removes or rewrites any line in that file. Neither condition required a human to touch anything. > > ### Measured on `2AMLogic/fasterhenry` (loom-worker-2) > > Installed surface `0.19.302`, source `0.19.437`. Three files sampled, each reported by the guard as `look like a local fix`: > > | file | identical to the install commit? | local-only lines | source-only lines it is missing | > |---|---|---|---| > | `.loom/scripts/create-pr.sh` | **yes — byte-identical** | 7 | 17 | > | `.loom/scripts/blame-issue.sh` | **yes — byte-identical** | 12 | 20 | > | `.loom/roles/guide.md` | **yes — byte-identical** | 8 | 45 | > > Verified with `git show 36171b2: | cmp -s - ` on a clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty), where `36171b2` is `Install Loom v0.19.174 and Repo Skills v0.11.17 (#7)`. So the working copy equals what the installer wrote and **no edit has ever been made** — the "local-only lines" are simply lines upstream has since changed or dropped across ~135 versions of drift. > > The repo does have 3 resync commits, so "never resynced" is not the explanation; those passes touched 12 other files. Any file a resync happens not to touch keeps the install commit as its last-touching commit, permanently. > > ### Why it is self-perpetuating > > The guard blocks the write → the file is not updated → its last-touching commit is still the install commit → condition 2 stays true → the next pass blocks again. `--force` is the only escape, and `--force` is exactly what an operator should be reluctant to use, because the message says a local fix would be lost. > > Net effect: `BLOCKED: N file(s) look like a local fix`, `resync-installed.sh` exits 1, and the scheduled unit goes red and stays red. > > ### Scope observed > > Surveying all 57 registered workspaces on loom-worker-2: > > | repo | files flagged | genuine? | > |---|---|---| > | `fasterhenry` | ~50 | **no** — sampled 3, all byte-identical to the install commit | > | `research` | ~13 | **no** (same shape; `install-metadata.json` has no `loom_version` at all) | > | `sky130-modexp` | 11 | **yes** — 2am#869, 3 already pinned in `.loom/resync-ignore` | > | `sg13g2-bandgap` | 1 (`scripts/tests/ci-wired.txt`) | **yes** — added by that repo's own PR #249 | > > So roughly 63 of 75 flagged files across the fleet are false positives, and they are the ones that keep two repos from ever resyncing. > > ### Suggested fix > > Stop inferring "was edited" from commit subjects. `install-metadata.json` already records the version the copy came from, so the question is answerable directly: compare the installed copy against **`defaults/` at the recorded `loom_version`/`loom_commit`**. Identical ⇒ unedited ⇒ update freely, regardless of what the last commit was called. Different ⇒ a real local change ⇒ block as today. > > That also fixes the guard for the case it was written for, since it no longer depends on how a commit was titled. Cheaper partial fixes, if the above is too invasive: > > - treat an `Install Loom …` commit as a routine baseline alongside a resync commit (removes the fasterhenry/research class, keeps the rest of the heuristic); > - and/or say in the block message which commit the decision was based on, so an operator can see it was the install commit and not an edit. > > ### Found via > > 2am#1128, unblocking loom-worker-2's stranded checkouts. Related: 2am#869 tracks the genuine local-fix instances on `sky130-modexp`, where this guard is working correctly and has 3 files pinned. >
## Consolidated from #9345 >
Original body of #9345 (verbatim)
> ## What happened > > On 2026-09-28, in `2AMLogic/gf180-parasynth`, `main` was 3 commits behind `origin/main`. Per `check-main-freshness.sh`'s remediation I ran: > > ``` > git merge --ff-only origin/main > ./.loom/scripts/resync-installed.sh # no --dry-run > ``` > > `resync-installed.sh` updated 70 files and removed 3, including files under `.agents/skills/*` and `.gitignore` (the loom-daemon-managed block). It then printed the usual "tree is dirty with only resync output" suggestion to commit. > > I tried to land that via the documented sanctioned path: > > ``` > ./.loom/scripts/land-resync-commit.sh --dry-run > ``` > > It refused: > > ``` > ERROR: Refusing to land: the working tree has non-resync dirt alongside resync output: > ERROR: .agents/skills/loom-architect/SKILL.md > ERROR: .agents/skills/loom-builder-pr/SKILL.md > ERROR: ... (8 more .agents/skills/*.md paths) > ERROR: .gitignore > ERROR: This script only ever commits the known resync-managed surfaces. > ERROR: Resolve (or commit) the unrelated change yourself, then re-run. > ``` > > ## Root cause > > `land-resync-commit.sh`'s `is_resync_surface_path()` allowlist (around line ~275) is: > > ``` > .loom/hooks/* | .loom/scripts/* | .loom/roles/* | .loom/docs/* | \ > .loom/bin/* | .loom/runtimes/* | \ > .claude/commands/loom/* | .claude/README.md | \ > .github/CONFIGURATION.md | \ > .loom/install-metadata.json | .loom/CLAUDE.md | .gitattributes) > ``` > > It does not include `.agents/skills/*` (which `resync-installed.sh` itself resyncs "marker-gated, #8673") or `.gitignore` (which `resync-installed.sh` regenerates via the resolved `loom-daemon` binary as part of every run). So on any repo where `resync-installed.sh` actually touches those two surfaces — which appears to be every repo running the current `defaults/`, given this was a plain `resync-installed.sh` run with no special flags — `land-resync-commit.sh` treats its own sibling script's normal output as "unrelated dirt" and refuses to land it. > > This isn't the #8004/#8005/#7818 credential-safety class (those paths are intentionally excluded); `.agents/skills/*` and `.gitignore`'s loom-managed block are legitimate resync payload with no credential content. > > ## Impact > > The two scripts have silently drifted out of sync: `resync-installed.sh`'s set of managed surfaces grew (at least for `.agents/skills/` per #8673, and the `.gitignore` regeneration path), but `land-resync-commit.sh`'s allowlist mirror was not updated to match. Every resync run that touches either surface now requires manual intervention instead of the documented one-command land path — exactly the ad hoc behavior `land-resync-commit.sh` was written (per its own header, #6646) to eliminate. > > ## Suggested fix > > Add `.agents/skills/*` and `.gitignore` to `is_resync_surface_path()` in `land-resync-commit.sh`, and add a regression test (mirroring the existing `test-land-resync-commit.sh` cases) that runs `resync-installed.sh` for real (or a fixture of its output) and asserts every path it can touch is covered by the allowlist, so the two scripts can't re-diverge silently. > > ## Workaround used this session > > Reverted the resync output (`git checkout -- .` in the primary clone) rather than hand-committing outside the sanctioned script, to keep `main` clean for the sweep in progress. No commit was landed. >
## Consolidated from #9550 >
Original body of #9550 (verbatim)
> ## Context > > `defaults/scripts/resync-installed.sh`'s OUTPUT-DIR STAGING MODE (#6106) says `--output ` "creates a disposable, DETACHED git worktree at HEAD under ". When invoked from a linked feature worktree (the documented use case, since the worktree restriction forbids writing to the primary checkout from there), the staging worktree is created at the **primary checkout's** HEAD, not the invoking worktree's. If the feature branch already has commits (here: an earlier tool's resync commit), the staged commit's parent is the primary HEAD, so the documented "turn it into a commit (and PR) from the staging worktree" cannot be fast-forwarded into the feature branch; the operator has to cherry-pick, and removing the staging worktree first leaves the commit dangling. > > ## Suggested acceptance criteria > > - [ ] `--output` bases the staging worktree on the invoking checkout's HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` from cwd) or takes an explicit `--base ` > - [ ] The header comment states which HEAD is used > - [ ] The completion message suggests `git cherry-pick ` when the invoking branch is ahead of the staging base >
## Consolidated from #9613 >
Original body of #9613 (verbatim)
> ## Context > > `resync-installed.sh` resolved its defaults source from `.loom/loom-source-path`. The path pointed at a directory containing a copied `defaults/` tree but no `package.json` and no `.git`. The resync still ran, then re-stamped `.loom/install-metadata.json` with `loom_version` / `loom_commit` = `unknown` and an empty source remote. That unparseable stamp was committed to the consumer's main. Downstream checks then couldn't compare versions, and the local-fix guard's content-lineage check had no commit to resolve against. > > ## Suggested acceptance criteria > - [ ] If the resolved source has no `package.json` or no git metadata, refuse with a clear error, or warn loudly and skip the metadata re-stamp. Never write `unknown` into a tracked file. > - [ ] Test: a source dir with only `defaults/` produces the refusal or warning, and leaves `install-metadata.json` unchanged. > >

issues.title: Role-tick executions get no loom.runtime.usage span and no session.summary trace join
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up from #9013 item 5 (Judge review of the telemetry mega PR A, #9008).

Sweep dispatch (`sweep_registry::spawn_process`) calls
`observability::tracing::prepare_child` to hand its child a `TRACEPARENT`
and persist a trace context keyed by the sweep's own execution id, then
`observability::runtime_usage::join::open` to open a `session.summary` trace
join entry, and at the terminal transition `runtime_usage::finish_sweep`
journals the `loom.runtime.usage` span and closes the join entry.

`role_runner`'s tick dispatch (`role_runner/launch.rs::run_role_with_timeout`)
has none of this. A Judge/Champion/Doctor/etc. role tick that runs outside a
sweep — the role-runner cron path, `autonomous.roleRunner`, and GitHub Actions
cron dispatch of the five non-daemon-native roles — currently emits no
`loom.runtime.usage` span and gets no trace join at all, so its transcripts'
`session.summary` records can never carry a `trace_context`, and its token
usage never shows up as a `loom.runtime.usage` span in SigNoz.

## Why this is its own issue

Doing this properly is a **design decision**, not mechanical plumbing:

- Sweeps have a natural "execution id" (`sweep_id`) that both the trace store
  and the join entry are keyed by; a role tick has no equivalent identity
  today — `tick_anchor` (a timestamp string) is the closest thing, and
  whether that's the right execution key (and whether it's stable enough
  across `run_role_with_timeout`'s retry/timeout paths) needs a decision, not
  an assumption.
- The usage-span emission needs a **role-tick usage reader** analogous to
  `usage_source::sweep_tokens_by_model`, keyed by the tick's own log/anchor
  rather than a sweep id — that reader doesn't exist for the role-runner path
  today.
- The join entry needs an **issue** to key on (`join::open(root, execution,
  issue)`), but a role tick is not always scoped to one issue (Judge/Champion
  reviewing a PR set, Doctor fixing a build, Auditor scanning the repo) — the
  right attribution (an issue when the tick names one, otherwise no join
  entry at all) needs to be decided per role, not defaulted.

Given that, #9013 explicitly scoped this out of its own PR (see that issue's
own acceptance criteria, which allow closing a hard sub-item with a written
rationale rather than forcing a fix) and filed this issue to track it as
follow-up work instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the role-tick "execution id" role_runner should key a persisted
      trace context on (or reuse `tick_anchor` if that's sufficient).
- [ ] `run_role_with_timeout` (or its terminal-transition call site) opens a
      trace-join entry — scoped to an issue when the tick names one — mirroring
      `sweep_registry::spawn_process`'s `join::open` call.
- [ ] A role-tick usage reader (or a generalized version of
      `usage_source::sweep_tokens_by_model`) totals the tick's own token usage.
- [ ] At the tick's terminal transition, journal a `loom.runtime.usage` span
      and close the join entry, mirroring `runtime_usage::finish_sweep`.
- [ ] A test: a role-tick execution (Judge/Champion/Doctor, non-sweep)
      produces a `loom.runtime.usage` span and joins to a `session.summary`
      record.

## Non-goals

- Closing the "subagent transcript whose head names no issue stays unjoined"
  gap — that is documented, intentional behavior (never guess an issue from
  prose), not a bug; #9013 added a regression test pinning it.
## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/launch.rs` — `run_role_with_timeout` (`launch.rs:10`) is the tick dispatch call site; needs the new execution-id decision, a `join::open` call, and the terminal-transition span/join-close, mirroring what `sweep_registry::spawn_process` does for sweeps.
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs` — the sweep-side reference implementation to mirror: calls `observability::tracing::prepare_child` (`spawn_process.rs:173`) and `observability::runtime_usage::join::open` (`spawn_process.rs:206`).
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs` — the sweep-side terminal-transition reference: calls `observability::runtime_usage::finish_sweep` (`outcome_journal.rs:914`) to journal the span and close the join entry.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/tracing.rs` — `prepare_child` (`tracing.rs:47`) takes an `execution: &str, issue: Option<u32>` pair; the role-tick path will call this (or an equivalent) once the execution-id decision above is made.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/runtime_usage/join.rs` — `open`/`open_at` (`join.rs:103`, `join.rs:113`) take `(root, execution, issue: u32)` — note `issue` is non-optional here, which is exactly the "not every role tick names one issue" design question the acceptance criteria call out.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/runtime_usage.rs` — `finish_sweep` (`runtime_usage.rs:142`) is the terminal-span-plus-join-close reference to mirror or generalize.
- `loom-daemon/src/usage_source.rs` — `sweep_tokens_by_model` (`usage_source.rs:246`) is the existing sweep-keyed usage reader; the new role-tick usage reader (AC item 3) is either a sibling function here or a generalization of this one.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/` (new test module or existing `role_runner/tests.rs`) — home for the new role-tick execution test (AC item 5).

All paths verified present at `9324e5809` (2026-09-29) via `grep -rn` against `loom-daemon/src/`; re-verify against current `main` before implementing, since this is an actively-developed area of the daemon.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a new test in `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs` (or a new module) drives a non-sweep role tick (Judge/Champion/Doctor) through `run_role_with_timeout` and asserts it produces a `loom.runtime.usage` span and a `session.summary` trace-join record — this is AC item 5, restated as the concrete test target.
- [ ] Automated tests: cover the "tick names no issue" branch (Judge/Champion reviewing a PR set, Doctor fixing a build, Auditor scanning the repo) and confirm the decided per-role attribution behaves as designed — no join entry, or a join entry keyed some other way, per whatever AC item 1/3 above settle on.
- [ ] Manual verification: run a role tick locally (e.g. via `autonomous.roleRunner` or a direct role-runner invocation) and confirm the emitted `loom.runtime.usage` span and `session.summary` join entry appear in the trace store the same way a sweep's do.

issues.title: demand ledger: filter parked PRs from changes debt (Doctor-cap loom:blocked) so build back-off can't latch; fix buildBackoff docs rows
issues.body:
## Summary

Two non-blocking findings from the Judge review of #9419 (#9410, build back-off), recorded here so they aren't lost.

### 1. Changes debt still counts PRs that no role will drain (stuck-engaged risk)

#9419 filters merge debt with `MERGE_HOLD_LABELS` (`loom:blocked`, `loom:operator`, `loom:operator-only`) at record time in `role_runner/demand.rs`, so `loom:pr` PRs that Champion can't merge no longer hold the back-off engaged. The **changes** axis has no such filter. PRs parked at the Doctor-cycle cap carry `loom:blocked` + `loom:changes-requested`. Doctor skips them, so no role drains them, yet they still count toward `review_debt + changes_debt + merge_debt`. On a host with enough of them, the back-off can stay engaged and hold every unstarred build. This is the same class of risk #9419 removed for merge debt.

**Fix:** apply the equivalent filter to the changes axis at record time. Exclude the PRs Doctor won't pick up, using the label set from doctor.md's skip rules, defined once as a constant. Use the rows the queue-gate listing already returns, so no new forge call is needed. Also consider whether the review axis has a similar parked state, i.e. a label combination Judge skips. Add unit tests that parked PRs don't contribute to debt.

### 2. `buildBackoff` rows in the wrong docs table

`defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` ~L3543: the three `autonomous.workFinder.buildBackoff.{enabled,high,low}` rows were added to the 5-column starvation-escape table with only 4 cells, so they render shifted by one column. Move them to the 4-column config reference table, after the `saturationBrake.starvationEscapeSecs` row (~L4615). The new subsection's own table is correct.

(A third, cosmetic note: the dispatch-plan slot header / `loom-daemon queue` plan line shows `SATURATION-HELD` but not the build back-off. The back-off already shows in row gates and the tick summary, so this is optional.)

Related: #9410 / #9419 (build back-off), #9392 / #9413 (demand ledger), #9391.

---

## Curator enhancement (verified against `origin/main` 76f888f14)

### Where the axes are recorded today

- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs` `forge_queue_probe()` (~L399-422): the queue-gate listing for judge (`loom:review-requested`) and doctor (`loom:changes-requested`), per `work_queue_labels()` (~L69-75). Each listing's rows go to `demand::record_listing(demand::global(), root, label, &rows)` (L416). No new forge call is needed: the rows already carry `labels`.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/demand.rs`:
  - `MERGE_HOLD_LABELS` (L314) = `["loom:blocked", "loom:operator", "loom:operator-only"]`
  - `count_axis_rows(axis, rows)` (L321-331) counts open PR rows and applies the hold filter **only** when `axis == DebtAxis::Merge`. Review and changes count every open PR row.
  - `record_listing` (L335-341) calls `count_axis_rows`. `forge_merge_probe` (L347-365) uses it for the post-champion `loom:pr` count.

### Exclusion set per axis (what the owning role skips)

| Axis | Role that drains it | Labels the role skips (autonomous Finding Work) | Constant to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Merge (`loom:pr`) | Champion | `loom:blocked`, `loom:operator`, `loom:operator-only` | `MERGE_HOLD_LABELS`. **Unchanged.** |
| Changes (`loom:changes-requested`) | Doctor | `loom:blocked`, `loom:operator-only` | Reuse `crate::work_finder::PARK_LABELS` (`work_finder/labels.rs` L31). It is exactly `["loom:blocked", "loom:operator-only"]`. **Not** `MERGE_HOLD_LABELS`. |
| Review (`loom:review-requested`) | Judge | none | no filter |

Citations:
- **Changes axis.** `defaults/roles/doctor.md` Priority 2 query (~L439): `label:loom:changes-requested -label:loom:blocked -label:loom:operator-only`. The comment above it says it mirrors the work-finder's `PARK_LABELS`. The note at ~L458-467 (#7660) says `loom:operator` is **deliberately not** excluded: Champion keeps `loom:operator` on stale held PRs it routes to Doctor, so Doctor still drains them. Reusing `MERGE_HOLD_LABELS` here would hide real Doctor work (the #6720 class of bug), so the two sets must stay different. The Doctor-cycle-cap park is `loom:blocked` + `loom:changes-requested` (`defaults/.agents/skills/loom-champion/SKILL.md` L27, "Capped-PR Recovery"), and it falls in this set.
- **`loom:treating` stays counted.** Doctor's jq also skips `loom:treating`, but that label is a live claim, meaning a Doctor is draining the PR. That is real in-flight debt, not a parked PR. Do not add it to the exclusion.
- **Review axis.** `defaults/roles/judge.md` L304 and L522: Judge's queue is plain `pr list --label="loom:review-requested"` with no label exclusions. The only hold-aware logic (~L936-947) is the stale-verdict guard refusing to *re-queue* held PRs, which does not affect draining. There is no parked review state, so no review filter. If a future judge.md change adds an exclusion, add it then.

### Implementation guidance

In `demand.rs`, replace the `axis != DebtAxis::Merge || !held(r)` special case with one per-axis lookup, for example:

```rust
/// Labels whose presence means the axis's owning role will not drain the PR.
fn axis_park_labels(axis: DebtAxis) -> &'static [&'static str] {
    match axis {
        DebtAxis::Merge => &MERGE_HOLD_LABELS,               // champion-pr-merge.md
        DebtAxis::Changes => crate::work_finder::PARK_LABELS, // doctor.md Priority 2 (#5272, #7660)
        DebtAxis::Review => &[],                              // judge.md: no exclusions
    }
}
```

Then filter with `!r.labels.iter().any(|l| axis_park_labels(axis).contains(&l.as_str()))`. Each set stays defined once. Update the doc comments on `count_axis_rows`, `record_listing` and `forge_queue_probe` to name the changes filter.

**Out of scope:**
- The queue gate's `Ok(true)` still fires on a queue where every PR is parked, so Doctor can be dispatched with nothing to do. This issue only changes what the ledger *counts*, not the dispatch gate. File it separately if it matters.
- The dispatch-plan header / `loom-daemon queue` plan line showing the build back-off (cosmetic note 3). The back-off already shows in row gates, the tick summary and `health`.

### Docs fix (`defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`, line numbers confirmed)

1. Cut L3543-3545 (`buildBackoff.enabled` / `.high` / `.low`). They sit inside the 5-column starvation-escape table (header L3539 `| | Config | Env | Default | Effect |`) with only 4 cells.
2. Paste them into the 4-column config reference table (header `| Config key | Env override | Default | Notes |`) immediately after the `saturationBrake.starvationEscapeSecs` row at **L4615** (L4612 after the cut), before `quarantine.enabled`. They already have the right 4-cell shape (`key | *(config only)* | default | notes`), so no cell edits are needed.
3. Update the two prose spots that describe the axis filters: ~L3709-3713 (concurrent-dispatch ledger paragraph: "the `loom:pr` count leaves out PRs held for a human ...") and ~L3770-3771 (build back-off "Input" bullet: "The merge axis excludes operator-held PRs ..."). Each should say the changes axis also excludes `loom:blocked` / `loom:operator-only` (Doctor's Priority 2 skip set, not `loom:operator`) and that review is unfiltered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `count_axis_rows(DebtAxis::Changes, rows)` excludes open PR rows carrying `loom:blocked` or `loom:operator-only`, including the Doctor-cap park (`loom:changes-requested` + `loom:blocked`).
- [ ] AC2: On the changes axis, a PR carrying `loom:operator` (without the other two), `loom:treating`, or no hold label **is still counted**.
- [ ] AC3: The review axis is unfiltered: a `loom:review-requested` PR with any of `loom:blocked` / `loom:operator` / `loom:operator-only` still counts.
- [ ] AC4: The merge axis is unchanged. The existing `operator_held_prs_are_not_merge_debt` assertions still pass (`Merge == 2`, `Review == 5`).
- [ ] AC5: The changes exclusion set is defined in exactly one place, reusing `work_finder::PARK_LABELS`. No new literal label array is added in `demand.rs`.
- [ ] AC6: Via `record_listing(..., "loom:changes-requested", rows)`, an all-parked listing records the changes axis as `Some(AxisDebt::default())` (observed, zero), not `None`. This mirrors the existing merge-axis assertion.
- [ ] AC7: The three `buildBackoff.*` rows appear only in the 4-column config reference table, right after `saturationBrake.starvationEscapeSecs`. The starvation-escape table has only its two 5-cell rows. Every row in both tables has the header's column count.
- [ ] AC8: The ledger / back-off prose (~L3709, ~L3770) states the changes-axis exclusion and that review is unfiltered.
- [ ] AC9: `cargo test -p loom-daemon role_runner::tests::demand` and `cargo clippy -p loom-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

## Test Plan

Add a test in `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests/demand.rs` next to `operator_held_prs_are_not_merge_debt` (~L113-143), e.g. `parked_prs_are_not_changes_debt`. Use rows labelled `loom:changes-requested` + one of: nothing, `loom:blocked`, `loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator`, `loom:treating`. Assert `Changes == 3` (plain, operator, treating), `Review == 5` and `Merge == 2`, where the merge count is unaffected by the new code path because operator / blocked / operator-only rows are excluded there as before. Then assert via `record_listing` + `ledger.host_debt(HOUR).changes` for the mixed listing and for an all-parked listing (AC6). Update the stale comment in the existing test ("Review / changes debt is unaffected by the same labels") so it names only review.

Docs check: run `awk -F'|' 'NR>=3535 && NR<=3550 {print NR": "NF}'` over the starvation table and over the rows around `starvationEscapeSecs` in the config table, before and after. Each table should show one uniform field count.

- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/demand.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests/demand.rs`
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`

Read-only references (not edited): `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/labels.rs` (`PARK_LABELS`), `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs` (`forge_queue_probe`), `defaults/roles/doctor.md`, `defaults/roles/judge.md`.

issues.title: [eta] projected stage-boundary times (stage_marks) in eta-explanation/v1
issues.body:
**Epic:** #9289 (ETA as a Loom primitive) · follow-on to slice 1a (#9339) / 1b (#9355), consumed by phase 6 (#9329)

## Context

The merged `eta-explanation/v1` core carries, per estimate (`start`/`finish`/`land`):

- one **terminal scalar** — `result.{p25,p50,p75}_sec` + `result.eta_p50_at` (`as_of + p50`);
- per-stage **distributions on the simulated path** — `stages[]` (grid, p25/p50/p75/p90, `reached_with_probability`, `mean_visits`);
- the current stage's **conditioning** (`age_sec`, `f_age`, `n_above`, `truncate_inverse_cdf`);
- the rework **branches** (per-attempt change-requested probabilities, expected rounds).

What it cannot express is the **projected entry time of each future stage boundary** — "PR opens ~T1, approved ~T2, merged ~T3". That is exactly the shape a per-item detailed timeline wants to render. 2AMLogic/loom-ui's issue page (#114) draws one such timeline (past label transitions per item, e.g. `#/repos/rjwalters/loom/issues/<n>`); the operator has asked that it also show the predicted *future* events with their ETAs, cut off from the real history. Until this exists the dashboard computes an interim projection from its own stage-dwell distributions (2AMLogic/loom-ui issue #359, interim, to be retired) — which is at odds with the operator's ruling on #9289 that ETA is a Loom primitive the dashboard only displays.

A client also can't just sum the `stages[]` p50s:

1. the current-stage residual is the **conditioned** quantity (inverse-CDF above `f_age`, truncated) — only `f_age`/`n_above` are exposed, so a client re-implements the estimator's arithmetic;
2. rework revisits (`mean_visits > 1`) interleave with that conditioning — a plain sum ignores the per-path simulation `combination` already ran (`monte_carlo_grid_resample`, drawn);
3. `stages[]` is budget-droppable (`enforce_cap`), while a display timeline wants one self-contained, cap-surviving list.

The marks cost nothing new: they are percentiles of the *cumulative* path time over the draws `combination` already made, under the existing seed.

## Proposal (minimal)

- `EstimateResult.stage_marks: Vec<StageMark>` (or a sibling on `Explanation` — estimator's call), where
  `StageMark { stage: Stage, p25_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, p50_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, p75_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, mean_visits: Option<f64> }`:
  - `*_at` = `as_of` + that percentile of the stage's **cumulative entry time** over the simulated paths; `None` when the stage is unreachable or its distribution has no samples (no fabricated values);
  - the terminal mark's `p50_at` equals `result.eta_p50_at` (asserted in tests);
  - for `start`-kind estimates the path starts at dispatch, so the marks read as the planned future from "now".
- **`eta.snapshot` stays slim** (phase 6's scope is unchanged): the marks ride on the explanation, which the dashboard already fetches on demand by `estimate_id`.
- `enforce_cap`: drop `stage_marks` as one named unit (`"result.stage_marks"`) alongside the stage grids — the terminal scalar survives.
- The `--explain` output (slice 1c's consumer) renders the marks as a compact timeline line: `stage × time`, so the CLI shows the same projected future.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `stage_marks` in the `eta-explanation/v1` schema; docs updated (`defaults/docs/eta.md`, telemetry schema/collector where the explanation ships, `daemon-reference`).
- [ ] Golden fixture (`loom-daemon/src/eta/fixtures/explanation-golden.json`) extended; a test recomputes the cumulative percentiles from the same seed and compares field-for-field.
- [ ] Consistency: terminal mark `p50_at == result.eta_p50_at` for `land`/`finish`.
- [ ] Cap behavior: marks dropped before `features`, named in `truncated`; terminal scalar always survives.
- [ ] No new emission, no extra draws: same seed, same path, computed from existing simulation output.
- [ ] Dashboard follow-up: 2AMLogic/loom-ui#359 renders the projected timeline from these marks once #9329 lands, and retires its interim projection.


## Data precondition: condition role-attempt dwell on work actually done

Observed 2026-09-28 against the live 30-day `stage-durations` aggregate (the same spans the ETA
distributions are built from): every `loom.role_attempt` row is dominated by no-op / early-exit
attempts — p50 runs in **milliseconds** (builder 0/0/0/0, judge ≈ 36 ms, doctor ≈ 31 ms) while the
p95s carry the real work (curator ≈ 5.9 min, champion ≈ 5.2 min). The interim dashboard projection
(2AMLogic/loom-ui#359, patched by #400) survives this by dropping an unmeasured term rather than
painting it, but the same gap defeats the native estimator's build/review-role distributions: a
p50 of milliseconds makes the in-stage residual and the `stage_marks` of every boundary past a
role-attempt stage collapse to "now".

- The dwell feeds (and the `eta-explanation` distributions built on them) should condition on the
  attempts that actually did the stage's work (e.g. an attribute `loom.attempt.worked`, or emitting
  the dwell only for attempts that produced the stage's outcome), or carry both conditioned
  percentiles;
- until then, a consumer with no conditioned distribution should treat the role stage as
  unmeasured and say so (no fabricated values) rather than reading the all-attempts p50.

**Follow-up filed (2026-09-28, Curator enrichment):** the "Data precondition" section above described a real but broader data-quality gap in the `loom.role_attempt` dwell feed that predates and is orthogonal to `stage_marks` itself (it affects every `eta-explanation/v1` consumer reading a role-attempt stage's `p50`, not just this field). Split out to #9420 so it can be curated/prioritized independently and #9366 isn't blocked on fixing the upstream dwell conditioning. #9366's own scope is unaffected: `stage_marks` should compute correctly from whatever distributions `stages[]` already carries, including the currently-unconditioned ones — the "no fabricated values" discipline in the Proposal above (marks are `None` only when a stage is unreachable or has no samples) already covers this issue's obligation; it does not need to detect or special-case the milliseconds-collapse, since that is a property of the input distribution `stage_marks` is a query over, not a new one it introduces.

Related: #9289 · #9339 · #9355 · #9329 · #9420 · 2AMLogic/loom-ui#114 (issue page timeline)

issues.title: telemetry: PRs aren't reliably linked to their issue (slice PRs lack Closes, pr_number on 2.7% of sweep.outcome, model field is the config arm)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

**Per-issue work can't be summed reliably, because PRs aren't reliably linked to the issue they implement.** Found while building per-issue effort for the story-points experiment (#9429), over 329 landed issues (2026-08-15..09-29):

- **Slice PRs are invisible to GitHub's issue↔PR link.** Slices reuse `feature/issue-N` but often omit `Closes #N`, so `closedByPullRequestsReferences` misses them. 19 of 329 sweep-landing PRs (from D1 `pr_number`) were not in that connection.
- **Some issues land through many PRs.** 20 issues had more than one merged PR on `feature/issue-N`; `2AMLogic/gf180-pll#237` has **47**. Their lifecycle churn is up to 835× the landing PR's size. Without a reliable link, "work delivered for issue N" is either under-counted (landing PR only) or needs branch-name scraping.
- **The sweep record rarely names its PR.** `sweep.outcome.pr_number` is present on 2.7% of outcomes (697 of 26,260), so telemetry can't make the link either.
- **The recorded model is the config arm, not what ran.** `sweep.outcome.model` records the arm ("sonnet" on every record checked), not the model that ran. The real model has to be inferred from the dominant entry in `tokens_by_model`. Tokens per hand-written line differ ~1.5× between Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 landings, so this matters for any token-based measure.

### Want

1. Every PR opened by a Loom role for issue N carries a machine-readable link: `Closes #N` for the final PR, `Refs #N` plus a `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer for slices and partial PRs.
2. `sweep.outcome` always carries `pr_number` (and `pr_numbers[]` when a sweep opens more than one) whenever a PR was opened, merged or updated.
3. `sweep.outcome.model` carries the model(s) that actually ran (dominant model + `models_used`); keep the arm under `config.arm`.

### Acceptance (as originally filed)

- [ ] For a week of landings, 100% of Loom-opened PRs resolve to their issue via either GitHub's closing reference or the `Loom-Issue` trailer.
- [ ] `pr_number` is present on every `sweep.outcome` whose sweep opened or updated a PR (contract test).
- [ ] `model` reflects the actual model on a mixed Opus/Sonnet sweep (contract test).

Related: #9441 (disposition), #9446 (sweep_facts rollup), 2AMLogic/2am#1610 (storyline landed-size facts, which need this link to sum per issue).

---

## Verified corrections

- **2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `9135761f6`** (code read of `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs`, `git log`/`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and `gh pr view 9481`): **Want items 2 and 3 already shipped today**, in PR #9481 ("feat(telemetry): sweep facts — disposition, token status, lineage, landing size; claim-label safety; retention + rollups", merged 2026-09-29T14:29:28Z, merge commit `31e7fa58`), which its own body lists under "Partially addressed": *"#9465 — telemetry half ships: `pr_numbers[]` (every sampled PR, first-seen order) and `model` = dominant model that actually ran (arm stays `config.arm`). The `Closes #N` / `Loom-Issue:` trailer convention is the role-prompt half, deferred to the role-prompt authoring discipline."* This matches @turian's comment on this issue (2026-09-29). Concretely, in `outcome_journal.rs`:
  - `pr_numbers` (plural, `Vec<u32>`, first-seen order) is now populated from `self.sampled_pr_numbers(sweep_id)` (line ~732) and carried on `SweepOutcomeRecord.pr_numbers` (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs:922`).
  - `model` is reassigned (lines 753-764) to the dominant `(input+output)` model in `tokens_by_model`, falling back to the dispatched model only when no transcript was attributed. The comment at line 753 reads: *"Issue #9465: `model` names what actually ran — the dominant model in the per-model breakdown — with the dispatched model as the fallback when nothing was attributed. The dispatch-time arm stays under `config["arm"]` (#4809)."*
  - `config["arm"]` is inferred from the **original dispatched** model (`infer_arm_from_model`, lines 525-541) — this insertion happens *before* the `model` variable is reassigned to the dominant-actual-model at line 757, so arm and actual-model are correctly decoupled, not accidentally re-deriving arm from the post-swap value.
  - **Only item 1 (the PR-body/commit-message linking convention) remains unimplemented.** Revised scope and acceptance criteria below reflect this.

- **2026-09-29, verified by `gh issue list`** (open-issue search for related telemetry work): the still-**2.7%**-style low `pr_number` population rate this issue's own numbers describe is very likely explained by a *different*, already-filed root cause — **#9476** / **#9477** (near-duplicate; both `loom:triage`, unassigned as of this pass), which document that `loom-daemon` has **two independent code paths** emitting `sweep.outcome` for the same `sweep_id` (`observability::collector::terminal_records`, the live event-bus path, which *always* passes `pr_number: None`/`model: None`/every-other-rich-field-absent — see `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs:586-599`; vs. `sweep_registry::outcome_journal::append_outcome_telemetry_journal`, the rich derivation this issue's Verified-correction entry above describes). The dashboard ingests with `INSERT OR IGNORE` against a `(kind, sweep_id)` unique index, so **first writer wins** — and the live/impoverished path is always first, silently discarding the rich journal record for ~87% of sweeps (#9477's own measurement). **This means the rich `pr_number`/`pr_numbers`/`model` derivation already correct per the entry above frequently never reaches the durable store at all** — a data-pipeline/ingest-race bug, not a gap in the derivation logic this issue set out to fix. Fixing that race is out of scope for *this* issue (#9476/#9477 own it); see "Related Open Work" below for how this issue's own AC is narrowed to not duplicate it.

- **2026-09-29, verified by reading `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md`** (lines 444, 483-486, 658): the standalone schema doc is now **stale** relative to the shipped code above — its worked example still shows `"model": "opus"` with no `arm` key and omits `pr_numbers` from the field list, and its `models_used` row explicitly asserts the *old*, now-incorrect semantics: *"`model` names the **dispatched** model, so a sweep that escalated to `claude-opus-5` through the Doctor ladder still reports `model: "sonnet"`."* That sentence is false as of PR #9481. This doc fix is in scope for this issue (see Affected Files).

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29)

### Revised Problem Statement

Two of the three original "Want" items shipped today in PR #9481 (see Verified corrections). The remaining, narrower problem: **Loom roles have no convention for reliably referencing the issue they're implementing on non-final PRs of a plain (non-`loom:epic`) issue.** Today's documented convention (`defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` § "Partial increments (family/epic issues)", lines 738-747) only prescribes a non-closing `Part of #N` / `Contributes to #N` reference for PRs against issues explicitly labeled `loom:epic`/`loom:epic-phase` or whose body declares a family of work. An **ordinary** issue that happens to land through several merged PRs on the same reused `feature/issue-N` branch (Doctor rework, a Judge-rejected-then-fixed cycle that produced a separate PR, a builder that intentionally shipped a first slice without declaring epic status) has **no documented reference requirement at all** for its non-final PRs — this is the actual gap behind the original issue's "19 of 329 sweep-landing PRs missing from `closedByPullRequestsReferences`" and "20 issues landed through >1 merged PR" findings.

### Revised Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` extends the closing-keyword/`Part of #N` convention to cover **any** multi-PR landing of a single issue — not only declared `loom:epic`/`loom:epic-phase` families — and documents a `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer (in addition to, not instead of, `Closes #N` / `Refs #N` or `Part of #N`) as the machine-parseable form a script can grep for without depending on GitHub's closing-keyword parser or prose-phrase matching. State plainly whether this trailer is **required** on every Loom-opened PR or **only** on non-final/slice PRs (the original issue's "Want" implies the latter: `Closes #N` alone suffices for a single-PR landing).
- [ ] `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder.md`'s PR checklist (around line 1308, "PR body uses `Closes #N` ... or `Part of #N` ...") is updated to reference the extended convention.
- [ ] A parser or lint (e.g. a `defaults/scripts/tests/test-*.sh` case, following the existing pattern that already tests `merge-pr.sh`'s `Part of #N` parsing for the code-span pitfall at builder-pr.md:749-762) confirms a `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer round-trips correctly and survives the same code-span/backtick pitfall (#8796) documented for `Part of #N`.
- [ ] Add contract tests for the **already-shipped** derivation logic in `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs` that PR #9481 did not add tests for: (a) `pr_numbers` reflects every sampled PR in first-seen order (not just the latest), (b) `model` resolves to the dominant `tokens_by_model` entry rather than the dispatched model on a mixed-model sweep (e.g. dispatch `sonnet`, transcripts dominated by `claude-opus-5` via a Doctor escalation), and (c) `config["arm"]` is still derived from the *original dispatched* model, not the post-reassignment `model` value. None of `outcome_journal/tests.rs`'s existing `arm`-focused tests (lines ~98-196, Issue #4809) actually exercise the model-swap path together with a populated `tokens_by_model` fixture — verify this gap is real before writing tests (grep the test file for a fixture combining both an `arm`-eligible dispatch model *and* a differently-dominant `tokens_by_model` row; none was found in this pass, but re-check against current `main` since #9481 may have landed sibling tests after this curation).
- [ ] Update `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (worked example at lines 437-481, and the `models_used` row at line 658) to reflect the shipped semantics: `model` is the dominant actually-run model with dispatch as fallback, `config.arm` (when inferred) carries the original dispatch-time arm, and `pr_numbers` is documented as a top-level field alongside `pr_number`.
- [ ] The original "100% resolution for a week of landings" AC is a **measurement**, not a unit test — defer it to a follow-up Auditor/Guide-style check run *after* both this issue's trailer convention *and* #9476/#9477's ingest-race fix have landed and had a week of real PRs to observe (the trailer convention alone cannot be verified end-to-end without the ingest-race fix, since #9476/#9477 shows the derived data frequently never reaches the durable store). Do not attempt to satisfy this AC synchronously in this issue's own PR — state that explicitly in the PR body instead.

### Out of scope for this issue / Related Open Work (absorbed or disregarded, per curation convention)

- **#9476** ("two paths emit sweep.outcome per sweep and INSERT OR IGNORE keeps the impoverished one") and **#9477** ("the collector's sweep.outcome wins the INSERT OR IGNORE race...") — **absorbed**: these two (themselves likely near-duplicates of each other — flagging for a future Curator/Champion pass, not resolved here) are the real root cause of the low `pr_number` population rate this issue measured. This issue's AC is revised above to explicitly NOT attempt fixing the dual-emission/ingest race — that belongs to #9476/#9477. Cross-link both from this issue's implementation PR (`Refs #9476, Refs #9477`) so a reader lands on the right issue for the ingest-side fix.
- **#9441** (disposition) / **#9444** (attempt lineage, rework) / **#9446** (sweep_facts rollup) — **disregarded** for this pass: all three are either already merged (per #9481's "Closed by this PR" table) or track independent fields this issue's remaining scope (PR-body convention + doc fix + contract tests) does not touch.
- **2AMLogic/2am#1610** (storyline landed-size facts) — **disregarded**: cross-repo consumer, no action needed in this repo beyond what's already delivered.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` — extend the `Closes #N` / `Part of #N` convention beyond declared epics/families; document the `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder.md` — update the PR checklist line (~1308) to match.
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal/tests.rs` — add the missing contract tests described above (no production-logic change expected; PR #9481 already shipped the derivation).
- `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` — correct the stale `model`/`arm`/`pr_numbers` documentation (lines ~437-481, ~658).
- Possibly a new `defaults/scripts/tests/test-*.sh` (or an existing one, e.g. a `merge-pr.sh`-adjacent test) for the `Loom-Issue:` trailer's parse/round-trip behavior — check `defaults/scripts/tests/` for the existing `Part of #N` parser test before adding a new file.

All paths above verified present on `origin/main` @ `9135761f6` (2026-09-29).

issues.title: session.summary records in SigNoz are unjoinable: loom.repo is the cwd basename, loom.issue is almost never set, trace_id is empty
issues.body:
## Problem

The `session.summary` records that #8714 G3 introduced are reaching SigNoz but **can't be joined to an issue or a repo**. Live SigNoz, 2026-09-26..29, measured 2026-09-29:

- 4,121 `session.summary` rows (service `loom`) with useful counters: `loom.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}`, `loom.turns`, `loom.wall_ms`, `loom.tool_errors`, plus `session.analysis` `loom.cost_usd`.
- `loom.issue` is present on **1** row.
- `loom.repo` is the **cwd basename**, not the forge slug. Values include worktree/workspace names (`wood-reward`, `the-next-milestone-should-be-a`, `Downloads`, `agent-afb133cdd702752a5`) and only 131 rows are named `issue-N`.
- `trace_id` is empty on every row, so there's no join through the sweep or story trace either.

So per-issue session cost is unrecoverable, even though the counters are exactly what the effort-measurement work (#9429/#9430) needs.

## Want

- `loom.repo` = the `owner/name` forge slug resolved from the session's git remote; omitted if there isn't one. Never a directory name.
- `loom.issue` and `loom.pr_number` filled whenever the session ran inside a sweep or an issue worktree (`.loom/worktrees/issue-N`, `feature/issue-N` branch), or under a role tick that names an issue (see #9231 for role ticks).
- `trace_id` / `parent span` set from the sweep's persisted trace context (the `runtime_usage::join` entry), so a session nests under its `loom.sweep` / story trace.
- Interactive (non-sweep) sessions stay issue-less, but carry `loom.session_kind=interactive` so they're excluded deliberately, not by accident.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Over one day on a fleet host, ≥95% of sweep-originated `session.summary` rows carry `loom.issue` and a slug `loom.repo`, and share the sweep's trace id.
- [ ] A test covers a Superset-style worktree whose directory name has nothing to do with the repo name.

Related: #8714 (G3), #9231, 2AMLogic/2am#1426, #1331.

issues.title: [Epic #9429] story-points: estimate-vs-actual calibration loop
issues.body:
Parent epic: filed separately (Fibonacci story points — size-weighted throughput). Depends on: phases 1–4 (points assigned, telemetry joined, throughput flowing).

## Goal

Close the loop: score assigned story points against actual clean-landing cost, so "did we get the story points right?" has a standing, queryable answer — and the rubric gets revised when it drifts.

This mirrors the ETA accuracy work (`defaults/observability/signoz/eta-queries.sql`, #9289): the estimator differs (Curator vs. heuristic) but the scoring discipline should be the same, including the provenance rule that every view groups by the rubric's revision so a rubric change mid-window shows up as two populations instead of a silent average.

## Work

- [ ] Committed calibration queries: per assigned bucket, the distribution of actual clean-landing tokens / LOC / wall-clock (median, p25–p75); rank correlation between assigned points and each actual measure — do bigger estimates actually cost more?
- [ ] Per-bucket drift: median actual per assigned point — is a "3" really bigger than a "1" by roughly the ratio the rubric claims?
- [ ] Misassignment report: outliers in both directions (a "1" that cost like an "8"; an "8" that landed trivially) — this is what teaches the Curator
- [ ] Revision path: the rubric doc records its revision history; when calibration says a bucket bound is wrong, updating the rubric is a normal, expected change, not an incident
- [ ] Churn accounting: sweeps excluded by the clean-landing filter (repair loops, re-judges) are counted separately, never silently dropped

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One committed query answers "how accurate are assigned points?" for any window
- [ ] Results are separated by the clean-landing filter (churn is excluded from the score but counted)
- [ ] A documented rubric revision has happened at least once as a *result* of calibration output — or the report states the rubric held within stated tolerance

issues.title: bug(sweep-lease): fence/publish/renew pass -R to gh api, so every lease read/write fails when LOOM_REPO is set
issues.body:
## Problem

`defaults/scripts/sweep-lease-fence.sh`, `sweep-lease-publish.sh`, and `sweep-lease-renew.sh` each define `gh_repo_args()`, which emits `-R $LOOM_REPO` when `LOOM_REPO` is set, and splice it into `gh api` calls against `repos/{owner}/{repo}/...`. `gh api` has no `-R`/`--repo` flag:

```
$ gh api -R owner/repo repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/1/comments
unknown shorthand flag: 'R' in -R
```

So on any host that sets `LOOM_REPO`, every lease read and write fails:

- the **fence** hits its "could not fetch comments" fail-open path and lets the push/PR-open through unconditionally;
- **publish** writes no lease comment (exit 2, "best-effort");
- **renew** exits 1 on every cycle.

The test stubs for all five lease suites swallow `-R` (`-R) shift 2 ;;`), which is why this was never caught. Same family as #8263 (`gh api --repo`), which fixed other call sites.

## Fix

Address the repo in the endpoint path (`repos/$LOOM_REPO/...`, falling back to gh's `{owner}/{repo}` placeholder when unset) and drop the `-R` splice from `gh api`. Make the stubs reject `-R` the way real `gh api` does, and add a `LOOM_REPO`-set case per suite that asserts the endpoint path targets that repo.

## Acceptance

- [ ] No `gh api` call under `defaults/scripts/` receives `-R`/`--repo`
- [ ] fence/publish/renew suites cover `LOOM_REPO` set, with stubs that reject `-R`

issues.title: Extend the #8925 blocked-by marker to extract_blocker_refs, dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh, and individual loom:blocked apply sites
issues.body:
## Original Issue

## Context

Follow-up from #8925 ("Blocked PRs have no unblock path"), which added:
- PR enumeration to the unblock sweep (`check_and_unblock_prs()`).
- The structured `<!-- loom:blocked-by=#N -->` marker convention, understood
  by `guide-unblock.md`'s `parse_dependencies()`.
- A doc reconciliation (`label-state-machine.md` now agrees with
  `PARK_LABELS` that `loom:blocked` IS skipped by the work finder).
- Backfilled the marker onto the two of the five named PRs that still
  carried `loom:blocked` with a clear, single, comment-only dependency
  (#8131 → #8136, #8351 → #8354). #8314 and #8853 no longer carry
  `loom:blocked` (already resolved by other automation between filing and
  this pass). #8440's `loom:blocked` is a human quarantine/contamination
  hold (`HUMAN_HOLD`, not a dependency wait) — deliberately left unmarked;
  see the triage comment on that PR.

#8925 scoped the fix to the mechanism (enumeration + marker + doc
reconciliation) and this two-PR backfill. The following adjacent gaps were
identified but are out of scope for that PR:

## 1. `champion-common.md`'s `extract_blocker_refs` does not read the marker

`champion-pr-merge.md`'s "closed issue → find referencing blocked issues"
reverse scan (~L2375-2533) uses its own cross-repo-aware parser
(`extract_blocker_refs`, `champion-common.md`) rather than
`guide-unblock.md`'s `parse_dependencies()`. It was NOT updated by #8925 to
recognize `<!-- loom:blocked-by=#N -->`, so a park recorded only via the new
marker (no matching prose phrase) will be invisible to that reverse scan
even though the primary unblock sweep (`guide-unblock.md`) now reads it.
Bring the two parsers into agreement — either by having
`extract_blocker_refs` also check the marker (mirroring
`parse_dependencies`'s stage-0), or by consolidating on one shared parser if
that is cleaner.

## 2. Curator's `dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh` `named-dependency` path

`curator.md`'s "When Dependencies Complete" section drives
`./.loom/scripts/dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh named-dependency` for the
non-closing-PR dependency case (an issue's own `## Dependencies` checklist).
Consider whether this script should also recognize the structured marker for
consistency, or whether the checklist form is different enough in kind
(explicit task list vs. a single blocker reference) that it should stay
checklist-only. Needs a design decision, not just a mechanical port.

## 3. Individual role sites that apply `loom:blocked` don't mention the marker

#8925 centralized the marker convention in `label-state-machine.md`,
`guide-unblock.md`, and a `.github/labels.yml` comment, but did not touch
the individual apply sites that instruct a role to add the label
(`builder.md`/`builder-complexity.md`'s decomposition-park flow, `doctor.md`,
`curator.md`'s multiple apply sites, `champion-pr-merge.md`'s Capped-PR
park). Consider adding a one-line pointer to the marker convention at each
site (or at least the highest-traffic ones — Doctor stand-downs and
Champion's Capped-PR Recovery Pass) so the convention is discoverable at the
point of use, not only in the reference docs. Mind the markdown-token /
role-prompt-budget ratchets (`.loom/docs/file-size-policy.md`) — several of
these files are already large; a load-gated pointer or a very short addition
is likely needed, not a full rationale block.

## 4. #8440 needs a human decision

PR #8440's `loom:blocked` is a `HUMAN_HOLD` (branch contamination concern
raised by @turian, 2026-09-24) — not a resolvable dependency. It is
correctly excluded from the marker backfill; a human still needs to resolve
the underlying contamination concern directly. Not really "work" for this
follow-up beyond flagging it here for visibility.

## Out of scope for this issue too (already noted in #8925)

- #8922 (missing conflict signal on the `loom:review-requested` path) and
  #8923 (PR/queue latency investigation) are separate, already-filed
  companions from the same original triage pass.
- #8940 (the daemon's #4123 open-PR dispatch guard counting bare `#N`
  mentions) is a distinct root cause in `loom-daemon/src/worktree_ops/gh.rs`,
  unrelated to the unblock-sweep/park-legibility mechanism.

---

## Verified corrections

- **2026-09-28, verified against `origin/main` @ `ad398b26e0f5ce451359a540f3cdc74db1af7527`**: Item 1's premise is **false as of the shipped implementation**. This issue was filed 2026-09-26T15:56:49Z, ~8 hours *before* PR #9146 (the #8925 implementation) merged (2026-09-26T23:53:50Z), and describes an anticipated `<!-- loom:blocked-by=#N -->` marker. The format that actually shipped is different: `<!-- loom:park Blocked by: #N by=<role> at=<RFC3339> reason="..." -->` (`defaults/docs/park-record.md`), and its design deliberately reuses the existing `Blocked by`/`Depends on`/`Requires` phrase vocabulary specifically so no second parser needs updating — see park-record.md's own "The grammar" section: "`guide.md`'s `parse_dependencies`, `dep_recheck::extract`'s `DEPENDENCY_PHRASES`, `warn-operator-gated.sh` and `detect-dependency-cycle.sh` already match `Blocked by`."
  Confirmed by direct extraction test: `champion-common.md`'s `extract_blocker_refs` (unmodified, as it stands on `origin/main`) correctly parses `#8322` out of a sample park-record marker (`<!-- loom:park Blocked by: #8322 by=doctor at=2026-09-19T12:09:00Z reason="needs an architecture ruling" -->`) with zero code change:
  ```
  $ extract_blocker_refs "$BODY_CONTAINING_PARK_RECORD"
  #8322
  ```
  **Item 1 needs no code change and is dropped from this issue's scope** — `extract_blocker_refs` already reads a park record correctly today.
- **2026-09-28, verified against `origin/main`**: Item 2's premise narrows for the same reason. `dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh named-dependency`'s phrase matching (`Blocked by`/`Depends on`/`Requires`/`**Epic**`) also already covers the park record's `Blocked by: #N` text wherever it appears in a body. The only genuinely open question is the narrower one the issue itself already flagged as "a design decision, not a mechanical port": whether the `## Dependencies` **checklist** fingerprint (a distinct, structurally different shape — one bullet per dependency) should special-case a bare park-record marker that isn't written as a checklist bullet. This is optional/exploratory, not required for interop.
- **2026-09-28, verified**: none of the five named apply sites (`curator.md`, `doctor.md`, `builder.md`, `builder-complexity.md`, `champion-pr-merge.md`) reference `park-record.md` or the park-record convention on `origin/main` today — item 3's premise stands, unchanged.
- **2026-09-28, verified**: PR #8440 (item 4) is still open, still carrying `loom:blocked` as a human hold (unchanged since this issue was filed) — no action needed here beyond what's already noted.

## Curator Enhancement

### Problem Statement (revised scope)

This issue's original item 1 (porting `extract_blocker_refs` to recognize a new marker) is now moot: the park-record format that actually shipped in #8925/PR #9146 deliberately reuses the `Blocked by: #N` phrase already recognized by every existing parser in the fleet, so no port is needed there. The issue's remaining, still-valid scope is:

1. **(Required)** Add a short pointer to `defaults/docs/park-record.md` at the role-prompt sites that instruct applying `loom:blocked` for a dependency wait, so the convention is discoverable at the point of use rather than only in the reference doc.
2. **(Optional, needs a design decision — do not block on this)** Decide whether `dep-recheck-fingerprint.sh named-dependency`'s `## Dependencies`-checklist fingerprint should also special-case a park-record marker that isn't written as a checklist bullet, or whether the checklist form is different enough in kind that it should stay as-is.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `curator.md` gains a one-line pointer to `defaults/docs/park-record.md` at its `loom:blocked`-apply sites (currently lines ~751, ~1034, ~1406 on `origin/main` — re-verify line numbers at implementation time, this file changes often).
- [ ] `builder.md` gains the same pointer at its decomposition-park `loom:blocked`-apply sites (currently lines ~307, ~310, ~798, ~811, ~823, ~985).

issues.title: noopCooldown is host-local (peer host re-dispatches inside the window), and the same release is also counted as a prless failure
issues.body:
## Problem

Two distinct defects in the accounting of a single no-op release, both observed
in one `loom-daemon` log for one issue, and both of which let a `noopCooldown`
window be ignored.

### 1. `noopCooldown` is host-local, so a peer host re-dispatches inside the window

`autonomous.workFinder.noopCooldown.cooldownSecs` defaults to 3600 and is
recorded into the recording host's own registry/`activity.db`. On a two-host
fleet sharing one repo, the peer host has no knowledge of it and re-offers the
candidate immediately.

Evidence — `~/.loom/daemon.log` on `loom-worker-*`, repo `2AMLogic/llm-cim`,
issue #1, 2026-09-25:

```
[06:38:29.656] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 no-op release recorded via IPC
    (RecordNoopRelease, #6670): epic tracking container, no direct buildable work…
[06:38:29.656] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 no-op-release cooldown armed —
    1 consecutive no-op release(s), next dispatch allowed in 3600s (#6670)
```

The issue's forge timeline then shows it re-claimed (`loom:issue` →
`loom:building`) at **06:41:45Z** — 196 s into a 3600 s cooldown — by a sweep on
the other host, and again at 10:34:18Z and 11:29:47Z. The recording host itself
honoured the window correctly and never re-dispatched; only the peer did.

This is the same class of problem `record-noop-release.sh`'s `--workspace-root`
default fixed for multi-*workspace* daemons (#6957) — one hop further out: the
cooldown is invisible across *hosts*, so on any multi-host fleet the effective
suppression is "one host stops trying" rather than "the fleet stops trying". The
lease-record mechanism (#6179) already establishes a forge-backed,
cross-host-readable channel for exactly this kind of shared claim state.

### 2. The same release is also counted as a `prless` **failure**

Immediately after the no-op cooldown was armed, the daemon classified the same
release as a PR-less failure:

```
[06:39:28.067] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 dispatch backoff armed — 1 consecutive
    failed dispatch(es), next attempt allowed in 60s (#4485; cause=Generic)
[06:39:28.067] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 insta-crashed (1/3 consecutive, <60s,
    no checkpoint) (#3939)
[06:39:28.067] [WARN] sweep_registry: issue #1 released without a pull request
    (1/3 consecutive) — next dispatch allowed in 300s (#7972). Failure: sweep exited 0
    after 213s without opening a pull request, without a phase checkpoint, and without
    a `.no-changes-needed` marker
```

So one release simultaneously armed a 3600 s no-op cooldown **and** a 300 s
prless-retry window and an insta-crash strike. The two paths disagree about what
happened, and the *shorter* window is the one whose semantics are wrong for this
outcome.

The stated discriminator is the `.no-changes-needed` marker, and the daemon
reports it absent — yet the orchestrator clearly took the no-op path (it issued
`RecordNoopRelease`). Either the sweep records the no-op without writing the
marker `sweep.md` step 1 reads from, or the daemon looks for the marker somewhere
the sweep did not write it (e.g. the wrong worktree root, or after the worktree
was reaped). Whichever it is, a self-reported no-op should not also accumulate
insta-crash strikes toward quarantine.

## Suggested fix

1. Make a no-op cooldown visible fleet-wide, not just host-locally — e.g. publish
   it alongside the lease record (#6179) or via the peer-coordination channel the
   registry already uses to re-advertise live peer claims (#4431), so a peer host
   yields the same way it yields to a fresh peer lease.
2. Make the no-op and prless-failure classifications mutually exclusive for one
   release: if `RecordNoopRelease` arrived for the issue in this dispatch, suppress
   the prless-failure/insta-crash accounting instead of arming both. Separately,
   reconcile the marker check with whatever the sweep actually writes, so the
   discriminator the code relies on is the one the orchestrator produces.

Context: `2AMLogic/llm-cim#105` (a ~12-session thrash loop on `loom:epic`
containers). Related: #8881 (Mode A/B pre-flight has no `loom:epic` skip rule),
#8911 (find-work tiers 1/2 bypass the configured skip labels).

issues.title: Flaky test: role_runner shrinking_the_ring… fails on its random-draw precondition (OTLP job only, same commit passes elsewhere)
issues.body:
## Symptom

`role_runner::tests::shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor`
fails non-deterministically on its **precondition** assert, not on the behaviour it
exists to pin:

```
thread 'role_runner::tests::shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor'
panicked at loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs:5121:5
```

`loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs:5121` is:

```rust
assert!(!orphaned.is_empty(), "precondition: host 1 must have owned something to orphan");
```

## Evidence it is non-deterministic, not a real regression

Observed on PR #8662 at head `3bcd26eb2`, where **two jobs of the same CI run, on the
same commit, disagreed**:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| Rust Unit Tests (`process-per-test`) | 8123 run, **8123 passed**, 0 failed |
| Rust OTLP Feature Build & Test | 8190 run, 8189 passed, **1 failed** (this test) |

Run: https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/actions/runs/35776125577

The same job passed on that branch's base commit (`039725289`) on `main`
(run `35771235363`). PR #8662 touches only `.github/workflows/release.yml`,
`defaults/docs/release-cadence.md` and `loom-daemon/src/release_resolve/` — nothing
that can reach `role_runner`.

## Likely cause

The test is `#[serial]` and mutates global shard state via `ShardEnvGuard`, then builds
a 12-workspace fleet of `tempfile::TempDir`s and asserts that a 2-shard ring leaves at
least one of them **not** owned by host 0. Ownership is derived from the workspace path,
which is a randomly-named temp directory — so the precondition is a statement about a
random draw, and it is also exposed to whatever global env/shard state a neighbouring
serial test left behind. Both are enough to make the *precondition* (not the assertion
under test) fail occasionally.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the precondition deterministic rather than drawn: use fixed, known workspace paths
(or seed/choose paths until both shards are non-empty) so the test asserts the
reassignment behaviour it is named for, and never fails on the setup. Failing that,
assert the ring split up front and skip/retry the draw rather than panicking.

## Impact

A red `Rust OTLP Feature Build & Test` on healthy PRs — exactly the false red
`.loom/docs/ci-principles.md` calls out, and it blocks merges until someone
re-runs the job by hand.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Problem statement, evidence (two CI jobs on the same commit disagreeing), root-cause analysis, and suggested fix direction are already clear and well-argued. Verified the test exists exactly as cited: `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs:5110` (`shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor`), with the precondition assert at line 5121 matching the panic message verbatim. `ShardEnvGuard` (line 4928) and the `#[serial]` attribute are present as described. `gh run view 35776125577` confirms the linked CI run's conclusion is `failure`. Duplicate check surfaced only unrelated cross-references (PR #8662, the same PR this issue's own evidence table cites — absorbed; and #8681, an unrelated docs-parity issue that only cross-references this one as an example of a different auto-label pattern — disregarded as out of scope).

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor`'s precondition (`orphaned` must be non-empty) can no longer fail on an unlucky random draw — either by using fixed/deterministic workspace paths, or by choosing/seeding paths until the ring split is guaranteed non-trivial before asserting.
- [ ] The behavior under test (reassignment of the departed host's slice to the survivor) is still exercised and still fails if that behavior regresses — the fix must not weaken the test into a tautology.
- [ ] The fix does not depend on evaluation order or leftover state from a neighboring `#[serial]` test (per the issue's own "Likely cause" section).
- [ ] Re-run the affected job (`Rust OTLP Feature Build & Test`) or an equivalent repeated-run harness enough times to gain confidence the flake is gone (a single green run does not prove non-determinism is fixed).

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs` — the test itself (starts at line 5110), and `enabled_workspace()`/`ShardEnvGuard` (line 4928) if the fix changes how workspace paths or shard state are set up.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: the fixed test passes deterministically; run it repeatedly (e.g. `cargo test --workspace shrinking_the_ring -- --test-threads=1` in a loop, or via any existing flake-detection harness) to confirm the precondition no longer depends on a random draw.
- [ ] Automated tests: the full `role_runner::tests` module still passes under both the default and OTLP feature builds.
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm the fixed assertion still fails if the reassignment behavior itself is deliberately broken (i.e. the test still tests what it's named for).

<!-- loom:complexity=mechanical -->

Why `mechanical`, not `routine`: this is a self-contained test-only fix (no production code path changes) with an unambiguous verification method — a mistake is obvious from re-reading the diff, and correctness is directly checkable by running the test repeatedly.
