issues.title: Codex session-exec: host timeout leaves the container worker running
issues.body:
## Problem

Found during the scheduled #4496 Milestone-1 preflight on robb-studio, 2026-09-23 16:54 UTC. **A session-managed Codex worker survives termination of its host adapter process group.** The daemon can report a role timeout and release its concurrency slot while the container-side invocation is still running. This prevents #4496 from relying on its bounded time/spend window or cleanup/restart evidence.

Split out of #4496 per its prerequisite-defect scope guard; this belongs to the #6896/#6926 persistent session-exec path. No live Codex model call or production credential was used to reproduce it.

## Verified evidence

- Running host daemon: `0.19.316`, commit `82128525b094d5971adc844dc9befdb98fe3163a`.
- Source checked: `a38da01d5fb04d4cb6047126c4e75902be41df0c`; `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` and `loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs` are identical to the running daemon commit.
- Disposable container image ID: `sha256:d40047d2b948ba38cc1eaaf4ce2e9c578c47afeca4d1b3a8efd81148816dc868` (the image used by the current managed sessions).
- Launched the actual `spawn-codex.sh` with `LOOM_ROLE=curator`, `LOOM_CODEX_SANDBOX=read-only`, a synthetic profile and session marker, and a fake `codex` executable that writes its PID then `exec sleep 300`.
- The container had networking disabled and only the synthetic fixture mounted read-only. No production profile, GitHub config, or token directory was mounted.
- Sent SIGTERM to the host adapter's process group, matching `role_runner::terminate_timed_out`; host adapter exited **-15**. Container worker PID **8 remained alive**. A subsequent host-group SIGKILL attempt also left the container worker alive.
- Removed the disposable container and fixture afterward. No production configuration or account health state was changed.

The fake worker proves that host cancellation does not guarantee container invocation termination. It does not claim that a live Codex invocation was deliberately orphaned.

## Relevant code

- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh`: `CODEX_INVOKE` builds an attached `docker exec`; the capture path runs it through `tee`. Its only trap removes the temporary stderr file. There is no container-side per-invocation cancellation handshake.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs::terminate_timed_out`: signals the host process group, waits/reaps, and records the timeout. That process group does not contain the container-side worker.
- Preserve the #6896 invariant: the long-lived account session container and canonical authentication store survive individual invocations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A timed-out/cancelled session-exec invocation terminates its own container-side worker and descendants within a documented grace period, before the caller reports cleanup complete or makes the slot available again.
- [ ] Invocation ownership is explicit and collision-safe. Cancellation cannot kill another invocation, the interactive account session, container init, or the entire persistent session container. Do not use broad `pkill codex`/account-wide kills.
- [ ] Cover TERM and escalation, normal completion, launch failure, cancellation/startup races, and a disconnected/crashed host launcher. State the recovery guarantee for host SIGKILL/daemon restart; do not leave a claim of bounded execution dependent only on an EXIT trap that SIGKILL cannot run.
- [ ] Preserve normal stdout/stderr, exit status, transcript/session attribution, terminal feedback, account selection and refresh-in-place behavior; do not copy credentials or weaken hook/sandbox checks.
- [ ] Bare-metal Codex dispatch remains unaffected.
- [ ] Add a deterministic regression using a fake worker. Include a disposable real-Docker smoke that verifies the intended worker and descendants are gone while a sibling invocation and the session container remain alive. No model spend or production credentials required.
- [ ] Re-run the focused Codex adapter/session tests and relevant Rust timeout tests; return the evidence to #4496 so its live plan can resume.

## Existing checks

Current focused mock suites pass **494/494** assertions (`test-spawn-codex.sh` 267, session-exec 10, capability checker 27, hook provisioning 69, bridge 121). They do not cover this host/container cancellation boundary. The exact daemon commit also has green Rust unit tests, Rust lint/build, and Codex Adapter Smoke in [CI run 35870272608](https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/actions/runs/35870272608).

## Minimal transport reproduction

This reduced example demonstrates the Docker boundary behind the full adapter reproduction above. Use a locally available disposable shell-capable image; mount no credentials. The outer `finally` removes only this test container.

```python
import os, signal, subprocess, time, uuid
name = "loom-cancel-probe-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
image = "sha256:d40047d2b948ba38cc1eaaf4ce2e9c578c47afeca4d1b3a8efd81148816dc868"
p = None
try:
    subprocess.run(["docker", "run", "-d", "--name", name, "--network", "none",
                    "--entrypoint", "/bin/sh", image, "-c", "exec sleep 600"], check=True)
    p = subprocess.Popen(["docker", "exec", name, "/bin/sh", "-c",
                          "echo $$ > /tmp/probe.pid; exec sleep 300"], start_new_session=True)
    for _ in range(50):
        r = subprocess.run(["docker", "exec", name, "cat", "/tmp/probe.pid"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode == 0:
            break
        time.sleep(0.1)
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("probe did not start")
    pid = str(int(r.stdout.strip()))
    os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    p.wait(timeout=10)
    alive = subprocess.run(["docker", "exec", name, "/bin/sh", "-c", "kill -0 " + pid])
    print("container worker survived:", alive.returncode == 0)  # observed True
finally:
    if p is not None and p.poll() is None:
        os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        p.wait(timeout=10)
    subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", name], check=False)
```

## Curator assessment — 2026-09-23

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

Curating this issue per user request through the in-session sweep. Keep this as one coherent cancellation fix: splitting ownership, cancellation and abrupt-death recovery into separately releasable changes would leave the bounded-execution claim unsafe. Complexity is **complex** because signal races and shared-container process ownership can escape ordinary happy-path tests. A narrow supervisor plus adapter wiring and regression tests is the intended scope; this is not a session-container redesign.

Verified against `origin/main` **`0d0a5e6b71d3a7ffafd6764c4322a6de05e7936a`** (fetched 2026-09-23):

- `git show origin/main:defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` at lines 987–1056 shows a direct attached `docker exec`, the only trap deleting the stderr temporary file, and the stderr `tee` capture pipeline. The no-capture path also directly execs the transport. The original reproduction therefore still targets the current implementation.
- `git show origin/main:loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs` at lines 223 and 1405–1432 shows a **5-second** TERM grace and an immediate break once the host child exits. A wrapper that exits before container cleanup is acknowledged cannot satisfy the existing timeout/slot-release contract.
- `git show origin/main:loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper/container_stop.rs` at lines 1–49 shows that #8435 addresses cancellation of **ephemeral sweep containers** through whole-container stop/kill. It is related precedent, not a solution for this persistent per-account container. Do not apply its whole-container teardown to this path.
- `check-duplicate.sh --include-merged-prs --issue 8773` reported only related open #4496; that issue explicitly delegates this prerequisite defect here. `premise-check.sh --issue 8773` returned `VERDICT=out-of-scope`, exit 0.

## Implementation guidance and scope boundaries

- Establish unique per-invocation ownership **before** starting Codex, with a container-side supervisor capable of terminating/reaping that invocation's process tree. Do not key cancellation solely by a reusable PID, account name, role name or shared container name. Demonstrate isolation from a concurrent sibling in the same container. Any metadata must contain identifiers only, never prompts, auth contents or provider credentials.
- Prefer a small Rust-owned supervision/transport component with thin adapter integration, consistent with ADR-0018 and the shell budget. The exact mechanism remains Builder's choice; a host EXIT/TERM trap alone cannot handle SIGKILL. A container-side lease/watchdog or equivalent fail-closed lifetime mechanism needs an explicit bounded recovery contract.
- Separate two guarantees: **cooperative timeout/cancellation** waits for acknowledged worker/descendant cleanup before the launcher exits and the caller releases its slot; **abrupt host SIGKILL/disconnect/restart** has a documented maximum recovery delay. Explain any transient overlap and how caller/restart behavior avoids falsely claiming cleanup complete. Do not promise instantaneous cleanup after an uncatchable signal. Budget the supervisor grace against the caller's 5-second escalation or adjust the narrow caller handshake as needed.
- Cover headless captured and no-capture execution paths. Preserve the existing interactive login/session surface and bare-metal dispatch behavior. Preserve stdout/stderr separation, exit status, transcript/session attribution, account feedback, account selection, hook/sandbox enforcement and refresh-in-place.
- Existing persistent session images can predate the new host binary. If the design requires a new in-container executable, feature/version-check it and fail closed with a precise update prerequisite; never silently revert to unsupervised `docker exec`. Record whether the fix works with the currently deployed image or requires a session-image rollout before #4496 resumes. No production rollout is part of this issue's test run.
- Scope excludes changes to account provisioning/authentication, runtime admission or capability claims, routing/scheduled-role defaults, a general remote-job service, and #4496's live model canary. The synthetic regression can satisfy this issue without production credentials or model calls.

## Affected Files

Existing paths verified with `git ls-tree -r origin/main --name-only` at the commit above:

- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` — integrate supervised session invocation while retaining current adapter contracts. Edit canonical source, not installed mirrors.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-spawn-codex-session-exec.sh` — retain/update session argv, workdir and environment contract coverage.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-spawn-codex.sh` — existing contract suite to re-run; avoid growth in this oversized file, using a focused sibling test when needed.
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/mod.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/lib.rs` — narrow wiring if introducing a Rust supervision subcommand/module (new sibling implementation/test files are expected as needed, not missing prerequisites).
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs` — verify timeout/cleanup ordering; modify only if the selected handshake requires it, respecting file-size ratchets.
- `docker/session/README.md` — document per-invocation cancellation, grace/recovery bounds and image compatibility/update prerequisite.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/ci-wired.txt` — register any new shell-subject regression in the appropriate existing CI tier; any new shell file also needs its allowed test/stub category in `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt`.

Reference only: `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper/container_stop.rs` demonstrates the distinct ephemeral-container cancellation contract; it is not a mandate to refactor that path.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Add deterministic fake-worker coverage that fails against the current adapter and proves normal completion/exit-code/stdout/stderr preservation, worker launch failure, TERM, TERM-resistant escalation, cancellation before/during startup, and lost/killed host launcher. Assert ownership cannot target container init or sibling invocations, including stale invocation metadata/PID reuse handling where applicable.
- [ ] Exercise the **actual adapter** against a disposable, network-disabled Docker container with synthetic profile metadata and no production mounts/model calls. Run two uniquely identifiable fake workers concurrently; include a descendant process and a TERM-resistant case. After cancellation, prove the targeted worker and descendants are gone, while the sibling and persistent container remain alive. Cover abrupt host SIGKILL within the documented recovery bound. Always clean up only this test's disposable container.
- [ ] Prove cooperative cleanup ordering through the role-runner timeout path or an equivalent focused integration harness: worker/descendant cleanup must precede timeout completion/slot reuse, not merely occur eventually after the host child is reaped.
- [ ] Re-run `test-spawn-codex.sh`, `test-spawn-codex-session-exec.sh`, `test-check-runtime-capabilities.sh`, `test-provision-codex-hooks.sh`, `test-guard-codex-bridge.sh`, and relevant Rust role-runner timeout/supervisor tests. Run required lint, shell-budget/file-size and build gates for the changed surfaces.
- [ ] Record exact tested commit, disposable image ID, supervisor/worker exit observations and measured grace/recovery bound in the PR. Return the result and any required image-rollout prerequisite to #4496. Do not call the live canary ready before that prerequisite is verified.

issues.title: Decide whether worktree.sh's stale-reset liveness veto should use the widened (#7466) any-open-fd signal
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Surfaced during Judge review of #9040 (#8195 slice 6).

`loom-daemon/src/worktree_cli/reset.rs`'s liveness rung reaches
`worktree_ops::safety::find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory`, the **cwd-only**
signal the retired shell used. The sibling
`find_processes_using_directory` has matched **any open file descriptor** under
the directory since #7466; the two now share one `/proc` walk and one `lsof`
parse behind a `cwd_only` flag, so this is a single boolean, not two
implementations.

Slice 6 deliberately did **not** widen it — a port is not the place to change a
guard's trigger, and widening is not free here: a refusal costs a worktree
handed to the next Builder still carrying drift (the #6291 class), whereas the
#7466 caller (the watchdog's `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fd`) takes false
positives to eliminate missed detection of untracked build output. That
reasoning is recorded at the function.

The doc comment in `safety.rs` says the widening "is filed separately rather
than smuggled in here", but no such issue exists — this is that issue. Nothing
is broken; this is a behaviour question to answer with its own evidence.

Scope to decide:
- Does the stale-worktree reset path (which never runs `git clean`) want the
  wider any-open-fd signal, or is cwd-only correct for it?
- If widened: add a differential/unit scenario with an open-FD-but-cwd-elsewhere
  holder. `loom-daemon/tests/worktree_reset_differential.rs`'s three liveness
  scenarios currently spawn cwd holders only, so a widening would not be caught
  by that harness as written.
- If cwd-only is confirmed correct: correct the "filed separately" wording in
  `find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory`'s doc comment to point here (or to the
  decision), so the claim is verifiable.

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Gather evidence for the tradeoff named in `find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory`'s doc comment (`loom-daemon/src/worktree_ops/safety.rs`, as of `eeb7def8`, 2026-09-27): how often the #6291 class (a worktree handed to the next Builder still carrying drift, because reset was refused) actually occurs, vs. how often a process holds an open FD under a stale-looking worktree without its cwd being there.
- [ ] Decide: does `worktree.sh`'s stale-worktree reset path (the veto in `loom-daemon/src/worktree_cli/reset.rs` in front of a `git reset --hard` that never runs `git clean`) widen to the any-open-fd signal, or stay cwd-only?
- [ ] Record the decision and its rationale at `find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory`'s doc comment, replacing the stale "is filed separately rather than smuggled in here" sentence with a concrete pointer to this issue's resolution (whichever way it goes).
- [ ] If widened: route the reset-path veto through the any-open-fd signal (`find_processes_using_directory`, or a `cwd_only=false` call into the shared probe) instead of `find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory`, and add a differential scenario to `worktree_reset_differential.rs`'s corpus with a holder whose open FD is under the worktree but whose cwd is elsewhere — the existing three scenarios (root cwd, 3-levels-deep cwd, cwd with spaces, per that file's own comment) are all cwd holders and would not catch this widening if it silently regressed.
- [ ] If kept cwd-only: no functional change to either `safety.rs` function or the reset-path call site — only the doc-comment correction above.

### Implementation Guidance

Both signals already share one `/proc` walk and one `lsof` parse behind a `cwd_only: bool` parameter (`find_processes_proc`/`find_processes_lsof` in `safety.rs`) — #7466 unified the implementation, so whichever way this is decided, it is a call-site change (which function/flag the reset path invokes), not new detection logic.

The tradeoff is already stated at the function (`safety.rs`, `find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory` doc comment, as of `eeb7def8`):
- `find_processes_using_directory` (any open FD) gates the watchdog's `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fd` mid-build recovery, where a false negative destroys a live writer's untracked build output — it takes false positives on purpose.
- `find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory` (cwd only) gates the stale-worktree reset path, which never runs `git clean`; its refusal costs a worktree handed to the next Builder still carrying drift (the #6291 class) — false positives are not free here.

This is a genuine engineering tradeoff resolvable by evidence (incident history, or a reasoned judgment call documented at the function), not a business/authority decision — routine for Builder to resolve and record, per this repo's "Issues Are Suggestions" autonomy model.

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/worktree_ops/safety.rs` - `find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory` doc comment (always); function body only if widening the reset-path veto
- `loom-daemon/src/worktree_cli/reset.rs` - the liveness veto call site (currently `safety::find_processes_with_cwd_in_directory`), only if widening
- `loom-daemon/tests/worktree_reset_differential.rs` - scenario corpus, add an FD-elsewhere-but-cwd-outside scenario only if widening

### Test Plan

- [ ] Manual verification: N/A — this is a guard-behavior decision verified by the differential test harness, not a user-facing feature
- [ ] Automated tests: if widening, add and pass a new `worktree_reset_differential.rs` corpus scenario with an open-FD-but-cwd-elsewhere holder; if staying cwd-only, the existing three scenarios (root cwd, 3-levels-deep, cwd-with-spaces) must continue to pass unchanged
- [ ] Edge cases: confirm `cargo test -p loom-daemon worktree_reset_differential` and the existing `safety.rs` unit tests (e.g. `find_processes_lsof_result_is_a_superset_of_the_cwd_only_parser`) still pass after the change

issues.title: ci_telemetry tests: env_overrides_config races config_defaults_are_flags_off_and_config_values_resolve
issues.body:
## What

\`loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/tests.rs\` has a flaky test-isolation bug, unrelated to any specific feature — found incidentally while verifying #8850.

\`env_overrides_config\` (around line 1157) mutates process-wide environment variables (\`std::env::set_var(INTERVAL_SECS_ENV, "45")\` and others) to test env-override precedence in \`resolve()\`, then removes them at the end of the test body. It is marked \`#[serial_test::serial]\`, which only serializes it against *other* \`#[serial]\`-marked tests.

\`config_defaults_are_flags_off_and_config_values_resolve\` (around line 1096) calls \`resolve(&CiTelemetryConfig::default())\` and asserts \`resolved.interval_secs == DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECS\` (120) — but it is **not** marked \`#[serial]\`. Rust's default test runner runs tests in parallel across threads within the same process, so this test can observe \`env_overrides_config\`'s env vars mid-mutation, causing a flaky failure (observed: \`left: 45, right: 120\`).

## Evidence

Observed directly in CI-equivalent local run (\`cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib ci_telemetry\`, default parallel threads):

\`\`\`
---- ci_telemetry::tests::config_defaults_are_flags_off_and_config_values_resolve stdout ----
thread 'ci_telemetry::tests::config_defaults_are_flags_off_and_config_values_resolve' panicked at loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/tests.rs:1100:5:
assertion \`left == right\` failed
  left: 45
 right: 120
\`\`\`

\`45\` is exactly the value \`env_overrides_config\` sets for \`LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL_SECS\` before removing it — confirming the race.

## Proposed fix

Add \`#[serial_test::serial]\` to every test in this module that calls \`resolve()\` (or otherwise reads the env vars \`env_overrides_config\` mutates), so they're all serialized against each other. \`config_defaults_are_flags_off_and_config_values_resolve\` and likely a couple of sibling config-resolution tests are the ones missing the marker — an audit of every test that reads \`ENABLED_ENV\`/\`ORG_ENV\`/\`INTERVAL_SECS_ENV\`/\`LOG_CAPTURE_ENABLED_ENV\`/\`LOG_CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES_ENV\` (directly or via \`resolve()\`) is the concrete scope.

## Not in scope for #8850

This is pre-existing and unrelated to #8850's credential-rejection change — neither the test nor the \`resolve()\` code path it exercises is touched by that PR.

issues.title: Fold forge_cached_view's self-contained ETag store into the shared forge_listing primitives (after #9261)
issues.body:
Follow-up to #9254 (single-object `gh issue view` / `gh pr view` ETag reads).

## Problem

#9254 was built before "PR A" (#9251 / #9252, tracked by PR #9261) landed. PR A moves the private disk-ETag primitives in `loom-daemon/src/forge_listing.rs` (`disk_cache_dir`, `disk_cache_path`, `DiskEntry` / `read_disk_entry` / `write_disk_entry`, `fetch_listing_once`) into a shared `pub(crate)` module. Because it had not merged, #9254 took the curator-sanctioned fallback and shipped a **minimal self-contained store** inside `loom-daemon/src/forge_cached_view.rs` (cache dir, `view-*` entry paths, `DiskEntry`, atomic write, 7-day age pruning, credential-identity keying, and a conditional `gh api --include` fetch).

That leaves two copies of the same ETag-store logic.

## Ask

Once #9261 merges:

- Replace the self-contained store in `forge_cached_view.rs` with the shared primitives from PR A. Keep the `view-` filename prefix, `--invalidate [N]` semantics, and the age-based pruning (or move pruning into the shared store).
- Record each view call (200 / 304, `core` pool) through PR A's stats sink, so view reads show up in the same accounting as the listing reads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `forge_cached_view.rs` has no private `DiskEntry` / `read_entry` / `write_entry` / `cache_dir`; it uses the shared module.
- [ ] View 200/304 calls are recorded via the shared stats sink.
- [ ] Existing `forge_cached_view` unit tests and `defaults/scripts/tests/test-gh-cached.sh` still pass.

Depends on #9261. Refs #9254, #9243.

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `83abe1f97`)

### Dependency status
The stated dependency is satisfied: PR #9261 **merged 2026-09-28T17:05Z** (`gh pr view 9261` → MERGED). The shared module is `loom-daemon/src/forge_etag_store.rs` (511 lines, on `origin/main`), which exposes `disk_cache_dir`, `disk_cache_path`, `entry_path_in`, `DiskEntry`, `read_disk_entry`, `write_disk_entry`, `private_dir`, `Target`/`resolve_target`, `repo_scope`, `credential_scope`, `cache_key`, and `fetch_conditional(caller, gh_bin, cwd, &Target, url, etag)`. Note the primitives are no longer in `forge_listing.rs` (which now does `use crate::forge_etag_store as store`), so read the ACs' "shared module" as `forge_etag_store`.

### Problem Statement
`forge_cached_view.rs` still carries its own copy of the store (`cache_dir` L327, `credential_identity` L363, `entry_path` L382, `DiskEntry` L394, `read_entry`/`write_entry`, and a private `fetch_conditional` L466 that shells out to `gh api --include` itself). Line numbers as of `83abe1f97` — re-check before relying on them. Beyond duplication, the private copy has real gaps versus the shared store: it reads entries with no `private_dir` ownership/permission check (the shared `read_disk_entry` refuses a planted `(etag, body)` in a directory another local user could write), writes with default file modes, and never records its calls in `forge_call_stats`, so view reads are invisible to `loom-daemon status`.

### Implementation Guidance (routine; approach checked by reading code, not yet compiled)
1. **Filename prefix needs a parameter.** `forge_etag_store::entry_path_in` hardcodes `listing-{hash}.json` (L80). View entries are `view-{entity}-{number}-{hash}.json`, and `invalidate` (by number) and `prune_stale` depend on that shape. Add a prefix-taking variant (e.g. `entry_path_with_prefix(dir, prefix, key)`, with `entry_path_in` delegating to it with `"listing-"`) rather than changing listing filenames. The AC's "keep the `view-` filename prefix" is what forces this.
2. **Replace, don't wrap:** delete `DiskEntry`, `read_entry`, `write_entry`, `cache_dir`, `entry_path`, `repo_scope`, `credential_identity` and the private `fetch_conditional`; use `store::disk_cache_dir()`, `store::read_disk_entry`/`write_disk_entry`, `store::resolve_target`/`cache_key`, and `store::fetch_conditional("forge_cached_view", …)`.
3. **Keep in the view module:** `VIEW_PREFIX`, `view_files`, `invalidate`, `prune_stale`/`VIEW_ENTRY_MAX_AGE` (the AC allows either keeping it or moving it into the shared store; keeping it is the smaller diff — the listing store has no age pruning I could find, not exhaustively verified).
4. **Behaviour deltas to watch:** (a) shared `fetch_conditional` adds `--hostname` from `Target.host`; the private one never did — intended for non-github.com remotes, but confirm the `test-gh-cached.sh` stub gh tolerates the extra arg; (b) cache keys change (shared `cache_key` vs the local `repo_scope|credential_identity|url` format), so existing on-disk `view-*` entries are simply orphaned and age out via `prune_stale` — one `200` per hot entry, acceptable; (c) shared `fetch_conditional` returns `Result`, whereas the view path treats any failure as "decline" (`None`) — map errors to `None`.
5. **Stats:** `fetch_conditional` already calls `record_gh_api(caller, …)`, so passing a distinct `&'static str` caller (suggested `"forge_cached_view"`) satisfies the stats AC. Not verified: whether `forge_call_stats` or `status`/dashboard enumerate callers in a fixed list that would need the new name added — grep for it during implementation.

### Affected Files
- `loom-daemon/src/forge_cached_view.rs` — remove private store; call shared primitives; update unit tests (they call the private `fetch_conditional(&gh, cwd, dir, entity, n, repo)` at L789/L850 and `invalidate`/`prune`)
- `loom-daemon/src/forge_etag_store.rs` — add prefix-parameterized entry-path helper (listing behaviour unchanged)
- `loom-daemon/src/forge_call_stats.rs` — only if a caller allow-list exists (unverified)
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-gh-cached.sh` — should pass unchanged; edit only if the stub rejects `--hostname`

### Test Plan
- [ ] Automated: existing `forge_cached_view` unit tests (updated for the new signatures) pass; `git grep -nE 'struct DiskEntry|fn read_entry|fn write_entry|fn cache_dir' loom-daemon/src/forge_cached_view.rs` returns nothing.
- [ ] Automated: new test that a view `200` then `304` produces one `Ok` and one `NotModified` record for caller `forge_cached_view` in `forge_call_stats` (mirror `forge_call_stats_tests.rs`).
- [ ] Automated: `--invalidate 42` and `--invalidate` still drop only `view-*` entries and leave `listing-*` untouched (existing test at ~L813–835 covers this shape).
- [ ] Automated: an entry in a group/world-writable cache dir is not served (inherited from `read_disk_entry`; one regression test is enough).
- [ ] Shell: `defaults/scripts/tests/test-gh-cached.sh` passes.

issues.title: prless-retry hold posts a comment but usually does not apply loom:blocked, so dispatch continues — 2,641 claims across 55 issues
issues.body:
## Summary

`#7972`'s `loom:prless-retry` hold **posts its comment without applying `loom:blocked` on most firings**, so it does not park the issue and dispatch continues. Combined with per-host claim counters across four dispatch hosts, this reproduces `#7972`'s own failure shape ("14 claims, 55 label events, 4 hours, zero PRs") at fleet scale, the day after `#7972` closed.

Measured across the fleet on 2026-09-27: **55 open `loom:blocked` issues carrying a prless-retry hold, 2,641 lease claims, 174 hold comments.**

## The defect, in one timeline

`rjwalters/loom#8812`, 2026-09-24 — lease/hold comments in time order, against that issue's `loom:blocked` label events:

```
06:33  claim  host-d0749b00
06:43  claim  host-e1d4c843
06:57  claim  host-d0749b00
06:59  HOLD COMMENT POSTED          <- 3 claims reached
07:00  claim  host-d9142cf3         <- claimed again 45s after the hold
07:02  claim  host-34209a6e
07:06  claim  host-e1d4c843
07:07  HOLD COMMENT POSTED
07:12  claim  host-d9142cf3
07:14  HOLD COMMENT POSTED
07:15  claim  host-34209a6e
07:17  HOLD COMMENT POSTED
07:21  claim  host-e1d4c843
07:23  HOLD COMMENT POSTED
```

`loom:blocked` label events on that issue over the same window: **`labeled` ×1 (at 07:23:03), `unlabeled` ×0.**

So the first **four** holds posted a comment and applied no label. `loom:blocked` is what `PARK_LABELS` consults; the comment is inert. Between 06:57 and 07:23 the `loom:issue` ↔ `loom:building` pair cycled 9 times at ~90s each, straight through four "held" notices.

The ~90s cycle matches the failure text the holds themselves record — *"sweep exited 1 after 82s / 94s / 104s without opening a pull request, without a phase checkpoint, and without a `.no-changes-needed` marker"*. 33 of the 54 holds I sampled fall in a 77–110s band.

## It generalizes

| Issue | hold comments | `loom:blocked` labeled | unlabeled |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rjwalters/loom#8812` | 5 | 1 | 0 |
| `rjwalters/loom#8818` | 5 | 2 | 1 |
| `rjwalters/loom#8699` | 5 | 2 | 1 |
| `2AMLogic/gf180-temp-por#312` | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| `2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2417` | 3 | 1 | 0 |
| `2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2451` | 4 | 1 | 0 |
| `2AMLogic/sky130-comparator#99` | 3 | 1 | 0 |

Hold comments exceed label writes in every case, across 4 repos and both owners.

## Second contributing factor: per-host counters, no shared state

Claims on the held set come from all four dispatch hosts, roughly evenly (`host-d9142cf3` 25, `host-34209a6e` 25, `host-e1d4c843` 19, `host-d0749b00` 12 — issues where a host was recorded). Each host appears to count its own 3 consecutive prless claims independently, so the fleet burns up to 4×3 = 12 claims before any single host trips its threshold. `#7972` was diagnosed and fixed on a single-host loop; the multi-host case does not appear to be covered.

## Scale

Across the 55 held issues: **2,641 lease claims, 174 hold comments, 69 lease-yields.** 48 of 55 have more than one hold comment; 32 have three or more.

Two outliers are severe:

| Issue | comments | lease claims | holds | span |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2AMLogic/sg13g2-bandgap#4` | **2,500** | **1,456** | 14 | 2026-08-09 → 2026-09-26 (48d) |
| `2AMLogic/sky130-sar-adc#121` | 632 | 383 | 16 | 2026-08-25 → **2026-09-27, still active** |

Two costs, not one: the wasted dispatch itself, and the comment bloat. A 2,500-comment issue is effectively unreadable, and every subsequent Curator/Judge/unblock read pays for it — which is its own compounding drag on exactly the roles meant to resolve the state.

`sg13g2-bandgap#4` is worth singling out: it is a **gap-to-T1 tracker**, which the operator ruling of 2026-09-15 (recorded in `2AMLogic/2am`'s `FLEET.md` § "Gap-to-T1 tracker convention") says is *never promotable* and must rest on `loom:blocked`. It currently carries `loom:issue` **and** `loom:blocked` together — the `#7071` shape — so the work finder still sees it as a ready candidate. 1,456 claims over 48 days on an issue that by design can never produce a PR.

## Suggested fix

1. **Make the hold's label write the primary deliverable, not the comment** — the same discipline `judge.md` already states for verdicts ("The `gh pr edit` label command is the PRIMARY deliverable"). If `loom:blocked` cannot be applied, the hold has not happened and should be retried or loudly failed, not left as a comment.
2. **Share the prless counter across hosts** (or key the threshold on the issue's own hold-comment count, which is already durable on the forge) so four hosts cannot each spend a full runway.
3. **Exclude `loom:issue` + `loom:blocked` from the candidate filter**, per `#7071` — `sg13g2-bandgap#4` shows that row is still reachable in the dispatch path.

## What I did not verify

- **Why the individual sweeps exit 1 at ~90s.** I did not obtain a sweep transcript; the 2AM host holding `activity.db` locally has no rows for these dispatches (they ran on the four fleet hosts). The exit cause is unknown and may itself be several causes. This report is about the hold failing to park, which is independent of why the underlying build failed.
- **`sg13g2-bandgap#4` and `#8818`/`#8699` also show `loom:blocked` being *removed*** (1 unlabeled each on the loom pair; repeated add/remove cycling on the bandgap tracker). I did not establish what removes it — the unblock sweep (`guide.md`'s `check_and_unblock`) clearing a prless hold it mistook for a resolved dependency is a plausible second mechanism, since a prless hold writes no park record and the routine reads body dependencies only. Worth confirming separately rather than assuming.
- One known measurement caveat: the 55-issue set comes from `gh search issues "prless-retry" --label loom:blocked --state open`, so it counts issues *currently* held and open. Issues whose hold was cleared, or that were closed, are not in it — the real claim total is higher, not lower.

## How to reproduce the measurement

```sh
# the held set
for o in 2AMLogic rjwalters; do
  gh search issues "prless-retry" --owner "$o" --state open --label loom:blocked \
    --limit 100 --json repository,number
done

# per issue: claims vs holds vs label writes
gh issue view "$N" --repo "$NWO" --json comments --jq \
  '[.comments[].body] as $b
   | {leases: ($b|map(select(test("loom:lease host=")))|length),
      holds:  ($b|map(select(test("loom:prless-retry")))|length)}'

gh api "repos/$NWO/issues/$N/timeline" --paginate \
  | jq -s 'add|[.[]|select(.event|test("labeled"))|select(.label.name=="loom:blocked")|.event]
           |group_by(.)|map({(.[0]):length})'
```

---

Filed from `2AMLogic/2am` during a fleet-wide blocked-issue pass (attended operator session). Cross-ref `#7972` (the mechanism, closed 2026-09-23), `#7071` (the `loom:issue`+`loom:blocked` candidate-filter row), `#8925` (`PARK_LABELS` / park-record contract).

issues.title: ETA history must be fleet-global: host-local journals make ETAs empty on most hosts, biased on others, and inconsistent across the fleet
issues.body:
Part of #9289 (ETA as a Loom primitive). Raised by the operator on 2026-09-28 while reviewing slice 1a (#9339).

### Problem: ETA history is host-local, so ETAs are wrong
`eta::history` (#9339) builds stage distributions only from the **local** host's `.loom/logs/sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl`, plus the local `eta-stage-samples.jsonl` in slice 1b. A daemon therefore estimates only from the sweeps *it* ran:

- **No samples on most hosts:** the operator Mac has **zero** rjwalters/loom sweep outcomes, because loom sweeps run on fleet workers, so `land-v1` refuses every loom estimate there (`insufficient_samples`).
- **Biased where there are samples:** a worker's history reflects its own hardware, token pool, repo mix and luck. It is small-n and not representative.
- **Hosts disagree:** two hosts give different ETAs for the same issue, and the dashboard gets whichever host's `eta.snapshot` arrived last.
- **Human stages are invisible locally:** Judge wait, approval and merge dominate lead time (~40–70% measured 2026-09-28), and they happen on the forge, not in any one host's sweep.
- **Backtests would inherit all of this.** (#9325)

### What "global" means
One fleet-wide sample set per `(repo, stage)` that every host estimates from, so ETAs agree across hosts and use all the evidence.

### Options
1. **The forge as source of truth for stage boundaries.** This is Loom's own coordination layer. Stage transitions come from label events that every host already lists (ETag-cached). The D32 `storyline` reconciler already derives `story.*` spans globally from exactly this.
   - For: it is complete and host-independent.
   - Against: API cost if every daemon re-derives history. A backfill-once-then-incremental cache is required.
2. **SigNoz as the shared journal.** Every host exports `sweep.outcome` and `eta.*`. A daemon periodically pulls a fleet-wide sample snapshot (e.g. every 15–60 min) into a local cache file, and the estimator stays a pure function over that snapshot, so backtests remain leak-free.
   - Blocker: fleet workers don't export to SigNoz yet (harness-ops #249). As of 2026-09-28 SigNoz has 8 `loom.phase` spans in 30 days, while the D32 `story.*` spans from storyline *are* global and present.
3. **Peer exchange.** Hosts share their samples like the peer-claims transport. This adds a new sync surface; not recommended.
4. **Hybrid (recommended to evaluate).**
   - Human and forge stages (`review_wait`, `doctor` rounds, `merge_wait`, intake) come from forge-derived or D32 story data.
   - In-sweep machine stages (`curator`, `builder`) come from fleet `sweep.outcome` via SigNoz once #249 lands.
   - Local journal is a fallback and freshness supplement only.

### Requirements
- Each explanation records `history.scope` (`local` | `fleet`), the sources used, per-source and per-host sample counts, and the snapshot id/as-of time, so forensics can tell which view produced a number.
- Hosts at the same snapshot produce byte-identical estimates for the same input (determinism across the fleet).
- The estimator stays pure over a snapshot. Fetching happens outside it, so backtests (#9325) replay a global history with no leakage.

### Evidence
2026-09-28: the operator asked "when will #9289 land" using the 1a code. Local history was empty, so the only workable input was a history rebuilt from GitHub label timelines of the last 60 merged loom PRs: 46 PRs, 41 builder / 25 curator / 75 judge / 22 doctor / 46 merge samples, with first-attempt Judge rejection at 20/46.
---

## Curator Enhancement — 2026-09-30

Verified against `origin/main` @ `fcce3f66c` (see below):
`loom-daemon/src/eta/explanation.rs` already reserves the shape this issue asks
for — `HistoryScope::Fleet` exists as a variant with the doc comment "Reserved
for #9343; never produced yet", and `HistoryRecord` already carries
`samples_by_source`/`samples_by_host` maps matching the "Requirements" section's
per-source/per-host sample-count ask. `loom-daemon/src/eta/history.rs` documents
the host-local limitation inline (`# Limitation: history is host-local (#9343)`)
and points at this issue as the intended direction. This confirms the issue's
own analysis against the current code, not a duplicate/already-fixed situation.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `HistoryScope::Fleet`-producing path exists: at minimum, forge-derived
      stage boundaries (Option 1) populate a fleet-wide sample set per
      `(repo, stage)`, since this is the one option with **no** external
      blocker (unlike Option 2/SigNoz, blocked on fleet workers exporting —
      harness-ops#249, not this repo).
- [ ] `HistoryRecord` for a fleet estimate records `scope=fleet`, its sources,
      and per-source/per-host sample counts (the fields already exist; wire a
      real producer).
- [ ] Determinism: two hosts estimating from the same named snapshot (same
      snapshot id/as-of time) produce byte-identical `HistoryRecord` /
      estimate output — add a test that runs the estimator twice against one
      fixture snapshot and diffs the output.
- [ ] The estimator itself stays pure over a snapshot — fetching/caching is a
      separate step, so `#9325`'s leak-free backtest harness can replay a
      fleet snapshot with no behavior change to the estimator's core.
- [ ] A backfill-once-then-incremental cache avoids re-deriving full history
      from the forge API on every daemon tick (evidence section already
      measured 46 merged PRs' worth of label timeline for one backfill; make
      the ongoing cost incremental, not repeated).
- [ ] The SigNoz-sourced portion (Option 2 / the "hybrid" machine-stage half)
      is explicitly out of scope until harness-ops#249 lands fleet-worker
      export — this AC set covers only the forge-derived half plus the
      scope/producer plumbing; do not block this issue on that external
      dependency.

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/eta/history.rs` — currently host-local by construction
  (`StageSamples` reads one host's file); needs a fleet-scoped producer
  alongside the existing local one.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/explanation.rs` — `HistoryScope::Fleet` variant and
  `HistoryRecord` fields already exist; wire a real fleet producer into them.
- `loom-daemon/src/eta/heuristics/{start_v1,finish_v1,land_v1}.rs` — the
  estimators that currently read local-only history; must accept a fleet
  snapshot input without losing purity (see AC above).
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/eta.rs` — SigNoz/telemetry surface, relevant
  once the machine-stage half is unblocked.
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/eta_cmd.rs` — CLI surface for inspecting/backfilling
  history; likely needs a fleet-snapshot subcommand or flag.
- New: a forge-derived stage-boundary cache module (backfill + incremental
  update) — file location to be determined during implementation, likely
  under `loom-daemon/src/eta/`.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: determinism test — same snapshot, two simulated hosts,
      identical `HistoryRecord`/estimate output.
- [ ] Automated: fleet-scope producer unit tests (sample counts, source
      attribution) mirroring the existing local-scope tests in
      `loom-daemon/src/eta/tests/`.
- [ ] Automated: `#9325`'s backtest harness still passes with no leakage when
      fed a fleet snapshot fixture instead of a local journal.
- [ ] Manual verification: on a host with zero local rjwalters/loom sweep
      outcomes (the operator Mac case cited in Evidence), `land-v1` no longer
      returns `insufficient_samples` once fleet history is wired in.

### Dependencies

- Option 2 (SigNoz-sourced machine-stage samples) is blocked on fleet workers
  exporting to SigNoz — tracked externally as harness-ops#249, not in this
  repo. This does **not** block the forge-derived half (Option 1) covered by
  the Acceptance Criteria above; implement that first and treat the SigNoz
  half as a follow-up once harness-ops#249 lands.

issues.title: dashboard: add a Live tab — perpetually-updating status board
issues.body: ## Summary The fleet dashboard (`dashboard/web`) has tabs for Fleet, Queue, Charts, Tokens, Spend and Feed, but none of them works as a status board you can leave open on a second monitor. Fleet and Queue are dense, drill-down-oriented views. Feed is a bare list of topic strings. Add a **Live** tab (`#/live`): a full-width status board that keeps updating and is readable at a glance from across the room. ## What the Live tab shows 1. **Headline tiles:** hosts online / total, sweeps running, ready-queue depth, blocked count, and peak token usage. Each tile animates when its value changes. 2. **In-flight sweep cards:** one card per active sweep with repo#issue (linked), host, model/effort, and a phase stepper (curator → builder → judge → doctor → merge) that highlights the current phase. Elapsed-in-sweep and in-phase timers tick every second. New cards animate in, and cards for sweeps that have finished animate out. The cards are keyed by `sweepId` so a poll never replays an animation. 3. **Host strip:** one pill per host with a status dot (ok/throttled/degraded/stale/missing), a CPU-load meter, the sweep count, and a pulse on busy hosts. 4. **Activity ticker:** recent live-tail events (`/api/events` or `/public/events`) rendered as readable sentences ("#123 entered judge on mac-1", "#98 completed · success"), newest first, with an entry animation. 5. **Connection indicator:** a "LIVE" dot that pulses while the SSE stream is open and dims while it reconnects, plus the time of the last snapshot. ## Technical notes - A new panel route `live` in `src/router.ts` (`PANEL_ROUTES`), with a mounter in `src/panels.ts`, a nav link in `index.html`, and a `PANEL_STATUS` entry. - The panel owns its data. It polls `fetchFleetState()` on a short interval (about 5s), holds a `LiveFeedClient` for events, and runs a 1s clock tick. The tick only rewrites timer text; it never rebuilds the DOM. - The DOM is keyed and reconciled by `sweepId`/`hostId` so CSS animations (entry, pulse, value flash) are not restarted on every poll. This is the "durable local state" case the README's "When to overturn this" section anticipates, but it stays small and contained to this one view, so no framework is added. - The view-model logic lives in a DOM-free module (phase index, event sentence, tile values) and is unit-tested. The view is tested with happy-dom, like the sibling panels. - The panel tears down cleanly: it stops polling, closes the SSE connection, clears the tick, and pauses while the tab is hidden, consistent with `main.ts`'s visibility handling. - It honors `prefers-reduced-motion` and the unknown-is-not-zero rule (`—`, never `0`). - The public (anonymous) viewer works through the `/public/*` routes, as the other panels do. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `#/live` renders the board, and the nav shows a **Live** link that highlights when active. - [ ] Sweep timers advance each second without a full re-render (test: the same DOM node persists across ticks and polls). - [ ] Navigating away tears down polling, SSE, and the tick timer (test). - [ ] `cd dashboard/web && npm run check` passes. - [ ] The README's view table documents the Live tab. ## Affected Files - `dashboard/web/src/router.ts` - add `"live"` to `PanelRouteName` and `PANEL_ROUTES` (`/live` → `live`) - `dashboard/web/src/panels.ts` - add a `PANEL_STATUS["live"]` entry and wire the new panel's mounter alongside the existing `charts`/`tokens`/`spend`/`feed` panels - `dashboard/web/index.html` - add a `Live` nav link (line 19 area, after the existing Feed link) - `dashboard/web/src/livePanel.ts` (new) - the Live tab's DOM-owning panel: polls `fetchFleetState()` (`dashboard/web/src/fleet.ts`/`api.ts`) on ~5s interval, holds a `LiveFeedClient` (`dashboard/web/src/sseFeedClient.ts`, already used by `liveFeedPanel.ts`'s Feed tab) for the activity ticker, and runs a 1s tick for timer text only - `dashboard/web/src/views/liveViewModel.ts` (new, suggested name) - DOM-free view-model module: phase index for the curator→builder→judge→doctor→merge stepper, event-to-sentence mapping, tile value derivation — unit-tested without a DOM - `dashboard/web/src/liveFeedPanel.ts` - reference implementation for the SSE-client usage pattern (`LiveFeedClient`, `frameKey`) the new ticker should follow - `dashboard/web/README.md` - add the Live tab row to the view table (see existing rows at lines 30-36) - `dashboard/web/src/livePanel.test.ts` / `dashboard/web/src/views/liveViewModel.test.ts` (new) - happy-dom test for teardown/keyed-DOM persistence, plain unit tests for the view-model ## Test Plan - [ ] Manual verification: run the dashboard dev server, navigate to `#/live`, confirm tiles/cards/host strip/ticker render and update on poll without visibly re-rendering. - [ ] Automated tests: `livePanel.test.ts` (happy-dom) asserts the same DOM node persists across ticks/polls (keyed by `sweepId`/`hostId`), and that navigating away stops polling, closes the SSE client, and clears the tick interval. `liveViewModel.test.ts` covers phase-index derivation, event-sentence formatting, and the unknown-is-not-zero rule for tile values. - [ ] Edge cases: zero hosts online, a sweep finishing mid-poll (card animates out), SSE disconnect/reconnect (connection indicator dims/pulses), `prefers-reduced-motion` set (animations suppressed). - [ ] `cd dashboard/web && npm run check` passes.

issues.title: Champion critical-file hold: bare .sql pattern false-positives on reference queries (defaults/observability/)
issues.body:
## Problem

Champion's critical-file hold (criterion #3, `CRITICAL_PATTERNS` in `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md` ~line 1044) uses a **bare substring pattern `".sql"`**. That matches any path containing `.sql` — including **reference/query SQL that nothing executes**, e.g. `defaults/observability/signoz/ci-queries.sql` added by #9348 (SigNoz reference queries documented for ci-observability, never run by build, release, or migration machinery).

The intended target of a `.sql`-ish pattern — schema migrations — is already covered by two other entries in the same list: `"migrations/"` and `"_migration.py"`.

## Observed cost (2026-09-28, #9348)

- The hold armed on every head, so each human release was durable only for one head (#9016).
- The PR was *also* cycling through #8248 required-check-freshness re-dates (main moves every few minutes). Every re-date head re-armed the hold, so release → merge attempts kept colliding with fresh holds across multiple full CI rounds.

## Proposal

Narrow the pattern so reference SQL stops arming the hold:

1. **Drop the bare `".sql"` entry** from `CRITICAL_PATTERNS`, keeping `"migrations/"` and `"_migration.py"` (already present) as the migration-surface guards, **or**
2. Keep `.sql` matching but scope it to real schema paths (path-prefix patterns such as `migrations/`, `schema/`, `db/` — per this repo's conventions) and/or add an explicit exclusion for `defaults/observability/**` (SigNoz reference queries live there by design).

Option 1 is simpler; option 2 is conservative. Either way, document the decision in the pattern list's comment so the next "why doesn't my `.sql` file hold?" question has an answer.

## Constraints

- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md` is a role prompt: a non-trivial change needs the pressure-test + conflict-audit treatment from `role-prompt-authoring.md`, and file-size ratchet budget (offset lines).
- Regression risk to check: `test-champion-*` suites and the version-only carve-out tests reference criterion #3 behavior.

issues.title: forge-helpers/worktree-forge-pr-check: URL-encode branch in Gitea API path; build fd-3 refusal JSON with jq (unescaped headRefName)
issues.body:
## Context

Two low-severity integrity fixes from the independent security audit (2026-09-26 session). Both are "untrusted forge value interpolated into a machine-readable surface" — no code execution, but a hostile value corrupts the surface:

1. **Gitea API URL built by string interpolation** — `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:506`:
   `gitea_api DELETE "repos/$FORGE_OWNER/$FORGE_REPO/branches/$branch"` (the GitHub arm at `:508` uses the same interpolation). `$branch` can be forge-derived. Ref names cannot contain `..` (ref-format forbids it), so there is **no path traversal** — but a name with URL metacharacters (``,`` `` ` ``` `, `?`, `#`, `%`) silently produces a different, wrong API call.
2. **Unescaped `headRefName` inside emitted JSON** — `defaults/scripts/lib/worktree-forge-pr-check.sh:270` (cross-repo PR refusal):
   `echo '{"success": false, …, "headRef": "'"$_WT_OPEN_PR_HEAD_REF"'"}' >&3` — a `headRefName` containing `"` (legal in a ref name) yields **malformed JSON** on the machine-readable refusal channel (fd 3); consumers see an unparseable "error" and fall back to their worst-case handling.

## What changes

1. URL-encode the variable path segments before interpolation at both arms of `forge_delete_branch` (and any other `gitea_api`/`gh api` path-construction site taking a forge value — grep `branches/\$` and `refs/heads/\$` in `defaults/scripts/`): a small `url_encode_path_segment()` helper in the same lib (`%XX` for everything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`).
2. Build the fd-3 JSON with `jq -n` (args via `--arg`):
   `jq -n --arg headRef "$_WT_OPEN_PR_HEAD_REF" --arg headRepo "$_WT_OPEN_PR_HEAD_REPO" --argjson pr "$_WT_OPEN_PR_NUMBER" '{success:false, error:"shadowed-cross-repo-pr", issueNumber:($issue|tonumber), prNumber:$pr, headRepo:$headRepo, headRef:$headRef}'`
   (guard the `--argjson pr` against the existing empty/`null` case the literal form already tolerates).
3. Sweep the other literal-JSON `>&3` emitters in `worktree-forge-pr-check.sh` for the same class (they interpolate `issue_number` — numeric, safe — but `origin_fetch_result` and any future forge value are not).

## Out of scope

- Ref-name validation at git sinks (separate HIGH issue filed with this one).
- mcp-loom shell-string fix (separate issue).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `forge_delete_branch` with a branch name containing URL metacharacters issues a correctly percent-encoded request (test with a stubbed `gitea_api` capturing the path).
2. The cross-repo refusal JSON parses with `jq` for a `headRefName` containing `"`, `\`, and `<`/`>` (test: emit with an adversarial name, pipe through `jq -e .`).
3. No remaining `>&3`/`--json` emitter in `worktree-forge-pr-check.sh` interpolates a non-numeric forge value into a JSON literal (grep-auditable).

issues.title: observability: per-issue dispatch disposition spans (loom.dispatch.disposition) so SigNoz can answer "why hasn't repo#N started"
issues.body:
## Problem

The question "why hasn't `owner/repo#98` started yet?" cannot be answered from SigNoz today. It can only be answered on the host that listed the issue (`loom-daemon queue`, #8852), or from the native HTTPS dashboard.

What reaches OTLP from each work-finder tick on `main` (0.19.451):

| Signal | Where | Per-issue? |
|---|---|---|
| `loom.dispatch.decisions{reason}` delta counters (25 reasons) | `observability/ops/dispatch.rs:27` `decision_counts`, `:102` `tick_points` | No. Counts only. |
| `loom.queue.issues{state,reason}` gauges (23 dispositions, zeros included) | `observability/ops/queue.rs:27` | No. Counts only. |
| `loom.queue.oldest_wait{state}`, `loom.queue.starved{state}`, `loom.queue.starved.by_reason{reason}`, `loom.queue.dispatch_wait*` | `observability/ops/dwell.rs` | No |
| `loom.dispatch.tick` root span (`loom.dispatch.result/seen/dispatched/errors/max_concurrent`, `events: []`) | `observability/ops/dispatch.rs:118` | No |
| `loom.dispatch.admission` child span per `dispatch()` attempt (`loom.issue`, `loom.dispatch.admission_result`, `loom.dispatch.reason`) | `observability/ops/dispatch.rs:162`, built from `work_finder/tick_report.rs:321` | Yes, but only for candidates that reached `dispatch()`. It has **no `loom.repo`**, so the issue number is ambiguous across a multi-repo host. |
| `queue.snapshot` per-issue ranked rows | `observability/queue_snapshot.rs` | Yes, but **native-HTTPS only**. `otlp/mapping.rs:548` routes it away from SigNoz. |

Every candidate that is filtered before `dispatch()` has no per-issue record in SigNoz. That covers `workspace_halted`, `parked`, `deferred_capacity`, `deferred_ramp_cap`, `deferred_saturation`, `deferred_repo_cap`, `deferred_out_of_slice`, the backoffs and cooldowns, `host_constraint`, `host_class_refused` and `quarantined`. That is almost every "why is it waiting" answer.

### Live evidence (SigNoz AWS store, read-only ClickHouse, last 24h, 2026-09-27)

- Only `host.id=MacBook-Air.localdomain` exports loom telemetry. Fleet hosts are not wired yet (2AMLogic/2am#1345, harness-ops #249).
- 1411 `loom.dispatch.tick` spans, about 60/h. 1385 of them are `result=halted_main_red`, 23 are `saturation_held` and 2 are `all_skipped`.
- `loom.queue.issues{reason="workspace_halted"}` currently reads 17 and peaked at 20. Earlier peaks: `deferred_saturation` 5, `open_pr` 5, `open_pr_backoff` 5, `workspace_commands_missing` 7.
- 5 `loom.dispatch.admission` spans in total (#319, #323, #334, #351, #355, all `refused/pr_open`). `attributes_string['loom.repo']` is empty on every one.
- Result: SigNoz knows that 17 issues are held by `workspace_halted`. It cannot say which 17 or in which repos. For any one issue, it cannot say whether its last-tick reason was the admission brake, a park label or rank/capacity.

### Mapping the operator's three example reasons

| Operator term | Loom reality |
|---|---|
| `admission_brake` | `QueueDisposition::DeferredSaturation` (`deferred_saturation`). Decisions reason `saturation`, tick result `saturation_held`. |
| `dependency_blocked` | Loom has no issue-dependency gate. The nearest states are `parked` (the issue carries a `PARK_LABELS`/`SKIP_LABELS` entry such as `loom:blocked` together with `loom:issue`) and `labelled_blocked` (`loom:blocked` without `loom:issue`; never listed, only in native `queue.snapshot` via #8957). |
| `lower_tier` | `tier:*` labels do **not** affect order (`types/ready_queue.rs:8`). "Ranked behind others" means the issue was a candidate and lost the slot: `deferred_capacity` (machine cap full), `deferred_ramp_cap` (per-tick admission cap), `deferred_repo_cap` (per-repo cap) or `deferred_out_of_slice` (repo sharding). All four have `state=ready`, distinct from the `blocked` hard holds. The rank (`workspace_priority`, `loom:urgent`, `createdAt`, number via `candidate_cmp`) is on the row but not exported. |

The reason taxonomy already exists and is finer than the operator's three terms (`QueueDisposition`, 23 tick values). The gap is only that it is never exported per issue to OTLP.

## Design

### 1. New span `loom.dispatch.disposition`, emitted on change plus a periodic refresh

Add `SpanName::DispatchDisposition` (`"loom.dispatch.disposition"`). Emit one zero-duration span per `(repo, issue)` ready-queue row when one of these holds:

- **transition**: its disposition differs from the last one emitted for that key, including first sight; or
- **refresh**: the last emission for that key is older than `LOOM_DISPATCH_DISPOSITION_REFRESH_SECS` (default `600`).

Also emit one terminal span with `loom.queue.transition=left_queue` when a previously emitted key disappears from a successfully listed repo. Do not emit it when the repo's listing failed this tick; follow the `dwell.rs` rule for that case. This way "not in the queue any more" is distinguishable from "no data".

Why a span and not span events on `loom.dispatch.tick`:
- `SpanRecord::bounded` (`telemetry/trace/span.rs:164`) keeps only 6 event names and truncates events to 32 per span. A ready queue is routinely larger than 32.
- Child spans are the pattern #8907 already uses for `loom.dispatch.admission`, so the query shape is the same.

Why not a metric label: issue number and repo must never be metric labels (`OPS_METRIC_LABEL_KEYS` contract, `telemetry/ops.rs:32`).

Why not every row every tick: about 20 rows at 60–240 ticks/h is 1.2k–4.8k spans/h/host of redundant rows. With transitions plus a 10-minute refresh it is about 6 × waiting-rows per hour plus real changes. A lookback of 10 minutes or more still always contains the current state of every queued issue.

### 2. Attributes (every value a closed vocabulary or a bounded integer; no titles or bodies)

| Key | Value | Allowlist |
|---|---|---|
| `loom.repo` | forge `owner/repo` slug. **Never a local path.** Rows whose slug cannot be resolved are dropped and counted on the tick. | already in `bounded_attributes` |
| `loom.repo.visibility` | `public`/`private`, same resolution as `queue.snapshot` | already allowed |
| `loom.issue` | issue number | already allowed |
| `loom.queue.disposition` | `QueueDisposition::as_str()` wire name (`deferred_saturation`, `parked`, …) | **new**, add to `OPS_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS` |
| `loom.queue.state` | `running`/`ready`/`blocked` (`QueueDisposition::state`) | **new** |
| `loom.queue.rank` | 1-based rank in dispatch order | **new** |
| `loom.queue.transition` | `changed` / `refresh` / `left_queue` | **new** |
| `loom.queue.previous_disposition` | prior wire name, or absent on first sight | **new** |
| `loom.queue.park_label` | only for `parked`/`hard_exclusion`: the matching label, **only if it is in `PARK_LABELS ∪ SKIP_LABELS`** (closed set). Otherwise absent. | **new** |
| `loom.pr_number` | only for `open_pr`: the linked PR number (structured `detail`, same rule as `queue_snapshot::exportable_detail`) | already allowed |

Free-form `detail` (dispatch-error text) is **never** exported.

Every new key must also be added to the gateway collector's span `keep_keys` in `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml`; the existing contract test enforces this.

### 3. Also fix `loom.dispatch.admission`: add `loom.repo` (+ `loom.repo.visibility`)

Give `tick_report::Admission` its `workspace_idx`. Resolve the slug in the same way as §4, so `loom.issue` is no longer ambiguous on a multi-repo host. If the slug is unresolved, omit `loom.repo` rather than export a path.

### 4. Where in code

- New module `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/disposition.rs`. Its pure core is a `DispositionTracker { last: HashMap<(String /*slug*/, u32), (QueueDisposition, DateTime<Utc>)> }` plus `fn diff(&mut self, rows, listing_ok_repos, now, refresh) -> Vec<Emission>`. The one side effect is `record(...)`. Model it on `ops/dwell.rs` (static `OnceLock<Mutex<_>>` tracker) and `ops/stage_dwell.rs` (collector-driven, OTLP-only, uses `slug_cache`).
- Driver: call `super::ops::disposition::record(slug_cache).await` from the collector's periodic sample next to `queue_snapshot::record` / `stage_dwell::record` (`observability/collector.rs:606-609`). It reads `work_finder::last_tick_summary()`, whose rows are already ranked with `rank`, `repo` root, `disposition` and `detail` (`work_finder/ready_queue.rs:146` `finish`). It resolves roots to slug and visibility through `collector::resolve_repo_slug_cached` / `resolve_visibility`, which `queue_snapshot::resolve_repos` already uses. Refactor that helper to share it; do not copy it.
  - Gate on `super::global_ops_sink()` (OTLP), **not** on the native `queue_snapshot` sink. It must work on a host with only an OTLP exporter, which is the operator Mac's configuration.
  - Skip when `last_tick_summary().at` has not advanced (same `is_new_tick` guard).
  - Tradeoff to document in the module: sampling happens at collector cadence, so a disposition that lasts less than one collector interval can be missed. Only the last-tick state per interval is exported. That is acceptable for the "why is it waiting" use.
- Parenting: store the last tick span's `TraceContext` in `ops/dispatch.rs::record_tick` (for example `static LAST_TICK: Mutex<Option<(DateTime<Utc>, TraceContext)>>`). Parent the disposition spans to it when its tick timestamp matches the summary; otherwise emit them as roots. Derive span ids with `derived_child(&[name, slug, issue, instant])`, never randomly (trace-identity policy).
- Stamp `provenance::stamp` on each span, as the admission spans do.
- Cap at 256 disposition spans per record call. Count dropped rows in a new `MetricName::QueueDispositionRowsDropped` (`loom.queue.disposition_rows_dropped{reason="unresolved"|"truncated"}`), a delta counter. Do not put this on the tick span, which has already been emitted.
- `single-workspace` loop: roots are empty (`workspace #N`), so rows are unresolved and dropped, the same as `queue.snapshot`. Record this in the docs.

### 5. SigNoz query recipe (to add to `defaults/observability/signoz/fixture-queries.sql` and `defaults/docs/observability.md`)

```sql
-- Why hasn't owner/repo#98 started? (latest first, all hosts)
SELECT timestamp, resources_string['host.id'] AS host,
       attributes_string['loom.queue.disposition'] AS disposition,
       attributes_string['loom.queue.state']       AS state,
       attributes_string['loom.queue.rank']        AS rank,
       attributes_string['loom.queue.transition']  AS transition,
       attributes_string['loom.queue.park_label']  AS park_label
FROM signoz_traces.signoz_index_v3
WHERE name IN ('loom.dispatch.disposition', 'loom.dispatch.admission')
  AND attributes_string['loom.repo']  = 'owner/repo'
  AND attributes_string['loom.issue'] = '98'
  AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20;
```

For `workspace_halted` rows, join to the parent `loom.dispatch.tick` (`result=halted_main_red`) through `parentSpanID`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SpanName::DispatchDisposition` = `"loom.dispatch.disposition"`, round-trip tested next to `DispatchAdmission`.
- [ ] Unit tests for the pure tracker (`ops/disposition_tests.rs`):
  - first sight emits `changed` with no `previous_disposition`;
  - the same disposition within the refresh window emits nothing;
  - the same disposition after the window emits `refresh`;
  - a change emits `changed` with `previous_disposition`;
  - a key missing from a successfully listed repo emits `left_queue` once;
  - a key in a repo whose listing failed emits nothing and keeps its state;
  - an unresolved root is dropped and counted;
  - more than 256 rows are truncated and counted.
- [ ] Attribute test: every emitted key survives `SpanRecord::bounded()`. `loom.repo` is never an absolute path. `loom.queue.park_label` appears only for a label in `PARK_LABELS ∪ SKIP_LABELS`. Free-form `detail` (a `DispatchError` row) is never exported.
- [ ] `loom.dispatch.admission` spans carry `loom.repo` when resolvable. Extend the existing `admission_spans` test.
- [ ] `OPS_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS` and `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` span `keep_keys` both contain the new keys. The existing contract test passes.
- [ ] No-op when no ops sink is registered (test mirrors `record_tick`'s early return).
- [ ] Docs: `defaults/docs/observability.md` lists the span, attributes, cadence and cardinality bound. The query recipe is in `defaults/observability/signoz/fixture-queries.sql`. The mapping table above (operator term → disposition) is in the docs.
- [ ] Live check after merge and a daemon update on the operator Mac: the §5 query returns rows for a currently queued issue within 10 minutes.

## Out of scope

- Splitting `workspace_halted` by cause (red main / gate / token pool / drain / breaker). The row does not know the cause today (`types/ready_queue.rs:40`). File separately if wanted.
- Exporting `labelled_blocked` (forge-side `loom:blocked` without `loom:issue`) to OTLP. It is not a tick outcome.
- An issue-dependency gate (there is none; see the mapping table).
- Fleet coverage. Until 2AMLogic/2am#1345 wires loom-worker-1/2 and robb-studio, this answers only for issues the operator Mac's daemon lists.

Refs: #8907 (closed; typed refusals + admission spans), #8852 (queue rows), #8856 (dwell), #8860 (tick span), #9034 (`host_class`). Tracking: 2AMLogic/2am#1306.
