issues.title: Admit Codex mutable roles using verified private-clone containment
issues.body:
Part of #4489; third implementation step in the operator-requested private-clone workstream. #4496 remains the production evidence gate.

## Problem

Independent repositories prevent a container worker from damaging a shared host checkout, but the daemon currently admits Codex from a static capability manifest where worktreeIsolation is partial. The adapter additionally requires managed native hooks for mutable roles. Merely removing the host mount would therefore still leave Builder, Doctor and full sweeps unusable.

The operator requested isolated copies as the fastest integration path, with optimization deferred. Implement a distinct, verified execution context; do not globally declare native Codex hook parity complete.

## Recommended implementation

Extend admission so private-clone containment can satisfy the repository-isolation requirement for a launch whose account, container, mounts, private Git root and exclusive job lease are validated. Carry the validated context through account selection and spawn, and recheck its identity at execution. A configuration flag, environment variable or container label alone is insufficient evidence.

For this mode, the whole private clone is the worker's owned repository sandbox; local disposable base-checkout edits are not host-main edits. Existing issue branches/worktrees remain the workflow. Explicitly document this scope of isolation so it is not mistaken for native per-worktree hook parity.

Reconcile the adapter's mutable-role preflight with that context. Replace only the filesystem-isolation obligation covered by independent clones. Inventory the remaining obligations of the existing hook bridge—protected remote branch mutations, destructive actions outside the owned workspace, Loom lifecycle controls and credential boundaries—and retain or provide an enforceable mechanism for each. A Docker boundary does not prevent an authenticated force-push. Where a required policy is unproven, refuse with the precise remaining requirement rather than silently waive all hook checks.

Keep ordinary host/shared-mount Codex admission unchanged. Record execution-specific capability provenance in diagnostics and status. Support the already selected runtime preference order without altering repository-specific preference or scheduled-role settings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Builder, Doctor and sweep-lifecycle admission can use verified private-clone isolation through the normal runtime path. Read-oriented roles keep their existing requirements; every path still checks remaining role capabilities.
- [ ] Bare-host, host-repository-mounted, shared-Git, shared-account-lease and unverifiable sessions remain refused for the new containment claim. Missing/stale container identity and a mount/lease change between preflight and launch fail closed.
- [ ] Global Codex hooks/worktreeIsolation values are not changed to yes based on this feature. Admission records distinguish verified clone containment from native hook parity.
- [ ] The managed-hook preflight is explicitly reconciled with clone mode; there is no unconditional skip flag, trust bypass, test-only environment variable or prompt-only policy standing in for enforcement.
- [ ] Tests prove allowed private issue-branch edits/commit/push and denial of host/sibling/peer-repository writes, arbitrary host control/executor access and protected-remote destructive operations using disposable local fixtures.
- [ ] Preserve workflow/credential protections and test the actual launch path, including attempts via shell, patch, helper and any supported secondary mutation channel. Do not claim container isolation makes credentials or forge operations harmless.
- [ ] Update the runtime/guardrail documentation with an obligation-to-mechanism table, supported image/CLI/protocol versions, evidence requirements, remaining limitations and rollback to the prior runtime.
- [ ] Automated tests cover both explicit Codex selection and capability-aware fallback. No change silently makes an unverified Codex account eligible or falls through from an explicit runtime pin.
- [ ] Prepare the private-clone test matrix for #4496, including an actual daemon-dispatched bounded full lifecycle after disposable-repo success. Mock/CI evidence cannot satisfy the live go/no-go; do not enable fleet defaults here.

## Implementation starting points — curator must verify

Verified against origin/main at 135183d9b2527cb2cc81d2c5d8e0ba1f2213c645:

- `loom-daemon/src/runtime_admission.rs` — full sweeps are a single runtime launch checked against Builder requirements.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/runtime_preflight.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs` — capability-aware selection and dispatch.
- `defaults/runtimes/codex.json` — partial native capabilities and their live evidence requirements.
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` — mutable-role hook readiness gate.
- `defaults/docs/guardrail-parity-codex.md` — current hook bridge covers filesystem, destructive-command and workflow policies.

Use Rust for execution-context verification and admission; keep one shared decision path.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8785 — private workspace and exclusive lease; merged in #8800.
- [x] #8786 — normal daemon launch, recovery and observability inside that workspace; merged in #8830 (`d678331b6`).
- [ ] #8839 — protected private-session guard code/policy/hook-registration boundary (Builder-discovered 2026-09-24: mid-session edits to `.loom/config.json` or the bridge disable force-push denial; mutable admission must consume this boundary).

Existing #8256/#8322 cover tool-policy infrastructure and should be reused where applicable; they are not a reason to widen this issue into a policy-engine rewrite. Required missing protection discovered during curation must be named concretely.

<!-- loom:premise-check exists=yes deliberate=yes reversal=no verdict=clear -->
premise-evidence: defaults/runtimes/codex.json — native Codex isolation remains partial pending its own evidence gate.
premise-evidence: loom-daemon/src/runtime_admission.rs:1 — mutable full sweeps intentionally require Builder capabilities.
premise-extends: add an evidence-backed containment mechanism for the explicitly selected private-clone execution context; preserve native capability truth, existing host/shared-mount refusals, and the requirement to satisfy every applicable safety obligation.

## Curator implementation handoff — 2026-09-24

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

Verified against `origin/main` at `e86b361c1`. The former dependency holds are resolved. This is a security-sensitive admission change, not a capability-manifest promotion. Keep the original acceptance criteria above as the completion contract.

### Verified corrections

- #8786 now provides `tokens_pool::private_workspace::dispatch::Selection`, which owns the selected account and exclusive lease. Preparation validates actual Docker settings/mounts/ownership and runs outside the sweep-registry lock. `transport::run` adopts the inherited open file description, checks the durable job/container identity again, and launches by container ID. Reuse these mechanisms; do not introduce a second account-selection pass.
- Capability rejection currently occurs **before** that preparation in `sweep_registry/private_dispatch.rs`; preference selection also rejects Codex using the static manifest. The worker independently repeats static admission in `worker_setup::execute`. Updating only `runtime_admission.rs` or only the shell adapter will therefore leave a broken or inconsistent path.
- `worker_setup::setup` installs the managed hook bridge, but successful installation is **not proof of hook trust or policy readiness**. It currently reports setup ready without a final trusted-hook verification. The mutable adapter preflight remains a separate enforcement obligation.
- #8256 and #8322 are still OPEN. Their proposed role-tool-policy module is absent from this build base. Existing managed guards are available; do not import assumptions about the unmerged #8314 implementation or make this issue a general role-policy rewrite.
- The session image pins Codex `0.149.1` (`docker/session/Dockerfile`), while the bridge documentation/schema pin is `0.146.0`. The implementation must document and test the supported combination instead of treating the CLI minimum version as protocol evidence. The current private transport protocol is `loom-private-workspace-v1`.

### Implementation sequence

1. Introduce an execution-specific admission context whose construction requires the validated `Selection`/lease. Keep configuration parsing, inventory checks and status probes unable to manufacture this proof. Override only the repository-isolation requirement covered by the private clone; continue checking every other role requirement and retain the static API's refusals for ordinary host/shared sessions.
2. Thread context and provenance through explicit selection, the capability-aware preference walk, scheduled roles, unlocked sweep preparation, adapter preflight and worker execution. Explicit pins never fall through. Drop rejected candidates' temporary leases/reservations; keep Docker work outside scheduler/registry locks. Revalidate the bound container, mounts, private Git root and lease immediately before execution.
3. Reconcile managed hooks narrowly. Retain verified/trusted enforcement for remote-operation and Loom-workflow policy; clone containment cannot replace those guards. No fabricated trust receipts, blanket bypass flags or environment-only containment claim. If the tested CLI/policy combination cannot enforce a required rule, return that precise unmet obligation before claiming work.
4. Record context/provenance in diagnostics and durable status without credentials or raw operator configuration. Preserve recovery ownership and the existing prohibition on automatic private account/runtime failover. Update the guardrail/private-dispatch docs and the #4496 test matrix; leave production runtime defaults unchanged.

### Obligation → mechanism to preserve and prove

| Obligation | Existing base / required work |
| --- | --- |
| Host, sibling and peer repository isolation | Actual Docker mount/security inspection, private named volume and independent Git root, exclusive account/volume ownership. Bind this evidence to admission and recheck at launch. |
| Exclusive writer and stale-context refusal | Owned lease descriptor plus durable job/container identity; preserve #8786 cancellation/recovery behavior and test preflight-to-launch changes. |
| Protected remote operations | Managed destructive-command policy, or another demonstrated enforceable mechanism. Docker/network availability alone is insufficient. Verify protected remote refs remain unchanged after denied force-push/deletion attempts. |
| Loom lifecycle controls | Retain managed workflow guards for merge/helper and control mutations. Private `run-job` refusal and MCP/plugin/profile audit already restrict host control; preserve them. |
| Credential boundary | External per-account profile, narrow selected mounts/environment and redacted outputs. The selected profile and forge access remain sensitive; prove peer profiles and exported records cannot expose credentials. |
| Control/guard integrity | The clone is writable and its current helpers/bridge resolve inside it. Before relying on that bridge for admission, demonstrate how edits to policy/config/guard files cannot silently disable required enforcement; refuse an unproven path. |
| Secondary mutation channels | Cover shell, patch and helper calls through the actual launch. Preserve denial of unsupported channels such as `write_stdin`; MCP/plugin/control audit is not permission to introduce another unguarded executor. |

### Affected files / test entry points

All existing on the verified build base; new verifier modules may be added beside these:

- `loom-daemon/src/runtime_admission.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/runtime_preference.rs` and `runtime_preference/resolve.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/runtime_preflight.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/private_dispatch.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/tokens_pool/private_workspace/{dispatch,transport,worker_setup,control,docker,lease,export}.rs`
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` and the existing managed hook/provisioning boundary
- `loom-daemon/tests/private_workspace_docker.rs` and its `dispatch.rs`/`auth.rs` fixtures
- `defaults/docs/guardrail-parity-codex.md`, `defaults/docs/private-session-dispatch.md`, `docker/session/Dockerfile` (version contract reference)

### Verification plan

- Shared Rust admission tests: Builder/Doctor/sweep-lifecycle, unchanged read roles, an additional unmet capability, missing proof, explicit Codex refusal without fallback, and Claude → verified Codex → Z.ai preference selection. No promotion of global partial capabilities.
- Disposable Docker tests through production `SweepRegistry::dispatch_unlocked` and `ScriptRoleInvocationRunner`, then the real adapters/supervisor/worker: allowed issue edit/commit/push plus required denied operations above. Do not substitute a synthetic freeform selection for actual mutable-role admission.
- Negative variants: host/shared Git/mount, peer profile or volume attachment, busy lease, changed/replaced container, stale/missing identity and mutation between preparation and launch. Assert refusal before model/claim where appropriate and inspect filesystem/remote refs afterwards.
- Reuse the complete Linux daemon and existing UID-1000/public-source CI fixture. Run Docker tests with their normal parallel execution as well as focused failures; preserve profile permissions. All credentials/remotes/accounts must be disposable synthetic fixtures.
- Check structural/shell/version gates, relevant Rust tests and Clippy, then PR CI and the required post-merge gate. Real authenticated daemon-dispatched lifecycle evidence remains #4496, after disposable success; CI does not establish the production go/no-go.

issues.title: Record cumulative dispatch-paused time attributable to drain-and-restart rolls, per host per day
issues.body:
## Context

Split out of #8514 (AC #4), which shipped the other three acceptance criteria:
supersede-not-stack for an overtaken pending roll, the live `drain.roll` status
fields, and a documented per-path worst-case-pause decision. This is the one
remaining criterion from that issue's revised list:

> The cumulative dispatch-paused time attributable to rolls is queryable per host
> per day — scope during implementation whether this is a new live counter or an
> aggregation over the existing `daemon.drain.*` event-bus history.

#8514 deliberately left it out because, unlike the other three, **neither of the
two suggested implementations is correct as suggested** — both lose exactly the
data they are meant to measure. That needs its own design decision, not a
tacked-on counter.

## Why the two suggested approaches do not work as-is

| Suggested approach | Why it loses the data |
|---|---|
| A new live counter (e.g. `paused_today_secs` on `DrainState`) | A **successful** roll ends by restarting the daemon process. An in-memory counter is zeroed by the very event that closes the pause interval it is accumulating, so the counter systematically under-reports: it can only ever see pauses that ended in an *abort*, a *refusal-abandon*, or a #8514 *supersede* — never a pause that actually completed its roll. |
| Aggregating `daemon.drain.*` event-bus history | The event bus is an in-memory ring buffer (`loom-daemon/src/event_bus.rs`), so it has the same restart-amnesia problem *plus* eviction: on a busy host the drain events that bound a multi-hour pause can be evicted by unrelated sweep traffic before anything reads them. |

## Proposed approach: a small persisted per-day ledger

Follow the precedent already set by `ArtifactRollRecord` in
`loom-daemon/src/auto_update.rs` — a small JSON file next to it, "persisted so it
survives the restart the roll itself performs".

- A `PausedLedger` (suggested home: `loom-daemon/src/ipc/drain_ledger.rs`, next to
  #8514's `drain_roll.rs`) holding a `BTreeMap<NaiveDate, u64>` of UTC-day →
  paused seconds, loaded on daemon start and written on each transition.
- `record(started_at, ended_at)` must **split an interval across UTC midnight**
  rather than attributing the whole pause to the day it ended — a 2h budget
  starting at 23:10Z straddles two days.
- The **in-progress** pause must be included in "today" when queried, otherwise a
  host currently sitting paused reports `0` for the thing being asked about.
  Reuse #8514's `drain_roll::paused_secs()` for the live portion.
- Retention: keep a bounded window (suggest 30 days) and prune on write, so the
  file cannot grow without bound.

### Restart-boundary correctness (the part that needs care)

A pause that ends in a successful roll ends with the process exiting. The interval
must be closed **before** `EXIT_RESTART` is returned, not after — i.e. at the
supervisor's restart decision point, not in a `Drop`. Equally, a daemon killed
mid-pause (SIGKILL, host reboot) leaves an open interval; on the next start the
ledger should reconcile it rather than dropping it silently or double-counting it
on a later close. Persisting `started_at` of the open interval alongside the daily
totals is enough to do this.

### Writes must never be able to affect the fail-safe

`DrainState`'s transition bookkeeping is #6007's fail-safe state machine, and an
earlier simpler form of it deadlocked the work finder. The ledger is purely
observational: a write failure must be logged and swallowed, and nothing in
`drain_refusal_decision` / `refuse_roll_deadline` / `abort` may ever *read* it.
Keep it strictly write-side.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cumulative dispatch-paused seconds attributable to drain-and-restart rolls
      are recorded per UTC day and survive the daemon restart a successful roll
      performs.
- [ ] An interval spanning UTC midnight is attributed to both days in the correct
      proportion, not wholly to one.
- [ ] A query made *while* a pause is in progress includes the elapsed portion of
      that pause in today's total.
- [ ] The totals are queryable from `loom-daemon status --json` (suggested:
      `drain.paused_by_day`, alongside #8514's `drain.roll`) and rendered in the
      text status.
- [ ] Ledger writes cannot fail a drain transition; a corrupt/unreadable ledger
      file degrades to "start a fresh ledger + WARN", never a panic or a refused
      drain.
- [ ] Retention is bounded and pruned on write.

## Affected files

- `loom-daemon/src/ipc/drain_roll.rs` — #8514's live projection; `paused_secs()`
  is the live-portion helper to reuse.
- `loom-daemon/src/ipc.rs` — `DrainState`'s transition points (`begin`, `abort`,
  `refuse_and_resume`, `refuse_roll_deadline`'s `Abandoned` arm) are where
  intervals open and close.
- `loom-daemon/src/auto_update.rs` — `ArtifactRollRecord` is the persistence
  precedent (location + atomic-write shape to copy).
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/status_render/drain_render.rs` — #8514's `drain_json` /
  `roll_line`; the new totals belong in the same block.
- `loom-daemon/src/types.rs` — `DaemonStatusReport` (add the field
  `#[serde(default)]`, as `drain_roll` is).
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` — the drain/roll section #8514 extended.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests for the midnight-splitting arithmetic, including an interval
      spanning more than one full day.
- [ ] A round-trip test: write a ledger, reload it, assert totals survive.
- [ ] A test asserting an in-progress pause is included in today's total and that
      the total advances between two queries.
- [ ] A test asserting an unreadable/corrupt ledger file yields a fresh ledger and
      does not fail the drain transition.
- [ ] Status JSON/text tests asserting the new field renders and is absent-safe
      from a pre-change daemon.

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Dependencies

- [x] #8514 / its implementing PR #8660: merged 2026-09-25 (PR #8660) — `loom-daemon/src/ipc/drain_roll.rs` and `paused_secs()` now exist on `origin/main`, verified — it introduces `loom-daemon/src/ipc/drain_roll.rs` and `paused_secs()`, which this issue's ledger design reuses for the live (in-progress) portion of the pause total.

Dependency resolved — verified against `origin/main` 2026-09-25 (fetch & symbol check): `drain_roll.rs`, `paused_secs()`, `ArtifactRollRecord`, `DrainState::begin/abort/refuse_roll_deadline`, and `status_render/drain_render.rs` all present. Ready for implementation.

issues.title: feat(dispatch): repository affinity and track-focused dispatch with cross-repo CI interleaving
issues.body:
## Original Issue

### Problem Statement
With ~40 repos across the fleet, Loom's global work-finder frequently scatters dispatches across too many repositories at once. Within a single repo, spawning multiple concurrent branches across related files leads to merge conflicts, continuous rebasing against `main`, and long intervals before returning to dependent issues.

### Proposed Solution
Implement **Repository Locality & Track Affinity** in `work_finder::candidate_cmp`:

### Key Requirements
1. **Intra-Repo Focus (Track Locality):**
   - Cap active concurrent builder sweeps per repository (e.g. max 1–2 concurrent branches per repo) to prevent intra-repo rebase storms.
   - When an issue in an active epic/track completes, prioritize its immediate downstream dependent issue in the same repo before context-switching away.
2. **Inter-Repo CI Interleaving:**
   - While Repo A is waiting for CI checks or Judge review to complete, dispatch workers to Repo B or Repo C.
   - When Repo A's PR merges or requires follow-up, re-engage Repo A immediately to maintain momentum.
3. **Reduced Rebase Overhead:**
   - Minimizes the time between branch creation and merge, keeping PRs close to the base tip and eliminating freshness guard staleness loops (#8919).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `work_finder` enforces configurable per-repo concurrency caps (`maxConcurrentPerRepo`).
- [ ] Comparator prioritizes sequential issues within an active repo track over cold context switches.
- [ ] Interleaves sweeps across repos during CI wait windows without idling fleet workers.


---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

### Problem Statement

The global work-finder fills **one shared concurrency budget** in a single
globally-sorted order, with no notion of how many sweeps a given repo already
has in flight. `tick_multi_with_caps` seeds `occupancy` as the *sum* of every
dispatcher's occupancy (`work_finder.rs:1894`) and then dispatches while
`occupancy < max_concurrent` — so nothing stops the whole budget landing in one
repo when that repo happens to own the top-sorted candidates. Concurrent
branches within a repo then race the same `main` tip, which is where the rebase
churn and freshness-guard staleness loops come from.

`candidate_cmp` (`work_finder.rs:620`) is a pure 4-key total order —
`(workspace_priority asc, urgent first, createdAt asc, number asc)` — with no
input from dispatcher state.

### Scope correction: three requirements, three different verdicts

The three Key Requirements in the original issue are **not** equally well
founded. Verified against `origin/main` @ `baea639f`, 2026-09-26:

**1. Per-repo cap — real, and the substance of this issue.** No per-repo
concurrency bound exists anywhere in `loom-daemon/src/` (`grep -rn
'per_repo\|perRepo\|max_per_repo' loom-daemon/src/` returns only
`RepoStatus`/token-pool hits, nothing in the admission path). Build this.

**2. "Comparator prioritizes sequential issues in an active repo track" — real,
but the stated design does not fit the code.** Track affinity needs to know
*which repos are currently active*, which is dispatcher state, not candidate
state. Putting it inside `candidate_cmp` would mean either threading live
occupancy into a pure comparator or perturbing a documented total order that
has existing ordering tests. See Implementation Guidance for the partition-based
alternative, which reuses an established pattern instead.

**3. "Interleave to Repo B/C while Repo A waits on CI" — already emergent
behaviour; do NOT build a mechanism for it.** The #4123 open-PR guard already
makes an issue whose PR is in flight a non-candidate: `dispatch()` returns
`OpenPrDispatchError`, the finder records `Qd::OpenPr` / `skipped_pr_open` and
moves to the next candidate in global order, which is by construction some other
repo's work (`work_finder.rs:2262-2276`). Re-engagement on merge is likewise
automatic — the issue closes, the next dependent issue becomes eligible on the
following tick (default 60s, `DEFAULT_WORK_FINDER_INTERVAL_SECS`,
`work_finder.rs:160`). **Acceptance criterion 3 is satisfied by existing
behaviour.** The Builder should verify this with a test that pins it, not add a
second interleaving path.

### Suspected Cause (unverified)

The original issue attributes rebase churn to intra-repo dispatch concurrency.
That is plausible and matches the mechanism above, but **it has not been
measured** — no one has correlated observed rebase/staleness events against
concurrent-sweep-per-repo counts. A Builder who instruments this and finds the
dominant cause is elsewhere (e.g. `main` merge rate alone, independent of
per-repo sweep count) has produced a complete, successful outcome and should say
so rather than forcing a cap onto a mechanism measurement rules out.

### Interaction with #9060 / PR #9066 (read before starting)

#9060 (**raising** the global ceiling, implemented in the open PR #9066) and this
issue (**adding** a narrower per-repo ceiling) pull in opposite directions but
compose cleanly: the per-repo cap is a second, independent brake, exactly as
`deferred_ramp_cap` is independent of `deferred_capacity`. Two constraints
follow:

- **Do not start until #9066 merges.** It rewrites the `configured_max`
  resolution path and adds `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/configured_max.rs`;
  starting now guarantees a conflict in `work_finder.rs`.
- **`maxConcurrentPerRepo` must resolve on the same hot-reload path #9066
  establishes**, not as a startup-frozen value. A per-repo cap that needs a
  daemon restart to retune reintroduces precisely the defect #9060 exists to
  remove.

### Implementation Guidance

**Use the #6243 repo-sharding partition as the template, not the comparator.**
`tick_multi_with_caps` already partitions the *already-sorted* candidate list by
repo and preserves each partition's relative order (`work_finder.rs:2186-2206`),
with an explicit **work-conservation** fallback: when the preferred partition is
empty it falls back to the deferred one rather than idling. Both the per-repo cap
and track affinity belong at that layer.

**Per-repo cap (requirement 1).** Add a second counter to pass 2's dispatch loop
alongside the existing `occupancy` / `admitted_this_tick` pair:

- Seed a per-workspace occupancy map from each dispatcher's **own**
  `WorkDispatcher::occupancy()` — already per-repo, and already the value
  `tick_multi_with_caps` sums for its global seed (`work_finder.rs:1894`). No new
  forge reads.
- Defer (never drop) a candidate whose repo is at its cap, incrementing it on
  each successful dispatch exactly as `occupancy` is at `work_finder.rs:2250`.
- Add `QueueDisposition::DeferredRepoCap` and `TickReport::deferred_repo_cap` so
  the deferral is visible in the ready-queue view instead of silently vanishing —
  mirror `DeferredOutOfSlice`, which is documented as "purely observational"
  (`work_finder.rs:1094-1098`).

**Default must be `None` (uncapped).** The issue proposes "default: 1–2". A
non-`None` default silently throttles every existing fleet on upgrade — a repo
running 5 concurrent sweeps today would drop to 1–2 with no operator action.
Follow `extra_skip_labels` and `preferred_slice`, both of which default to a
no-op, and make this opt-in. Changing the shipped default is an operator call,
not a Builder one.

**Track affinity (requirement 2).** After the existing sort and slice partition,
apply a stable partition that floats candidates whose repo already has a live
sweep ahead of cold repos, preserving relative order within each group. Keep
`candidate_cmp` untouched so its ordering tests stay valid. This must be
subordinate to the per-repo cap — affinity decides *ordering*, the cap decides
*admission* — or the two fight and affinity wins, defeating requirement 1.

**Starvation is the main risk.** A per-repo cap plus affinity can strand a
low-priority repo indefinitely. The work-conservation rule from #6243 is the
guard: if applying the cap leaves zero admissible candidates while candidates
exist, admit in the original global order rather than idling the fleet.

### Affected Files

Verified present on `origin/main` @ `baea639f`, 2026-09-26.

- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` — `WorkFinderConfig` (~:2409) gains
  `max_concurrent_per_repo`; `read_work_finder_config` (~:2452) parses
  `autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrentPerRepo` with the same soft-fail /
  zero-is-absent contract as `max_concurrent`; pass 2 (~:2216-2250) gains the
  per-repo counter and deferral; the partition step (~:2186) gains the affinity
  pass.
- `loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs` — new `QueueDisposition::DeferredRepoCap`
  variant.
- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/tests.rs` — multi-repo dispatch tests (see Test
  Plan).
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` — config-key table (~:4168 documents
  `autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrent`; add the sibling key) and the dispatch
  cap narrative (~:3029).
- `defaults/docs/dispatcher-repo-sharding.md` — the #6243 doc this feature's
  partition sits next to; state how the two compose.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: per-repo cap bounds admissions — a queue of N candidates all in
      one repo with `maxConcurrentPerRepo = 1` admits exactly 1 and records
      `deferred_repo_cap` for the rest, with the global cap non-binding.
- [ ] Automated: the seed is honoured — a repo already at its cap via
      `WorkDispatcher::occupancy()` admits 0 new sweeps this tick.
- [ ] Automated: `None` is a no-op — with no `maxConcurrentPerRepo` configured,
      admissions are byte-identical to today (guards the upgrade path).
- [ ] Automated: work conservation — when the cap leaves zero admissible
      candidates but candidates exist, the fleet does not idle.
- [ ] Automated: track affinity orders an active repo's next issue ahead of a
      cold repo's, **without** exceeding the per-repo cap.
- [ ] Automated: `candidate_cmp`'s existing ordering tests still pass unmodified
      (the comparator must not be perturbed).
- [ ] Automated: pins requirement 3's existing behaviour — a candidate whose repo
      has an open linked PR is skipped as `Qd::OpenPr` and the next dispatch goes
      to another repo.
- [ ] Manual: `cargo test -p loom-daemon work_finder` and
      `cargo clippy -p loom-daemon -- -D warnings` pass.
- [ ] Edge cases: single-workspace `tick` unaffected; `maxConcurrentPerRepo`
      greater than `maxConcurrent` is harmless; a zero value is treated as absent,
      never as a cap of 0 (which would deadlock the repo).

## Dependencies

- [x] #9060: the zero-downtime `maxConcurrent` tuning work, implemented by the
      open PR #9066 (`feature/zero-downtime-tuning`). #9066 rewrites the
      `configured_max` resolution path in `work_finder.rs` and adds
      `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/configured_max.rs`. Building this issue
      before it lands guarantees a conflict in `work_finder.rs`, and
      `maxConcurrentPerRepo` must resolve on the hot-reload path #9066
      establishes rather than as a startup-frozen value.

**Cleared 2026-09-26**: PR #9066 merged (`a6feb8c2` on `main`). The
sequencing blocker is gone and this issue is ready to build.

## Verified corrections

- **2026-09-26, verified against `origin/main` @ `baea639f`** (`grep -rn
  'per_repo\|perRepo\|max_per_repo' loom-daemon/src/`): no per-repo concurrency
  cap exists in the admission path today; the only matches are `RepoStatus` and
  token-pool fields. Requirement 1 is genuinely unimplemented.
- **2026-09-26, verified against `origin/main` @ `baea639f`** (read
  `work_finder.rs:589-627`): `candidate_cmp` is a pure 4-key total order and
  `PriorityCandidate` carries `workspace_idx` but no liveness/in-flight field.
  The issue's "prioritize in candidate_cmp" framing cannot be implemented
  without either threading dispatcher state into the comparator or changing the
  documented order — hence the partition-based alternative above.
- **2026-09-26, verified against `origin/main` @ `baea639f`** (read
  `work_finder.rs:2262-2276`): the #4123 open-PR guard already skips a candidate
  whose PR is in flight (`Qd::OpenPr` / `skipped_pr_open`) and proceeds to the
  next candidate in global order. Acceptance criterion 3 describes existing
  behaviour, not new work.
- **2026-09-26, inferred, NOT measured**: the causal link from intra-repo
  dispatch concurrency to the observed rebase/staleness churn is the original
  issue's hypothesis. No measurement correlating concurrent-sweeps-per-repo with
  rebase events was performed during curation.

- **2026-09-26, re-verified after PR #9066 merged, against `origin/main` @
  `a6feb8c2`**: the hot-reload path this issue must follow now exists as
  `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/configured_max.rs` —
  `ConfiguredMaxReloader::refresh()` (`:114`) re-resolves the ceiling from the
  primary workspace every multi-workspace tick. `maxConcurrentPerRepo` should
  resolve through that same module rather than a startup-frozen value. All six
  files in Affected Files re-confirmed present on `a6feb8c2`; the `~:` line
  hints in that section were taken at `baea639f` and have shifted, so treat
  them as locators, not line numbers.

issues.title: Unify the two wildcard rules in the per-role tool restriction: spawn-claude's substring test fails open where spawn-codex's exact match fails closed
issues.body:
## Problem

The per-role tool-restriction control (#8256) has **two different definitions of "wildcard"**, one per consumer, and they disagree in a direction that fails **open** on the enforcing path.

- **`spawn-claude.sh`** space-joins the declared capabilities and tests `[[ "$caps" != *"*"* ]]` — a **substring** test. Any element merely *containing* `*` disables the restriction entirely.
- **`spawn-codex.sh`** asks jq for `(.toolPolicy.allowedCapabilities | index("*")) | not` — an **exact element** match. Only a literal `"*"` element disables it.

They diverge on exactly one input shape: a declared capability that **contains** `*` without **being** `*` — say `"cloud-*"`.

| Declared allowlist | `spawn-claude.sh` | `spawn-codex.sh` |
|---|---|---|
| `["*"]` | unrestricted | unrestricted |
| `["cloud-cli"]` | restricted (28 deny specs) | restricted |
| `["cloud-*"]` | **unrestricted — 0 deny specs** | **restricted** |

PR #8939 (landing #8322's daemon port) faithfully mirrors both rather than quietly unifying them — `RoleToolPolicy::deny_specs()` follows Claude's substring rule, `is_restricted()` follows Codex's exact rule — and pins the difference with `the_two_wildcard_rules_diverge_only_on_a_star_bearing_substring`. That was the right call for a port (unifying inside a port would be a silent behaviour change to a security control), but it means the divergence now exists in **three** places instead of two, and the decision is still open.

## Why the `["cloud-*"]` row matters

`cloud-*` is not a capability name. The namespace is exactly four literals: `remote-shell`, `cloud-cli`, `forge-secrets`, `credential-store`. An unknown string is documented as **inert** — "an unknown string in `allowedCapabilities` is inert, never a wildcard."

Except on the Claude path it is not inert. It is a **full disarm**. A role author who reasonably writes `"cloud-*"` expecting glob semantics, or who typos a name containing `*`, silently turns off every restriction for that role on the `--disallowedTools` path — and gets the opposite answer on the Codex path. The failure is silent in both directions: no warning, no log line, and the two runtimes disagree about the same role file.

This is the inverse of the intended posture. The module doc for the port states the control "fails open on identity, closed on capability" — a glob-looking capability name should fail **closed** (inert, restriction stands), which is what the Codex rule already does.

## Why now is the cheap moment

**The divergence is currently latent.** Verified during #8322's build: all 12 `defaults/roles/*.json` on `origin/main` declare no `toolPolicy` at all, so every role resolves to *undeclared* (unrestricted) and neither rule is reachable in production today. Blast radius for changing it is **zero right now** and grows the moment the first role declares an allowlist — which is exactly what #8256 is for.

There is also a natural sequencing point. Once PR #8314's deferred Doctor pass wires both `spawn-claude.sh` and `spawn-codex.sh` to call `loom-daemon role-tool-policy` (the call-out shape #8939 provides), the two shell implementations **disappear** and there is exactly one place left to decide the rule. Deciding it at that moment costs one line; deciding it later means re-auditing three implementations and any role files written in the meantime.

## What to explore

1. **Pick one rule.** The recommendation from the evidence above is the **exact-element** rule (`index("*")`, Codex's): it makes an unknown-but-star-bearing string inert, matching the documented intent, and it fails closed. Confirm there is no consumer that genuinely needs substring semantics.
2. **Decide whether glob support is wanted at all.** If `"cloud-*"` *should* mean "every capability with the `cloud-` prefix", that is a feature, not a wildcard rule — and it should be implemented deliberately (prefix match against the four-name namespace) rather than falling out of a substring test. Explicitly rejecting glob support is also a fine answer; it just needs to be the recorded one.
3. **Make a malformed capability name loud.** Whatever rule wins, a declared capability outside the four-name namespace is a role-file authoring error. Consider warning on it rather than silently treating it as inert — a silent inert string and a silent full disarm are both bad, in opposite directions.
4. **Sequence with #8314.** Unification is cheapest as part of the Doctor pass that deletes the shell implementations. Until then, #8939's pinning test is the correct holding position.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One wildcard rule, defined once, used by both the `--disallowedTools` spec path and the Codex restriction-check path.
- [ ] A declared capability containing `*` without being `*` produces the same verdict on both paths.
- [ ] The chosen semantics for an unknown / glob-shaped capability name are documented in the module doc and in the role-JSON schema docs.
- [ ] `the_two_wildcard_rules_diverge_only_on_a_star_bearing_substring` is replaced by a test asserting the **unified** behaviour (not deleted silently).
- [ ] If the rule changes from what `spawn-claude.sh` does today, the change is called out as a deliberate behaviour change to a security control, with the reasoning recorded here.

## Notes

Surfaced by the Builder on #8322 while porting the logic to `loom-daemon` (PR #8939), which deliberately preserved both rules and named the difference rather than unifying it mid-port. Filed as the follow-up that decision implies.

Related: #8256 (the security control itself), PR #8314 (the shell implementations, currently the only place they exist), #8322 / PR #8939 (the daemon port that now mirrors both).

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Verified correction (2026-09-26, verified against `origin/main` @ `529485ced`)

The shell implementations this issue describes (`spawn-claude.sh`'s substring test, `spawn-codex.sh`'s `index("*")` test) are **not present on `origin/main` today** — they exist only on the unmerged branch behind PR #8314 (still `OPEN`, `loom:changes-requested`+`loom:treating`+`loom:ci-failure`; `git show origin/main:defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh | grep -c allowedCapabilities` → `0`). The daemon port (`loom-daemon/src/role_tool_policy.rs`), landed via merge train #8996 (from PR #8939/#8322), **is** on `origin/main` and already contains *both* divergent rules internally: `has_spawn_claude_wildcard()` (substring, backs `denied_capabilities()`/`deny_specs()`) and `is_restricted()` (exact-element match).

Practical effect: this issue's "the divergence now exists in three places" framing describes a future state, not today's build base. **Today there is exactly one place** carrying the divergence — this single Rust file — so a Builder dispatched into a fresh worktree off `origin/main` can satisfy every acceptance criterion below without touching any shell script. This also weakens "What to explore" item 4's sequencing rationale ("cheapest ... as part of the Doctor pass that deletes the shell implementations"): since the shell files don't carry this logic on `main` yet, there is no "three implementations to re-audit" today regardless of when #8314 lands — unifying now costs no more than unifying later, and removes one thing to track. This isn't a mandate to jump the sequencing call in "What to explore" item 4, just evidence that waiting buys nothing extra beyond what's already true (blast radius is zero either way — verified none of the 12 `defaults/roles/*.json` on `origin/main` declare a `toolPolicy`).

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/role_tool_policy.rs` — `has_spawn_claude_wildcard()` (substring rule), `is_restricted()` (exact-match rule), `denied_capabilities()` (consumes the substring rule), `deny_specs()`; the module doc's "The one deliberate asymmetry: two wildcard rules" section
- `loom-daemon/src/role_tool_policy/tests.rs` — `the_two_wildcard_rules_diverge_only_on_a_star_bearing_substring`, to be replaced per AC4 (not deleted silently), plus any new tests for the unified behaviour and the chosen unknown/glob-shaped-capability semantics
- No role-JSON schema doc exists yet under `defaults/docs/` or `.loom/docs/` mentioning `allowedCapabilities`/`toolPolicy` (verified: no matches repo-wide) — AC3's "documented ... in the role-JSON schema docs" likely means adding a new doc section rather than editing an existing one; check whether #8256/#8314 is already adding one before creating a duplicate
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh`, `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` — **not on `origin/main`** as of this curation pass (pending PR #8314); out of scope for this issue's Builder unless #8314 has merged by the time this is picked up (re-check before starting)

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: replace `the_two_wildcard_rules_diverge_only_on_a_star_bearing_substring` with a test asserting the unified rule for a `["cloud-*"]`-style declaration (both the deny-specs path and `is_restricted()` agree)
- [ ] Automated tests: add/extend cases for an unknown-but-star-bearing capability under the chosen semantics (inert vs. glob-prefix-match, per "What to explore" item 2)
- [ ] Automated tests: if a malformed/out-of-namespace capability now warns (per "What to explore" item 3), add a test asserting the warning fires
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon role_tool_policy` passes
- [ ] Manual verification: N/A — behavior is fully covered by the Rust unit tests above; no live host or session needed

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

**Why `complex`, not `routine`**: this is a security control (per-role tool restriction guarding against a persuaded read-only role reaching `ssh`/`aws`/`gh` secrets, #8256) where picking the wrong default on a glob-shaped capability name (fail-open vs. fail-closed) is exactly the kind of mistake that could pass tests and review unnoticed. The issue itself frames the resolution as open design questions (which rule wins, whether glob support is wanted, whether to warn), not a single obvious fix.

issues.title: merge-pr.sh: no way to choose the merge method (always squashes when squash is allowed)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Seen with loom-daemon 0.19.338 (d678331b6).

### Problem

`forge_detect_merge_method` always picks `squash` when the repo allows
squash. A caller can't ask for a merge commit on one PR, for example when a PR
carries commits whose SHAs other files reference, such as generated reports
that record the revision they were produced at. Squashing leaves those SHAs unreachable once
the branch is deleted. The workaround today is to disable squash in the repo
settings for the duration of the merge.

**Suggested fix:**

- add a `--merge-method squash|merge|rebase` flag, validated against the repo's
  allowed methods;
- and/or support a repo-level default in `.loom/config.json`;
- and/or support a PR label such as `loom:merge-commit`.

Related: #8191.

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Verified: the claim is accurate (2026-09-25, verified against `origin/main`)

`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-merge-method.sh:39-65` (`forge_detect_merge_method`)
has a fixed preference order — squash > merge > rebase — with no parameter or
env var to request a specific method, and `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh:461`
calls it unconditionally:

```bash
REPO_MERGE_METHOD="$(forge_detect_merge_method "$REPO_NWO" "$GH" 2>/dev/null || echo squash)"
```

`REPO_MERGE_METHOD` then flows into both the immediate-merge path
(`forge_merge_pr`, `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:347`) and the
`--auto` path (`forge_auto_merge` / `loom-daemon forge auto-merge`) with no
override anywhere in between. `forge_merge_pr` itself already accepts an
explicit `merge_method` parameter (line 348: `local ... merge_method="${4:-squash}"`)
— the missing piece is entirely at the call site: nothing ever passes anything
other than the auto-detected value.

**No PR-level or config-level override exists today** — confirmed no
`mergeMethod` key anywhere in `.loom/config.json`/`defaults/config*`, and no
`loom:merge-commit` (or similar) label in `.github/labels.yml`.

### Blocking implementation constraint: this repo forbids new shell logic here (read before implementing)

Both files this fix touches are frozen `contract`-category shell
(`scripts/shell-allowlist.txt:204-225`): *"the file's name is consumed by role
prompts, CI, or hooks... **contract is baseline-only**"* — the CI-enforced
Language Policy (`.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md` §"contract") **refuses
new logic in a `contract` file outright**, not just growth past a line
threshold. `merge-pr.sh`'s own allowlist entry says it plainly: *"The name
stays; new logic goes behind it into loom-daemon."* This exact class of
mistake — implementing a real feature as new bash in one of these files — is
what stalled #8654 and #8850 in this same repo; do not repeat it here.

**Implication for the fix**: the actual decision logic — "does the repo allow
the requested method; if not, what do we fall back to" — must be a
`loom-daemon` subcommand (e.g. extend `loom-daemon forge auto-merge`'s
existing `--method` handling, or add a new `loom-daemon forge merge-method
--repo <nwo> [--requested <method>]` that returns the resolved method,
validated against the repo's `allow_squash_merge`/`allow_merge_commit`/
`allow_rebase_merge` flags exactly as `forge_detect_merge_method` does today).
`merge-pr.sh` gets only thin CLI-flag wiring — parse `--merge-method`, pass it
to the daemon call, keep today's shell `forge_detect_merge_method` as the
no-daemon/below-version-floor fallback (same "delegate when available, current
behavior otherwise" pattern `loom_daemon_version_preflight` already
establishes elsewhere in this file). This also rides on rather than fights
#8191 (the umbrella epic porting `merge-pr.sh` to a daemon subcommand
entirely).

**Do not add a `loom:merge-commit` label.** This repo's Curator/CLAUDE.md
policy is to never invent new labels — pursue the CLI flag and/or config
default instead; drop that option from scope.

### Suggested precedence (design decision, not fully settled)

Explicit `--merge-method` CLI flag > `.loom/config.json` per-repo default >
today's auto-detect (squash > merge > rebase). Whichever is requested must
still be validated against the repo's actual allowed methods and fail
predictably (error, not silent fallback) if the requested method isn't
permitted — silently falling back to squash would reproduce exactly the bug
this issue reports, just with an extra ignored flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A caller can request `merge` or `rebase` explicitly (CLI flag and/or
      `.loom/config.json` per-repo default) and `merge-pr.sh` uses it instead
      of the auto-detected method, for both the immediate-merge and `--auto`
      paths.
- [ ] Requesting a method the target repo does not allow fails with a clear
      error naming the allowed methods — it does not silently fall back to
      squash.
- [ ] No request (today's behavior) is unchanged: falls back to the existing
      auto-detect preference order (squash > merge > rebase).
- [ ] The validation/resolution logic lives in a `loom-daemon` subcommand, not
      new logic in `forge-merge-method.sh`/`forge-helpers.sh`/`merge-pr.sh`
      (all three are frozen `contract`-category shell) — `scripts/check-file-size-budget.sh`
      and `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` both pass.
- [ ] No new label is introduced.

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` (`merge-pr.sh:461` where `REPO_MERGE_METHOD`
  is resolved, plus its arg-parsing block around `:493`) - add `--merge-method`
  CLI flag parsing (thin wiring only — delegates to the daemon, falls back to
  today's `forge_detect_merge_method` when no daemon/below version floor)
- `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-merge-method.sh` - reference only; the shell
  fallback path stays as today's implementation, not extended with new
  validation logic
- `loom-daemon/src/forge_cmd.rs` - new or extended subcommand: resolve +
  validate a requested merge method against the repo's allowed strategies
  (mirrors `forge_detect_merge_method`'s GitHub/Gitea branches); `--method` on
  the existing `auto-merge` subcommand (`:526`) is the nearest existing
  surface to extend or model this on
- `.loom/config.json` schema / `.loom/config.example.json` (if a config
  default is chosen) - new optional per-repo `mergeMethod` key
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-helpers.sh` (`:504-549` already covers
  `forge_detect_merge_method`'s auto-detect behavior) - add cases for an
  explicit requested method that is/isn't allowed
- New or extended `loom-daemon` Rust test module covering the new
  subcommand's validation logic

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: `loom-daemon` unit tests for the new merge-method
      resolution/validation subcommand — requested method allowed, requested
      method not allowed (clear error), no request (auto-detect unchanged)
- [ ] Automated tests: extend `test-forge-helpers.sh` / add a
      `test-merge-pr-*.sh` case exercising `--merge-method` end-to-end against
      a stubbed `gh`/daemon
- [ ] Manual verification: `./.loom/scripts/merge-pr.sh <pr> --merge-method merge --dry-run`
      against a repo that allows merge commits shows the requested method, not
      squash
- [ ] Manual verification: requesting a disallowed method fails with a clear
      error rather than silently squashing
- [ ] Edge cases: repo with only one strategy allowed; repo allowing all
      three; no-daemon / below-version-floor host falls back to today's
      behavior unchanged

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `mechanical`**: choosing where the validation logic lives
(new vs. extended daemon subcommand) and the CLI-flag/config precedence order
takes a small design decision, but a wrong choice is caught mechanically by
this repo's shell-budget/file-size CI gates (which already stalled two other
issues for exactly this mistake) — it will not silently pass review. Not
`complex`: no destructive path, no cross-cutting change, and `forge_merge_pr`
already accepts an explicit `merge_method` parameter, so the plumbing gap is
narrow.

issues.title: merge-pr.sh: #8248 freshness guard hard-blocks every merge when the rulesets API returns 403 (private free-plan repos)
issues.body:
Seen with loom-daemon 0.19.338 (d678331b6).

## Problem

On a private repository owned by a GitHub Free account or org,
`loom-daemon merge-pr stale-checks` calls
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/<base>`, and GitHub answers:

    HTTP 403: Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.

The guard fails closed (exit 2), so `merge-pr.sh` refuses **every** merge on
such repos. No flag bypasses it: `--allow-unapproved` and
`--redate-stale-checks` don't apply, and the only escape is to point
`LOOM_DAEMON_BIN` at a shim.

On these plans, rulesets and branch protection are unavailable, so nothing can
be a *required* check. The guard's question has a definite answer: "no
required checks, nothing can be stale."

**Suggested fix:** treat this specific 403 ("Upgrade to GitHub Pro …") as "no
rulesets / no required checks" and return CLEAN, perhaps with a warning. Keep
failing closed for other errors (network, auth scope, rate limit).
Alternatively, add a documented operator flag such as
`--skip-freshness-guard` that records a bypass comment, the way
`--allow-unapproved` does.

Related: #8191 (port merge-pr.sh to a daemon subcommand).

```
assertion `left == right` failed: corpus[0] gh_rc=0 PreMerge { conflicted: false, open_before_merge: true }: the port disagrees with the retired shell. Input: "{\"number\":123,\"state\":\"open\",\"labels\":[{\"name\":\"loom:building\"},{\"name\":\"loom:epic\"}]}"
  left: "INFO\tPartial-increment reset: PR #999 merged as a partial slice of #123; returning it to the ready queue\nSWAP\n"
 right: "INFO\tPartial-increment reset: issue #123 is not loom:building — skipping (idempotent)\n"
```

This is **not** related to PR #9276's diff (which only touches `merge_pr::worktree_preserve` and its own tests) — `merge_pr_partial_reset_differential.rs` and the module it exercises (`merge_pr::partial_reset`) were untouched by that PR.

Same commit's `Rust Unit Tests (1/3)`, `(2/3)`, `(3/3)` (non-OTLP) all passed, and the last 5 `main` CI runs were all green — this failed only in the `otlp`-feature partition, matching the pattern already tracked and closed in #8683 ("Flaky test: role_runner shrinking_the_ring… fails on its random-draw precondition (OTLP job only, same commit passes elsewhere)").

The test writes its corpus entry to a `tempfile::NamedTempFile` once per corpus item and then drives both the frozen shell (`tests/fixtures/merge-pr-partial-reset-retired.sh`, sourced by a `bash -c` subprocess) and the Rust `plan()` against it, repeated across `FLAGS × GH_RCS` combinations. The mismatch (Rust said "not loom:building — skipping", shell said "SWAP") is corpus[0], the very first entry ({"number":123,...,"labels":[loom:building, loom:epic]}) — this shape unambiguously *should* have the `loom:building` label, so the divergence looks like the frozen-shell side read stale/wrong tmpfile content rather than a real logic bug in `partial_reset::plan`.

Please: reproduce locally under load (e.g. run the differential test repeatedly alongside other nextest partitions to simulate OTLP-job resource contention), and either fix a race in the test harness (tempfile write/flush ordering, or shared-fd reuse under high parallelism) or mark it appropriately if it's an inherent test-harness limitation under nextest's per-binary parallelism.

Not blocking — this is `isRequired: false` on the PR's check (`Rust OTLP Feature Tests (1/3)`), and `mergeStateStatus` was `UNSTABLE`, not `BLOCKED`.
---

## Curator Enhancement

### Suspected Cause (unverified)

The test (`loom-daemon/tests/merge_pr_partial_reset_differential.rs:172-224`) writes
each corpus entry to a single `tempfile::NamedTempFile` once, then drives 8
combinations (`FLAGS` x `GH_RCS`) of the shell fixture against that same
unmodified file via `cat "$BODY"` inside the harness's `gh()` stub
(`merge_pr_partial_reset_differential.rs:96-97`). The file's content never
changes between those 8 reads, so an ordinary read-after-write race is not
obviously the mechanism — a genuine root cause has not been isolated yet. Two
untested hypotheses worth checking first:

- **Cross-test tmp-dir/fd interaction under high parallelism.** `cargo
  nextest` runs one process per test but many processes concurrently
  (`.config/nextest.toml`); this test isn't in the `daemon-integration`
  test-group, so nothing serializes it against other tests hammering
  `/tmp` on the same runner during the `otlp`-feature partition specifically
  (which runs a different, larger test set than the non-`otlp` partitions per
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml:446`).
- **`NamedTempFile` cleanup-on-drop ordering.** If a prior loop iteration's
  tempfile (a different corpus entry) is reused or its path recycled by the
  OS under resource pressure before `bash -c cat` opens it, a stale/short
  read is possible — this has not been confirmed by instrumentation, only
  inferred from the corpus[0] mismatch shape (Rust correctly saw the
  `loom:building` label; the shell transcript did not).

Both are hypotheses to test via reproduction, not established findings — see
Acceptance Criteria below.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The differential test is run repeatedly under simulated resource
      contention (e.g. `cargo nextest run -p loom-daemon --test
      merge_pr_partial_reset_differential --test-threads <N>` alongside a
      parallel `cargo nextest run --workspace` invocation, or via `stress-ng`
      CPU/IO load) to attempt local reproduction of the corpus[0] mismatch.
- [ ] If reproduced: root cause is identified and fixed (e.g. explicit
      `tmp.flush()`/`sync_all()` before spawning the shell subprocess, moving
      the test into a `max-threads = 1` nextest test-group if the harness's
      subprocess spawning is inherently contention-sensitive, or restructuring
      the corpus loop to write a fresh tempfile per FLAGS/GH_RCS iteration
      instead of reusing one across 8 reads).
- [ ] If NOT reproduced after reasonable effort: document the investigation
      in a code comment on the test (why it's believed to be a transient
      CI-runner artifact) rather than leaving it unexplained, and note in this
      issue what was tried.
- [ ] An explicit, measured refutation of either hypothesis above (i.e.
      "instrumented X, ruled it out") is a complete and acceptable outcome for
      this issue — it does not require forcing a fix onto a mechanism
      measurement rules out.
- [ ] No change to `merge_pr::partial_reset::plan` or the frozen shell fixture
      unless the investigation proves the divergence is a real logic bug
      rather than a test-harness artifact (current evidence — the shell
      transcript disagreeing with itself on unmodified input across 8 reads —
      points at the harness, not the port).

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/tests/merge_pr_partial_reset_differential.rs` — the
  differential test; likely site of any tempfile write/flush/read-ordering
  fix, or a nextest test-group reassignment.
- `loom-daemon/tests/fixtures/merge-pr-partial-reset-retired.sh` — the frozen
  shell fixture the test sources; read during investigation, not expected to
  need changes (it is a frozen verbatim copy by design).
- `.config/nextest.toml` — only if the fix is to move this test into a
  `max-threads = 1` test-group (see `[test-groups.daemon-integration]` for
  the existing pattern of declaring cross-process exclusion).

### Test Plan

- [ ] Manual verification: reproduce locally under load per Acceptance
      Criteria above; capture the reproduction command and its output in a PR
      description or code comment.
- [ ] Automated tests: no new tests expected unless the fix changes the
      corpus-loop structure (e.g. per-iteration tempfiles), in which case the
      existing `plan_agrees_with_the_retired_shell_on_every_input` test itself
      is the regression guard — it must continue to compare `CORPUS.len() *
      FLAGS.len() * GH_RCS.len()` cases and hit every outcome shape listed at
      `merge_pr_partial_reset_differential.rs:211-218`.
- [ ] Edge cases: N/A — this issue is about test-harness reliability, not new
      application behavior.

issues.title: [Epic #9429] story-points: extract clean-landing cost distributions from SigNoz and draft the Fibonacci rubric
issues.body:
Parent epic: #9429 (Fibonacci story points — size-weighted throughput). This is the phase the epic starts with.

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->
<!-- loom:points=5 -->

## Goal

Turn "did we get the story points right?" into data: extract the actual cost of **clean landings** and draft the Fibonacci rubric the Curator will use to assign 1/2/3/5/8/13 at curation time. This phase needs no story points, only actuals, so it works on history that predates the epic.

## Data source (consolidated from curator-stage findings, verified 2026-09-29)

- **Live SigNoz cannot support this phase.** Raw logs start 2026-09-22 (~7-day retention) and hold only 5 `sweep.outcome` records (export began 2026-09-25). `session.summary` is unjoinable (#9445). A local ClickHouse backup (`~/harness-ops-archive/backups/signoz-20260928-104907z/`) covers 2026-09-14..28 but the reload path is unconfirmed; anything before 2026-09-14 has no token record anywhere.
- **The usable history is Cloudflare D1 `loom-fleet-telemetry`**: 26,260 `sweep.outcome` records since 2026-08-15 (at its 500k-row cap and evicting, 2AMLogic/2am#1608). 329 landed issues (success + `pr_number`), 295 with tokens. Retention-safe home for these facts: #9446.
- The analysis must state the window and source actually used, and its limits.

## Clean-landing filter (a deliverable; state it and its exclusion counts)

- Target filter: `result = 'success'` with a landed PR (`result=success` alone is not "landed", #9441), `doctor_cycles = 0`, exactly one `judge` phase.
- **The target filter cannot be applied as written yet**: `doctor_cycles` exists only since 2026-09-18 (strict filter keeps 119) and "exactly one judge" needs per-phase data (#9443). Use the **relaxed filter** (one judge phase, no doctor phase): 284 of 329 landings. The doc states which filter was used and what each excluded.
- Known data caveats to record: tokens present on only ~10% of sweeps (#9440), ~19% of token values implausible (#9454), tokens are per sweep not per phase (#9443), rework cause not recorded (#9444).

## Anchor: landed size, NOT sweep tokens

Over 175 clean landings, tokens scale as hand-written lines^0.25 (a fixed Curator/Judge/repo floor dominates), and differ ~1.5x between Sonnet 5 and Opus 5. So bucket bounds are **not** anchored on raw sweep tokens. The primary anchor is **landed size**: the mean of standardized log hand-written lines, log hand-written files, and log model-normalized tokens (reliability alpha ~0.83; definition in #9466). "Hand-written" excludes generated EDA output (logs, JSON records, netlists, DEF). Tokens (model-normalized), wall-clock (`loom.total_duration_sec`, queue-sensitive, needs a queue-depth caveat) and raw lines are secondary cross-checks.

## Seed rubric table (measured medians per size class, tuning set)

| points | tokens | hand-written lines | files |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~14M | ~12 | 1 |
| 2 | ~19M | ~110 | 2 |
| 3 | ~30M | ~285 | 4 |
| 5 | ~50M | ~610 | 6 |
| 8 | ~73M | ~1,000 | 8 |
| 13 | ~110M | ~2,000 | 8+ |

The doc must also state the finding that **rubric wording barely affects accuracy** (seven variants differed by <0.04 on a paired n=240 test): the rubric's job is to define the units, not to be tuned prose.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Committed, backend-neutral query artifact under `defaults/observability/` (one definition; per-backend extraction where a backend table is read), following the cycle-time / sweep-facts parity discipline. May build on `sweep-facts/landed-size.sql` and `issue-effort.sql`.
- [ ] Distribution analysis over the actual available window (D1 primary), with source, window, filter and exclusion counts.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/story-points.md`: the rubric, seeded from the table above, with the landed-size anchor, cross-check ranges, Curator instructions for when measures disagree, and what "too big for one issue" means (split it).
- [ ] A verification note (evidence.md style) recording which queries ran live, against what data.

## Acceptance criteria

- Bucket bounds are derived from extracted distributions (landed-size anchor), not invented; the doc cites the query output.
- The filter used (relaxed, unless the strict one is applicable) is stated with exclusion counts; the data-source and window are stated.
- Bounds are not anchored on raw sweep tokens or on wall-clock.
- A Curator reading the doc can assign points to a fresh issue without further interpretation.
- The rubric doc stays within the file-size budget for agent-facing docs (the Curator prompt points at it, not inlines it).

## Affected Files

Existing (read/reference; must exist on `origin/main`):

- `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/landed-size.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/issue-effort.sql`
- `defaults/observability/cycle-time-queries.sql`

To be created by the Builder (new files, not yet on main):

- `defaults/docs/story-points.md` (rubric)
- a new query artifact under `defaults/observability/` (e.g. `defaults/observability/story-points-queries.sql`)
- a verification note (e.g. `defaults/observability/story-points-evidence.md`)

issues.title: Per-launch usage attribution and 429 bad-marking at the credential egress proxy (follow-up to #8674)
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #8674 (credential egress proxy, epic #6896). The proxy shipped in the first
increment is, structurally, the **single choke point** every proxied provider request passes
through on its way off the host: it already parses the request head, knows the launch record,
and streams the whole response back. Two things #8674 listed as bonus effects fall out of that
position and are not implemented yet.

## Scope

**1. Per-launch usage attribution.** Record, per launch record, the request and response byte
counts and the provider's own rate-limit / usage response headers
(`anthropic-ratelimit-*`, `x-ratelimit-*`, `retry-after`, and the provider's token-usage
headers where it sends them). This is observed at the wire, at the moment it happens, rather
than reconstructed after the fact from retained logs — and it is attributable to one launch by
construction, because the launch record is what authorized the request.

Note: #8674's body cited #8563/#8564 as doing the "reconstruct from retained logs" this would
replace. Curator checked both and that citation does not hold (#8563 is closed Kimi-pool
onboarding; #8564 is session-level token/model attribution for the fleet feed). Treat the
attribution work here as new, not as a replacement for either.

**2. Bad-mark on quota exhaustion at the proxy.** When the upstream answers `429` or a
provider-specific quota-exhausted shape, the proxy can mark the pooled account bad
*immediately* — it holds the account identity (`credential::Resolved::{provider, account}`
travel into the record) — instead of waiting for the child to exit and for exit-code
inference to run.

Keep both strictly non-secret: the credential must never enter a counter, a log line or an
exported metric, and the placeholder is a live bearer token for the launch's lifetime, so it
must not be logged either. The existing `Record`/`Placeholder` `Debug` impls redact; anything
added here must keep that property.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-launch request/response byte counts and captured rate-limit headers are recorded for
      each proxied launch and surfaced somewhere durable (launch record / telemetry), keyed by
      `launch_id`.
- [ ] A `429`/quota-exhausted upstream response on a pooled API-key route bad-marks the
      selected account at the proxy, and the existing exit-code-driven path does not
      double-mark it.
- [ ] Nothing added logs, exports or persists either the real credential or the placeholder —
      asserted by a test, as the current suite does for `Record`/`Placeholder`.
- [ ] Unproxied (env-passthrough) dispatch is unaffected.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8674 / its implementing PR #8701: merged 2026-09-24 (PR #8701, `7a04dbbc`) — the
      `egress_proxy::{Record, Registry, server}` types this issue's attribution and
      bad-marking hooks extend now exist on `origin/main`.

Dependency cleared — this issue is ready to build.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/server.rs` (lands with #8674/PR #8701) — add
  byte-count tracking and rate-limit-header capture on the request/response path; add the
  `429`/quota-exhausted detection hook
- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/registry.rs` (lands with #8674/PR #8701) — extend
  `Record` to carry per-launch usage counters, keyed by `launch_id`
- `loom-daemon/src/api_keys_pool` — bad-marking / account selection; wire the proxy's
  immediate `429` signal into the existing bad-mark path, guarding against double-marking with
  the existing exit-code-driven path
- Whichever test module covers `Record`/`Placeholder`'s existing redacting `Debug` impls
  (lands with #8674/PR #8701) — extend for the new usage-counter fields, confirming they
  don't leak the credential or placeholder either

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: per-launch byte-count and rate-limit-header capture, asserted against a
      fixture request/response pair
- [ ] Automated tests: a `429`/quota-exhausted response triggers exactly one bad-mark at the
      proxy, and the exit-code-driven path does not double-mark the same account (AC2)
- [ ] Automated tests: extend the existing `Record`/`Placeholder` redaction test to cover the
      new usage-counter fields — confirms neither the real credential nor the placeholder
      appears in any log, counter, or exported metric (AC3)
- [ ] Manual verification: unproxied (env-passthrough) dispatch is unaffected (AC4)

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Related

- Parent: #8674 · Epic: #6896
- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/{server.rs,registry.rs}`
- `loom-daemon/src/api_keys_pool` (bad-marking, account selection)

issues.title: Fleet captain: wire a first real singleton job, and make shell-driven arms visible in host.health
issues.body:
## Problem

#8848 shipped the fleet singleton-job captain gate: `fleet.captain` in the tracked `.loom/config.json`, `loom_daemon::fleet_captain`'s fail-closed match/refusal, the `loom-daemon fleet-captain <job>` CLI for schedule wrappers, `HostHealthRecord::is_captain` / `armed_singleton_jobs`, and the two dashboard flags.

Two gaps remain, both deliberately descoped there rather than half-done:

**1. No real singleton job runs on the gate yet.** The mechanism is complete and tested, but nothing in this repo declares itself a singleton. The downstream consumer (2AMLogic/2am#1132) is the first real user. Until at least one job is wired, the gate is exercised only by tests and by hand.

**2. `armed_singleton_jobs` is in-process only, so shell-driven arms never appear in `host.health`.** `fleet_captain::arm_singleton_job` maintains a process-lifetime `OnceLock<Mutex<BTreeSet<String>>>`. That is correct for a job running *inside* the daemon, but a `loom-daemon fleet-captain <job>` invocation is its own short-lived process — recording an arm there would be written and lost in the same breath. The CLI therefore deliberately resolves the gate **without** touching the registry (`cli/fleet_captain_cmd.rs`'s `evaluating_does_not_touch_the_armed_registry` test pins this), so a fleet whose singletons are all shell timers reports `armed_singleton_jobs: []` on every host.

The practical consequence: the dashboard's **"singleton armed on a non-captain host"** flag (#8848 AC5a) can only ever fire for in-daemon jobs. The **"no captain reporting"** flag (AC5b) is unaffected — it keys on `is_captain`, which `sample_host_health` computes directly.

## Proposal

- Wire a first real singleton job onto `arm_singleton_job` (or migrate one of 2am's hand-gated timers as the pilot) so the mechanism has a live consumer.
- Give shell-driven arms a durable cross-process registry so they reach `host.health`. The open design question is **staleness**: a file-backed `job -> last_armed_at` map needs a policy for when an entry stops counting as armed (a wrapper that is uninstalled never disarms itself). Candidate answers worth weighing:
  - a TTL derived from the job's own declared cadence (requires jobs to declare one),
  - a fixed conservative window (simple, but an arbitrary constant),
  - an explicit `loom-daemon fleet-captain disarm <job>` the wrapper calls on its own teardown (precise, but silently wrong when a host is re-imaged).

Pick one deliberately — the failure mode of guessing wrong is a permanently-stuck "armed" entry that makes the non-captain flag cry wolf, which is worse than the current honest empty list.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8848 (the base mechanism) — merged

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At least one real singleton job is gated by `fleet_captain`, and per-host jobs remain untouched
- [ ] A shell-driven arm via `loom-daemon fleet-captain` is visible in that host's `host.health.armed_singleton_jobs`
- [ ] The staleness policy is chosen explicitly, documented in `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`'s "Fleet captain" section, and covered by a test that asserts a stale entry stops being reported
- [ ] The dashboard's "singleton armed on a non-captain host" flag is demonstrated firing against a shell-driven arm, not only an in-daemon one

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/fleet_captain.rs` — durable registry alongside (or replacing) the in-process one
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/fleet_captain_cmd.rs` — an arming verb, currently check-only by design
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs` — `sample_host_health` merges the durable entries
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` — "Fleet captain (#8848)" section

## Test Plan

- [ ] A durable arm written by one process is read back by another (the daemon/CLI split this exists to close)
- [ ] A stale entry stops being reported under the chosen policy
- [ ] Re-arming refreshes rather than duplicating
- [ ] `armed_singleton_jobs` still omits (not `[]`) when nothing is armed — the existing `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]` contract must not regress

issues.title: post_init: add regression test asserting .loom/tokens.*/ and .loom/tokens-*/ appear in the generated .gitignore
issues.body:
## Observed

PR #9046 added two new entries to `EPHEMERAL_PATTERNS` in
`loom-daemon/src/init/post_init.rs`:

```rust
".loom/tokens.*/",
".loom/tokens-*/",
```

These close the gap that let a sibling copy of the token pool
(`.loom/tokens.shadow-disabled-<ts>/`) get swept into a public commit
(a9da48c2, see #9047 for the credential-rotation follow-up). The existing
`creates_gitignore_with_all_patterns_when_none_exists` test in the same file
spot-checks dozens of other `EPHEMERAL_PATTERNS` entries via
`contents.contains(...)`, but was not extended to assert these two new
patterns are present in `update_gitignore`'s output. `cargo test -p
loom-daemon --lib post_init` still passes (27/27, per the PR) because nothing
in the suite exercises the new lines either way — the omission is silent.

## Suggested test

Add to `creates_gitignore_with_all_patterns_when_none_exists` (or a small new
test):

```rust
// #9046: sibling copies of the token pool must be ignored too.
assert!(contents.contains(".loom/tokens.*/"));
assert!(contents.contains(".loom/tokens-*/"));
```

Optionally also assert `git check-ignore`-equivalent matching behavior against
a couple of concrete sample paths (e.g. `.loom/tokens.shadow-disabled-20260101T000000Z/x.token`,
`.loom/tokens-backup/x.token`) so a future glob-syntax mistake fails a unit
test instead of requiring another live leak to notice.

Discovered while judging PR #9046 (this is a coverage gap, not a defect in
#9046's own fix — manual verification in that PR's description, via `git
check-ignore -v --no-index`, already confirmed the patterns work as intended).

---

## Curator Enhancement

Clear problem statement and a concrete suggested test already exist in the original issue. Adding the required sections; no scope change.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `creates_gitignore_with_all_patterns_when_none_exists` (in `loom-daemon/src/init/post_init.rs`) asserts `contents.contains(".loom/tokens.*/")` and `contents.contains(".loom/tokens-*/")`, following the file's existing dated-comment convention (e.g. `// #9046: sibling copies of the token pool must be ignored too.`).
- [ ] At least one concrete sample-path check (e.g. via a glob-matching helper or a literal string constructed the same way `EPHEMERAL_PATTERNS` entries are matched elsewhere in this file) confirms `.loom/tokens.shadow-disabled-20260101T000000Z/x.token` and `.loom/tokens-backup/x.token` are actually covered by the emitted patterns — not just that the literal pattern strings appear in the `.gitignore` output.
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib post_init` passes.

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/init/post_init.rs` — extend `creates_gitignore_with_all_patterns_when_none_exists` (verified present at line 790 on `origin/main`); the two target patterns are already emitted at lines 259–260 (`EPHEMERAL_PATTERNS`).

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: the new assertions described above, run via `cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib post_init`.
- [ ] Manual verification: N/A — this issue is itself a test-coverage addition; no separate manual step needed.
- [ ] Edge cases: verify the glob patterns don't also over-match an unrelated path (e.g. a plain `.loom/tokens/` dir used elsewhere in the repo, if any) so the new assertions catch a future glob-syntax regression rather than just a literal-string typo.
