issues.title: Observability & Tuning: Fleet-wide token burn rate (TPM/RPM), account exhaustion downtime, and worker concurrency scaling
issues.body:
## Problem

To optimize throughput and maximize token utilization across LLM subscriptions (Claude, Codex, etc.), operators need visibility into whether the fleet is hitting quota ceilings, idling due to account exhaustion, or constrained by static per-host concurrency limits.

## Proposal

1. **Fleet-Wide Token Burn Tracking:**
   - Export aggregate and per-provider/model TPM and RPM metrics to SigNoz.
   - Compare actual consumption against theoretical subscription/tier limits.
2. **Account Exhaustion & Rotation Downtime:**
   - Measure duration and frequency of account backoffs, 429s, and proxy account rotations.
   - Alert/report when all accounts in a pool are exhausted simultaneously.
3. **Worker Concurrency Profiling & Headroom Tuning:**
   - Profile RAM, CPU, and disk headroom per worker to determine if builder/judge concurrency can safely scale up (e.g. from 1–2 to 4–6 parallel jobs per host).
   - Measure useful vs wasted tokens (landed PRs vs timed-out / aborted / `skipped_load` attempts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Real-time TPM/RPM metrics aggregated across accounts visible in SigNoz.
- [ ] Account exhaustion downtime tracked.
- [ ] Concurrency limits per host configurable and observable relative to host resource pressure.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-25, against `main` @ `277db2ce`)

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

### Scope decisions

- **Proposal 3 (concurrency scaling) is split out to #8928** (`loom:operator-decision`). The cap is already configurable (`autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrent`) and already observable: `loom.dispatch.max_concurrent`, plus the host memory/swap/volume gauges from #8909. What remains is operator judgement. "Useful vs wasted tokens" needs per-run attribution, so it belongs to #8908 and #8052.
- **#8908 stays open, with a clean boundary.** #8908 attaches *per-execution* token counts to `loom.runtime.run` spans (a trace join). This issue exports *host-wide, time-bucketed* burn and pool state, independent of any run. The triage note called #8908 a prerequisite; that no longer holds, because phase 1 samples the Claude transcript store by time window directly and never joins to a span.
- **#8058 does not have to land first.** The pool gauges measure the `exhausted` flag that actually gates selection today. That is the true "dispatch is starved" signal, even though it is over-broad per model class. A `model` label can follow #8058.
- **#8052** is the offline `activity.db` report and has no code overlap.
- **#8856 (dwell/starvation)** is being built in parallel. Keep new `MetricName` variants in one contiguous block and rebase before merging.

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 (this issue):** Claude real-time burn, pool gauges for every pool (Claude, Codex, and API-key providers such as ZAI/Kimi), snapshot-derived exhaustion counters, and the four #8909 Judge carry-overs.
- **Phase 2, #8930:** per-event interval readers for Codex, OpenCode (GLM) and Kimi. Their existing readers fold whole sessions by creation time, which is wrong for rates.
- **Phase 3, #8931:** reason-classified account marks (429 / exhausted / session limit) at the provider-health-feedback seams, plus pool-hold spans.

### Phase 1 design

Everything goes through `observability::ops`, the path added in #8909. Nothing runs when no OTLP exporter is registered.

A new `observability/ops/quota.rs` is called from `collector::sample_snapshots` on the existing 5-minute snapshot cadence:

1. **Claude burn.** Walk `claude_projects_dir()` for `*.jsonl` files (including `subagents/`) whose mtime is on or after the window start. Decode records with `script_helpers::transcript_usage::usage_from_record`. Group by `message.id`, keeping the first timestamp and the per-counter max, the same dedupe `activity::transcript_parse` uses. Count a message only when its first timestamp falls in `(prev_end, now − 60s]`. The lag lets streamed chunks finish.
   - Emit delta counters with `interval_start = prev_end`, labels `provider=claude` and `model`: `loom.llm.tokens.input`, `.output`, `.cache_read`, `.cache_write` (unit `{token}`), and `loom.llm.requests` (distinct message ids, unit `{request}`). TPM and RPM are rates over these counters in SigNoz.
   - Skip `<synthetic>` records. The first sample after start only initialises the window, so history is never replayed.
2. **Pool state**, per provider. Sources: the `tokens.snapshot` accounts (Claude, Codex) and `api_keys_pool::list_accounts` for enabled accounts (ZAI, Kimi, …).
   - `loom.pool.accounts{provider,state=usable|exhausted}` gauge.
   - `loom.pool.exhausted{provider}` gauge: 1 when at least one account is exhausted and none are usable.
   - `loom.pool.exhaustions{provider}` delta: accounts newly exhausted since the previous sample.
   - `loom.pool.exhausted_seconds{provider}` delta: seconds since the previous sample while the pool reads as exhausted (sample-and-hold). This is the downtime number.

No new label keys are needed; `provider`, `model` and `state` are already allowlisted.

### Required carry-overs from #8909's Judge

- [ ] (a) Apply `bounded_points()` at **emit** time in `OpsSink::emit_metrics_since`, so NaN/∞ values and oversize labels never reach the on-disk queue. An empty batch after bounding enqueues nothing.
- [ ] (b) Add a `debug_assert!` in `MetricPoint::label` for keys outside `OPS_METRIC_LABEL_KEYS`.
- [ ] (c) Refresh the datapoint-allowlist list in the privacy section of `defaults/observability/collector/README.md` so it matches `config.yaml`.
- [ ] (d) Run `df` once per `host.health` sample: sample the bytes once, then derive `host.health`'s GB fields from them and pass them to `ops::host`.

### Acceptance criteria (phase 1)

- [ ] A fixture test covers the Claude burn fold: messages attributed by first-chunk timestamp, streamed duplicates counted once, a window boundary splitting messages with no double count, `<synthetic>` skipped, and requests equal to distinct ids.
- [ ] A unit test covers pool metrics for a mixed Claude/Codex/API-key account set: usable/exhausted counts, `exhausted = 1` only when zero accounts are usable, `exhaustions` counting new transitions only, and `exhausted_seconds` accruing only while the pool is exhausted.
- [ ] Every new `MetricName` has a kind, unit and description, round-trips through serde, and is documented in `telemetry-schema.md` § `metric.points` and `observability.md` §3c.
- [ ] Carry-overs (a)–(d) have tests where testable. (a) needs a NaN point and an oversize label dropped before the queue; (b) needs a `#[should_panic]` test under `debug_assertions`.
- [ ] Observability off, or no OTLP exporter configured: no transcript or pool reads happen.

### Test plan

`cargo test -p loom-daemon observability::ops` and `cargo test -p loom-daemon telemetry`, plus clippy.

issues.title: Fleet singleton jobs: first-class captain placement so fleet hosts can be identical
issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

## Problem
A multi-host Loom fleet has two kinds of scheduled job:
- **Per-host jobs** watch *this* host: the daemon watchdog, clean, resync, drift. Every host runs them.
- **Singleton jobs** watch *one shared thing*: a forge-wide queue check, a public feed staleness check, a shared edge queue pull, a token-pool anomaly check. Exactly one host may run each one, because `gh-alert`-style dedup is read-then-write with no lock (the #6714 race class), so two hosts file duplicate alerts.

Loom has no concept of the second kind. Operators (2AMLogic/2am) place singletons by hand-installing a timer on a chosen host and documenting it in prose. Three consequences follow:
- Hosts that should be identical aren't. 2AMLogic/2am#1125 found `loom-worker-2` carrying two singleton timers that `loom-worker-1` lacks.
- An image-built or rebuilt worker silently loses the singletons, or duplicates them.
- Nothing enforces "exactly one". Wrappers each reinvent a fail-closed host gate: 2am's `batch-fleet-reconcile-schedule.sh` and `loom-wake-pull-schedule.sh` do it by hand, and others don't.

## Proposal
- **A fleet-level designation of which host runs singletons**, e.g. `fleet.captain: <host id>` in the machine or host config tier, compared against `host_identity()` (LOOM_HOST_ID). Assigned by the operator, with no election. 2am's vocabulary is "captain" (2AMLogic/2am FLEET.md §Host topology), meaning assigned rather than elected.
- **Declared singleton jobs** that the daemon, or the schedule helper Loom ships, arms **only** when this host is the captain, and refuses on any other host (fail closed, with a message naming the captain). Per-host jobs are unchanged.
- **Observability:** `host.health` reports `is_captain` plus the singleton jobs armed here. The dashboard flags any singleton armed on a non-captain, and a fleet with no captain reporting.
- **Optional later:** a lease, so a captain that is down for longer than N hours can be noticed. Not failover; just an alert.

## Why upstream
Identical fleet hosts (golden image, `fleet add-worker`) are a Loom-level goal. Hand-placed singletons are the part that currently can't be made identical. Downstream tracking: 2AMLogic/2am#1132 (move 2am's singletons to the captain), 2AMLogic/2am#1125 (identical workers).

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-25)

Problem statement, proposal, and rationale are already clear and well-argued. Adding the required sections, a scope clarification, and precise pointers into this repo's existing code that the Proposal builds on.

### Scope clarification: `gh-alert`, `batch-fleet-reconcile-schedule.sh`, `loom-wake-pull-schedule.sh` are 2AMLogic/2am tooling, not loom's

Verified against this repo (`rjwalters/loom`) — none of these three exist here (`grep -rn` for each returns zero hits; `find` for the two script names returns zero hits). They're referenced correctly as *consumer-repo* precedent (2AMLogic/2am hand-rolling the fail-closed gate this issue wants to make first-class), not as something already present in loom to extend. A Builder should not go looking for them in this tree.

### `host_identity()` / `LOOM_HOST_ID` — already exists, this is what `fleet.captain` compares against

`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/mod.rs:807` (`pub fn host_identity() -> String`), precedence `LOOM_HOST_ID` env (`HOST_ID_ENV` const, `mod.rs:189`) > `$HOSTNAME` > the `hostname` binary > `UNKNOWN_HOST` sentinel. This is the "operator-controlled, stable across launch contexts" identity issue #5063 already established fleet-wide — `fleet.captain: <host id>` is compared against this, not a new identity concept.

### Where `fleet.captain` belongs: tracked `.loom/config.json`, not a host-local env var

`.loom/config.json` has no `fleet` key today (top-level keys: `version, offlineMode, autonomous, buildGate, guards, branchProtection, terminals, safehouse, sweep, guide, runtimes, observability`). The existing precedent for *which config tier a fleet-wide knob belongs in* is the role-runner sharding table at `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md:5315-5327`: a value that must be **identical fleet-wide** belongs in the **tracked** `.loom/config.json` (a committed file is identical fleet-wide by construction) — e.g. `shardCount`/`shardKey` — while a value that must **differ per host** stays host-local-only (env var), e.g. `shardIndex`. Since every host must agree on who the captain is, `fleet.captain` follows the `shardCount`/`shardKey` precedent: tracked `.loom/config.json`, not an env var. (There is a separate, weaker-fit candidate — the untracked, operator-provisioned `~/.loom/fleet.json` / `FleetRegistry` in `loom-daemon/src/fleet/mod.rs:679` — but that's SSH/drain-state bookkeeping, not a config-value store, and isn't distributed to every host the way a tracked repo file is.)

### Closest existing fail-closed pattern: `host_affinity.rs` (#7456) — issue-scoped, not fleet-config-scoped, but the shape to mirror

`loom-daemon/src/host_affinity.rs` (416 lines) already implements the exact shape this issue wants at fleet-config scope: a `HostConstraint` struct (`required: BTreeSet<String>`), `matches(host_id)` — empty set = runs anywhere, non-empty = exact membership only, **no partial/case-insensitive fallback** (its own "Fail-closed semantics (load-bearing)" doc block). Two enforcement points: `work_finder`'s autonomous tick (via `IssueLike::host_constraint()`, `mod.rs:393`) and `loom-daemon dispatch <issue>` CLI (`cli/dispatch.rs:145,161-185`, refuses naming the required host(s) unless `--ignore-host-constraint` is passed, wired at `main.rs:388-392` / `daemon_service.rs:184-193`). This issue's captain-gate is a **new, separate mechanism** (fleet-config-scoped, not issue-scoped) — cite `host_affinity.rs` as the pattern to mirror stylistically (fail-closed match, named-host refusal message, explicit override flag), not as code to extend directly.

### Contrast, not precedent: #6714's filing lock is deliberately fail-*open*

The issue's own "#6714 race class" reference is this repo's fleet-wide issue-filing lock (`loom-daemon/src/peer_claims.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/filing_lock.rs`) — a cross-host TTL mutex via peer-claim ads. It explicitly **degrades open** (`filing_lock.rs:109`; disabling it makes every acquire degrade open) rather than fail-closed, and it's a distributed lock, not an election/assignment. Worth noting so a Builder doesn't mistake it for prior art to extend — it solves a different problem (mutual exclusion under uncertainty) with the opposite failure direction from what this issue wants (fail-closed captain gating).

### `host.health` already exists — this is what gains `is_captain`

`HostHealthRecord` (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs:961`, variant `TelemetryRecord::HostHealth` at `mod.rs:259`) already ships with fields including `dispatch_halted`/`halt_reason` — the nearest existing analog to the boolean-plus-reason shape `is_captain` needs. Constructed in `sample_host_health()` at `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs:704-753`, where the new field(s) would be populated. Every optional field on this struct follows an established `#[serde(default)]`, omit-when-unmeasurable contract; `is_captain` (and an armed-singleton-jobs list) should follow the same pattern.

### Dependencies

None. This is a self-contained design-and-build issue; nothing else in the open queue blocks it.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fleet.captain: <host id>` is a recognized key in the tracked `.loom/config.json` schema, documented in `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md`'s canonical config-knob table (mirroring the `shardCount`/`shardKey` "identical fleet-wide, tracked" precedent, not the `shardIndex` "host-local" one)
- [ ] A declared-singleton-job mechanism (daemon-side, or the schedule helper Loom ships) compares its own `host_identity()` against `fleet.captain` and arms **only** on a match; on a non-match it refuses with a message naming the current captain (mirroring `host_affinity.rs`'s named-host refusal message style, e.g. `cli/dispatch.rs:145`)
- [ ] Per-host jobs are provably unaffected — no existing per-host cron/timer/tick gains a captain check
- [ ] `HostHealthRecord` (`telemetry/mod.rs:961`) gains an `is_captain` field (and an armed-singleton-jobs list), populated in `sample_host_health()` (`observability/collector.rs:704-753`), following the struct's existing `#[serde(default)]` contract
- [ ] The dashboard (`dashboard/src/redaction.ts` allowlist + `dashboard/src/publicPage.ts` or the `dashboard/web/src` frontend) flags (a) a singleton armed on a non-captain host, and (b) a fleet with no host reporting `is_captain: true` at all
- [ ] No `fleet.captain` declared at all leaves today's behavior fully unchanged (no singleton mechanism exists yet, so this is mostly forward-looking, but the config parse itself must degrade gracefully on an absent key)
- [ ] The "optional later" lease/alert-on-down-captain item is explicitly out of scope for this issue's acceptance — do not implement it here; a follow-up issue can pick it up once the base mechanism ships

### Affected Files

- `.loom/config.json` schema / parsing (wherever the top-level config struct is defined in `loom-daemon/src/`) — add the `fleet.captain` key
- `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` — canonical config-knob table, new `fleet.captain` row citing the `shardCount`/`shardKey` tier precedent (§ near line 5315)
- `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs` (`HostHealthRecord`, line 961) — add `is_captain` (+ armed-jobs list) field(s)
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs` (`sample_host_health()`, lines 704-753) — populate the new field(s)
- New module or function near `loom-daemon/src/host_affinity.rs` / `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/mod.rs` (near `host_identity()`, line 807) — the captain-match/fail-closed-refusal logic itself
- `dashboard/src/redaction.ts` (line 125, `host.health` allowlist) — allow the new field(s) through to the public dashboard
- `dashboard/src/publicPage.ts` or `dashboard/web/src` views — render the two flag conditions (singleton on non-captain; no captain reporting)
- Whichever schedule-wrapper surface Loom ships for declared jobs (if one doesn't exist yet, this issue may need to introduce a minimal one — scope this explicitly during implementation rather than assuming a specific existing file)

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a captain-match/no-match unit test mirroring `host_affinity.rs`'s `HostConstraint::matches` coverage — declared captain matches `host_identity()` (arms), does not match (refuses with the captain named), and no `fleet.captain` declared at all (behavior explicitly defined, not merely "whatever falls out")
- [ ] Automated tests: reuse the `RecordingDispatcher.current_host_id`-style injection pattern from `work_finder/tests.rs:216-224` (inject host identity as a test double rather than mutating process env) for any test touching the new captain-gate logic, to avoid the cross-test env races `host_identity_env_precedence` (`sweep_registry/mod.rs:1698`) already guards against with its RAII env guard
- [ ] Automated tests: `HostHealthRecord` serialization round-trips `is_captain` correctly and omits/defaults sanely when unset
- [ ] Manual verification: on a two-host test/staging setup, declare one as `fleet.captain`, confirm a declared singleton job arms there and refuses (with the captain named in the message) on the other
- [ ] Manual verification: dashboard correctly flags a synthetic "singleton armed on non-captain" and a synthetic "no captain reporting" state
- [ ] Edge cases: `fleet.captain` naming a host id that never reports `host.health` (typo, decommissioned host) — confirm this surfaces as "no captain reporting" rather than silently leaving every singleton unarmed with no signal

issues.title: forge_get_check_runs reads only the first 30 check-runs; merge-pr --auto's settle-wait cannot see the rest
issues.body:
Found while reviewing #8426 (#8410). Once that lands, `merge-pr.sh --auto`'s client-side settle-wait is the **only** check-settling mechanism: the server-side arm is gone.

## Observed

`forge_get_check_runs` (`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh`, the `gh api "repos/$nwo/commits/$commit/check-runs"` call) passes no `per_page` and no `--paginate`, so GitHub's default page size of 30 applies:

```
$ gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/commits/c53dcaa85860fe090be88d6c1d374cd59e5439b5/check-runs --jq '"\(.total_count) \(.check_runs|length)"'
39 30
```

This repo's CI produces 39 check-runs per head, so 9 are invisible to the settle-wait, both to its pending count and to its failed-required classification.

## Suspected impact (unverified)

The rows appear to come back newest first, so the long-running test suites are probably visible and the missing rows are early structural gates. The forge's own ruleset should still refuse a synchronous merge whose required checks have not passed, unless the merging identity has a bypass. That needs checking. This is present on `main` today; #8426 makes it load-bearing.

## Suggested fix

Add `per_page=100` and/or paginate. Also fail closed (treat as pending) when `total_count` exceeds the number of rows returned, so a future growth past any page size cannot silently shrink the checked set. Pin it with a test fixture where `total_count > len(check_runs)`.

Measuring that the missing rows never include a required check, and closing this with that evidence, is a valid outcome.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Confirmed on `origin/main` @ current head: PR #8426 ("merge-pr --auto settles checks and re-validates in-process instead of arming a server-side merge") **merged 2026-09-25T14:34:02Z** — so the scenario this issue flags as "once that lands" is now live, not hypothetical: `merge-pr.sh --auto`'s client-side settle-wait (`_wait_for_checks_then_sync_merge`, `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` ~line 2035) is the only check-settling mechanism today, and it relies entirely on `forge_get_check_runs` (`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:652`), which still passes no `per_page`/`--paginate` to `gh api repos/$nwo/commits/$commit/check-runs` (line 690). Marking `loom:urgent` — this is a live gap in the mechanism this repo relies on to avoid merging PRs whose required checks have not actually passed (see CLAUDE.md § "CI is dumb and reliable, on purpose").

No duplicates found (`check-duplicate.sh --include-merged-prs --issue 8895`).

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `forge_get_check_runs` retrieves every check-run for a commit, not just the first page (add `per_page=100` and/or `--paginate` to the `gh api` call at `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:690`).
- [ ] When the fetched row count is less than `total_count`, the caller fails closed (treats settlement as not-yet-reached / still pending) rather than silently trusting a truncated set.
- [ ] A regression test fixture exercises `total_count > len(check_runs)` and confirms the fail-closed behavior (per the issue's own Suggested fix).
- [ ] Existing `test-forge-helpers.sh` / `test-merge-pr-check-runs-404-fallback.sh` / `test-merge-pr-wait-for-checks-empty-settle.sh` suites stay green.
- [ ] Alternative closing condition (also acceptance-satisfying per the issue body): if investigation shows the missing rows can never include a required check (e.g. GitHub's check-runs endpoint is confirmed to always return required checks in the first page), document that finding with evidence and close without a code change.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` — `forge_get_check_runs` (GitHub branch, ~line 690): add pagination and/or a fail-closed total-count check.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-helpers.sh` — existing `forge_get_check_runs` coverage; extend or add a case for `total_count > len(check_runs)`.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-check-runs-404-fallback.sh` — exercises `forge_get_check_runs`'s distinguished exit codes; verify pagination changes don't disturb the 404/500/network-error paths.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-wait-for-checks-empty-settle.sh` — exercises the settle-wait loop's trust of a `forge_get_check_runs` read; extend for the truncated-page case if the fail-closed behavior needs loop-level coverage.
- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — `_wait_for_checks_then_sync_merge` (~line 2035), the sole caller now that #8426 removed the server-side arm; reference only unless the fail-closed check needs to live here instead of inside `forge_get_check_runs`.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: new fixture in `test-forge-helpers.sh` (or a new dedicated test file) pinning `total_count > len(check_runs)` → fail-closed/pending, per Acceptance Criteria.
- [ ] Automated tests: existing forge-helpers and merge-pr check-runs/settle-wait suites stay green.
- [ ] Manual verification: `gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/commits/<head>/check-runs --jq '"\(.total_count) \(.check_runs|length)"'` against a commit with >30 check-runs, before and after, confirming the fetch now returns the full set.
- [ ] Edge cases: a repo/commit with exactly 30, and with >100, check-runs (page-boundary and multi-page cases).

issues.title: merge: re-run stale required checks in place (grant fleet App Actions: write) so approved PRs stop losing loom:pr to re-date commits
issues.body:
## Problem

Approved PRs with green CI get stuck in a loop just before merging, and when several merge close together the loop may never end:

1. A PR is Judge-approved (`loom:pr`) and its CI is green.
2. Another PR merges, and `main` gets new commits (at least the post-merge version bump).
3. `merge-pr.sh`'s required-check freshness guard (#8248) refuses the merge, because the green checks started before the new base tip.
4. The fleet merge identity (`loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]`, a GitHub App) has no **Actions: write** permission, so it can't re-run the stale checks. As its fallback (#8508, `--redate-stale-checks`), it pushes a tree-identical no-op commit.
5. The head SHA moves, so the stale-verdict guard clears `loom:pr` and puts the PR back to `loom:review-requested`.
6. The PR waits for another Judge pass. Meanwhile something else merges, and the loop starts again at step 2.

Each lap costs a full CI run plus a Judge pass, and it resets whenever `main` moves.

## Evidence (2026-09-25)

- **PR #8909** was approved at `6f77b070`. The bot pushed the re-date commit `efb141c5` ("chore: re-date required checks for PR #8909 (#8248 guard, automated by #8508)"), and the stale-verdict guard then cleared `loom:pr`. The git tree is **identical** on both commits (`89d2e775fdb4abe54dbfe3111c6bcc77502d31c8`), so a review of the same code was thrown away.
- **PRs #8426 and #8471** each needed two separate Judge re-reviews that afternoon, both of which found no changes (a clean rebase, then another stale-check refusal), before they could merge. **#8906** is in the same queue.
- **An operator token with `repo` + `workflow` scope *can* re-run a job in place** (`POST /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{id}/rerun`), keeping the head and the approval. So the missing piece is only the App's permission.

## Proposed fix

1. **Permission (human/admin action):** add **Actions: Read and write** to the `loom-fleet-dispatch` GitHub App, then accept the updated permission on each installation (rjwalters/loom first). GitHub has no API for changing an App's permissions; it has to be done in the App settings UI by the App owner.
2. **Code:** in `merge-pr.sh`'s freshness-guard path (`loom-daemon merge-pr redate-checks`), try re-running the stale required-check jobs **in place** first, then wait and retry the merge. Fall back to the tree-identical no-op push only if the re-run is refused (403, missing permission). The head never moves on the happy path, so `loom:pr` survives.
3. **Optional, separate decision:** when a push is tree-identical to the head that was approved (same git tree SHA), the stale-verdict guard could keep `loom:pr`. That removes the loop even for installs without Actions: write. It changes the "a verdict is about a specific tree" invariant only in the case where the tree really is the same, but it needs a deliberate decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On an installation with Actions: write, a freshness-guard block on an approved PR is resolved by re-running the jobs in place: no new commit, the head SHA is unchanged, `loom:pr` is kept, and the merge completes on the next attempt once the re-run is green. Verified on a live PR.
- [ ] On an installation without Actions: write, the behaviour is unchanged: the existing #8508 tree-identical re-date plus one-push bound and escalation still applies. Covered by a test with the rerun endpoint returning 403.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md` and the GitHub App setup / authentication docs list Actions: write as a recommended App permission and explain why.

## Related

#8248 (freshness guard), #8508 (re-date fallback, closed), #5686 (fresh Judge after head move).

---

## Curator enhancement (2026-09-25)

### Scope split
| Item | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| 1. Grant `loom-fleet-dispatch` **Actions: Read and write** | **Operator step**, below. The code work does not wait for it: without the grant the new code falls back to today's #8508 behaviour. |
| 2. Re-run stale required jobs in place (code) | **This issue.** |
| 3. Keep `loom:pr` on a tree-identical push | **#8918** (`loom:operator-decision`). It changes a verdict invariant, so a human decides. |
| Comment finding: a busy `main` beats even in-place re-runs | Partly handled here (required-only re-runs, then an immediate merge). Input-aware staleness and a fast required-checks workflow move to **#8919**. |

### Operator step (human/admin, cannot be done from code)
1. GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → `loom-fleet-dispatch` → Permissions → Repository → **Actions: Read and write** → Save.
2. On each installation (rjwalters/loom first), accept the updated permission request.
3. Check: on the next freshness-guard block, the merge-pr output says `LOOM-RERUN-…` and no `chore: re-date required checks` commit appears.

### Platform fact the design depends on (verified 2026-09-25, twice)
GitHub runs **one re-run per workflow run at a time**. After one `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{id}/rerun`, the run is `in_progress`. Any further job re-run in the same run returns `403 {"message":"The workflow run containing this job is already running"}`. I reproduced this on `ci.yml` run 36152790007, and the comment above (PR #8692) records the same result. Jobs that are not re-run are carried into the new attempt with their **original** `started_at`, so per-job re-runs cannot refresh several stale required checks. All 19 required contexts on `main` are in the single `ci.yml` run.

**Decision: re-run the whole workflow run** (`POST /actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun`, the same call as `gh run rerun <id>`), issuing one call per workflow run that holds a stale required check. The required jobs are fast and run in parallel, so they come back fresh in about a minute even though the full run takes about 8. The cost is a full CI cycle's compute. Moving the fast required checks into their own small workflow, so that re-running it is cheap, is a CI restructuring and is tracked in **#8919**.

### Implementation plan (Rust, `loom-daemon merge-pr redate-checks`; no new shell)
- New module `loom-daemon/src/merge_pr/rerun.rs` plus its tests. `redate::remedy` calls it **first**, after the existing head-moved check.
  - Read the live inputs: base tip, required contexts and the head's check runs. The check-run projection gains the job id, the app slug and the workflow run id (parsed from `details_url` `/actions/runs/<run>/job/<job>`). The base ref comes from the PR itself (`pulls/{n}` `.base.ref`), so no new CLI flag is needed and a new shell cannot break against an old binary.
  - List **every** stale required context (green, `started_at` < base tip), not just the first. If any stale context is not a GitHub Actions job, in-place re-run cannot produce complete evidence, so fall back to the push path.
  - Loop until a bounded deadline:
    - Re-read the inputs. If the head has moved, return `HeadMoved` (exit 3).
    - For each workflow run that holds a stale required job and has not yet been re-run by this call, `POST actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun`.
    - On `201`, that run is in flight.
    - On `403` with "already running", **wait**. This is not a missing permission, so never push.
    - On any other `403`, or a `404`, while **nothing has been re-run yet**, the result is `Refused`. Fall through to the existing #8508 tree-identical push, with its one-push-per-head bound and escalation unchanged.
    - On any other error, the result is `Failed` (exit 1, the refusal stands).
  - A re-run required job that concludes non-green is a failed re-run, and the refusal stands (exit 1). This is real red evidence, for example a tightened ratchet.
  - When every required context is fresh and none is pending, the result is **fresh**.
  - When the deadline passes first, the result is **pending**. The head is unchanged, `loom:pr` is kept, and the next pass continues.
- Exit contract (skew-safe in both directions):
  - `0`: pushed (unchanged), **or** re-ran in place and still pending, **or** fresh without the proceed opt-in. `merge-pr.sh` maps this to exit 4 (re-queue), which is what champion-pr-merge.md already expects.
  - `5` (new): re-ran in place and now fresh. Returned **only** when the caller sets `LOOM_REDATE_ALLOW_PROCEED=1`. This is an environment variable rather than a flag, so an old binary ignores it and still pushes. On exit 5 the new `merge-pr.sh` returns 0 from the freshness guard and merges straight away, which shortens the race described in the comment.
  - `1`/`3`/`4`: unchanged.
- Wait budget: `--rerun-wait-secs` (env `LOOM_REDATE_RERUN_WAIT_SECS`, default 600), polling about every 10 s.
- `merge-pr.sh`: an edit within the existing line of the one-line `_check_required_check_freshness`. It sets the env opt-in, handles `rd==5`, and fixes the exit-4 wording, which currently always claims a fresh Judge review is needed. **No line-count growth**: the file is frozen by the ratchet.
- Docs: `defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md` (the exit-4 row and the #8508 section) and the GitHub App setup/auth docs, which should list Actions: write as a recommended permission and say why. Also update the `redate.rs` and `cli/merge_pr_redate.rs` headers.

### Acceptance criteria (refined)
- [ ] Unit tests with a stub `gh` cover these cases:
  - The workflow runs holding stale required jobs are re-run in place (one call per run) and nothing is pushed.
  - A 403 for a missing permission falls back to the #8508 push, with its bound and escalation unchanged.
  - A 403 for "already running" waits and does not push.
  - A red re-run is `Failed`.
  - A head move is `HeadMoved`.
  - A passed deadline is `Pending`.
  - Fresh returns exit 5 only with the opt-in.
- [ ] A stale required check that is not a GitHub Actions job goes straight to the push fallback.
- [ ] Existing `redate` and `stale_checks` tests pass unchanged, apart from the mechanical update to the `CheckRun` constructor.
- [ ] The `merge-pr.sh` line count is unchanged, and the shell suites covering `--redate-stale-checks` pass.
- [ ] The docs list Actions: write as a recommended App permission.
- [ ] Live verification of AC1 (a freshness block resolved by an in-place re-run on a real PR) happens once the operator grants the permission. It can be checked with an operator token in the meantime.

issues.title: Observability: Pipeline stage dwell time, queue turnaround latency, and dispatch starvation metrics
issues.body:
## Problem

Operators cannot easily determine whether Loom workers are starved for work, blocked on upstream stages, or idling between orchestrator ticks. While raw role durations exist in SigNoz, end-to-end pipeline velocity and queue wait times are unmeasured.

## Proposal

Add telemetry and metrics for pipeline throughput and feeder velocity:

1. **Worker Turnaround / Idle Gap:** Measure latency between a worker finishing a sweep/role and the next sweep being dispatched/started.
2. **Stage Dwell Time Distribution:** Track duration spent in each stage across the lifecycle:
   - `Issue Created` → `loom:curated`
   - `loom:curated` → `loom:issue` (Approval latency)
   - `loom:issue` → `loom:building` (Queue dispatch latency)
   - `loom:building` → `loom:review-requested` (Build duration)
   - `loom:review-requested` → `loom:pr` / Merged (Judge & merge queue latency)
3. **Dispatch Admission & Starvation Signals:** Export counters/spans when a sweep attempt exits prematurely due to worktree locks, lease collisions, or no eligible work found.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Stage dwell time metrics exported to OTLP / SigNoz.
- [ ] Worker idle-between-jobs time tracked per host.
- [ ] Admission failure reasons (lock contention, lease conflict, empty queue) visible in telemetry.

issues.title: dashboard: show a sweep's live Spot compute jobs as nested subprocesses
issues.body:
## Goal
On dashboard.2amlogic.com, show each active sweep's live Spot batch jobs (SPICE grids submitted by `klt sim --backend batch`) **nested under that sweep** as subprocesses, instead of only in the separate "running compute" list (#8305). The operator asked for this on 2026-09-24, after ruling that the AWS workers send SPICE to Spot (2AMLogic/2am#1004). Once that ruling is live, a worker's sweeps spend most of their SPICE time off-host, and the dashboard should show which sweep is paying for which instance.

## Today
- The `ephemeral_compute` launch record is emitted from the **submitting host**, by 2am's `batch-fleet-provision.sh launch`, which inherits the environment of klt, and klt inherits the sweep's.
- D1 already indexes `sweep_id` on any record kind (`telemetry.ts` `extractRecordFields`), but nothing sends one.
- The link breaks at three points:
  1. The daemon sets no `LOOM_SWEEP_ID` on the sweep child. Only `LOOM_TERMINAL_ID=daemon-<id>` carries the id (`sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs`).
  2. 2am's `report_record` drops string extras other than `instance_id` and `instance_type`.
  3. The Durable Object's `ActiveComputeState` and the web `ActiveComputeJob`/`parseActiveComputeJob` whitelist fields, and `sweepId` isn't among them.

## Plan
1. **Daemon:** `cmd.env("LOOM_SWEEP_ID", sweep_id)` on the sweep child.
2. **2am** (`batch-fleet-provision.sh`): stamp `sweep_id` on both launch-record emissions. Read it from `$LOOM_SWEEP_ID`, falling back to a `$LOOM_TERMINAL_ID` of the form `daemon-<id>` for daemons that predate step 1. Allow it as a string extra restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.
3. **Backend** (`fleetState.ts`): carry `sweepId` on `ActiveComputeState`.
4. **Web:** add `sweepId` to `ActiveComputeJob`; `buildFleetView` joins jobs to sweeps **by `sweepId` alone**. The compute entry's `hostId` is the submitter's ingest identity, and it doesn't always match the sweep's host.
   - Render a nested "subprocesses" list under the sweep in the fleet overview card and in the host-detail sweep row: instance type, Spot, elapsed time, and the leaked flag.
   - Jobs with no matching live sweep stay in the "running compute" section, so an orphaned instance is never hidden.

## Redaction
No change to what's public. `ephemeral_compute`'s public allowlist stays `["kind"]`, and `activeCompute` stays empty for unauthenticated viewers, so the nesting only renders for Access-authenticated viewers.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A sweep that submits a batch job shows it nested under the sweep, both on the fleet card and in host detail, while the job is live.
- [ ] The job disappears from under the sweep when its completion record retires it.
- [ ] A job whose sweep isn't in `activeSweeps` still appears in "running compute", and a leaked job is still flagged.
- [ ] The public snapshot is unchanged.

issues.title: Investigate PR approval invalidations: 34 stale-SHA re-reviews vs 19 healthy repair laps
issues.body:
## Problem

`loom-daemon pr-latency` (#8923) measured the PR pipeline across 80 PRs on 2026-09-26 and found that **approval invalidations are the largest single source of measured waste** in the sample:

- **PL5a approval invalidations: 34** — a PR was in the `loom:pr` (approved) state and went back to `loom:review-requested`.
- **PL5b repair laps: 19** — the healthy loop (Judge rejected, Doctor fixed, review again).

So the fleet is spending **more** Judge laps re-reviewing work that had *already been approved* than it spends on the rejection-and-repair loop that is supposed to be the normal cost of review.

Each PL5a event is a full extra Judge review of a PR that had already passed. Unlike a repair lap, nothing was wrong with the work — the verdict was invalidated because the head SHA moved past the verdict's recorded marker.

## Evidence

`#8935` alone was approved and sent back to review **three times in 80 minutes**:

```
17:46:21  labeled loom:pr
18:01:09  labeled loom:review-requested   <- invalidation 1
18:31:20  labeled loom:pr
18:33:57  labeled loom:review-requested   <- invalidation 2
18:39:24  labeled loom:pr
18:41:36  labeled loom:review-requested   <- invalidation 3
18:54:04  labeled loom:pr
```

Other repeat offenders in the same sample: #8954 (2), #8962 (2), #9052 (2).

The mechanism is `claim_reconciliation::invalidate_verdict` (`loom-daemon/src/claim_reconciliation.rs`, `reconcile_pr_verdicts` ~L3396): it clears the verdict label and re-applies `loom:review-requested` when the head SHA has moved past the verdict's recorded marker. That behaviour is **correct** in isolation — a verdict against a stale SHA is not a verdict. The question this issue asks is whether the *rate* is acceptable, and what is moving those SHAs.

## Investigation needed (measure before changing anything)

The same discipline #8923 used applies here — do not assume the mechanism:

1. **What moves the head SHA after approval?** Candidates worth separating: a Champion/merge-path rebase, a Doctor push racing an approval, an auto-format or version-bump commit, a stacking operation. Each implies a different fix.
2. **Is the re-review substantive?** If the second verdict is identical to the first in every case, the re-review is pure cost; if it ever differs, the invalidation is doing real work and the rate is the price of correctness.
3. **Is there a cheap equivalence test?** E.g. a SHA move whose diff-vs-base is unchanged (a pure rebase onto a moved `main`) arguably should not invalidate a verdict at all, whereas new commits obviously should.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The causes of head-SHA movement after approval are categorised and counted over a real sample, not assumed.
- [ ] For each category, a decision is recorded: invalidation is correct and stays, or it is avoidable and how.
- [ ] If any category is avoidable, one is implemented, with the PL5a count before/after reported from `loom-daemon pr-latency`.
- [ ] PL5a and PL5b remain counted separately — conflating the waste with the healthy repair loop is explicitly out of bounds (it would turn 34 into 53 and make correct behaviour look like half the problem).

## Notes

Discovered while implementing #8923; measuring this satisfies that issue's AC5, and this issue owns *acting* on it. Fixing it means changing verdict/reconciliation behaviour, which did not belong in #8923's already-complex measurement PR.

Figures are reproducible with `loom-daemon pr-latency --repo rjwalters/loom --limit 80` and will drift — re-measure before acting on any single number.

issues.title: merge-pr.sh: the 'requires-daemon: merge-pr >= 0.19.172' floor is stale; fail-closed loom-pr-guard needs >= 0.19.375
issues.body:
## Problem

`defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` declares its `merge-pr` daemon floor as

```
# requires-daemon: merge-pr >= 0.19.172   verdict-contradiction guard (#8112, landed in #8124)
```

but several `merge-pr` sub-subcommands were added later, and at least one of them is **fail-closed** (it refuses the merge when the daemon cannot answer):

| call site | first `VERSION` carrying it | fail direction |
|---|---|---|
| `merge-pr loom-pr-guard` (#8926, `e3275d0e5`, merged at 0.19.374) | 0.19.375 | **closed** — refuses the merge |
| `merge-pr stale-checks` (#8416, `8f86ef09c`, merged at 0.19.220) | 0.19.221 | closed — refuses the merge |
| `merge-pr head-sync-retry` (#8429, `3916b4909`, merged at 0.19.230) | 0.19.231 | see `_HMR_*` handling |
| `merge-pr delete-branch` (#8191 local-branch-cleanup slice) | first release after it merges | advisory: warns and keeps the branch |

(Versions from `git show <merge-commit>:VERSION`; the post-merge bump adds one.)

So a host running, say, 0.19.300 passes the declared floor, then has every merge refused by the `loom:pr` guard. The refusal's `_mp_daemon_roll_hint` then says "requires loom-daemon >= 0.19.172 … the resolved binary reports 0.19.300". The operator is told to roll to a floor the host already satisfies. That is the exact failure #8285/#8386 introduced the marker to prevent.

`scripts/check-daemon-subcommand-versions.sh` tracks floors per **top-level** subcommand (`merge-pr`), not per sub-subcommand, so it cannot notice any of this. #8897 is the same blind spot for `merge-pr-refs` modes. This issue covers the `merge-pr` family's marker. It should be fixed together with #8897, or it should reference it.

## Suggested fix

- Raise the `merge-pr` floor to the version that first carries its newest **fail-closed** sub-subcommand (0.19.375 as of this writing). It has to stay at or below `VERSION`, which the checker enforces.
- Consider teaching `check-daemon-subcommand-versions.sh` to key on `(subcommand, sub-subcommand)` for the `merge-pr` / `merge-pr-refs` families. The floor would then move mechanically when a new sub-subcommand lands. Otherwise every future slice of #8191 repeats this.
- Keep the edit to `merge-pr.sh` zero-growth, since it is frozen by the file-size ratchet. A marker edit is an in-place change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `merge-pr` floor marker names a version at or above the first release carrying every fail-closed `merge-pr <x>` call in the script.
- [ ] `test-merge-pr-daemon-version-floor.sh` (or a successor) fails when a fail-closed `merge-pr <x>` call is added without the floor moving.

Found while building the #8191 local-branch-cleanup slice.

issues.title: forge_events Phase 2 follow-ups: queueHeadWake naming, per-loop wake amplification, and wake-counter visibility
issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Summary

Non-blocking findings from the Judge review of PR #8994 (ADR-0021 Phase 2,
epic #8764). None of them blocked that merge — the seam is correct,
default-off, and well tested. Items 1 and 2 are best settled **before** any
consumer is defaulted on (Phase 3), because one is a user-facing config key
and the other is an operator-facing bound.

## Observed (measured on `feature/issue-8766` @ `6ebc3236`)

### 1. `forgeEvents.events.queueHeadWake` names an effect it does not produce

The flag ticks `claim_reconciliation`'s periodic pass. That is a defensible
loop to attach a wake to, but it is **not** a queue-head re-check:

- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/ready_queue.rs` re-derives the ready queue
  *inside every work-finder tick*; there is no separate head-re-check loop.
- Releasing a claim early therefore does not move the head early — the work
  finder still has to tick before the freed issue is dispatched.
- `WORK_FINDER_EVENT_TYPES` is still `["issues", "issue_comment"]`, so a
  `pull_request` close (the canonical "a merge released a claim" signal, and
  the one event type #8989 named for the widening) does **not** wake the loop
  that actually moves the head.

Two candidate dispositions, either is fine:

- Rename the key/env to what it does (`claimReconcileWake` /
  `LOOM_FORGE_EVENTS_CLAIM_RECONCILE_WAKE`) while it is brand new and
  default-off, so the rename is free; **or**
- Keep the name and add `"pull_request"` to `WORK_FINDER_EVENT_TYPES` (with a
  test), which makes the key's name true — this is exactly the one-line
  widening #8989's acceptance offered conditionally and that PR #8994 closed
  without adopting or explicitly declining.

### 2. The documented amplification bound is the work-finder's, not every loop's

`wake.rs`'s `DEFAULT_MIN_SPACING_SECS` doc and `defaults/docs/forge-events.md`
§4.1 both state the general formula (`interval / minSpacingSecs`) correctly,
then work the example only for the smallest case ("2x at the work finder's 60s
default"). Measured cadences of the three wired loops against the shared 30s
floor:

| Loop | Default cadence | Max early-tick multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| work finder | 60s | 2x |
| watch monitor (`DEFAULT_WATCH_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SECS`) | 120s | 4x |
| claim reconciliation (`DEFAULT_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECS`) | 600s | **20x** |
| claim reconciliation, safehouse (`DEFAULT_SAFEHOUSE_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECS`) | 1800s | **60x** |

Claim reconciliation is also the heaviest `gh` consumer of the three: each pass
runs `reconcile_workspace` + `reconcile_pr_claims` + `reconcile_pr_verdicts`
per registered workspace root.

Suggested: state the per-loop multiplier in §4.1's table, and consider whether
the spacing floor should be per-consumer (or derived from the loop's own
cadence) rather than one shared 30s constant.

### 3. The wake counters are not surfaced anywhere at runtime

`WakeCounters { prompts, early_ticks, throttled }` is populated and asserted by
tests, but nothing reads it outside tests: no `loom-daemon status` line
(contrast Phase 1's `cli/status_render/forge_events_line.rs`), and no per-tick
log — only the one-shot "armed" `log::info!` at spawn. An operator who arms a
consumer has no way to see whether it is doing anything. Since ADR-0021's plan
is explicitly "run it and measure before defaulting on", the measurement
surface is worth having before Phase 3.

### 4. Inverted "in which case" in four wiring comments

All four read as if the *armed* case were the plain interval; the intended
antecedent is the disarmed case:

- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` (two sites, `spawn_work_finder_task` and
  `spawn_multi_work_finder_task`)
- `loom-daemon/src/claim_reconciliation.rs` (`spawn_periodic_reconciliation_task`)
- `loom-daemon/src/watch_registry/monitor_loop.rs`

e.g. "Disarmed unless `forgeEvents.events.workFinderTick` is on, in which case
it is exactly `tokio::time::interval(interval)`." Comment-only; a one-word fix
each ("otherwise").

### 5. `EarlyTicker::tick` is not cancel-safe, unlike the `Interval::tick` it replaces

Every current call site is a bare `.await`, so nothing is wrong today. But
`EarlyTicker` is documented as a drop-in for `tokio::time::Interval`, whose
`tick()` **is** cancel-safe; `EarlyTicker::tick` can consume a `Notify` permit
and then be dropped inside a `select!`, silently losing that wake. Worth a
`# Cancel safety` paragraph on the method so a future caller does not assume
the `Interval` contract.

### 6. PR #8994's body says "28 tests in `forge_events/wake/tests.rs`"

Measured: 24 test functions (`cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib forge_events::`
reports 24 `wake::tests::*` cases, all passing). Cosmetic; noted only because
the repo treats measurable claims as measurable.

## Inferred (hypothesis, not measured)

The practical cost of item 2 scales with registered workspace count and open
`loom:pr` / `loom:changes-requested` PR count, neither of which I measured on a
live fleet host. The #4429 breaker still caps the worst case, so this is a
traffic-efficiency question rather than a safety one — but it should be
measured, not assumed, before `queueHeadWake` is defaulted on.

## Out of scope

- Any change to a loop's decision logic, threshold, or cadence constant.
- Memo integration (ADR-0014 Lever A) — Phase 3.

## Context

- PR: #8994 · Issue: #8766 · Epic: #8764 · ADR: `docs/adr/0021-forge-event-plane.md`
- Prior disposition issue: #8989 (closed by #8994)
- Docs: `defaults/docs/forge-events.md` § 4.1

issues.title: #8248 freshness guard: in-place re-runs still lose to a busy main (input-aware staleness or a fast required-checks workflow)
issues.body:
## Problem

Split out of #8914, covering the second finding in the comment on that issue. **In-place re-runs of stale required checks can still lose to a busy `main`.**

The #8248 freshness guard treats **any** base-tip move after a required check started as making that check's green result stale. On 2026-09-25 `main` moved at 14:26, 14:47 and 14:58 UTC, and each move landed before a full CI run (about 8 min) finished. PR #8641 lost the race three times, including twice with operator in-place re-runs.

#8914 reduces the window. It re-runs only the stale **required** jobs, in place, and merges as soon as they are fresh. There is a platform limit, though. Verified 2026-09-25: GitHub allows **one** job re-run per workflow run at a time, and a second `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` in the same run returns `403 "The workflow run containing this job is already running"`. All 19 required contexts on `main` live in the single `ci.yml` run, so they are re-run one after another, at roughly 12–20 s each (a few minutes in total). That is much shorter than the full run, but it is not zero.

## Candidate directions (need a design pass, possibly an operator decision)

1. **Input-aware staleness.** A base move whose diff touches no ratchet/baseline file and no input of any required check does not make the checks stale. This narrows #8248's "any move" rule, so it needs a precise definition of "required-check input" and must fail closed when that input set can't be determined. #8248's incident (a baseline tightened under an in-flight PR) must stay covered.
2. **Put the required checks in their own fast workflow.** If the required ratchet/lint jobs lived in a separate workflow (for example `required-checks.yml`), a single whole-run re-run (`POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun`) would refresh all of them in parallel in about 1 minute, instead of one job at a time inside `ci.yml`. This is a CI restructuring, so check it against `ci-principles.md`.
3. **Merge serialization.** Have Champion hold off merging other PRs while one PR's in-place re-run is in flight.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A design decision is recorded for which of these (if any) to pursue.
- [ ] Any change to #8248's staleness predicate keeps the 2026-09-18 incident timeline refused (see `stale_checks/tests.rs`).

Related: #8914, #8248, #8508, #8641.

issues.title: Route daemon Codex jobs into private clones with recoverable logs and checkpoints
issues.body:
Part of #4489 and the operator-requested private-clone workstream in #6896. Second implementation step.

## Problem

The Codex session adapter currently sends the host working directory and host workspace context to the container. Host status, worktree cleanup and sweep checkpoints likewise assume host-visible files. A private clone is not usable by the daemon until execution paths and retained job state are mapped explicitly.

## Recommended implementation

Wire the private-clone workspace and exclusive account lease from #8785 through the existing runtime/account selection and spawn-worker → spawn-codex → supervised session-exec path. Preserve the logical host repository identity for scheduling and reporting; resolve all child working-directory, project-root, worktree and hook paths to the private container workspace.

Prepare and verify the selected workspace before claiming an issue or starting model work. Hold the lease until worker termination is acknowledged, including descendants. Integrate with the #8773 cancellation protocol rather than inventing another lifetime mechanism.

Stream output through the existing host supervisor. Preserve the minimum durable checkpoint, branch/PR and artifact metadata needed for status, resume and cleanup through a narrowly scoped export/control interface. Do not regain file visibility by mounting host repositories or daemon control-state directories read-write into the worker.

Exchange code using the forge: fetch the configured base or resumable issue branch, push the issue branch, and create/update its PR through existing helpers. Any worktrees the role needs remain entirely inside the private clone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scheduled standalone roles and explicit/scheduled sweep launches use the same selected account, validated workspace and lease. All account paths respect one active job per account; unavailable/busy sessions yield an accurate reason and release temporary reservations.
- [ ] Child cwd, Loom context, installed helpers, guard bridge locations and runtime instructions resolve within the private clone. No stale host-absolute worktree path is passed as an executable child path.
- [ ] A credential-free integration fixture exercises the normal adapter chain through prepare, issue branch mutation, push/PR handoff, log capture and cleanup. Existing capability restrictions remain in force until #8787.
- [ ] Dashboard/status retain runtime, provider, account, logical repository, sweep/role identity and terminal outcome; logs remain accessible after cancellation or container loss without secret material.
- [ ] Daemon restart and worker interruption preserve checkpoints and branch/PR association. Unpushed work is retained; account failover must explicitly stop for recovery when the remote branch/checkpoint is insufficient to resume.
- [ ] Cancellation, host-supervisor death, failed startup, container disappearance and hung cleanup do not release a lease while a child can still write. Existing #8773 tests continue passing.
- [ ] Reapers and cleanup target the owned private workspace and lease, never the host's similarly named worktree. Cleanup/export inputs cannot select arbitrary host paths.
- [ ] Audit MCP/control and run-job paths reachable from the worker: no helper may turn a private-clone request into arbitrary host-repository writes or mounts. Map supported jobs to the owned workspace; refuse unsupported host-path-dependent jobs explicitly in the first version.
- [ ] Existing Claude and host-mounted session dispatch retain their behavior. No global runtime capability/default change ships here.

## Implementation starting points — curator must verify

Verified against origin/main at 135183d9b2527cb2cc81d2c5d8e0ba1f2213c645:

- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` — session invocation currently uses the host cwd and forwards workspace/worktree paths.
- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/mod.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/runtime_preflight.rs` — selection, reservation, preflight and normal launch seam.
- `loom-daemon/src/session_exec.rs` — supervised child ownership, cancellation and cleanup acknowledgement.
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/log_paths.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/cli/sweep_checkpoint.rs` — host observability, recovery and cleanup assumptions.

Implement new executable logic in Rust; limit shell changes to adapter wiring.

## Affected Files

Re-verified present on `origin/main` @ `b9f1359d3594b9c51fbaba966fa3beeda659fee2`, 2026-09-23 (curator pre-flight):

- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` - adapter wiring only: stop forwarding host cwd/workspace paths when the private-clone lease from #8785 is active
- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/mod.rs` - runtime/account selection seam; resolve workspace before claim
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs` - reservation/dispatch seam; route to the private-clone workspace path
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/runtime_preflight.rs` - preflight seam for scheduled standalone role launches
- `loom-daemon/src/session_exec.rs` - supervised child ownership, cwd resolution, cancellation/cleanup acknowledgement
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/log_paths.rs` - log path resolution; must point at exported logs, not host worktree paths
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper.rs` - cleanup/reaping must target the owned private workspace, never a similarly-named host worktree
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/sweep_checkpoint.rs` - checkpoint export/import through the narrowly scoped control interface

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: the credential-free integration fixture named in Acceptance Criteria #3 — exercise prepare → claim → issue-branch mutation → push/PR handoff → log capture → cleanup entirely against the private-clone workspace, with no host-repository mount.
- [ ] Automated tests: extend or add coverage in `loom-daemon`'s existing `session_exec`/`sweep_registry` test modules for lease-not-released-while-child-can-write across cancellation, host-supervisor death, failed startup, container disappearance and hung cleanup (AC #6) — confirm existing #8773 tests still pass.
- [ ] Automated tests: reaper/cleanup unit test confirming a private-clone job's reaping never touches a host worktree of the same logical name (AC #7).
- [ ] Manual verification: run a scheduled standalone role and a sweep-dispatched job through the private-clone path back-to-back, confirming both share the same account-selection/lease/workspace machinery and the one-active-job-per-account invariant holds (AC #1).
- [ ] Manual verification: kill the daemon mid-job and restart it; confirm the checkpoint and branch/PR association survive and unpushed work is retained (AC #4).
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm existing Claude and host-mounted Codex session dispatch are unaffected — no global runtime default changes (AC #8).

## Dependencies

- [x] #8785 — independent-clone workspace lifecycle and exclusive account lease. **Closed** via merged PR #8800 ("feat: add account-private Codex session workspaces"), confirmed 2026-09-23.

#8787 follows this change. #4496 remains the live rollout/canary gate; passing fixture tests here does not authorize production mutable Codex work. Coordinate with the existing #8776 lock-lifetime fix without duplicating it.

issues.body:
## Context

Sub-issue of #8714 (slice 5 of 5, "G3 `session.analysis`, then G4"). Parent issue's own scoping — see #8714 for the full gap analysis. This is the last slice in the parent's suggested ordering, riding on the `session.summary` sibling sub-issue (slice 2) for its input data.

## Part A — G3: `session.analysis`

### Problem

`session.summary` (sibling sub-issue) carries raw counters only — no derived signal. There is no per-session anomaly/quality rollup on the wire at all.

### Proposal

A `session.analysis` record kind, derived from `session.summary`: retry loops detected, longest tool call, cost in USD computed from the single pricing table, anomaly flags (e.g. `tokens > p99 for role`). **LLM-written prose summaries are explicitly a later slice, not this issue** (per #8714) — this is bounded, mechanical derivation only.

Must obey the same wire-safety rule as `session.summary`: no prompts, generated code, raw tool arguments/output, keys or emails on the wire.

## Part B — G4: event-bus topics with no record kind

### Problem

`daemon.drain.*`, `daemon.capacity.advisory`, `daemon.preflight.advisory` and `epic.issue.*` have no `daemon.event` record kind, so the wire schema doesn't cover the whole frozen event-bus taxonomy. Per #8714: "Follow-on, not blocking" — i.e. this half has no dependency on Part A landing first, and could in principle ship independently, but is bundled into this slice per the parent's own suggested ordering.

### Proposal

Give the four named event-bus topics a `daemon.event` record kind so they can be shipped through the same exporter(s) as everything else (the G1 sink list, sibling sub-issue).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `session.analysis` record kind exists, derived from `session.summary` records, containing retry-loop detection, longest tool call, USD cost (from the existing single pricing table), and at least one anomaly flag class (e.g. a token-count percentile-based flag).
- [ ] `session.analysis` obeys the same wire-safety rule as `session.summary` — extend the redaction test suite for this record kind too.
- [ ] `daemon.drain.*`, `daemon.capacity.advisory`, `daemon.preflight.advisory`, and `epic.issue.*` each carry a `daemon.event` record kind and are shippable through the configured exporter(s).
- [ ] No LLM-written prose summary is introduced in this slice (explicitly deferred, per #8714's Proposal for G3).

## Affected Files

- New module for `session.analysis` derivation (exact location TBD — likely alongside wherever `session.summary` is defined, per the sibling sub-issue)
- The existing single pricing table (exact location TBD — grep for the cost-by-* SQL views mentioned in #8714's "What already exists" table, or the pricing table they read from) — reused, not reimplemented, for the USD cost field
- `loom-daemon/src/event_bus.rs` (~lines 80-95 per #8714's citation) — the in-memory event bus; add the `daemon.event` record kind for the four named topics
- Redaction test suite (same file the `session.summary` sibling sub-issue extends) — extend again for `session.analysis`

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a fixture pair of `session.summary` records (one with a detectable retry loop, one without) produces the expected `session.analysis` output
- [ ] Automated tests: extend the redaction test suite for `session.analysis` — no prompt, tool output, key, or email appears in the derived record
- [ ] Automated tests: each of the four named event-bus topics produces a `daemon.event` record when emitted, and the record is exporter-shippable
- [ ] Manual verification: a day of daemon work produces both `session.analysis` rows and `daemon.event` records visible in whatever backend is available for testing

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `complex`**: both halves are bounded, mechanical derivations from already-well-specified inputs (`session.summary`'s fields; the four named, already-frozen event-bus topics) — a mistake would surface as an incorrect derived value or a missing record kind, caught by straightforward test comparison, not a silent architectural regression.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8757 (`session.summary`, sibling sub-issue, slice 2 of #8714's decomposition): merged 2026-09-23 — Part A can now derive from its landed record shape.

Part B (G4) has no dependency on Part A or the sibling sub-issue and could be built independently, per #8714's own "Follow-on, not blocking" note — bundled here only per the parent's suggested ordering.

## Related

- Parent: #8714 (observability multi-sink export)
- Sibling sub-issue: G3 `session.summary` (this issue's Part A derives from its output)
- Sibling sub-issue: G1 multi-exporter (both record kinds ship through its sink list)

issues.title: dispatch_plan B: fleet-wide merge of host plans as a shipped rule (merge_plans + shared fixture with dashboard)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Split out of #9288 by its Curator (https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9288#issuecomment-5867611696); the operator chose to file this separately rather than fold it in.

**Depends on #9288** (PR A: host-local `dispatch_plan` annotation). Do not start until it merges.

**B — fleet merge as a shipped rule (ask 2).** `work_finder/dispatch_plan/merge.rs`: `merge_plans(&[HostPlan]) -> FleetPlan`. Rule: fold by `repo#issue`; primary = most advanced `plan_state` (running > next > queued > blocked), tie → the host whose `shard.host_shard == owning_shard`, tie → lower `position`, tie → host id. Fleet order = `plan_state` rank, then round-robin interleave of hosts' `position` (position asc, host id asc). Cross-host `workspace_priority` is deliberately **not** compared (per-host, unsynced). Pin with one JSON fixture read by both the Rust test and `dashboard/web/test/workQueue.test.ts` (fixture precedent: `dashboard/test/fixtures/sweep-identity.json` — whether Rust reads it too is not traced); port to `workQueue.ts` replacing `mergeFleetQueue` / `compareItems`. Optional `loom-daemon queue --fleet` when a fleet-state URL is configured. New `defaults/docs/dispatch-plan.md`. ~5 points, `complex`.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `834d085f`)

### Status update

**Dependency #9288 is done.** It closed 2026-09-28T11:15:35Z via PR #9316
("feat(work_finder): publish the dispatch plan — shaped position, plan_state,
gate and slots"), merged 2026-09-28T11:15:34Z. Confirmed on `origin/main`:
`loom-daemon/src/types/dispatch_plan.rs` and
`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/dispatch_plan.rs` both exist, with `RowPlan`
(`position`, `plan_state`, `keys`, `gate`, `in_slice`, `hot`, `owning_shard`,
`repo_cap`), `PlanState`, `PlanGate`, `PlanShard` (`host_shard`,
`shard_count`), `PlanSlots`, and `DispatchPlanContext` all landed. There is
**no `HostPlan` or `FleetPlan` type yet** — this issue's `merge_plans(&[HostPlan]) -> FleetPlan`
is new surface to add, not an extension of an existing one.

**Related open work (#9063) disregarded**: `check-duplicate.sh --issue 9310`
surfaced #9063 (Champion PR-merge batching), which name-checks
`dispatch_plan.rs` in its own Affected Files as "worth checking whether
merge-train bundling composes with or duplicates" this plan abstraction. Read
it — it's a different subsystem (PR-merge batching under CI congestion, not
fleet dispatch-order merging) and only flags the overlap as something to be
aware of during its own design, not a scope conflict with this issue. No
absorption needed.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/dispatch_plan.rs` (or a new sibling module —
      see Implementation Guidance) exports `merge_plans(&[HostPlan]) -> FleetPlan`
      implementing the fold-by-`repo#issue` rule from the original issue body:
      primary = most advanced `plan_state` (`running` > `next` > `queued` >
      `blocked`), tie → host whose `PlanShard::host_shard == owning_shard`, tie
      → lower `position`, tie → host id.
- [ ] Fleet order = `plan_state` rank, then round-robin interleave of hosts'
      `position` (position asc, host id asc).
- [ ] Cross-host `workspace_priority` (`dashboard/src/queueState.ts:91`,
      `loom-daemon/src/cli/ready_queue_cmd.rs`) is NOT compared during the
      merge — it stays per-host/unsynced, matching the original issue's
      explicit exclusion.
- [ ] A JSON fixture pins `merge_plans`'s expected output and is read by BOTH
      the Rust test and `dashboard/web/test/workQueue.test.ts` — whether the
      existing `dashboard/test/fixtures/sweep-identity.json` precedent is
      literally read by Rust too was not traced by the original issue text;
      confirm during implementation rather than assuming.
- [ ] `dashboard/web/src/workQueue.ts`'s `mergeFleetQueue`/`compareItems`
      (`workQueue.ts:147`, `:190`) is ported to consume the new merge rule,
      replacing its current ordering logic.
- [ ] New doc `defaults/docs/dispatch-plan.md` describes the fleet-merge rule
      (the existing `dispatch_plan.rs` module doc covers only the host-local
      Phase A annotation, not this fleet-merge step).
- [ ] Optional: `loom-daemon` gains a fleet-view of the merged plan (e.g. a
      `--fleet` flag on the existing `ready_queue_cmd.rs` CLI surface) when a
      fleet-state URL is configured — the original issue leaves this optional,
      so treat it as a stretch goal, not a blocking AC item.

### Implementation Guidance

- **File layout is undecided, not settled.** The original issue names
  `work_finder/dispatch_plan/merge.rs`, implying converting the current
  single-file `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/dispatch_plan.rs` (214 lines as of
  `834d085f`) into a `dispatch_plan/` module directory. An equally valid
  alternative is a new sibling file (e.g.
  `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/dispatch_plan_merge.rs`) that imports the
  existing types without restructuring the module. Either satisfies the ACs;
  pick based on how large `merge_plans` + its tests end up being.
- `HostPlan` (per-host: hostname/id + `Vec<RowPlan>`-equivalent keyed by
  `repo#issue`) and `FleetPlan` (the merged, ordered result) are new types to
  define — there is nothing to extend today.
- The comparator keys (`PlanKey` in `types/dispatch_plan.rs:61`) already carry
  the per-row ordering inputs; the merge rule's tie-breaks (position, host id)
  layer on top rather than replacing them.

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/dispatch_plan.rs` — extend, or split into a
  `dispatch_plan/` module with a new `merge.rs` (see Implementation Guidance)
- `loom-daemon/src/types/dispatch_plan.rs` — add `HostPlan`/`FleetPlan` types
- `dashboard/web/src/workQueue.ts` — replace `mergeFleetQueue`/`compareItems`
  with the ported merge rule
- `dashboard/web/test/workQueue.test.ts` — update to read the shared JSON
  fixture
- New: a JSON fixture shared by the Rust test and `workQueue.test.ts`
- New: `defaults/docs/dispatch-plan.md`
- Optional: `loom-daemon/src/cli/ready_queue_cmd.rs` — `--fleet` surface

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a Rust unit test in `dispatch_plan`'s test module
      exercising `merge_plans` against the shared JSON fixture (tie-break
      ordering: plan_state rank, owning_shard, position, host id).
- [ ] Automated tests: `dashboard/web/test/workQueue.test.ts` updated to
      assert the ported merge/compare logic against the same fixture.
- [ ] Manual verification: with two synthetic host plans covering the same
      `repo#issue` at different `plan_state`s, confirm the merged fleet order
      matches the rule (most-advanced state wins, tie-breaks apply in order).
- [ ] Edge cases: two hosts both `blocked` on the same issue with no shard
      match (tie-break falls through to position, then host id); a single-host
      fleet (merge is a no-op pass-through).

### Dependencies

- [x] #9288 — merged via PR #9316 (2026-09-28T11:15:34Z). Cleared; no longer
      blocking.

issues.title: Build failure on main (11e5ff1e0): eta.rs:589 calls queue_blocked::list_open with 2 args after #9261 made it 3 — every open PR is red
issues.body:
`main` at `11e5ff1e0` does not compile. Every open PR's CI is red as a result, and every PR merge ref inherits the failure. This is a semantic merge conflict between two PRs that merged within ~90 minutes of each other; neither PR's own CI could have caught it.

## The error

```
error[E0061]: this function takes 3 arguments but 2 arguments were supplied
   --> loom-daemon/src/observability/eta.rs:589:19
    |
589 |             match super::queue_blocked::list_open(root.clone(), label).await {
    |                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ argument #3 of type `&'static str` is missing
note: function defined here
   --> loom-daemon/src/observability/queue_blocked.rs:143:21
error: could not compile `loom-daemon` (lib) due to 1 previous error
```

## How the two halves landed

- **PR #9355** (`8321f2431`, merged 15:36 UTC) — commit `090db28a8`, "feat(eta): tracker, eager stage journal, eta.estimate/eta.outcome (#9289 slice 1b)" — **added** the call site `loom-daemon/src/observability/eta.rs:589`, calling `list_open(root.clone(), label)` against the then-current 2-parameter signature.
- **PR #9261** (`11e5ff1e0`, merged 17:05 UTC) — commit `376c8b1c4`, "feat(daemon): forge-call accounting + identity-keyed, disk-backed listing cache (#9251, #9252)" — **changed** `queue_blocked::list_open` to take a third `caller: &'static str` parameter and updated the call sites that existed *on its own base*, which did not yet include `eta.rs:589`.

Each PR was green against its own base. The conflict only exists in the union, and git reports no textual conflict because the two edits are in different files.

## Evidence

- `main`'s own push run is red with exactly this error: run `36455689238` (CI, `11e5ff1e0`, conclusion `failure`).
- The immediately preceding main commit `b4b5f06fd` is green.
- Downstream jobs fail 127 (`./target/debug/loom-daemon: No such file or directory`) because the daemon build never produces a binary — `Install Surface Checks`, `Installer Integration Tests`, `Native Port Suites`, `Codex Adapter Smoke`, `Daemon Checks`, `Release Build Check` and all `Rust Unit Tests` / `Rust OTLP` shards are collateral, not independent failures.

## Fix

Pass the missing `caller` argument at `loom-daemon/src/observability/eta.rs:589`, matching the `&'static str` caller-label convention `376c8b1c4` established for the other `list_open` call sites (use a caller string that identifies the ETA review-label scan, consistent with its siblings). Then confirm `cargo clippy --package loom-daemon --package loom-api -- -D warnings` is clean.

Worth a sweep of the rest of `376c8b1c4`'s signature changes for the same shape: any call site added by a PR that was already open when `376c8b1c4` merged is exposed the same way.

## Why this is urgent

`main` is the base of every open PR. Until this lands, no PR can go green, and the #8248 required-check-freshness guard will keep re-dating PRs into red runs. Surfaced while reviewing PR #9363, whose tree is unmodified and previously approved but is red purely from this base breakage.
