issues.title: ci-telemetry: a never-completing workflow run pins a repo's watermark indefinitely
issues.body:
Split out of #8898 (the "smaller gaps noted in the same review" list). #8898's PR
fixed the re-run gap only and deliberately left this one alone — confirmed still
present on that branch.

## Problem

`poll_repo` (`loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/poll.rs`) advances a repo's watermark
to `oldest_incomplete.unwrap_or(newest).max(watermark)`. A run that never reaches
a completed state (cancelled-but-stuck, a workflow abandoned mid-flight, a
`queued` run whose runner never arrives) is `hold()`-ed every cycle, so
`oldest_incomplete` stays at that run's `created_at` and the watermark never moves
past it — forever.

#8898's `.max(watermark)` clamp does **not** fix this: the clamp only stops the
watermark moving *backwards*. When the watermark is already older than
`oldest_incomplete`, `max` picks `oldest_incomplete`, which is the pinned value.

Consequence: the repo's listing floor (`runs_floor` = the older of the watermark
and the trailing 24h rescan window) is the pinned watermark once it is more than
24 hours old, so every cycle re-lists a window that grows without bound — one
extra runs page per 100 runs, per repo, per `intervalSecs`, indefinitely. It also
makes `ci-telemetry status`'s per-repo watermark misleading as a freshness signal.

## Suggested fix

Bound the hold: stop holding for an incomplete run once it is older than some
age (the rescan window is the natural bound, since anything inside the window is
re-listed regardless of the watermark), and/or treat a run that has been
incomplete across N cycles as abandoned. Either way, the run stays visible for as
long as the rescan window covers it, and the watermark is free to advance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run that never completes does not hold a repo's watermark past some
      bounded age; the watermark advances to the newest completed run.
- [ ] A run that is merely slow (completes within the bound) is still held and
      still exported exactly once — `an_in_progress_run_holds_the_watermark_and_is_emitted_once_it_completes`
      keeps passing.
- [ ] A fixture test pins the behaviour: an in-progress run older than the bound,
      several cycles, and the watermark is past it while the run is still exported
      if it completes inside the rescan window.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` — the watermark/in-progress paragraph
      (~line 225) and the "Re-runs" bullet describe the new bound.

## Not in scope

The other three gaps from the same review, each worth its own issue if it
matters: a renamed repo re-emits its runs; the runs list is not ETag-cached; a
crash between export and ledger write can emit duplicate histogram points.

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/poll.rs` - bound `hold()`/`oldest_incomplete` by age (or cycle count) so a never-completing run stops pinning the watermark past the rescan-window bound; likely changes `hold`'s signature to take `ctx.now`/`ctx.rescan_window` (or `ctx.initial_lookback`) so it can decide whether to hold at all.
- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/tests.rs` - add a fixture test for the bounded-hold behavior alongside the existing `an_in_progress_run_holds_the_watermark_and_is_emitted_once_it_completes` (line 583).
- `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` - the "Runs that are still in progress are not recorded yet" paragraph (currently ~line 304-307) and the "Re-runs" bullet (currently ~line 409-420) both describe the watermark hold as unbounded today; both need updating. (Line numbers as of 2026-09-27 — re-verify before editing.)

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: new fixture test in `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/tests.rs` — an in-progress run older than the bound, several cycles, watermark advances past it; a separate case confirms a run that completes within the bound is still held and still exported exactly once (`an_in_progress_run_holds_the_watermark_and_is_emitted_once_it_completes` must keep passing unmodified or be extended consistently with the new bound).
- [ ] Manual verification: `cargo test -p loom-daemon ci_telemetry::` passes locally.
- [ ] Edge cases: a run exactly at the bound boundary; multiple never-completing runs at different ages in the same cycle.

issues.title: Investigate and reduce PR latency: the review queue is 4h deep, but approved-awaiting-merge is 68h and changes-requested is 90h
issues.body:
## Problem

PR time-to-merge is strongly bimodal, and the slow mode is not where it is commonly assumed to be.

**Merged-PR sample** (last 40, 2026-09-23 22:18Z → 2026-09-25 16:11Z, ~0.96 PRs/hour into `main`):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Median merge latency | 0.69h (41 min) |
| p90 | 16.4h |
| Max | 32.0h |
| PRs force-pushed at least once | 8/40 |
| `loom:merge-conflict` applied | 0 |
| `loom:changes-requested` / `loom:ci-failure` events | 9 / 5 |

That sample suffers survivorship bias — the genuinely stuck PRs have not merged, so they are absent from it. **The open-PR queue is where the latency actually lives** (ages as of 2026-09-25 ~16:40Z):

| Queue | Count | Median age | Oldest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loom:review-requested` | 4 | **3.9h** | 22.3h (#8823) |
| `loom:pr` (approved, awaiting merge) | 5 | **68.5h** | 91.2h (#8531) |
| `loom:changes-requested` | 10 | **89.6h** | 183.1h (#8131) |
| held/other | 1 | 105.0h | #8486 |

So: **Judge throughput is not the bottleneck.** The review queue is four PRs deep with a median age under four hours. Two other queues are.

### Queue A — approved but unmerged (median 68.5h)

Four of the five `loom:pr` PRs carry an operator gate: #8531 (`loom:operator`), #8613 (`loom:operator`), #8680 (`loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator-decision`), #8893 (`loom:operator`). Only #8695 is a plain `loom:pr`. `WORK_PLAN.md` already names this as "Operator Attention: Merge-Risk-Hold Pileup" — implementation is finished and only a human merge decision is missing. These PRs age while fully built.

### Queue B — changes-requested that never come back (median 89.6h)

Ten PRs, and the oldest four are all also `loom:blocked`, mostly with a companion failure label: #8131 (`loom:merge-conflict`, 183h), #8314 (`loom:ci-failure`, 155h), #8351 (`loom:ci-failure`, 147h), #8440 (114h). Doctor is not clearing these, and `loom:blocked` means nothing re-queues them on its own. rjwalters/repo#192 (cited in `daemon-reference.md`) documents the adjacent stall mode: a verdict label with nothing to re-queue it.

## Proposal

This is a **research + improvement** task. Measure first, then act; do not assume a mechanism.

**Phase 1 — measure.** Decompose time-to-merge into its real segments rather than PR-open→merge:

- `loom:review-requested` → first Judge verdict (queue wait)
- verdict → `loom:pr` (approval path)
- `loom:pr` → merged, **split by whether an operator gate label is present** (this is the suspected dominant term)
- `loom:changes-requested` → next Doctor push, and the fraction that never get one
- count of verdict invalidations via `reconcile_pr_verdicts` (a re-review is a full extra lap)

Ideally this lands as a queryable artifact rather than a one-off script — PR #8692 (`loom:pr`) already commits cycle-time question/rollup/extract SQL for the shipped-work side, and this is the natural companion question set for the *unshipped* side.

**Phase 2 — mediate.** Candidate levers, to be chosen by what Phase 1 shows, not now:

- Surface queue ages where the operator sees them (`loom-daemon queue` landed in #8906 for the *issue* ready-queue; the PR queues have no equivalent view).
- Alert when a `loom:pr` PR exceeds an age threshold under an operator gate — the hold is legitimate, the silence is not.
- Give `loom:changes-requested` + `loom:blocked` PRs an explicit aging/escalation path so they cannot sit for 183h with no owner.
- Decide whether some operator-gate classes can be narrowed so fewer finished PRs need a human.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-segment latency is measurable on demand, not by hand-written one-off queries.
- [ ] The `loom:pr` → merged segment is reported split by operator-gate presence.
- [ ] The count and age of `loom:changes-requested` PRs with no subsequent Doctor push is reported.
- [ ] At least one mediation is implemented, chosen by the Phase-1 numbers, with the reasoning recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Verdict invalidations (stale-SHA re-reviews) are counted, so re-review cost is visible.

## Notes

Filed from a triage pass over PR/queue state, not a Builder run. All figures above are reproducible from `gh pr list` / the issue timeline API at the stated timestamps and will drift; re-measure before acting on any single number.

Related: the companion issues on telemetry record-kind registration contention and on the missing `loom:merge-conflict` signal for `loom:review-requested` PRs — both describe ways a PR makes an extra, avoidable lap through these queues.

issues.title: fleet-config: sync the fleet store at daemon start and on a timer
issues.body:
Follow-up to the `loom-daemon fleet-config` PR (branch `feature/fleet-config`), which reads an operator's fleet state store (`fleet.repo` / `LOOM_FLEET_REPO`) **on explicit command only**.

## Problem
With a store configured, a host still converges on it only when someone runs `fleet-config render` / `roster --apply` by hand. A store change lands as a reviewed commit and then sits unapplied until a human touches each host.

## Proposal
When `fleet.repo` is set, the daemon syncs from the store:
- **at startup**, before config-dependent loops are spawned: `fetch`, then `render` (machine tier + host-local tier), so the process that starts is the one configured by the store;
- **on a timer** (`fleet.syncIntervalSecs`, env override; the steady state is one conditional `304` per tick): `fetch` + `render --check` + `roster --check`, logging and publishing drift as an event / `status` field; applying automatically should be a separate opt-in (`fleet.autoApply`), since `roster --apply` deregisters workspaces.

Constraints to keep: roster stays fail-closed (no cached fallback, a both-flags record is a hard error); an unreachable forge at startup must not block boot (use the last good snapshot for config, skip roster); unset `fleet.repo` stays byte-identical.

## Acceptance
- Daemon start with `fleet.repo` set renders from the store before loops start; unset is unchanged.
- Timer-driven drift is visible in `loom-daemon status` without writes unless `fleet.autoApply` is on.
- Tests with an injected transport (no network).

issues.title: stale-checks: consumer repos' unspecced required contexts go stale on ANY base move — add per-repo input scopes or a conservative fallback
issues.body:
## Problem

The #8919 freshness guard (`loom-daemon merge-pr stale-checks`, table in `loom-daemon/src/merge_pr/stale_checks/inputs.rs`) fails closed for any required context with no spec in `SPECS`: *"A required context with no spec here is stale whenever D is non-empty."* That makes sense for loom's own repo, where the table is maintained. But `SPECS` is loom-owned and hardcoded, so **every consumer repo's required checks are unspecced**. In a consumer repo, any base move therefore marks every sibling PR stale.

Observed on 2026-09-30 in `2AMLogic/klayout-tools`, with 20 Judge-approved PRs queued:
- Each merge made every remaining PR's `Lint (ruff)` result stale.
- Each PR then needed a fresh CI run (a re-date push, which resets the verdict and, after one try, escalates to `loom:operator`) before it could merge.
- The queue could not drain without an operator re-verifying lint on the merged tree for each PR by hand.

## Proposal (either, or both)

1. **Per-repo input scopes.** Let a consumer repo declare its required contexts' `global` / `scanned` / `coupled` path sets in a tracked file, e.g. `.loom/stale-check-inputs.json`, merged over `SPECS`. Loom's `SPECS` stays authoritative for loom's own contexts.
2. **A conservative fallback for unspecced contexts outside loom:** use #8248's `started_at` rule, or treat the check as stale only when the base move touched files matching the check's workflow `paths:` filter. Currently they are stale on ANY base move.

Also see #9571 (re-verify deterministic ratchets on the merged tree at merge time). With that in place, a declared-deterministic context would need no fresh CI run at all.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A consumer repo can make an unrelated base move NOT stale its lint or ratchet contexts without editing loom.
- [ ] Unspecced contexts keep failing closed where no declaration exists, unless the fallback is explicitly chosen.
- [ ] Tests cover a consumer-repo declaration.

<!-- loom:provenance v1 build=unknown unknown unknown prompts=unknown unknown sweep=none story=none trace=fca300c0b6d8d5a2a7a51cdde909ff72 host=robb-studio base=unknown run=loom-run/v1:script:robb-studio/loom-gap-issues:832ed94c-10ec-411f-902d-24b7e701c904 -->


---

## Curator: scoping decision (2026-09-30)

**Chosen: option 1 (a per-repo declaration file) only. Option 2 (a heuristic fallback) is rejected for now.**

Why not the fallback. A default like "the check's workflow file plus the repo's source roots", or the workflow's `paths:` filter, is a guess about what a check reads. It does not come from the repo's own text. `paths:` filters are a CI optimisation, not a statement of inputs (ci-principles: path filtering is not a correctness tool), and a lint config two directories up is invisible to them. Under ci-principles rule 9, when in doubt the guard must fall back to the broader answer, and for an unspecced context the broader answer is today's "any base move = stale". A consumer that wants narrowing states its inputs explicitly.

### Design
- **File:** `.loom/stale-check-inputs.json`, tracked in the consumer repo. It is JSON so it matches `.loom/config.json`, and `serde_json` is already a dependency.
  ```json
  { "version": 1,
    "checks": {
      "Lint (ruff)": { "global": ["pyproject.toml", "ruff.toml", ".github/workflows/lint.yml"],
                       "scanned": ["**/*.py"], "coupled": [], "removal_sensitive": false } } }
  ```
  `global`, `scanned`, `coupled` and `removal_sensitive` mean exactly what they mean for `CheckSpec` in `stale_checks/inputs.rs`, and the same five clauses are evaluated with per-file semantics. No new predicate is introduced.
- **Read from the base-branch tip** (`contents/…?ref=<tip_sha>`), never from the PR head. A PR cannot narrow its own freshness check. The file's own path is added to every declared spec's `global`, so a declaration change on either side interacts with every declared check.
- **Built-in `SPECS`/`REQUIRED_CHECKS` win** for any context they cover. The declaration only fills contexts loom has no spec for.
- The `ci.yml` block attribution from #9065 applies only to built-in specs. Declared specs always get whole-file `CiScopes::unscoped()` semantics, because that attribution maps jobs to loom's own components.
- **Fail closed.** Any doubt means the whole file is ignored, every unspecced context behaves as it does today (stale on any base move), and a `Warning:` is printed on stderr. Doubt covers: a read error other than 404, invalid JSON, unknown fields, `version` ≠ 1, an empty context name, an empty `global`, and a pattern that is empty, absolute, or contains `..`. A 404 means no declaration exists, and behaviour is unchanged with no warning.
- The file is only fetched when some green required context with a usable base move has no built-in spec. On loom's own repo it costs nothing.

### Relationship to #9571
This is complementary to #9571 and does not overlap it. #9589 lets a consumer state which inputs a check reads, which removes false staleness. #9571 (re-running a deterministic ratchet on the merged tree) is the backstop for real staleness, and could later read a `reverify` command from the same file. That is out of scope here.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Absent file (404):** an unspecced required context is stale on any non-empty `D`, exactly as today, and no warning is printed.
- [ ] **Declared context:** evaluated through the same `stale_reason` clauses. An unrelated base move leaves it fresh, and a base move that touches its `global`, or the same `scanned` file the PR touches, makes it stale. Per-file semantics hold.
- [ ] **Only listed contexts narrow:** a required context that is not in the file still refuses on any base move.
- [ ] **Built-in `SPECS` win** over a declaration for the same context name.
- [ ] **Malformed or unreadable file** (bad JSON, unknown field, wrong version, empty `global`, bad pattern, or a non-404 read error): all unspecced contexts stay stale on any move, with a `Warning:` on stderr that names the file and the reason.
- [ ] **Self-protection:** a change to `.loom/stale-check-inputs.json` on either side interacts with every declared context. The file is read from the base tip, not the PR head.
- [ ] Consumer-facing docs in `defaults/docs/` cover the format, the semantics, the fail-closed rules and an example, and link to ci-principles rule 9.
- [ ] `cargo check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt`, the stale_checks tests (including the ci.yml attribution tests) and the budgets are all green.

issues.title: feat(experiments): generalize sweep model-cost experiment to N configurable arms with a budget-fraction cap (Phase 1 of multi-model framework)
issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-27)

**This issue is epic-sized as filed.** It bundles four largely-independent pieces of
work — (1) N-arm/multi-runtime experiment assignment, (2) a budget-fraction spend
cap, (3) multi-judge blind cross-model evaluation to fight self-preference bias,
and (4) SigNoz Pareto-frontier reporting — several of which need an operator
decision before any code can be written (which GLM account/budget to spend,
whether Fable may be a routine experiment arm outside the Judge role). Per the
Curator's decomposition guardrails, this issue is **rescoped to the first
buildable slice** below; the rest is recorded as "Proposed follow-up phases" for
separate issues (not filed here — filing races with concurrent Curator passes).

### What already exists (read this before building)

Loom already ships a Builder-only, canary-gated **2-arm** model-cost A/B
experiment (issue #3725), documented in
[`sweep-execution-model.md`](https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/blob/main/defaults/.claude/commands/loom/sweep-execution-model.md)
→ "Model-cost experiment mode" and
[`model-cost-experiment.md`](https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/blob/main/defaults/docs/model-cost-experiment.md):

- `sweep.modelExperiment` / `LOOM_MODEL_EXPERIMENT` tri-state (`off`/`observe`/`experiment`), env-over-config, canary-gated by an **uncommitted** `LOOM_MODEL_EXPERIMENT_CANARY=1` or `.loom/CANARY` sentinel.
- Arm assignment is **hardcoded to exactly two Claude aliases**: `loom-daemon/src/script_helpers/sweep_experiment.rs:43` — `pub const ARM_MODEL: [(&str, &str); 2] = [("A", "opus"), ("B", "sonnet")]`.
- `assign_arm()` (`sweep_experiment.rs:346-353`) is a **deterministic 50/50 parity split** on `(issue_number + complexity_bit) % 2` — every eligible issue gets an arm; there is no "spend N% of budget on the experiment, the rest run normally" knob.
- The forced arm suppresses the tier-2.5 complexity-tier resolution (`sweep.tierModels` / `sweep.optimization`, `model_tiers.rs`) for whichever issue it applies to — see "Experiment-mode suppression" in `sweep-execution-model.md`.
- Telemetry is a durable JSONL store (`.loom/stats/sweep-model-stats.jsonl`, `append_record`/`build_record`) with a `harvest()` reader (`sweep_experiment.rs:905`) that rolls up cost/Judge-pass-rate/Doctor-cycles **per arm id already using a `BTreeMap<String, _>`, not a fixed A/B pair** — only the human-readable comparison view, `format_harvest_text`'s `find_arm("A")`/`find_arm("B")` pairwise text (`sweep_experiment.rs:1169`), assumes exactly two arms.
- Fleet-wide, `loom-daemon sweep-outcomes summary --group-by arm|model|complexity|model-complexity` (issues #8057/#8542) already computes success rate, cost-weighted tokens, duration percentiles, and first-pass Judge-approval rate per group, and OTLP export already stamps `loom.cost_usd` on spans (`loom-daemon/src/observability/otlp/mapping.rs:450-454`) — most of the raw "cost vs. quality" data plumbing this issue asks for already exists; it is not exported to SigNoz as `gen_ai.request.model` / `loom.experiment.arm` yet, and there is no Pareto-frontier view over it.
- **No-Fable-Judge invariant (#3702)**: Judge model resolution can never resolve to `fable`, and the model-cost experiment / tier-map machinery independently **never resolves any Builder arm to `fable` either** (falls through instead) — both must stay true after this change.
- A **same-model** multi-dimension Judge fan-out (correctness / security / test-coverage / perf, all reviewed by the *same* model) exists only as a deferred design sketch (`defaults/scripts/experiments/judge-fanout-*`, issues #3739/#3748) — it is explicitly **not** cross-model blind evaluation and does not address self-preference bias; it requires the top-level-only Workflow tool (#3289) and has never been run live.
- **Related, distinct-axis work**: issue **#8055** ("fleet-wide repo-stratified model A/B") generalizes arm *count* too (`--arms opus,sonnet,...`), but at **workspace** granularity (whole repos opted into an arm via `.loom-local/local.json` overlays, covering role-runner ticks too) rather than per-issue. It is currently `loom:blocked` on an operator retrospective window (2AMLogic/2am#897, concluding 2026-09-28) and is not a duplicate of this issue — this issue's unit of assignment stays **per-issue**, matching the existing #3725 mechanism it generalizes. Do not fold the two; cross-reference only.

### Gap between what exists and what #9122 asks for

| Ask (#9122) | Exists today | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| N-arm randomization incl. non-Claude runtimes | 2 fixed Claude-only arms | No config surface for arms; no runtime field |
| ~30% of budget to experimental arms | Every eligible issue gets an arm (100%) | No budget-fraction cap/gate |
| Multi-judge blind cross-model evaluation | Same-model fan-out sketch only, deferred, never run | No cross-model blind judge protocol at all |
| SigNoz cost/quality Pareto tracking | `loom.cost_usd` on spans; rich local `sweep-outcomes summary --group-by arm` | No `loom.experiment.arm`/`gen_ai.request.model`/`tokens_total` span attributes; no Pareto view |

## Scope of this issue (Phase 1): generalize the experiment to N configurable Claude arms with a budget-fraction cap

Generalize the existing hardcoded 2-arm A/B into a **config-driven N-arm weighted
assignment** with a **budget-fraction cap**, reusing all existing telemetry
plumbing. Stays **Builder-only** and **Claude-runtime-only** (aliases/pinned IDs
only) — non-Claude runtimes and multi-judge evaluation are explicitly out of
scope for this slice (see follow-up phases). Exact config-key/CLI-flag names
below are a starting proposal, not a hard requirement — the **behavior and
precedence** are the acceptance criterion, not the identifier spelling.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new config surface (proposed: `.loom/config.json` → `sweep.modelExperimentArms`, an array of `{id, model, weight}`) lets an operator declare 2+ named arms with relative weights. **Absent this config, `assign-arm`/`banner`/`record` behavior is byte-for-byte identical to today's hardcoded `ARM_MODEL` A/B pair** — every existing assertion in `defaults/scripts/tests/test-sweep-experiment.sh` (lines ~60-65) and `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/model_dispatch_tests.rs:225` keeps passing unmodified.
- [ ] With 3+ configured arms, assignment stays **deterministic and resume-safe** (same `(issue_number, complexity)` always yields the same arm — the property `assign_arm` already has) and **stratified by the Curator complexity marker**, exactly as today. Add a Rust unit test asserting that over a large synthetic sample of issue numbers (e.g. 2,000), each arm's observed frequency converges to its configured weight ratio within a stated tolerance, independently within each complexity stratum.
- [ ] A configured arm whose model alias/pinned ID resolves to `fable` is **rejected at config-load time** (loud stderr warning naming the arm id) and the run **falls through** to the default 2-arm behavior — mirrors `resolve-tier-model.sh`'s existing "never resolves to fable" refusal-and-fallthrough (not a hard sweep failure). New unit test.
- [ ] A configured arm naming a non-Claude runtime (e.g. `{"id":"glm","model":"glm-5.3","runtime":"opencode"}`) is rejected the same way — loud warning + fallthrough, never silently ignored and never dispatched. This is the explicit scope boundary that keeps this slice to one PR; see "Proposed follow-up phases" → Phase 2.
- [ ] A new budget-fraction cap (proposed: `sweep.modelExperimentBudgetFraction`, env `LOOM_MODEL_EXPERIMENT_BUDGET_FRACTION`, same env-over-config-over-default precedence pattern as `guards.rmScope`/`sweep.escalation`) bounds what fraction of `experiment`-mode-eligible issues receive **any** forced arm. Default `1.0` reproduces today's always-forced behavior exactly. The in/out-of-experiment decision must be a **separate deterministic hash** from the arm-selection hash (so changing the fraction doesn't reshuffle which arm an in-experiment issue lands on). An issue sampled **out** of the experiment gets `arm=null` in its stats record (reusing `observe` mode's existing null-arm convention — do not invent a new state) and **unmodified tier-2.5/tier-3 resolution** proceeds for it, exactly as if the experiment were off for that issue.
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/sweep-experiment.sh` and `loom-daemon/src/cli/legacy_script_cmds.rs::handle_sweep_experiment_command` (`AssignArm`/`Banner` match arms, ~lines 229-300) thread the already-loaded config (`model_tiers::load_config`) through to the new weighted-assignment + budget-fraction logic — both subcommands already accept `--config`, so no new plumbing surface is needed, only using it unconditionally instead of only under `--resolve`.
- [ ] `harvest()`'s roll-up (`sweep_experiment.rs:905`, keyed by `BTreeMap<String, _>`/`BTreeMap<(String, i64), _>`) needs **no change** — it is already arm-name-agnostic. Only `format_harvest_text`'s fixed `find_arm("A")`/`find_arm("B")` pairwise comparison (`sweep_experiment.rs:1169`) needs generalizing: keep the existing 2-arm pairwise text byte-identical when exactly 2 arms are observed in the stats file, and add a per-arm table (same columns already computed: cost, first-attempt Judge-pass rate, mean Doctor cycles, merge rate) when 3+ distinct arm ids are observed.
- [ ] The No-Fable-Judge invariant, the canary guardrail (uncommitted confirmation only), and the tri-state mode resolution (`off`/`observe`/`experiment`) are all unchanged — re-verified by the existing test suite plus the new fable-rejection test above. This issue does not touch Judge or Doctor model resolution at all.
- [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/sweep-execution-model.md` → "Model-cost experiment mode" and `defaults/docs/model-cost-experiment.md` document the new arms/budget-fraction keys with a worked 3-arm example (e.g. opus/sonnet/haiku), and explicitly state that non-Claude-runtime arms and multi-judge blind evaluation are deferred (link this issue's follow-up phases).

### Explicitly out of scope for this issue

- Non-Claude / multi-runtime experiment arms (GLM via OpenCode, Pi, etc.) — Phase 2 below.
- Multi-judge blind cross-model evaluation / self-preference mitigation — Phase 3 below.
- SigNoz span attribute additions or a Pareto-frontier dashboard/report — Phase 4 below.
- Fleet-wide / workspace-level assignment (that axis is #8055, separately tracked and currently blocked — do not duplicate).
- Any change to Judge/Doctor model resolution or the `sweep.escalation` ladder.

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/script_helpers/sweep_experiment.rs` (`ARM_MODEL`, `assign_arm`, `arm_model`, `resolved_arm_model`, `harvest`, `format_harvest_text`)
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/legacy_script_cmds.rs` (`handle_sweep_experiment_command`, `AssignArm`/`Banner` arms, ~lines 210-300)
- `defaults/scripts/sweep-experiment.sh` (CLI surface comment/usage)
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-sweep-experiment.sh`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/model_dispatch_tests.rs`
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/sweep-execution-model.md`
- `defaults/docs/model-cost-experiment.md`

Verify this enumeration against `origin/main` before starting — the curator ran
in a read-only worktree snapshot and line numbers may have drifted.

### Test Plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon sweep_experiment` (unit tests: weighted-frequency convergence, fable rejection, non-Claude-runtime rejection, budget-fraction null-arm path, unconfigured-repo byte-identical regression) — **run on the remote build box per `~/.claude` global build-box policy, never on the local Mac.**
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-sweep-experiment.sh` passes unmodified plus new assertions for 3-arm config and budget-fraction cutoff.
- [ ] Manual: `LOOM_MODEL_EXPERIMENT=experiment LOOM_MODEL_EXPERIMENT_CANARY=1 ./.loom/scripts/sweep-experiment.sh assign-arm --issue 100 --complexity routine` with no `modelExperimentArms` configured reproduces today's `A opus` output exactly.

## Proposed follow-up phases (not filed — separate Curator/Builder passes, to avoid racing concurrent issue-creation)

**Phase 2 — Non-Claude runtime experiment arms.** Extend the Phase 1 arm schema
with a `runtime` field and wire dispatch through the runtime-adapter contract
(#4167) so a Builder can be forced onto e.g. `opencode` + `glm-5.3`, with
usage/cost attribution parity via the existing native-runtime reader
(`defaults/docs/native-runtime-usage-attribution.md`, `loom-daemon/src/opencode_usage.rs`).
Must gate on API-key/account pool health before starting (cf. #8055's
`pool_preflight.rs` refusal-to-start-during-exhaustion ask) so an experiment
never begins during exhaustion and gets misread as a bad arm.

**Phase 3 — Multi-judge blind cross-model evaluation.** A genuinely new
Judge-dispatch mode: blind a diff/prompt and route it to a *different-provider*
judge (e.g. GLM judging Claude-authored output and vice versa) to mitigate
self-preference bias, distinct from the existing same-model multi-dimension
fan-out sketch (#3739/#3748, `defaults/scripts/experiments/judge-fanout-*`).
Must preserve the No-Fable-Judge invariant unconditionally and define a
disagreement/tie-break protocol when the two judges split. Likely epic-sized on
its own — recommend curating it as its own multi-phase issue once filed, not a
single PR.

**Phase 4 — SigNoz cost/quality Pareto reporting.** Extend OTLP export
(`loom-daemon/src/observability/otlp/mapping.rs`, which stamps `loom.cost_usd`
today but not `loom.experiment.arm` / `gen_ai.request.model` / `tokens_total`)
so sweep spans carry the attributes needed for a SigNoz Pareto-frontier view,
built over data `loom-daemon sweep-outcomes summary --group-by arm` already
computes (cost-weighted tokens, first-pass Judge-approval rate, duration
percentiles per arm/model) — this is mostly "expose existing numbers to
SigNoz," not "compute them for the first time." Related: #9204 (per-model token
breakdown on `loom.runtime.usage`), #8528 (SigNoz self-hosted trial).

## Operator decisions required (not for Curator/Builder to decide)

1. **The live experiment budget fraction to actually run** (the operator's
   ~30%-of-budget framing). The shipped code default in Phase 1 must stay
   `1.0` (inert unless a repo already opts fully into `experiment` mode +
   canary confirmation, matching today) — choosing an actual fraction for a
   real canary is a spend/risk call, the same class of decision as the
   existing uncommitted `LOOM_MODEL_EXPERIMENT_CANARY` confirmation gate.
2. **Which GLM (or other non-Claude) API-key pool/account(s) Phase 2 may spend
   against, and its budget ceiling** — a credentials-and-spend decision only
   an operator holds (analogous to the AWS ≤8-vCPU-without-asking-Robb norm
   for cloud compute spend).
3. **Whether Fable may be used as a routine experiment arm at all outside the
   Judge role** (the original issue's "fable-5.1 vs opus-5.5 for
   planning/curation" comparison). Fable is currently reserved for the
   objective escalation ladder or an explicit operator param, never a
   Curator/cost-profile speculation (`sweep-execution-model.md`) — spending
   Fable's constrained weekly-limit budget on routine curation experiments is
   a policy call, not an engineering default.

---

<details>
<summary>Original issue (as filed)</summary>

### Problem Statement
Loom currently uses static role-to-model mappings. When new models emerge (e.g. `fable-5.1` vs `opus-5.5`, `glm-5.3` vs `glm-5.3-flash`), operators lack an automated, data-driven mechanism to evaluate real-world sweep cost, duration, and output quality.

Furthermore, single-judge evaluations suffer from self-preference bias (LLMs favor their own generated code).

### Proposed Solution
Implement a randomized multi-model experimentation framework in Loom with multi-judge evaluation protocols and automated telemetry attribution:

### Key Requirements
1. **Configurable Experiment Arms & Budget Allocation:**
   - Support probabilistic model weighting in `.loom/config.json` (e.g. allocating ~30% of sweep budget to experimental arms).
   - Support head-to-head comparisons across tiers: `fable-5.1` vs `opus-5.5` for planning/curation; `glm-5.3` vs `glm-5.3-flash` vs `sonnet` for builders.
2. **Self-Preference Mitigation (Multi-Judge Blind Evaluation):**
   - Implement multi-judge blind cross-evaluation (e.g. Claude Judge evaluates GLM output and vice versa) with blinded prompt/diff presentation.
3. **SigNoz Telemetry Attribution:**
   - Stamp `loom.experiment.arm`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, and `tokens_total` on all sweep spans.
4. **Pareto Frontier Analytics:**
   - Track empirical trade-offs in SigNoz:
     - Cost per Landed PR ($)
     - First-Pass Success Rate (%)
     - Wall-clock Turnaround Time
     - CI Failure & Repair Loops

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Daemon work-finder supports probabilistic model selection per role based on configured experiment weights.
- [ ] Multi-judge blind ranking protocol prevents self-preference bias.
- [ ] SigNoz metrics allow plotting cost vs. quality Pareto curves across all model arms.

</details>

issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-27)

**Rescoped to the first buildable slice.** As filed, this issue bundles four
pieces that are each real work in their own right: (1) a new Curator estimate
marker, (2) a completion write-back of *already-computed* actuals to the
issue, (3) a CI-minutes join that does not exist anywhere in the codebase
today, and (4) an adaptive re-calibration feedback loop / dashboard that needs
historical data this issue's own write-back hasn't produced yet. Per the
Curator's decomposition guardrails, this issue is narrowed to (1)+(2) below;
(3) and (4) are recorded as follow-up phases in this body (not filed as
separate issues — a Curator pass does not file new issues, and filing would
race with concurrent Curator passes in the same sweep tick).

### What already exists (read this before building; verified 2026-09-27 against `origin/main`)

- **Estimate side**: the Curator already emits a coarse effort marker,
  `<!-- loom:complexity=<tier> -->` (`mechanical`/`routine`/`complex`), on
  every curated issue — see `defaults/roles/curator.md` "Complexity routing
  marker" section (mirrored verbatim in
  `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/curator.md` — the two files are byte-identical
  as of this pass). It currently drives Builder model routing
  (`resolve-tier-model.sh` / `sweep.tierModels`) but is never compared against
  actual cost. There is **no numeric point/estimate marker today** — only the
  3-value tier.
- **Actuals side is already ~90% built, just never written back to the
  issue.** `SweepOutcomeRecord` (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs:422-609`)
  already carries, per sweep: `tokens_in`/`tokens_out`/`tokens_by_model` (raw
  token burn, Issue #5357/#6384), `total_duration_sec` and `phase_durations`
  (wall-clock cycle time), `doctor_cycles` and `judge_verdicts` (from the PR's
  forge label timeline, Issue #8222), and `complexity` (the Curator's own
  marker for this issue, re-read at the same terminal transition — see
  `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal/complexity_signal.rs`). This
  record is assembled and appended **exactly once**, at a sweep's terminal
  transition, by
  `SweepRegistry::append_outcome_journal`/`append_outcome_telemetry_journal`
  (`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs:147-394`) — called from
  the reaper's dead-child handling and from `finish_cancel`, i.e. **already
  the single-fire hook this issue needs**, not something to build from
  scratch.
- **What's missing is the write-back itself.** Today the record goes to a
  local JSONL journal (`.loom/logs/sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl`,
  readable via `loom-daemon sweep-outcomes` /
  `loom-daemon sweep-outcomes summary --group-by complexity`, Issues
  #8057/#8542) and to the OTLP/SigNoz export path. **Nothing posts any of
  this back onto the GitHub issue.** `.loom/scripts/merge-pr.sh` (3055 lines)
  posts several kinds of audit/override comments but none carry token/duration
  telemetry.
- **CI minutes are captured, but not joined to a sweep/issue anywhere.**
  `loom-daemon ci-telemetry` (`defaults/docs/ci-observability.md`) polls every
  configured owner's GitHub Actions runs/jobs and emits
  `loom.ci.run.duration_ms`/`loom.ci.job.duration_ms` metrics plus `ci.run`/
  `ci.job` records into SigNoz — but this is keyed by **repo + run id**, with
  no existing join to a `sweep_id`, PR number, or issue. Building that join
  (by PR head SHA or branch name) is real, separate work — see Follow-up 1.

### Overlap with in-flight work (#9122)

**#9122** ("N-arm/multi-runtime model-cost experiment," curated 2026-09-27,
being built now per the operator) touches
`loom-daemon/src/script_helpers/sweep_experiment.rs`
(`extract_complexity_marker`, arm assignment/harvest) and the
`sweep-outcomes` summary/harvest path. This issue's Part B (below) only
*reads* the complexity marker via the existing
`sweep_registry/outcome_journal/complexity_signal.rs` path (not
`sweep_experiment.rs`) and does not need to modify
`sweep_experiment.rs`/`sweep_outcomes_cli.rs` — but re-check both files
against current `main` before starting, since #9122 may land changes to
adjacent code (`sweep_outcome_summary/`, the `sweep-outcomes` CLI surface) in
the interim. If a genuine conflict surfaces, prefer rebasing this issue's
change on top of #9122 rather than the reverse (#9122 is already in flight).

### In scope for this issue (single PR)

**Part A — Curator emits a numeric point-estimate marker.**

Add a second, closed-vocabulary, machine-readable marker alongside the
existing complexity tier:

```html
<!-- loom:points=<N> -->
```

- `N` MUST be one of a small fixed enumeration — recommend `{1, 2, 3, 5, 8,
  13}` (mirrors the existing "exactly one of N values, no synonyms" discipline
  used for `loom:complexity`, see #4448). Out-of-vocabulary values fall
  through the same way an out-of-vocabulary complexity tier does — treat it as
  a curation defect, not a style choice.
- This is a **coarse, uncalibrated ordinal estimate** of expected total sweep
  cost (tokens + wall-clock + iteration count combined) — the Curator's
  holistic judgment, not a formula. Loose guidance only: `mechanical`-tier
  issues typically land at 1-2, `routine` at 3-5, `complex` at 8-13 — but the
  Curator may deviate when the specific scope warrants; do not treat the tier
  as a rigid lookup table.
- Document the marker in `defaults/roles/curator.md` right next to the
  existing "Complexity routing marker" section (and its
  `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/curator.md` mirror), including the
  vocabulary table and the "always emit explicitly" rule the complexity marker
  already follows.
- Gate `loom:curated` on the marker's presence/validity the same way
  `loom:complexity` already is: extend the existing validator,
  `defaults/scripts/require-complexity-marker.sh` (the canonical path — the
  `.loom/scripts/` copy is a symlink to `defaults/scripts/` in this dogfood
  checkout, confirmed 2026-09-27), to also check for a valid `loom:points`
  marker, rather than adding a second new shell script (per
  `.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md`, a new `.sh` needs an allowlist
  category; extending an existing baseline script does not).

**Part B — `loom-daemon` writes the actuals back onto the issue.**

- Add a Rust code path (not a new shell script — see language policy above)
  that, at the **same terminal-transition call site** as
  `append_outcome_journal`/`append_outcome_telemetry_journal`
  (`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs`), and **only when
  `result == SweepResult::Success`** (merged — never on failure, cancelled, or
  blocked, to avoid comment spam on every dead-end sweep), formats a Markdown
  comment from the already-assembled `SweepOutcomeRecord` fields
  (`tokens_in`/`tokens_out`/`tokens_by_model`, `total_duration_sec`,
  `phase_durations`, `doctor_cycles`, `judge_verdicts`, `complexity`, and the
  new `points` marker read the same way `complexity` is) and posts it to the
  **originating GitHub issue** (not just the PR) via the existing forge-write
  helpers this module already uses for `skip_label_flip`/breaker-gating.
- **Opt-in, FLAGS-OFF by default**, consistent with every other `autonomous.*`
  toggle (`defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` § Operability): a new config key
  under the `autonomous` block (e.g. `autonomous.sweepOutcomeWriteback.enabled`,
  default `false`) with an `LOOM_*` env override, `env > config > default`
  precedence, resolved the same way neighboring toggles are.
- **Single-fire / idempotent.** The doc comment on `append_outcome_journal`
  already states it runs "at every site that already emits a terminal
  `SweepExited`/`SweepCrashed` bus event" — i.e., once per terminal
  transition. Wire the write-back into that same call so it inherits the
  single-fire property; add a test asserting no duplicate issue comment is
  posted if the terminal transition is somehow observed twice (defensive,
  since this is new forge-write behavior, unlike the local-journal append it
  rides alongside).
- **Explicitly excludes CI minutes** — see Follow-up 1. Do not attempt the
  join in this PR.

### Explicitly out of scope (follow-ups, not filed — see note above)

1. **CI-minutes join.** Correlate `loom-daemon ci-telemetry`'s `ci.run`/`ci.job`
   records (keyed by repo + run id, `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md`) to a
   sweep's `pr_number`/`sweep_id` (by PR head SHA or branch name), and add a
   `ci_minutes`-shaped field to the outcome record or a joined report. This is
   materially bigger than Parts A+B combined (new correlation logic spanning
   two independent subsystems) and does not block shipping token-burn +
   cycle-time write-back now.
2. **Adaptive calibration feedback loop.** Automatic re-calibration of
   `sweep.tierModels`/point-sizing when actual burn diverges from the
   `loom:points` estimate, plus a "pipeline drag" alert. Needs a meaningful
   history of `loom:points`-tagged, merged issues to be statistically
   meaningful — i.e., it depends on Part A+B shipping and running for a while
   first. May eventually relate to the existing shadow-mode Jev complexity
   classifier (`loom-daemon/src/jev_tier.rs`, Issue #8543), which already runs
   "beside the Curator's `<!-- loom:complexity=<tier> -->`" marker per its own
   module doc — not traced further here (unverified marker: worth the
   Builder's own look, not asserted as a fit).
3. **Calibration report/dashboard.** An aggregate view (SigNoz saved query, or
   a `loom-daemon sweep-outcomes summary --group-by points` extension in the
   spirit of the existing `--group-by complexity`, Issues #8057/#8542) comparing
   estimated points/tier vs. actual tokens/duration/cycle-count over time —
   the "detect pipeline drag" analytics layer the original Problem Statement
   ultimately wants. Natural next step once Part A+B have been running long
   enough to accumulate data.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `defaults/roles/curator.md` (and its `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/curator.md`
      mirror) documents the `<!-- loom:points=<N> -->` marker, its fixed
      vocabulary, and the "always emit explicitly" rule, next to the existing
      complexity-marker section.
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/require-complexity-marker.sh` (or an equivalently
      invoked check) is extended to reject `loom:curated` when
      `loom:points` is absent or out-of-vocabulary, mirroring its existing
      complexity-marker gate. Its test file
      (`defaults/scripts/tests/test-require-complexity-marker.sh`) gains
      coverage for the new marker.
- [ ] A new Rust code path in `loom-daemon` (not a new `.sh`) fires exactly
      once, at a sweep's terminal `Success` transition (the same call site as
      `append_outcome_journal`), and posts one Markdown issue comment
      containing: the Curator's `loom:points`/`loom:complexity` estimate,
      actual token burn, actual wall-clock duration (total and, if reasonably
      available, per-phase), Doctor cycle count, and first-pass Judge verdict.
- [ ] The write-back is gated behind a new opt-in `autonomous.*` config key
      (default `false`) with an `LOOM_*` env override, `env > config >
      default` precedence — matching the documented FLAGS-OFF convention.
- [ ] The write-back fires only on `SweepResult::Success`, never on
      failure/cancelled/blocked, and is covered by a test proving it does not
      double-post on a repeated terminal observation.
- [ ] The comment payload does **not** include CI minutes (Follow-up 1 is
      explicitly deferred — no half-built/fabricated CI-minutes field).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: points-marker parsing/validation, the
      record-to-Markdown formatting function in isolation (given a
      `SweepOutcomeRecord`, asserts the expected comment text/fields), and the
      opt-in-gating + single-fire behavior.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` documents the new config key in its
      Operability table, and `defaults/docs/observability.md` or
      `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` gets a short cross-link noting that
      CI-minute write-back is a named follow-up, not yet implemented.
- [ ] Builder does **not** run `cargo`/tests on an overloaded local machine —
      per this repo's remote-build convention, verification runs on the
      designated remote build box.

### Affected Files (verified against `origin/main`, 2026-09-27)

- `defaults/roles/curator.md` — new marker docs
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/curator.md` — mirrored marker docs
- `defaults/scripts/require-complexity-marker.sh` — extend validator
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-require-complexity-marker.sh` — new test coverage
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs` — write-back hook site
- `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs` — `SweepOutcomeRecord` is the actuals source (read-only reference unless a `points` field is added here too — Builder's call)
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal/complexity_signal.rs` — pattern to mirror for reading `loom:points`
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` — new config key documentation
- `defaults/docs/observability.md` or `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` — CI-minutes-deferred cross-link

### Related Open Work

`check-duplicate.sh --issue 9056` (2026-09-27) found **no open issues or PRs
cross-referencing #9056** and **no duplicates** against title/body. #8052
("per-role × model token consumption report + weekly-limit calibration") is
thematically adjacent but does not cross-reference this issue and targets a
different metric (role/model-level token reporting, not per-issue
estimate-vs-actual) — disregarded as a distinct scope, not absorbed.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Unit tests for points-marker extraction/validation (mirroring the
      existing `complexity`-marker test pattern).
- [ ] Unit test for the record→Markdown formatter, given a fixture
      `SweepOutcomeRecord`.
- [ ] Unit/integration test proving the write-back only fires on
      `SweepResult::Success` and does not double-post.
- [ ] Config-resolution test for the new opt-in flag (env > config > default,
      default false).
- [ ] Manual verification: with the flag enabled in a scratch config, confirm
      (via a dry-run/mock forge client, not a live post against this repo) that
      a successful sweep's terminal transition produces exactly one
      well-formed comment payload.

<details>
<summary>Original Issue</summary>

### Problem Statement
Loom currently lacks closed-loop effort estimation and empirical cost calibration. While tasks have estimated complexity, the actual execution cost (total tokens burned, CI minutes consumed, wall-clock cycle time) is not recorded back onto the GitHub issue upon completion. 

Without comparing estimated vs. actual story points:
1. Sizing models cannot calibrate against empirical drift.
2. We cannot detect when task execution is systematically slowing down or exceeding complexity estimates.

### Proposed Solution
1. **Curator Story Point Estimation:**
   - During issue triage/curation, Curator estimates the task's complexity / expected "story points" (e.g. estimated token budget, expected CI runs, expected builder turns).
2. **Post-Merge Telemetry Write-Back:**
   - When an issue/PR merges, Loom's completion hook posts an empirical summary comment on the issue:
     ```markdown
     ### 📊 Execution Telemetry & Story Points
     - **Estimated Story Points / Complexity:** `M (3 points)`
     - **Total Tokens Burned:** `14.2M` (Prompt: `200k`, Cache Read: `13.8M`, Output: `150k`)
     - **CI Minutes:** `18.4 min` (across 2 check suites)
     - **Wall-Clock Duration:** `1h 12m` (Intake → Merge)
     - **Variance:** `+12% vs baseline`
     ```
3. **Adaptive Calibration Feedback Loop:**
   - When actual token burn or cycle times significantly exceed estimates, trigger re-calibration of step-sizing and flag potential pipeline friction.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Curator role stamps estimated complexity / points on new issues.
- [ ] Completion hook writes back actual token counts, CI minutes, and wall-clock duration to the issue.
- [ ] Telemetry enables tracking estimated vs. actual velocity over time.

</details>

issues.title: fleet-config: apply rendered config without a daemon restart (live reload)
issues.body:
Follow-up to the `loom-daemon fleet-config` PR (branch `feature/fleet-config`).

## Problem
`fleet-config render` writes the machine tier and host-local tier, but many knobs are resolved once at daemon startup ([fleet-config-lifecycle](https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/blob/main/defaults/docs/fleet-config-lifecycle.md) lists `workFinder.maxConcurrent`, `hostBreaker`, `rateLimitBreaker`, …). A rendered change therefore needs a restart to take effect, which is exactly the "landed != effective" gap #5963 describes.

## Proposal
After a render changes a tier (or the timer sync of the sync-at-start follow-up detects it), reload what can be reloaded live and report precisely what still needs a restart:
1. Classify each changed dotted path as live-reloadable or restart-required (a table owned by code, not docs, so it cannot drift).
2. For live paths, signal the running daemon over IPC to re-resolve.
3. For restart-required paths, either request a drain-and-restart (`restart --drain`, opt-in) or surface "pending restart: <paths>" in `status`.

## Acceptance
- `render` output names which changed keys are live and which need a restart.
- A live-reloadable change is observable on a running daemon without restart; restart-required ones show in `status` until applied.

issues.title: observability: name the halt cause on workspace_halted loom.dispatch.disposition spans (follow-up to #9222/#9017)
issues.body:
## Problem

`loom.dispatch.disposition` spans (#9222, #9227) made every `QueueDisposition` value filterable in SigNoz — except that for `workspace_halted`, all six distinct hold causes collapse into one undifferentiated `workspace_halted` value. The span cannot answer "is this repo held because `main` is red, or because the token pool is dead, or because a drain is in progress?"

Today's documented workaround is a join: `defaults/docs/observability.md` tells operators to hop to the parent `loom.dispatch.tick` span via `parentSpanID`, and says plainly:

> the row itself does not say which of red-main / gate / token pool / drain / breaker caused the halt (out of scope for #9222; file separately if wanted)

This is that follow-up.

## The data already exists on the row

Since #9017, a `workspace_halted` row's `ReadyQueueRow::detail` carries the closed-vocabulary `work_finder::halt_cause::HaltCause` token verbatim — one of `main_red`, `gate_pending`, `token_pool`, `preflight_advisory`, `drain`, `breaker` (precedence in `halt_cause::causes_per_root`). Legacy cause-less callers record no detail, so absence is already meaningful.

The exporter drops it: `observability::ops::disposition::build_rows` extracts only two things from `row.detail` — `park_label` (`allowed_park_label`) and `pr_number` (`open_pr_number`). Nothing reads a halted row's cause token.

## Why it matters

A fleet audit (2AMLogic/2am#1306) wanted per-reason dispatch-rejection filtering: `pr_open_skip` vs. admission-brake vs. holds. The first two map cleanly to existing dispositions (`open_pr`/`open_pr_backoff`, `deferred_saturation`), but a held workspace reads as one bucket even though the remedies are disjoint: red-main means fix the repo, `token_pool` means add/wait for pool accounts, `preflight_advisory` means fix the workspace's `.mcp.json`, `drain` is operator intent, `breaker` is automatic suppression. Only `main_red`/`gate_pending` leak through today, indirectly, via the tick-span join — and only when the sampled tick happens to be the parent.

## Proposed change

- In `build_rows` (loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/disposition.rs), extract the halt-cause token for `QueueDisposition::WorkspaceHalted` rows, validating it against the closed `HaltCause::as_str()` vocabulary — structured token only, never free-form text, same rule as `open_pr_number`.
- Carry it through `DispositionRow` → `Emission` → `build_span` as a new attribute, e.g. `loom.queue.halt_cause`. Absent on cause-less legacy rows and on non-halted rows.
- Update `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` §`loom.dispatch.disposition` attribute table and rewrite the `defaults/docs/observability.md` "file separately if wanted" note to name the attribute; optionally add it to `defaults/observability/signoz/queue-dwell.sql` query 5's output columns.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: a `workspace_halted` row with `detail = Some("main_red")` produces a span whose attributes contain the cause token exactly; a cause-less legacy row produces no such attribute; a detail value outside the vocabulary is never exported.
2. `cargo test -p loom-daemon disposition` green, clippy clean, no file-size-ratchet regressions.
3. Both docs updated (attribute table + the observability.md note).

## Out of scope

- Sampling cadence (sub-collector-interval dispositions missed) — documented tradeoff, unchanged.
- Single-workspace-loop rows (none exist to export) — unchanged.

Refs: #9222 #9227 #9017

`main` is red on the **Shell Test Suites (hermetic)** job. Reproduced locally on
`origin/main` at `a3bfbaef9`:

```
$ bash defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-check-runs-pagination.sh
  FAIL: (3a) persistently truncated read: function fails (never returns 0 = 'safe to merge')
    Expected: '1'
    Actual:   '5'
=== Test Summary ===  Total: 42  Passed: 41  Failed: 1
```

The other 41 assertions in the suite pass, including every other (3a) assertion
(never settles, never short-circuits to the merge, narrates `TRUNCATED`, keeps
polling to the deadline). Only the exit code is wrong.

## Cause: two PRs merged back-to-back with a colliding contract

- **`4cfb0c067`** — "fix(merge-pr): distinguish --auto settle-wait timeout (exit
  5) …" (#8896 / PR #8988) changed `_wait_for_checks_then_sync_merge`'s bounded
  timeout path from `error()`'s exit 1 to **exit 5** ("not merged, not a failure:
  re-queue"). See `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh:2084-2086` and `:2138-2142`.
- **`60e5f3d13`** — "fix(forge-helpers): paginate check-runs and fail closed on a
  short read" (#8895 / PR #8986) added this suite, whose (3a) case asserts
  `assert_eq "1" "$rc"` (`defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-check-runs-pagination.sh:402`).

#8986 was written and verified against pre-#8988 `main`, and #8988 predates the
suite, so neither PR's own CI could see the collision. It only appears once both
are on `main`.

## Which side is right

Almost certainly the **test**: exit 5 is #8896's deliberate contract — a
persistently unreadable check-runs API is a re-queue, not a build failure — and
`defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md` documents it. A persistently
truncated read reaching the timeout is exactly that case. The (3a) assertion
should expect 5, with a comment naming why 5 rather than 1 (the important
property, that it never returns 0 = "safe to merge", is unchanged and already
asserted separately).

Worth confirming against #8896's docs before flipping the number: if the intent
was that a *truncated* read is distinct from a *timed-out-but-readable* one and
should still be a hard failure, then `merge-pr.sh` is what needs the branch, not
the test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bash defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-check-runs-pagination.sh` passes on
      `main` (42/42).
- [ ] Whichever side changes, the chosen exit code for "persistently truncated
      check-runs read, bounded wait expired" is stated in
      `defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md`.
- [ ] The (3a) case keeps asserting the real safety property — never 0, never
      "checks settled", never "proceeding to synchronous merge".

Found while building #8898 (PR #8991); the failure is on the PR's merge ref via
`main` and has nothing to do with that change.

issues.title: ci-telemetry poller misses re-runs of older workflow runs (created-at watermark) — #8824 AC3 gap
issues.body:
Follow-up to #8824 / #8847 (post-merge Judge finding, 2026-09-25).

## Problem
The `ci-telemetry` poller lists workflow runs with a `created>=<watermark>` filter (`poll.rs` `poll_repo` / `runs_path`). A re-run (attempt N>1) keeps the original run's `created_at`, so once newer runs have advanced the watermark, a re-attempt of an older run is never listed again and never exported. That is the common case (re-running a failed CI after newer pushes), so #8824 AC3 ("exactly once regardless of re-runs") is only partly met. The existing test passes only because the fixture ignores the `created=` filter.

## Suggested fix
Rescan a trailing window (e.g. `updated`-ordered or last N days) on each tick and rely on the existing export ledger for dedup; add a fixture that honors `created=` and asserts a late re-attempt of an old run is exported once.

## Smaller gaps noted in the same review
- A run that never completes can pin the watermark indefinitely.
- A renamed repo re-emits its runs.
- The runs list is not ETag-cached.
- A crash between export and ledger write can emit duplicate histogram points.

issues.title: Guard: rm-scope fast paths miss `NAME+=` / `NAME[0]=` / `mapfile` / `IFS= read` rebindings (fail-open past the catastrophic floor)
issues.body:
## Summary

The rm-scope same-command **literal fast path** (`rm_scope_literal_same_command_resolve()`, #6676/#6805) treats an
`rm` target as provably safe once it finds exactly one `NAME=<literal>` assignment in the same command. Its
"was NAME rebound?" test only recognises `NAME=`, and (for the mktemp path's `_mktemp_is_other_rebind()`)
`read NAME` / `printf -v NAME` / `for NAME in`. Several ordinary bash rebinding forms are **not** recognised, so
a rebinding that moves the value out of the vetted path is invisible and the guard allows the `rm`.

Measured on `main` (`bf2fb67c`-era, `LOOM_RM_SCOPE=repo`, cwd = repo root), each of the following **ALLOWS**:

```bash
d=/tmp/a
d+=/../../etc          # runtime target is /etc  <-- rm -rf /etc ALLOWED
rm -rf "$d"
```

| rebinding inserted between the assignment and the `rm` | literal fast path on `main` |
|---|---|
| `d+=/../../etc` | **allow** (runtime target `/etc`) |
| `d[0]=/etc` | **allow** |
| `mapfile -t d < /tmp/list` | **allow** |
| `IFS= read -r d < /tmp/list` | **allow** (the `^read` anchor misses a var-assignment prefix) |
| `read d < /tmp/list` | **allow** |
| `printf -v d /etc` | **allow** |
| `export d=/etc` | **allow** |
| `eval d=/etc` | **allow** |
| `unset d` | **allow** (harmless in effect — `rm -rf ""` — but the resolution claim is still false) |
| `d=/etc` | deny (correctly detected) |
| `d=$(echo /etc)` | deny (correctly detected) |

The `d+=` and `d[0]=` rows are the ones that matter: they defeat the **catastrophic top-level floor**, which is
supposed to be ungated. The guard substitutes the *lexically proved* path (`/tmp/a`) into the scope check and never
looks at what the shell will actually expand, so `rm -rf /etc` is admitted.

## How this was found

Surfaced while reviewing PR #9324 (issue #9304), which adds a `for NAME in <literal>…` sibling resolver. That PR's
new resolver is **stricter** than this one — it reuses `_mktemp_is_other_rebind()`, so it correctly denies
`read d` / `printf -v d` / `export d=` — but it inherits the `+=` / `[0]=` / `mapfile` / `IFS= read` / `eval` blind
spot. The gap is therefore family-wide and pre-existing, not introduced by #9324; it is filed separately so a
relaxation PR is not asked to carry an unrelated tightening.

## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)

Extend the shared rebind detection in `defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh` (plus the byte-identical
`.loom/hooks/` copy) so a segment that rebinds NAME by any of these forms poisons the resolution exactly as a
second `NAME=` assignment does:

- `NAME+=` (append)
- `NAME[` (array-element / associative assignment, since `$NAME` is `${NAME[0]}`)
- `mapfile`/`readarray` naming NAME
- `read` reached through a leading var-assignment prefix (`IFS= read -r NAME`) or other prefix words
- `eval` anywhere in the command (cannot be proved; fail closed)

Every one of these is a **tightening** — it converts currently-allowed commands into denies — so it needs the usual
pre/post differential verdict sweep (#8003 → #8035 → #8217 methodology) to show the allow→deny set is exactly the
intended one, and it will change the verdict of any real workflow that uses `+=` to build a scratch path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each row in the table above that names a real escape (`+=`, `[0]=`, `mapfile`, `IFS= read`, `eval`) fails
      closed on the literal fast path, the mktemp fast path, and the #9304 for-loop path.
- [ ] `d=/tmp/a; d+=/../../etc; rm -rf "$d"` denies (`rm-protected-path` or `rm-scope-unresolved-var`).
- [ ] A pre/post differential sweep records the full allow→deny flip set, with no unintended rows.
- [ ] `defaults/hooks/` and `.loom/hooks/` copies stay byte-identical; `check-guard-destructive-drift.sh`,
      `check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` and the full `tests/hooks/` corpus stay green.
- [ ] Any production shell growth carries a `Shell-Budget-Growth:` declaration in the commit body.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-30, verified against `origin/main` @ `aa20fc045`)

**Rightsizing verdict: right-sized as a standalone issue — do not split, do not batch.** The bypasses in the table above are *live on `main`* (measured pre-file), the fix is one tightening pass over the shared rebind detection, and the AC is already per-row testable. Kept separate from the for-loop resolver family (#9304 / #9323 / #9373 / #9601) so a live catastrophic-floor fix is not sequenced behind a blocked relaxation effort.

- **Affected Files (verified present on `origin/main` @ `aa20fc045`)**: `defaults/hooks/guard-destructive-generic.sh` (plus the byte-identical `.loom/hooks/` copy), `tests/hooks/test-guard-destructive-rm-scope.sh`.
- **Related but deliberately not consolidated**: #9373 (for-loop resolver soundness — same rebind-detection *technique*, different code path, sequenced behind a retry of closed PR #9324); #9601 (composed-shape *relaxation* — must land after this tightening, never before, or it inherits these bypasses); #9323 (one-liner for-loop escape, `loom:blocked`+curated). Cross-linked rather than absorbed: different consumers and sequencing.
- **Points**: 3.

issues.title: daemon: Issue dispatch_sweep takes 30–70s — ~20 serial gh calls under the registry mutex on a tokio worker; retry not idempotent
issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->
<!-- loom:points=3 -->

## Summary

An `Issue` `dispatch_sweep` takes **30-70s** inside the daemon against the MCP client's 30s timeout (`mcp-loom/src/tools/sweeps.ts:55`, `DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`). Observed 2026-09-29/30 on robb-studio: #9565 (~69s) and #9567 (30.6s) both reported **failure** to the caller though both sweeps spawned; the retry for #9565 failed with `lock collision`. Not host load (1-1.8x load on 28 cores, single `gh` ~0.3s); the latency is the handler's structure: ~20 sequential `gh` subprocesses + ~3.5s of fixed sleeps, mostly under the per-workspace `Mutex<SweepRegistry>`.

## Scope of THIS issue (first increment, decomposed)

This issue was too large for one PR. It is scoped to the two small, self-contained, low-risk items:

1. **Cache `resolve_owner_repo`** per workspace root for the daemon's lifetime (original item 2).
2. **Record the idempotency key at acceptance**, not at `finish`, so a same-key retry returns the in-progress sweep instead of a lock-collision error (original item 3).

Split into follow-ups (as of main 4f72ef288, 2026-09-30):
- #9573 - guard chain out of the registry mutex (original item 1; highest risk).
- #9575 - ack after claim / align `DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`; move work_finder/reaper/watchdog `gh` work off tokio workers (original items 4, 5).

## Verified state on main (4f72ef288, 2026-09-30)

Anchors in the original trace have moved:
- Dispatch handler: `loom-daemon/src/ipc/private_dispatch.rs` (~L72-105): `prepare()` (account/runtime admission) already runs in `spawn_blocking` outside the lock; Phase 1 takes `target.lock()` and calls `begin_prepared_issue_dispatch` (`sweep_registry/dispatch.rs:1679`), which still runs the whole guard chain under the lock; Phase 2 polls unlocked; Phase 3 `finish_issue_dispatch` re-locks and records the entry.
- `SweepRegistry::resolve_owner_repo`: `sweep_registry/guards.rs:1295` (honors `LOOM_REPO` first; otherwise spawns `gh repo view` every call, bounded by `reap_gh_timeout()`). Uncached. A separate `worktree_ops/gh.rs:480 resolve_owner_repo(repo_root)` exists that deliberately ignores `LOOM_REPO` (#5511) - do not merge the two semantics.
- Idempotency: `find_running_by_key` (`sweep_registry/mod.rs:1526`) only scans `entries` (Running/Pending), populated in `finish_issue_dispatch`. `begin_prepared_issue_dispatch` step 1 (`dispatch.rs:~1690`) dedups only against it. Between `begin` returning `Spawned` and `finish`, a same-key retry misses the dedup and is refused by the guard chain / `acquire_lock`.
- **Existing contract to change deliberately:** test `same_key_retry_during_the_unlocked_poll_window_is_refused_not_double_spawned` (`sweep_registry/dispatch/tests.rs:3312`) currently pins "refused, not double-spawned". The new behavior must still never double-spawn, but return the in-flight sweep id instead of an error; update that test's assertion and doc comment accordingly (it is a characterization test, so expect this change).

## Implementation guidance

- Cache: add a `OnceLock`/`Option<(String,String)>` field on `SweepRegistry` (or a process-wide `Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, (String,String)>>`) populated on first *successful* resolve; never cache `None` (failure must keep failing open/closed as today). Keep the `LOOM_REPO` env check outside the cache (env read is free and tests toggle it).
- Idempotency: add an in-flight map `idempotency_key -> sweep_id` (with pid unknown until spawn) written when `begin_prepared_issue_dispatch` decides to proceed (after step 1 dedup, before/at claim) and cleared in `finish_issue_dispatch` (both success and error) and on every early `Err` return from begin so a failed attempt does not wedge the key. `Done(DispatchOutcome{was_new:false})` for a hit. The sweep id must be allocated at acceptance so the retry can return the same id; check where `sweep_id` is currently minted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SweepRegistry::resolve_owner_repo` spawns at most one `gh repo view` per workspace per daemon lifetime after a successful resolve (test counting `gh` invocations via the existing fake-`gh` log fixture); failures are not cached.
- [ ] Retrying `dispatch_sweep` with the same `idempotency_key` while the first attempt is in flight (between `begin` and `finish`) returns the same sweep id with `was_new: false`, not an error, and never spawns a second child (update the #6592 window test).
- [ ] A begin that errors out (guard refusal, spawn failure) releases the in-flight key so a later same-key dispatch proceeds normally (test).
- [ ] No change to guard semantics: open-PR guard (#4123), cross-host collision (#7873), sole-claim confirmation, closed-issue guard refuse the same cases; all other existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `LOOM_REPO` override behavior unchanged.

## Test plan

`cargo test -p loom-daemon sweep_registry::` (guards, dispatch tests); new unit tests as above using the fake `gh` fixtures in `sweep_registry/dispatch/tests.rs` / `guards.rs`.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/guards.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/mod.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch/tests.rs`

issues.title: Extend sweep-outcomes summary --group-by complexity with a Curator-vs-Jev agreement column (step 3 of #8543)
issues.body:
## Problem

#8543 implemented the `loom-daemon jev-tier` shadow classifier and threaded `jev_tier`/`jev_confidence` onto `sweep_outcomes::OutcomeRecord` (the narrow #4644 journal, `sweep-outcomes.jsonl`). Its Proposal's step 3 — extending `sweep-outcomes summary --group-by complexity` with a Curator-vs-Jev agreement column and a first-pass Judge rate split by agree/disagree — was explicitly deferred: the issue's own dependency note says step 3 "needs #8542 ... to be meaningful," and #8542 (which journals the Curator's complexity tier) had not merged as of #8543's PR.

## Why this needs its own scoping, not just "wait for #8542"

`sweep-outcomes summary --group-by <dim>` (`sweep_outcome_summary.rs`) reads `telemetry::SweepOutcomeRecord` — the **richer** `sweep.outcome` telemetry journal (`sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl`), which already backs `model`/`repo`/`host`/`day`/`arm` grouping. This is a **different record type** from the narrow `sweep_outcomes::OutcomeRecord` (`sweep-outcomes.jsonl`) that #8543 added `jev_tier`/`jev_confidence` to. #8542 targets journaling the Curator's own tier — confirm which journal it lands the field on before starting this issue.

There is currently no single record carrying both tiers together. Building the agreement report needs one of:
- Adding `jev_tier`/`jev_confidence` to `telemetry::SweepOutcomeRecord` too (a second copy, mirroring how e.g. `credential`/`crash_classification` already differ per-journal), or
- A `sweep_id`-keyed join between the two journals at report-build time (`sweep_outcomes.jsonl` for Jev's tier, `sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl` for the Curator's tier + `judge_verdicts` first-pass rate).

## Scope (narrowed — see Curator Enhancement comment below, 2026-09-25)

#8542 landed more of the originally-scoped work than anticipated when this issue was filed. Remaining scope:

- Join `sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl` records to `sweep_outcomes.jsonl` records by `sweep_id` to pair each record's Curator tier (`SweepOutcomeRecord.complexity`) with Jev's tier (`OutcomeRecord.jev_tier`).
- Add an agreement column (`agree` / `disagree` / `unknown`) to the existing `--group-by complexity` / `--group-by model-complexity` output.
- Split the existing first-pass Judge approval rate (JDG1%/JDG_N, added by #8542) by agree/disagree, in addition to the existing per-tier split.

**Already done by #8542 (PR #8582) — do NOT reimplement:**
- `GroupBy::Complexity` / `GroupBy::ModelComplexity` (`loom-daemon/src/sweep_outcome_summary/group_by.rs`)
- Curator-tier resolution (`resolve_complexity`, `loom-daemon/src/sweep_outcome_summary/complexity.rs`, reading `telemetry::SweepOutcomeRecord.complexity`)
- First-pass Judge approval rate per complexity tier (`first_pass_verdict`/`accumulate_first_pass`/`render_first_pass_tail`, same file)

## Dependencies

- [x] #8542: **Resolved 2026-09-25.** Merged via PR #8582 ("feat(telemetry): journal Curator complexity tier and add --group-by complexity (#8542)"). Landed the Curator tier on the richer journal (`telemetry::SweepOutcomeRecord.complexity`) and `--group-by complexity`/`model-complexity` with a first-pass Judge rate — see "Scope" above for what's already done vs. what remains.
- [x] #8543: already shipped `loom-daemon jev-tier` and the Jev-tier checkpoint→`OutcomeRecord` plumbing this joins against.

Both dependencies are resolved. See the Curator Enhancement comment below for the corrected remaining scope, current Affected Files, and Test Plan.

issues.title: Cancellation: Docker discovery blocks the sweep registry lock before SIGTERM
issues.body:
## Problem

Cancellation can hold the sweep registry mutex for the entire Docker discovery timeout before it sends the host process-group SIGTERM. An unresponsive Docker daemon therefore delays status reads and unrelated sweep operations, including bare-metal issue sweeps.

Found while validating #8773 / PR #8775 for #4496. This is pre-existing behavior in the container-stop path introduced for #8435, separate from the persistent-session worker lifetime bug fixed by #8775.

## Evidence (2026-09-23)

- At PR head `d9ea97db9531799476421edb5ba2b4f5ea489e26`, the isolated local unit gate passed 8,043/8,044 assertions. `sweep_registry::reaper::tests::split_cancel_does_not_hold_lock_across_grace_window` failed repeatedly: an unrelated `get_status` was blocked about 4.86 seconds despite the fixture's 1-second cancellation grace.
- The host Docker service was unresponsive and a disposable-container creation returned `input/output error`; no production service was restarted.
- `SweepRegistry::begin_cancel` holds its caller's registry mutex and invokes `container_stop::begin_container_stop` before `signal_sweep(..., 15)`.
- `begin_container_stop_with` calls `list_issue_containers` synchronously before spawning its stop thread. That discovery uses `output_with_timeout(..., reap_gh_timeout())`, whose default is 5 seconds. Moving only `docker stop` to a thread leaves discovery under the lock.
- The same single regression passed in 1.343 seconds when the test was isolated from production Docker using an unused `DOCKER_HOST` Unix socket. The exact-head CI Rust unit suite also passed with responsive Docker. No test or threshold was weakened.

## Requested change

Keep Docker discovery and teardown from blocking the registry critical section or delaying delivery of host cancellation. Preserve the existing bounded, label-scoped container teardown and ownership rules; account-wide/container-wide cancellation of persistent Codex sessions remains prohibited.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deterministic fake Docker CLI whose `ps` stalls beyond the cancellation grace proves unrelated status reads remain prompt while cancellation is in progress.
- [ ] Host SIGTERM delivery is not delayed by slow or failed Docker discovery.
- [ ] Discovery and teardown remain bounded; no orphaned helper processes or unbounded retries are introduced.
- [ ] Existing container label filtering, graceful stop/escalation and sibling isolation contracts remain covered.
- [ ] The regression does not depend on the developer's live Docker service, production containers, credentials or model calls.
- [ ] Existing cancellation tests and full CI pass without weakening latency assertions.

## Relevant files

- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper.rs` (`begin_cancel`, `finish_cancel`)
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper/container_stop.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper/tests.rs`

Local evidence: `/tmp/loom-8773-build-gate-isolated.log`, `/Volumes/Stripe/loom-8773-fixture/isolated-docker-reaper.log`. These are test logs; do not attach ambient host state or credential files.

issues.title: tap_usage misses Pi's real message_end shape, so Pi launches read as unmeasured tap spend
issues.body:
## Problem

`loom-daemon/src/tap_usage.rs` (#8556) is meant to count a Pi launch's usage from assistant `message_end` events. Its test fixtures use a guessed shape, `{"type":"message_end","usage":{"input_tokens":…}}`, with the counters on the event itself. Pi 0.85.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, the pinned `PI_VERSION`) actually emits:

```json
{"type":"message_end","message":{"role":"assistant","provider":"…","model":"…","usage":{"input":1000,"output":200,"cacheRead":4000,"cacheWrite":300,"reasoning":5,"totalTokens":5500,"cost":{"input":0.1,"output":0.2,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0.3}},"timestamp":1790330401000}}
```

`read_event_usage` searches `event.tokens`, `event.usage` and `event`, but never `event.message.usage`. So a real Pi run's `message_end` yields no reading, and tap accounting (`tap_usage` on `sweep-outcomes.jsonl`, `config.tap_*` on `sweep.outcome`) reports Pi launches as **unmeasured**. That is the metered-backstop spend #8556 and ADR-0020 exist to see.

Found while building #8594's Pi reader (`loom-daemon/src/pi_usage.rs`). Its module doc's "Schema provenance" section records the package files the shape was read from (`dist/modes/print-mode.js`, `dist/modes/json-event.js`, `docs/json.md`, `pi-ai`'s `types.d.ts`).

## Also needed, to match Pi's semantics

- `usage.reasoning` is a **subset** of `output` per `pi-ai`'s `Usage` doc. `TapUsage::total_tokens` sums `reasoning` + `output`, so it would double-count reasoning for Pi once the scope is fixed.
- `usage.cost` is an object (`{…,"total":…}`), not a number. `read_f64(scope, "cost")` yields `None`, so the cost estimate is dropped.
- A `toolResult` message's `message_end` may carry nested `usage` (LLM work done inside a tool). That is real spend and needs a deliberate decision on whether to count it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fixture built from Pi 0.85.1's real `message_end` shape produces a measured `TapUsage` with correct input/output/cache counters and `cost_estimate` = `usage.cost.total`.
- Pi's `reasoning` is not double-counted in `total_tokens`.
- The existing OpenCode `step_finish` fixtures are unchanged.
- The `agent_end` exclusion still holds. `entry_appended` (which re-emits every persisted assistant message) is also excluded.
