issues.title: docs(observability): qualify SigNoz 'registering late costs latency, not data' with the gateway queue bound
issues.body:
Surfaced during Judge review of #8696 (SigNoz trial, part of #8528).

#8696 adds a README step, "Register the first user *before* expecting ingestion", which ends with:

> It is also recoverable rather than lossy — the gateway's sending queue holds the refused batches and drains them intact once the receiver opens, so registering late costs latency, not data.

The live observation behind it is sound (37/14/3 recovered after ~40 min, no re-send), but the general claim is broader than the gateway config supports. `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` configures the `otlp_http/signoz` exporter with a file-storage-backed `sending_queue` of `queue_size: 1000` requests and `block_on_overflow: false`. Recovery across the window works because a persistent queue re-queues retry-exhausted batches, but a busy fleet sending during a long un-registered window would overflow the 1000-request queue and drop data. The fixture (52 envelopes) never gets close to that bound.

**Suggested change (docs only):** qualify the sentence, e.g. "…drains them intact once the receiver opens, as long as the backlog fits the gateway's persistent sending queue (1000 requests; overflow drops, it does not block). Register before pointing real fleet traffic at the gateway."

**Acceptance:** the README sentence names the queue bound, and `grep -n 'queue_size' defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` agrees with the number quoted.

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=mechanical -->

### Affected Files

- `defaults/observability/signoz/README.md` — reword the sentence at line 130 ("...costs latency, not data.") to name the 1000-request queue bound and the overflow-drops behavior, per the issue's Suggested change above.

issues.title: [Epic #8764] Authorize the forge.event bus topic in the event-bus taxonomy and state the Generic-topic rule
issues.body:
## Summary

ADR-0021's Phase 1 publishes feed pages on the in-process event bus as
`Event::Generic { topic: "forge.event", payload }` — deliberately `Generic`,
so the frozen `Event` taxonomy (ADR-0009 / #1847: prompt topics are a closed
set with dedup discipline; daemon-originated state keeps its own variants) is
not broken by a forge-sourced prompt that has no daemon decision attached yet.

This issue authorizes `forge.event` in the event-bus taxonomy documentation and
decides how `Generic` prompt topics are governed going forward:

- **Add `forge.event` to the documented topic inventory** in
  `docs/event-bus` (or the doc that currently owns the prompt-topic table),
  with: publisher = `loom-daemon/src/forge_events.rs` (one prompt per
  non-empty verified feed page), payload schema
  (`source: "forge-event-feed"`, `host_id`, `count`, `first_seq`, `last_seq`,
  `types: string[]`), semantics = *routing hint only, never decision input*,
  and the dedup contract (per-page, not per-event; consumers must be idempotent
  and must tolerate prompts arriving without the events themselves — the
  journal is the copy, the prompt is the "check now").
- **State the `Generic`-topic rule explicitly:** a `Generic` topic is allowed
  only when (a) it is listed in the inventory, (b) it carries a `source`
  field, and (c) it never triggers a write to external state without a
  forge-verified re-read in the consumer. `forge.event` satisfies all three;
  future prompt topics must too.

## Why an issue and not just a doc edit

The topic freeze exists so a future agent cannot quietly invent a bus topic
that some other subsystem's one-shot-per-topic contract depends on being the
only publisher of. Making that rule explicit and listing `forge.event` in the
inventory turns this from a convention into a checkable one.

## Acceptance

- The topic inventory names `forge.event`, its publisher, payload schema, and
  the three `Generic`-topic rules above.
- A one-paragraph pointer from the inventory entry to ADR-0021 (the invariant
  source) and to `loom-daemon/src/forge_events.rs` (the implementation).

---

## Curator enrichment (2026-09-23)

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

### Corrected location: `docs/event-bus` does not exist

Verified against `origin/main` @ `2fa2190e` (`git ls-tree -r origin/main
--name-only | grep -i event-bus` → no results). There is no
`docs/event-bus` path in this repo. The actual documented topic inventory
this issue must extend lives in **two places that must be kept in sync**:

1. **`loom-daemon/src/event_bus.rs`** — the in-code source of truth: a
   module-level rustdoc table under `//! # Topic taxonomy (frozen for
   v0.10.0)` (starts at line 20 as of `2fa2190e`), immediately followed by
   `//! New topics require a follow-up issue — the taxonomy is intentionally
   pinned.` (line 43). This is the table a future `cargo doc` reader and the
   module's own authorization-history prose (which cites each authorizing
   issue, e.g. "#3873", "#3902", "#4090") consult.
2. **`defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`** — the docs mirror, under
   `## Event taxonomy (frozen for v0.10.0)` (line 207 as of `2fa2190e`), with
   its own copy of the table (lines 213–231) and the same "new topics require
   a follow-up issue" sentence (lines 209–211).

Both tables need the new `forge.event` row plus the authorizing-issue prose
paragraph (matching the existing style: "The `daemon.capacity.advisory` topic
was authorized by **#3902** (epic #3809) for …"), and the `Generic`-topic
governance rule (new prose, not currently stated anywhere — see below)
belongs in both files too, ideally as near-identical wording so they don't
drift.

**Pre-existing drift, out of scope for this issue but worth flagging so the
Builder doesn't assume the mirror is currently complete**: as of `2fa2190e`
(2026-09-23), `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`'s table is already missing

(#4494), `daemon.dispatch.headroom_advisory` (#4234), and

issue; it's called out here only so the Builder treats
`daemon-reference.md`'s current table as an incomplete snapshot, not the
full authoritative set, when writing the new `forge.event` row.

### Blocking dependency: ADR-0021 and `forge_events.rs` do not exist on `origin/main` yet

Verified against `origin/main` @ `2fa2190e` (2026-09-23):

Both are deliverables of the sibling phase issue **#8765** ("`[Epic #8764]
forge_events Phase 1: observe-only feed consumer`"), which ships
`loom-daemon/src/forge_events.rs` and `docs/adr/0021-forge-event-plane.md` per
its own body. As of this curation pass, #8765 carries `loom:building` (lease
`sweep-issue-8765-1790175280`, host `host-e1d4c843`, acquired
2026-09-23T14:54:42Z) with **no open PR yet**
(`closedByPullRequestsReferences` is empty) — i.e. neither file is merged or
even in review.

This issue (#8767) is itself already claimed `loom:building` in a *separate*,
concurrently-dispatched sweep (`sweep-issue-8767-1790175314`, same host,
34 seconds after #8765's claim) — so its own Builder phase may run before or
after #8765 merges, with no ordering guarantee between the two sweeps.

**Guidance for the Builder**, in priority order:
1. **Check first**: `gh issue view 8765 --json state,closedByPullRequestsReferences`.
   If #8765's implementing PR has merged, verify the publisher/payload
   details against the **merged code** (`loom-daemon/src/forge_events.rs`'s
   own doc comments and `Event::Generic` call site), not just this issue's
   restated schema above — the schema here is inherited from #8765's issue
   body at filing time and may have drifted during implementation review.
2. **If #8765 has not merged yet**: do not fabricate a pointer to files that
   don't exist. Either (a) hold this issue until #8765 merges, or (b) write
   the two doc tables' `forge.event` row and the `Generic`-topic rule text
   now, using #8765's issue body as the design-spec source (clearly workable

   and semantics), and open a fast, explicitly-linked follow-up comment (not

### Existing `Generic`-topic precedent (context only, not required scope)

Two `Event::Generic` topics already ship outside the frozen table, documented
ad hoc elsewhere in `daemon-reference.md` rather than in the frozen-table
section: `daemon.host_breaker.state` (`loom-daemon/src/host_breaker.rs`,
documented around `daemon-reference.md` line 4917) and `safehouse.chatops.*`
(`loom-daemon/src/safehouse_chatops.rs`). Neither is in the frozen table
today. The new `Generic`-topic rule this issue writes should be scoped
narrowly to what governs `forge.event`; reconciling these two pre-existing
examples against the new rule (are they compliant? should they move into the
frozen table?) is explicitly **out of scope** for this issue — flagged here
for awareness only, not as an added acceptance criterion.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/event_bus.rs` (module rustdoc table + prose) — exists on
  `origin/main`.
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (`## Event taxonomy` section) — exists

(`docs/adr/0021-forge-event-plane.md` and `loom-daemon/src/forge_events.rs`
are **referenced**, not edited, by this issue — see "Blocking dependency"
above for why they may not exist yet at build time.)

## Dependencies

- [x] #8765: `[Epic #8764] forge_events Phase 1` — ships
  `docs/adr/0021-forge-event-plane.md` and `loom-daemon/src/forge_events.rs`,

issues.title: Concierge Phase 4: digests, watch-result narration, and scoping interface parity (#4196)
issues.body:
## Context

Part of #4196 Phase 4 (follow-up to #7947 Phase 3b, PR #8744, merged 2026-09-23). Split out of #8745 item 2. Named as out of scope in #7947 and unchanged by PR #8744.

Three pieces the concierge persona does not yet have, each independently valuable:

1. **Digests.** Periodic room summaries of what the daemon has been doing (no automated "here's what happened while you were away" narration exists today — the persona is purely reactive, per `loom-daemon/src/concierge.rs`'s module doc: "the persona is a read-only narrator (`listen` / `propose` / `say`)").
2. **`watch` results posted back into the room.** `loom-daemon/src/watch_registry.rs` and `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/watch.md` implement registering a watch on an issue (3a's `watch <issue>` verb, per #8745's original text). Nothing currently narrates a watch firing back into the safehouse room — which is the half that makes asking for a watch worthwhile from the room in the first place.
3. **Interface parity.** What an operator can do in the room today is bounded by `safehouse_chatops`'s six typed verbs (`loom-daemon/src/safehouse_chatops/command.rs`) plus the concierge's five (`loom-daemon/src/concierge/intent.rs`'s `Verb`). This bullet is under-scoped — it needs its own scoping pass (enumerate what the MCP/IPC surface exposes today vs. what the room can reach) before it can be built, not a direct implementation.

## Suggested scoping order

Digests and watch-result narration are concrete and independently shippable; interface parity needs a scoping pass first (compare `loom-daemon`'s MCP tool surface — `mcp__loom__*` — against the six+five typed verbs) before it can become buildable acceptance criteria. Consider splitting further once that scoping pass runs, rather than building "parity" as a single open-ended item.

## Acceptance criteria (digests + watch-result narration; interface parity needs scoping first)

- [ ] The daemon can post a periodic digest into the configured safehouse room, respecting the same `safehouse.concierge` gating (`resolve_concierge_config`) and budget model (`loom-daemon/src/concierge/budget.rs`) as other concierge output.
- [ ] A registered watch (`loom-daemon/src/watch_registry.rs`) firing results in a room narration via the concierge's `say` path (`loom-daemon/src/cli/concierge.rs`'s `say` subcommand, which enforces the same `addresses_persona` non-command check that keeps `confirm <nonce>` unrepresentable).
- [ ] Neither digest nor watch-narration output can itself be read by 3a's `inbound_command` as an addressed command (reuse the existing `vet_say` gate rather than a new path).
- [ ] A scoping doc/comment enumerates the interface-parity gap concretely (MCP tool surface vs. typed verb surface) as a prerequisite for further decomposition.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/concierge.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/concierge/relay.rs` — the `say`/`vet_say` path digests and watch-narration would reuse
- `loom-daemon/src/watch_registry.rs` — where a watch firing is currently observed; needs a hook to notify the concierge/room path
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/concierge.rs` — likely home for a new `digest` subcommand or scheduled-tick hook
- `defaults/roles/concierge.md`, `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/concierge.md` — role prompt guidance for digest cadence and watch-narration phrasing
- `defaults/docs/safehouse.md` — document the new capabilities once landed

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a watch-fire event triggers exactly one room narration, gated the same way `say` already is
- [ ] Automated tests: digest output cannot be parsed as an addressed command by `inbound_command`
- [ ] Manual verification: against a provisioned safehouse, confirm a fired watch produces a room message and a digest tick produces a summary

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

**Why `complex`, not `routine`**: the interface-parity bullet is explicitly under-scoped and needs its own analysis before it is buildable; digests and watch-narration both touch the same relay/budget gating that #7947's security review treated as load-bearing, so a mistake there could bypass gating in a way tests written against the *existing* narrow verb set might not catch.

## Dependencies

None — #7947/PR #8744 (the concierge module itself) has already merged.

## Related

- Sibling decomposition: #8761 (durable room inbox), the live-verification issue for #8745 item 3.

issues.title: ci: check-pipefail-early-exit regression in test-merge-pr-worktree-path.sh blocks every PR (Structural Checks fail)
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`scripts/check-pipefail-early-exit.sh --quiet --require-baseline` (part of the
`Structural Checks` required CI job) currently fails on `main` itself, which
means it fails identically on every open PR rebased on current `main`,
independent of that PR's own diff.

## Reproduction

```
$ bash scripts/check-pipefail-early-exit.sh --quiet --require-baseline
ERROR: defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-worktree-path.sh has 1 pipefail + early-exit-consumer pipeline(s); baseline allows 0.
  defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-worktree-path.sh:747: grep -q
      git -C "$WTC_TMP/repo" worktree list --porcelain | grep -qxF "worktree $WTC_TMP/wt"; then
```

Confirmed on a clean checkout of `origin/main` (currently `638bffab1`) — no PR
diff involved.

## Suspected cause (unverified)

`git blame` attributes line 747 to commit `0e80f62bd2` ("fix(merge-pr): an
unrun worktree-contains check keeps the --worktree-path worktree (#8191
slice)", 2026-09-29 20:33:30), landed via #9602, and refined a few minutes
later by `f38eae711` ("test(merge-pr): make Test 8's block extraction literal
and shellcheck-clean") — which, per its own title, was specifically trying to
make this test shellcheck-clean and appears to have introduced the
`pipefail`-unsafe `grep -q` in a piped `git worktree list --porcelain | grep
-qxF ...` in the process. Neither PR's CI run caught it — `Structural Checks`
presumably wasn't required-and-blocking at merge time for one of the two, or
the check ran before this line existed in its final form.

## Impact

Every open PR against `main` since `0e80f62bd2`/`f38eae711` landed shows
`Structural Checks` (and, transitively, `Shell Syntax (macos-latest)`, which
runs the same repo-wide script) as `fail`, regardless of what that PR's own
diff touches — a repo-wide false-negative on the merge gate. Observed
independently while reviewing PR #9623 (unrelated `loom-daemon` change,
verified byte-identical to `origin/main` for this file).

## Fix

Rewrite the line 747 pipeline without a pipe (per the "HOW TO FIX A FINDING"
table in `scripts/check-pipefail-early-exit.sh`), e.g. capture `git -C
"$WTC_TMP/repo" worktree list --porcelain` into a variable first and grep the
variable with `<<<`, or add `# loom-lint: allow-pipefail-early-exit --
<reason>` if the SIGPIPE really cannot occur here.

issues.title: state: guard that every daemon-written .loom/state/ path is gitignored (the class behind #9544)
issues.body:
## Problem

The daemon writes runtime state under `.loom/state/` in its workspace root. On a host where the daemon's workspace is also a tracked checkout (e.g. loom's own clone on a launchd host), any such file that the managed `.gitignore` block does not cover can be committed by tooling that stages `.loom` wholesale.

It happened on 2026-09-28:
- A resync commit (`101aa8f66`) committed `.loom/state/eta/pending.jsonl`.
- The daemon rewrites that file constantly, so the checkout was permanently dirty.
- The consumer's resync tooling then refused to fast-forward it, and the clone fell 15–37 commits behind.
- Resyncs of other repos from that stale clone were refused as downgrades.

#9544 fixed this one file by ignoring `.loom/state/eta/`, following the per-directory pattern already used for `ci-telemetry/` and `fleet-captain/`. The class of bug is still open: the next new `.loom/state/<subsystem>/` repeats it.

## Proposal

- **A guard test:** enumerate every path the daemon writes under `.loom/state/` (or require new state dirs to register), and fail if one is not covered by the `post_init.rs` managed-gitignore list. A new subsystem's state directory can then never ship unignored.
- **Or invert the default:** ignore `.loom/state/*` and explicitly un-ignore the hand-maintained files that must stay tracked (e.g. `detect-unlabeled-epics-dismissed`).

Related, on the consumer side: tooling that stages `.loom` wholesale (`git add -- .loom`) should stage an explicit list of paths instead. Loom's own `land-resync-commit.sh` already does. At least one fleet consumer's resync script does not; that is tracked in that repo.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test fails if the daemon writes a `.loom/state/` path not covered by the managed ignore block.
- [ ] The documented contract says which `.loom/state` files are tracked and why.

issues.title: feat(telemetry): record candidate queue position and total candidate count on dispatch spans
issues.body:
### Problem Statement
When `work_finder` evaluates ready candidate issues on each tick, dispatch telemetry does not record an issue's queue rank at the moment of evaluation.

During retroactive queue bottleneck forensics in SigNoz, operators cannot distinguish whether an issue was skipped while sitting at **#1 on the critical path** (e.g. top priority item blocked by a hold) or whether it was simply sitting at **#45 in the backlog** waiting its turn.

### Proposed Solution
Enrich dispatch telemetry (`loom.dispatch.disposition` and candidate evaluation spans) with queue position metadata:
1. `queue.candidate_rank`: 1-indexed rank of this candidate issue in the sorted candidate pool on this tick.
2. `queue.total_candidates`: Total number of eligible candidate issues evaluated in the ready queue on this tick.
3. `queue.priority_score`: The composite score/weight (tier + repo priority + age + stars) used by the candidate comparator.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `loom.dispatch.disposition` spans record `queue.candidate_rank`, `queue.total_candidates`, and `queue.priority_score`.
- [ ] Operators can query SigNoz to isolate high-priority blocked issues (e.g. `WHERE queue.candidate_rank <= 5 AND loom.disposition = 'skipped'`).

### Context
Requested by @turian for retroactive queue bottleneck forensics.

issues.title: loom-daemon: one comment chokepoint (forge comment) that always appends the dashboard link
issues.body:
## Problem

Every issue/PR comment the loom fleet posts should end with a small visible link to the fleet dashboard — `[loom dashboard](https://dashboard.2amlogic.com/github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues|pull/<N>)` — so any comment is one click from its dashboard page. loom-ui already resolves that URL shape to the right page (2AMLogic/loom-ui#632, merged in `3ad60e7`: `/issues/N` and `/pull/N` → the issue page, repo/org shapes → repo/repo-list pages, whole-URL/scheme-less/bare-slug variations accepted).

Today the daemon has **no single comment chokepoint**: ~12 modules compose a body and POST it to `repos/{n}/issues/{n}/comments` ad hoc (`gh api -f body=…` or `gh issue comment`). Bolting the footer onto each site individually would be 12 chances to forget and 12 places to keep byte-identical — the exact failure mode the repo's existing structural guarantees (`loom:verdict-sha` appended in `post-verdict.sh`, `loom:provenance` appended in `create-pr.sh`) were built to avoid. Consolidate first, then the footer becomes structurally impossible to omit.

## Deliverables

1. **New `loom-daemon/src/forge_comment.rs` core** (sibling module, not a growth of an over-ratchet file):
   - `dashboard_footer(nwo, number, is_pr) -> String` — one visible line + one hidden marker, idempotent (no double append when the marker is already in the body):
     ```
     <body>\n\n[loom dashboard](https://dashboard.2amlogic.com/github.com/<owner>/<repo>/(issues|pull)/<N>)\n<!-- loom:dashboard-link -->\n
     ```
     Base URL from env `LOOM_DASHBOARD_URL`, default `https://dashboard.2amlogic.com`, trailing slash(es) trimmed. `is_pr` picks `pull/N` over `issues/N` (the resolver treats both as the issue page; the link itself should stay truthful).
   - `with_footer(nwo, number, is_pr, body)` and `post(gh, nwo, number, is_pr, body)` — the one POST path (`gh api repos/{nwo}/issues/{n}/comments -f body=…`; a PR IS an issue for comments, one endpoint serves both).
2. **New CLI verb** `loom-daemon forge comment <NUMBER> (--body TEXT | --body-file PATH) [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--pr]` → same core; repo resolves from the git `origin` remote when `--repo` is omitted (the convention the other `forge` verbs use). This is what the shell side (`post-comment.sh`, sibling issue) and agent prompts exec. Follow the file-size policy's sanctioned shape: thin `cli/` sibling module, `main.rs` takes exactly the +2 dispatch lines — disclose that in the PR description per the policy's "second legitimate increase" section.
3. **Migrate every daemon comment-POST site** to the core. Authoritative discovery (grep is the spec, this list is a starting point): `merge_pr/redate.rs` (`post_comment`), `merge_pr/sequence.rs`, `dep_classify` (apply/forge), `script_helpers/validate_phase.rs`, `watchdog/peer_coord.rs`, `sweep_registry/outcome_journal/writeback.rs`, `sweep_registry/guards.rs`, `claim_reconciliation/{verdict_invalidation,auto_merge_disarm}.rs`, `worktree_ops/gh.rs` (`comment()`), `quarantine_reconciliation.rs`, `role_runner/roster.rs`. Comment *readers* (`--paginate` GETs, `comment_trust`, `star_liveness`, `forge_check_claim`, `lease_co_occupancy`) are untouched.
4. **Footer on machine-marker comments too** (roster heartbeats, lease records, disarm notices): they are visible comments; the format contracts they carry (`loom:role-shard-roster`, `loom:lease`, verdict-sha capture greps) match specific hidden markers line-wise, so a trailing visible line does not break any parser — verify this against `verdict-staleness-guard.sh`'s `MARKER_TEST`/`MARKER_CAPTURE` and `defaults/docs/lease-record.md` before landing.
5. **Tests**: footer format + idempotence + env override; every migrated site's tests updated (many assert exact bodies); a format-pinning fixture the shell twin (sibling issue) asserts against, so the two implementations cannot drift.

## Constraints

- ADR-0018 (Rust owns behavior, shell reaches it) — this issue is the "owns behavior" half.
- File-size ratchet: check `scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` before touching anything near threshold; put new code in sibling modules. `main.rs`'s +2 is disclosed as above.
- No `--no-footer` escape hatch — omission must be structurally impossible; a caller that truly needs a bare body should not be posting through the chokepoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn 'issues/.*/comments' loom-daemon/src` shows POSTs only inside the `forge_comment` core (reads exempt)
- [ ] `loom-daemon forge comment 42 --body "hi" --repo o/r` posts a comment ending in the dashboard link; running the same body through `with_footer` twice does not double-append
- [ ] `LOOM_DASHBOARD_URL=https://d.example.com` changes the link base; unset yields `https://dashboard.2amlogic.com`
- [ ] `cargo test` green; format fixture documented in the module doc for the shell twin to pin against

issues.body:
Small polish batch following #9698 — three items too small to deserve separate issues.

## 1. Lease TTL hot-apply

`lifecycle.leaseTtlMinutes` is **startup-captured** (#9698): `resolve_lease_ttl_minutes()` reads a process global, so a config edit needs a daemon restart (documented interim). The work-finder trio re-reads config every tick and hot-applies; make the lease TTL behave the same. Complication: `claim_reconciliation`'s call sites have no repo root at hand — either thread the root through (forge_check_claim, orphan_recovery, claim_reconciliation) or register a config-watcher-style re-read. Keep the startup-capture fallback for processes that never resolve a root.

## 2. `loom-daemon hyperparams validate [--json]`

Run `startup_init`'s strict gate (unknown keys, types, ranges, crossed pair, unparseable vector) **without starting the daemon** — a config lint a check script or CI can call on a proposed `.loom/config.json` edit or `$LOOM_HYPERPARAMS` vector. Exit non-zero with the named violations; `--json` for tooling. The gate logic already exists in `hyperparams::validate_layer` — this is a CLI wrapper.

## 3. Docs pointers

- Link `defaults/docs/hyperparameters.md` from `daemon-reference.md`'s configuration section.
- Revisit the CLAUDE.md Configuration-section pointer dropped in #9698 (it pushed all 8 role prompt-prefix budgets past the ratchet) when budget headroom exists — CLAUDE.md is at 319/320 lines, so it fits only alongside a compensating removal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Lease TTL honors a committed-block edit without a daemon restart (or the limitation is re-documented with the reason it cannot)
- [ ] `hyperparams validate` gates a bad block/vector with named paths, exit ≠ 0
- [ ] Doc discoverable from daemon-reference.md

issues.title: forge-helpers: forge_get_required_status_check_contexts still fails closed on the plan-gated 403 (follow-up to #8844)
issues.body:
Follow-up to #8844 / PR #8871.

#8871 taught `loom-daemon merge-pr stale-checks` to read the one plan-gated
403 —

    HTTP 403: Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.

— as "this repository's plan has no rulesets/branch protection, so nothing can
be a *required* check", instead of failing the #8248 freshness guard closed on
every merge.

The **shell twin of that lookup was deliberately left alone**:
`forge_get_required_status_check_contexts` in
`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` still treats the same 403 as a lookup
failure (`ruleset_rc=1` → `return 1`).

### Why it was out of scope for #8844

Its three call sites in `merge-pr.sh` (the UNSTABLE fallback, the
no-required-checks fallback, and the stacked/auto path around lines 1998 /
2314 / 2532) only run when checks are **already failing or the PR is not in a
clean mergeable state**. So on a private free-plan repo it does not block an
otherwise-clean merge the way the freshness guard did — it refuses a merge
that something else was already refusing. The #8844 report's actual symptom is
fixed without it.

### Why it is still worth fixing

On such a repo *no* check can be required, so "one informational check is red"
is precisely the case the UNSTABLE fallback exists to unblock — and there it
fails closed for a reason that cannot be true. The operator sees a refusal
whose stated cause ("could not determine the required checks") is unanswerable
on that plan.

### Shape of the work

- Mirror `stale_checks::fetch::is_plan_gated`'s predicate: match the **message**
  (`upgrade to github` **and** `make this repository public`), never the status
  code — a missing token scope, SSO enforcement and a rate-limit refusal are all
  403s where required checks may genuinely exist.
- The lookup currently discards stderr (`2>/dev/null`) on both the ruleset and
  the GraphQL call, so the signature is not even visible to it; capturing it
  needs care because `defaults/scripts/lib/` is `contract` in
  `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt`, i.e. inside the portable-shell pool
  `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` ratchets (comments are free, code lines are
  not).
- Per-source, like #8871: a gated source configures nothing; a source that
  answered normally stays authoritative.
- Emit a visible warning on the same principle — a relaxation nobody can see is
  how a fail-open ships unnoticed.
- Extend `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-unstable-fallback.sh` (it already
  stubs `gh api repos/*/rules/branches/*`) with the plan-gated 403 → "no required
  checks" case and an other-403 → still-fail-closed case.

### Alternative worth weighing first

#8191 is porting `merge-pr.sh` to daemon subcommands. If the required-contexts
lookup is due to move to Rust soon, the right move may be to reuse
`stale_checks::fetch`'s union (now plan-gate-aware) from that port rather than
grow the shell helper — one implementation instead of two that must agree.

issues.title: merge-pr.sh: warn when a partial-increment trailer is backticked (the #3667 reset silently no-ops)
issues.body:
## Summary

`merge-pr.sh`'s partial-increment parser deliberately blanks inline code spans
before matching (#5234 — a backticked `Part of #N` is a hypothetical mention, not
a declared intent). That exclusion is correct. The gap it leaves is that a Builder
can write the convention's **exact** trailer text inside a code span — it reads as
"a literal piece of syntax, so put it in backticks" — and the PR then looks
completely right to a human reviewer and to Judge while silently defeating the
automation: `_partial_increment_refs` returns nothing, so the #3667
`loom:building` -> `loom:issue` reset no-ops with **no log line anywhere** and the
family/epic issue is stranded at `loom:building` indefinitely.

## Incident

Downstream on `rjwalters/kicad-tools`: merging PR #5686 into issue #5240, whose
body carried `` `Part of #5240` `` on its own line. The reset never fired; the
label swap and an explanatory comment had to be applied by hand. Filed there as
rjwalters/kicad-tools#5690; fixed there in PR #5692 (merged 2026-09-23) against
the **vendored** `.loom/` copies, pinned with a `.loom/resync-ignore` block whose
own comment says "unpin once the equivalent fix lands in rjwalters/loom's
defaults/ tree". Tracked there as rjwalters/kicad-tools#5693.

Two prior partial-increment merges on that same issue (#5649, #5488) used the
plain-text form and reset correctly — this is a body-shape trap, not a regression.

## Fix (detection, not a parser change)

Port the downstream fix into `defaults/`, so every consumer gets it and the pin
can be retired:

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — a non-blocking pre-merge warning
  (`_warn_backticked_partial_increment_trailers` plus two text helpers), in the
  same advisory style as the #4569/#4595 conflict warnings, called from
  `_check_partial_increment_close_conflict` **before** its empty-refs early
  return (the case it exists for is precisely the one where the ref list is
  empty). Pure text analysis, no extra forge calls.
- The matched shape is deliberately much narrower than the declaration anchor:
  the backticked trailer must be the **entire line** (modulo an optional
  list/blockquote marker, whitespace and one trailing punctuation mark), so the
  #5234 mid-sentence mention and a docs line listing trailers as examples stay
  silent, and fenced blocks are stripped first.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` — regression cases
  for the incident shape, the plain-text control, the #5234 prose control, docs
  prose, fenced blocks, the both-shapes case, list/numbered markers, and the
  `--dry-run` prefix.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` — a "write the trailer as plain
  text, never backticked" caution next to the existing trailer example.

The `loom-daemon merge-pr-refs` parser is **not** touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_partial_increment_refs`' answer for a backticked trailer is unchanged
      (still not a declaration)
- [ ] A whole-line backticked trailer emits a non-blocking warning naming the
      issue and quoting the offending line, and mutates nothing
- [ ] Plain-text trailers, mid-sentence backticked mentions, docs example lines
      and fenced blocks do not warn
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` passes

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` - add `_warn_backticked_partial_increment_trailers` (plus its two text helpers), called from `_check_partial_increment_close_conflict` before the `[[ -n "$partial_refs" ]] || return 0` early return (~line 1303)
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` - add regression cases: incident shape, plain-text control, #5234 prose control, docs prose, fenced blocks, both-shapes case, list/numbered markers, `--dry-run` prefix
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` - add a "write the trailer as plain text, never backticked" caution next to the existing `Part of #N` trailer example (~line 646)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` covers all cases listed in the Fix section and passes
- [ ] Manual verification: construct a PR body whose only partial-increment trailer is a whole-line backticked `` `Part of #N` `` and confirm `merge-pr.sh` (or its `--dry-run` path) prints the new non-blocking warning naming the issue and quoting the offending line, while `_partial_increment_refs` still returns nothing for it (AC #1 unchanged)
- [ ] Edge cases: verify no warning fires for (a) plain-text trailers, (b) mid-sentence backticked mentions (#5234 shape), (c) docs example lines, (d) fenced code blocks

issues.title: telemetry: cross-file message.id dedupe for sweep token sums; gen_ai input_tokens semantics (follow-up to #9313)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Follow-up from the Judge's non-blocking notes on #9313 (#9303).

1. **Transcript usage dedupe is per file, not cross-file.** `sum_transcript_usage_by_model` (via `UsageFold`) folds `message.id` within one transcript file. The quota burn reader (`loom-daemon/src/ops/quota/claude.rs`) dedupes ids across files. So a message copied into a resumed session's transcript counts once for quota but twice in `transcript_tokens::sum_sweep_tokens_by_model` (and so in `loom.runtime.usage` execution spans and the safehouse feed). This predates #9313 and is smaller than the ~2x it fixed. Fix: share one id set across all files summed for a unit.
2. **`gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` is uncached input.** This follows Anthropic's vocabulary and is documented in `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md`, but a generic OTel GenAI consumer would read it as total input. Decide whether to keep it, document it more loudly at the consumer (2AMLogic/2am#1520), or emit total input under that key.

Acceptance: (1) a test with the same `message.id` in two transcript files of one sweep counts it once; (2) a recorded decision on the alias semantics, reflected in telemetry-schema.md.

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Problem Statement

Confirmed against `origin/main` (verified, not inferred):

- **Claim 1 (cross-file dedupe gap) confirmed.** `UsageFold` (`loom-daemon/src/script_helpers/transcript_usage.rs:164-245`) dedupes on `message.id` via its own `by_id` map, but every summation path that iterates a sweep's several transcript files constructs a **fresh** `UsageFold` (or calls a helper that does) per file and merges the *summed* rows afterward — so the same `message.id` appearing in two files (a message copied into a resumed session's transcript) is counted once per file, not once per sweep. This is not limited to `sum_sweep_tokens_by_model` as named in the original report — the same fresh-fold-per-file loop shape appears in three more places (see Affected Files).
  - `loom-daemon/src/transcript_tokens.rs:425-428` already documents the per-transcript dedupe as a deliberate current property: "Dedupe happens per transcript **before** partitioning (`UsageFold`)".
  - **Path correction**: the quota burn reader is at `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/quota/claude.rs`, not `loom-daemon/src/ops/quota/claude.rs` (no `ops/quota` directory exists outside `observability/`). Its module doc (line 10) does confirm cross-file dedupe: "global across files, so a message copied into a resumed session counts once."
- **Claim 2 (`gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` alias semantics) confirmed.** `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md:1510` documents the `loom.runtime.usage` span's `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` alias as "(uncached input, like `loom.tokens.input`)" — i.e. it already diverges from a generic OTel GenAI consumer's likely reading (total input including cache reads/writes), exactly as the issue states.
- Context verified: #9313 (PR, merged 2026-09-28) closed #9303 and is the source of the Judge's non-blocking follow-up notes this issue tracks.

### Implementation Guidance

**Item 1 — share the dedup set across files.** The natural fix is to construct **one** `UsageFold` per summation call and feed it every file's text (`fold.add_text(&text)` per file) before reading totals off the single fold, rather than building a fold per file and merging already-deduped-per-file rows. `UsageFold::add_text`/`add` already compose correctly across repeated calls on the same instance — no change to `UsageFold` itself is obviously required, only to how its callers loop over a sweep's several files. Confirm this while implementing; `transcript_usage.rs` is listed below in case a shared-fold helper is worth adding there instead of duplicating the loop-and-share pattern four times.

**Item 2 — alias semantics decision.** The issue's own acceptance criterion only requires a *recorded* decision, not a specific outcome. Three options, as the issue notes: (a) keep `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` = uncached input as-is (status quo, already documented); (b) strengthen the documentation at the consumer side (2AMLogic/2am#1520, a different repo — out of scope for a change in *this* repo beyond linking it); (c) change the emitted value under that key to total input. Whichever is chosen, update `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md:1510`'s alias description to state the decision and why.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test with the same `message.id` present in two transcript files belonging to one sweep/unit counts it once in the summed totals (per the issue's own AC 1) — cover at minimum `sum_sweep_tokens_by_model`; extend to `sum_sweep_tokens`/`sum_sweep_tokens_split`/`sum_sweep_tokens_by_window` if the shared fix naturally covers them (see Affected Files).
- [ ] `role_tick_telemetry.rs`'s per-transcript-loop totals (`~:460-486`) are evaluated against the same cross-file gap and fixed if it applies, or explicitly noted as out of scope with a reason.
- [ ] A decision on `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` alias semantics is recorded in `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (keep / document more loudly / change to total input).
- [ ] Existing per-file dedup tests (e.g. `sum_transcript_usage_by_model_groups_by_model_speed_and_tier` in `sweep_experiment.rs`) continue to pass unmodified.

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/transcript_tokens.rs` — four functions share the same fresh-fold(or fresh-helper-call)-per-file loop: `sum_sweep_tokens` (:272), `sum_sweep_tokens_split` (:316), `sum_sweep_tokens_by_model` (:358, the one named in the original issue), `sum_sweep_tokens_by_window` (:439). Each needs to dedupe across the files it sums for one call, not per file.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_tick_telemetry.rs` (loop at :460-486) — same per-transcript-fresh-`UsageFold` shape, merging per-file `fold.rows()` into a running `totals` map; its own comment ("Deduped on `message.id` per transcript (#8186, #9303)") documents this as the current, and per this issue, incomplete, behavior.
- `loom-daemon/src/script_helpers/transcript_usage.rs` — `UsageFold` (:164-245) is the dedup structure itself; likely needs no behavioral change, only reuse across files by callers, but is the natural place for a shared-fold helper if the four call sites above would otherwise duplicate the same pattern.
- `loom-daemon/src/script_helpers/sweep_experiment.rs` — `sum_transcript_usage` (:591) and `sum_transcript_usage_by_model` (:676) are the single-file helpers currently invoked per-file by the `transcript_tokens.rs` loops; callers switching to a shared fold may bypass these for the multi-file summation paths (single-file callers, e.g. `observability/runtime_usage/record.rs`, are unaffected — they already process one transcript per call, so no cross-file gap exists there).
- `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (:1510) — record the alias-semantics decision (AC 2).

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: add a fixture with the same `message.id` split across two transcript files of one sweep/unit; assert the summed total (`sum_sweep_tokens_by_model` at minimum) counts it once, not twice.
- [ ] Automated tests: existing per-file UsageFold/dedup tests in `transcript_usage.rs` and `sweep_experiment.rs` still pass unmodified.
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm the `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` alias decision is reflected in `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` and matches what the code actually emits.

issues.title: remote-build guide: the gitignore-filter rsync form silently drops tracked files (macOS system rsync) — document the tracked-file-set sync
issues.body:
The remote-build guide's canonical tree sync silently drops **tracked** files under `defaults/.claude/commands/` when driven from macOS's system rsync, so a builder that follows the guide gets a host tree missing files the test suite reads — six suite failures that look like regressions and are not.

## Evidence (2026-09-29, issue #9366's remote verification)

Synced a clean loom worktree to the AWS build host with the filter form from the repo-skills runbook:

```bash
rsync -az --delete --filter=':- .gitignore' --exclude '.git/' --exclude 'target/' ./ host:build/issue-9366/
```

Result on the host: `defaults/roles/` synced complete, but `defaults/.claude/` arrived holding only three files — the whole `commands/` subtree was gone. `git check-ignore` on the source files reports **not ignored**, i.e. the filter did not fail loudly; macOS system rsync just mishandled the `:-` merge rule for that subtree. `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins` then failed six tests whose only cause was the missing files:

- `config_resolver::tests::test_conformance_fixture_matches_expected_json`
- `init::loom_payload_tree_tests::test_defaults_loom_tree_copy_and_manifest_enumerations_agree`
- `init::tests::test_real_defaults_claude_md_links_resolve_after_install` (`Failed to copy roles directory`)
- `jev_merge_risk::tests::axis_table_matches_champion_prompt` (`cannot read …/defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md`)
- `jev_tier::tests::tier_table_matches_curator_prompt` (`cannot read …/defaults/.claude/commands/loom/curator.md`)
- one `tokens_pool` test (environment-coincident; passed solo after re-sync)

Re-syncing the **tracked file set** fixed all of them; the same suite then passed 9904 in-run (PR #9422's remote-verification comment records the run).

## Proposal

Add a "Syncing the tree" subsection to `docs/guides/remote-build.md`:

1. Name the pitfall: `--filter=':- .gitignore'` is unreliable under macOS system rsync — silently, not loudly, and only for some subtrees, which is what makes it cost a debugging cycle.
2. Prescribe the robust form — sync exactly the tracked tree, which cannot drop tracked files and cannot leak gitignored secret files either:

```bash
git ls-files -z | rsync -az --files-from=- ./ <host>:build/<task>/
```

(with the worktree committed first — which the guide already wants — and `target/` never synced).
3. Give the failure signature above so the next builder pattern-matches in minutes instead of trusting six fake failures.

Cross-reference: the same filter form appears in the Repo Skills runbook (`references/remote.md` §5, upstream rjwalters/repo) — that copy is resync-owned here and needs its own upstream fix; this issue covers the Loom-side guide only.

issues.title: fleet-config propose: open PRs against the fleet store instead of hand-editing it
issues.body:
Follow-up to the `loom-daemon fleet-config` PR (branch `feature/fleet-config`), which makes the fleet store (`fleet.repo`) read-only from a host's point of view.

## Problem
Operators and attended sessions change the fleet by hand-editing the store repo. The most common edits (retier a repo, pause a host, adopt a host-local config change that was made on the host) have to be re-typed into JSON/YAML, and the host that observed the drift is the one place that knows the exact change.

## Proposal
`loom-daemon fleet-config propose` opens a PR against the store instead of writing it:
- `propose state <running|paused|stopped> [--host H] --reason …` edits `fleet/state.yml` (with `since`/`by`).
- `propose priority <repo> <N>` edits `repos.yml`, preserving comments and layout (a format-preserving edit, not a re-serialize).
- `propose adopt [--host H]`: turn `render --check` drift on this host into a PR that moves the on-disk values into `fleet/hosts/<H>/…`.

Constraints: always a branch + PR, never a direct push; the writer App needs `contents: write` + `pull_requests: write` on the store, a scope increase the operator must grant explicitly; the PR body carries the provenance marker; merges stay the operator's (merge commits only, per the store's own policy). Never touch the roster's `firewall` or `fleet` flags from this command.

## Acceptance

issues.title: Peer-claim channel is one-way on loom-worker-2 (advertised=3765, received=0) — every fleet-wide brake consumes nothing
issues.body:
## Problem

`loom-daemon status` on `loom-worker-2` reports, against a live daemon with
peer coordination attached:

```
Safehouse:   connected (room: !s6LTq3gA52tGRJTaY8:safehouse.2amlogic.com, socket: …)
Peer claims: none live (self_host: loom-worker-2, ttl: 120s,
             room: !WyzxHvMPAPaCqaXmL6:safehouse.2amlogic.com,
             advertised=3765 received=0 expired=0 dispatch_skipped=0)
```

**`advertised=3765`, `received=0`.** This host publishes peer-claim ads
continuously (`~/.loom/daemon.log` shows `sweep_registry: re-advertised N live
peer claim(s) (#4431)` every 30s) and has never received a single one from a
peer, on a fleet that has at least one other active host (`loom-worker-1`)
working the same repositories.

Every fleet-wide brake built on the peer-claim channel is therefore one-way on
this host: it contributes to the fleet's shared state but consumes none of it.
That includes, at minimum:

- `#4431` live peer dispatch-claim re-advertisement (`dispatch_skipped=0` —
  this host has never once yielded to a peer's claim)
- `#7477` fleet-wide no-op cooldown / dispatch backoff
  (`PeerClaimView::observe_noop_cooldown_at` / `observe_dispatch_backoff_at`)
- `#8001` fleet-wide token-pool exhaustion hold
- `#6352` / `#6714` / the filing-lock and completion lanes

## Why this was filed (provenance)

Split out of **#8912** while implementing that issue's defect #2. #8912's
defect #1 reported a peer host re-claiming `2AMLogic/llm-cim#1` 196 s into a
3600 s no-op cooldown (2026-09-25).

The curation on #8912 hypothesised that this was a **configuration** gap — that
the affected fleet simply had `safehouse.enabled: false`, so the #7477
mechanism was never attached, making it an ops/docs finding rather than a code
defect. **That hypothesis was tested and does not hold.** Measured on
`loom-worker-2`, 2026-09-28:

- `2AMLogic/llm-cim/.loom/config.json` does carry `safehouse.enabled: false` —
  but that is overridden at runtime: `LOOM_SAFEHOUSE_ENABLED=1` is exported
  into the daemon process (confirmed via `/proc/<pid>/environ`).
- `loom-daemon status` confirms safehouse is `connected` and a peer-claims room
  is configured, i.e. a publisher **and** a view are attached.
- So precondition "coordination is enabled" is satisfied, and the cooldown is
  *still* effectively host-local — because nothing arrives.

The #7477 publish/consume code itself was re-read during #8912 and **no defect
was found in it**. In particular the curator's TTL-sizing concern (a 120 s
`peerClaimTtlSecs` truncating a 3600 s cooldown) is **not** a bug:
`PeerClaimView::observe_noop_cooldown_at` stores its own expiry as
`received_at + remaining_secs` in a dedicated `noop_cooldowns` map, pruned by
`prune_expired_noop_cooldowns` against that expiry — entirely independent of
`self.ttl`. The 120 s TTL governs only the dispatch-claims map.

The residual suspect is therefore the **receive/subscribe path**, not the
sweep-registry brake logic.

## Investigation starting points

1. **Is anything delivered to the claims room subscription at all?** The claims
   room (`LOOM_SAFEHOUSE_ROOM_CLAIMS`) is distinct from the narration room
   (`LOOM_SAFEHOUSE_ROOM`). Confirm the daemon actually subscribes to the
   claims room, and that `safehoused` relays it.
2. **Is the peer publishing to the same room?** Verify `loom-worker-1`'s
   `LOOM_SAFEHOUSE_ROOM_CLAIMS` matches byte-for-byte, and that its own
   `advertised` counter is climbing.
3. **Is own-sender filtering too broad?** `observe_at` /
   `observe_noop_cooldown_at` drop ads whose `host == self_host`. If both hosts
   resolved the *same* `self_host` identity (or both fell back to
   `UNKNOWN_HOST`), every peer ad would be discarded as "our own". Note
   `self_host: loom-worker-2` looks correctly distinct here, so this is a
   lower-probability branch — but it is cheap to rule out.
4. **Why did #6157's degraded-coordination verdict not fire?**
   `PeerClaimView::evaluate_coordination` exists precisely to flag
   "advertising actively, receiving nothing" and the status line shows no
   degraded marker. Either it is not being evaluated on this path, its grace
   window is never reached, or the verdict is not surfaced in
   `loom-daemon status`. A fleet-wide one-way channel going unreported for
   3765 advertisements is itself a defect worth fixing, independently of the
   root cause.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified for `advertised>0, received=0` on a host with
      safehouse connected and a claims room configured.
- [ ] Either a code fix, or — if it resolves to fleet configuration — the
      specific misconfiguration named, corrected, and documented in
      `defaults/docs/safehouse.md`.
- [ ] `loom-daemon status` on both hosts shows `received` climbing, and
      `dispatch_skipped` becoming non-zero when a genuine cross-host contention
      occurs.
- [ ] Item 4 addressed regardless of root cause: a sustained one-way channel
      must surface as degraded in `loom-daemon status` rather than only as two
      counters an operator has to compare by eye.

## Notes

- `defaults/docs/safehouse.md` was updated in the #8912 PR to state that
  "fleet-wide" has **two** preconditions (coordination attached; ads actually
  arriving), and to record the `advertised=3765 received=0` measurement so the
  falsified config-only hypothesis is not re-derived. That section points here.
- #8912's defect #2 (a self-reported no-op release also being counted as a
  PR-less failure / insta-crash) is fixed separately and is not blocked on this.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `83abe1f97`)

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->
<!-- loom:points=5 -->

**Nature of this issue**: an investigation with a possible code fix, not a pre-scoped change. Root cause is unknown; a measured finding of "misconfiguration, no code defect" plus a docs fix and the item-4 status change is a complete, successful outcome. The Builder needs live access to `loom-worker-2` and `loom-worker-1` (or their logs); without it, do the code-only half (item 4) and report the rest as blocked on host access.

### Suspected Cause (unverified — not traced or run by this pass)

- `peer_claims.rs` now has a `ClaimKind::Heartbeat` (#8736/#8817) that anchors `evaluate_coordination`'s receive-quiet clock. If `received` counts only genuine peer *claims* while heartbeats reset the quiet clock, a host receiving peer heartbeats but no peer claims would show `received=0` **and** never go DEGRADED. That would explain item 4 without a broken channel, and it would make `received=0` mean "no peer has dispatched a claim this host could see" rather than "nothing arrives". Read `observe_at` / `observe_heartbeat_at` and the `received` increment to confirm or refute before believing it; check the status output for a heartbeat counter.
- Also worth ruling out (from the body's own list): claims-room subscription (`safehouse.rs` `ROOM_CLAIMS_ENV`), room-ID mismatch between hosts, own-host filtering (`UNKNOWN_HOST` never self-matches, `peer_claims.rs:1190-1252`, so that branch looks low-probability).

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/peer_claims.rs` — `observe_at`, `observe_heartbeat_at`, `evaluate_coordination`, `received` counter (item 4 semantics).
- `loom-daemon/src/peer_claims/brakes.rs` — `observe_noop_cooldown_at` (read-only reference, receive path for #7477).
- `loom-daemon/src/safehouse.rs` — claims-room subscription and `ROOM_CLAIMS_ENV` resolution (item 1).
- `loom-daemon/src/health.rs` — `peer_coordination` component / status rendering (`health.rs:2309`, `:2369`) for the degraded surface.
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/peer_claims_cmd.rs` — CLI view of the counters.
- `defaults/docs/safehouse.md` — record the root cause / corrected config.

(All paths confirmed present on `origin/main` via `git ls-tree`, 2026-09-29.)

### Acceptance Criteria (additions, keep the four above)

- [ ] The root-cause statement names the evidence (command + output from both hosts: `loom-daemon status` on each, the claims-room ID each resolved, and whether heartbeats are being received).
- [ ] If the cause is code: a regression test in `loom-daemon/src/peer_claims/coordination_tests.rs` reproducing "advertising, receiving heartbeats only / nothing" and asserting the verdict.
- [ ] Item 4 is verified by a test, not by inspection: a host with sustained `advertised>0` and zero genuine peer claims for longer than the degrade grace (`LOOM_PEER_COORDINATION_DEGRADE_GRACE_SECS`, default 1200s) either reports DEGRADED, or the status line states explicitly why it does not (e.g. heartbeats seen).

### Test Plan

- [ ] Manual verification: `loom-daemon status` on `loom-worker-1` and `loom-worker-2`; compare resolved claims rooms byte-for-byte and read both counters over a few minutes.
- [ ] Automated tests: extend `peer_claims/coordination_tests.rs` per the criteria above; `cargo test -p loom-daemon --lib peer_claims`.
- [ ] Edge cases: `UNKNOWN_HOST` fallback on either host; peer that only heartbeats (idle) vs. peer that dispatches.
- [ ] Out-of-band: confirm `dispatch_skipped` becomes non-zero on the next real cross-host contention on the live fleet (this is a live-run criterion, not CI-checkable).

issues.title: telemetry: sweep.outcome needs a disposition — result=success includes no-op re-dispatches and 98% of failures are unclassified
issues.body:
## Problem

`sweep.outcome.result` can't answer "did this sweep land work?" and can't say why a sweep failed. Measured on the `loom-fleet-telemetry` D1 store, 26,260 outcomes, 2026-08-15..09-29:

- **`success` does not mean landed.** Only 337 of 8,808 successes carry `pr_number`. 4,825 successes finish in under 300 s with no PR, no tokens and no phases. These are re-dispatch/no-op sweeps (the issue was already done, or the Curator closed or rescoped it). One issue (`2AMLogic/sg13g2-bandgap#4`) has 1,526 sweeps, 970 of them "successes", over 40 days. 472 issues have more than one success.
- **`failure` is mostly unclassified.** `failure_class` is present on 1.9% of outcomes (since 09-18). Of 16,898 failures:

| Failure type | Count |
|---|---|
| Under 60 s with no phase info (spawn/preflight deaths; 725 at exactly 0 s) | 5,326 |
| Stopped after curator only | 2,810 |
| ≥60 s with no phase info at all ("unknown") | 6,373 |
| Showed a substantive signal (judge `fail` or a doctor phase) | 235 |

- There's no field that distinguishes "the environment broke" (account exhausted, spawn death, rate limit, cancel cap) from "the work was hard" (judge rejected, doctor loop).

Any throughput or effort metric built on `result` (#9429 story points, #9433 points-landed/day, ETA #9289) currently has to reverse-engineer this from `pr_number` presence and duration heuristics.

## Want

A required, low-cardinality `disposition` on every `sweep.outcome`:

| disposition | meaning |
|---|---|
| `landed` | PR created/merged for the issue in this sweep |
| `noop_already_done` | issue already closed/landed; nothing to do |
| `curator_closed` / `curator_rescoped` | Curator closed or relabeled instead of building |
| `env_failure` | spawn/preflight death, account/pool exhaustion, rate limit, host/infra fault |
| `substantive_failure` | judge rejected / doctor loop exhausted / builder could not complete the work |
| `cancelled` | operator/cap cancellation (with `cancel_reason`, e.g. the ~45-min cap seen at 2,720–2,733 s) |
| `unknown` | only when truly unobservable — counted, never silently merged |

Plus: `failure_class` becomes **mandatory** whenever `disposition ∈ {env_failure, substantive_failure, unknown}`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every new `sweep.outcome` carries `disposition`; `unknown` < 5% on a fleet host over a week.
- [ ] `landed` ⇔ a PR exists for the issue from this sweep (contract test).
- [ ] Short no-op re-dispatches report `noop_already_done`, not `success`-indistinguishable-from-landing.
- [ ] `telemetry-schema.md` updated; existing `result` kept for compatibility.

Related: 2AMLogic/2am#1221 (silent re-dispatch of sweep deaths), #8525 item 2/5 (outcome classification on spans), #9429.

issues.title: feat(config): consolidate all Loom operational hyperparameters into a unified, structured config file
issues.body:
### Problem Statement
Currently, operational hyperparameters governing Loom's execution, scheduling, thresholds, and worker dynamics are scattered across codebase constants, CLI flags, role definitions, and disparate configuration fragments (e.g. comparator priority weights, timeout bounds, retry ceilings, token budgets, merge-train batch sizes, and backoff multipliers).

This dispersion creates two major bottlenecks:
1. **Lack of Run Provenance:** It is difficult to record and audit the exact point-in-time hyperparameter configuration under which a particular fleet run, sweep, or benchmark was executed.
2. **Barrier to Automated Tuning:** Systematic hyperparameter optimization (e.g., CMA-ES / Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy, Bayesian optimization, or automated sweep search) cannot easily tune, sample, or mutate parameters against fleet cycle time and token-efficiency metrics.

### Proposed Solution
Create a centralized, typed, and structured hyperparameter configuration schema (e.g. `hyperparameters.yml` or a structured `hyperparameters` block within Loom fleet config) consolidating all operational tunables into one place.

#### 1. Consolidated Hyperparameter Scope
- **Dispatch & Scheduling:**
  - Candidate comparator scoring weights (tier weight, repo priority multiplier, age decay factor, dependency depth weight).
  - Tick intervals, idle turnaround duration, and per-host concurrency limits.
- **Timeouts & Lifecycle Limits:**
  - Sweep timeouts, skipped-load admission brake duration, worker lease TTL, and shell budget execution bounds.
- **Rework & Review Bounds:**
  - Max rework / retry attempt ceilings, re-review backoff multipliers, and stale base-branch staleness window.
- **Merge Trains & Batching:**
  - Merge-train batch sizes, speculative merge queue timeouts, and path-filter invalidation thresholds.
- **Model / Role Execution Budgets:**
  - Token budget caps, temperature settings, and max generation tokens per role (`curator`, `builder`, `judge`, `doctor`).

#### 2. Optimization & Provenance Features
- **Snapshot / Span Stamping:** Stamp the active hyperparameter config hash (or vector) onto `loom.story` and `loom.dispatch` OTLP telemetry spans for run-level provenance.
- **Tuning Interface:** Ensure the config can be programmatically injected/overridden via CLI flags or parameter vector files to support external optimizer loops (like CMA-ES).
- **Validation & Defaults:** Comprehensive schema validation (types, range bounds) with well-documented baseline defaults.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Centralized hyperparameter schema and structured configuration file implemented.
- [ ] Point-in-time hyperparameter snapshot / hash stamped into SigNoz telemetry spans.
- [ ] Support for loading and overriding parameter sets programmatically for optimization experiments (e.g. CMA-ES).
- [ ] Schema validation ensuring invalid parameter combinations fail fast at startup.

### Context
Requested by @turian for configuration auditing and automated CMA-ES fleet performance optimization.

issues.title: Prefer human-directed PRs throughout landing with a disableable planning policy
issues.body:
## Problem

Human-directed PRs should reach landing promptly while autonomous fleet work continues. Today an explicit `loom:operator-priority` star accelerates work, but ordinary PR scheduling does not distinguish an interactive human-driven session from autonomous execution; unlabeled PRs can wait behind the entire labeled review queue.

This issue records the operator's agreed design and request to implement it.

## Agreed behavior

**A human-directed PR gets the next available opportunity to move toward landing, at every stage.** An agent producing a PR in an interactive session counts as human-directed because a human drove that session. AI authorship is irrelevant.

Record work origin explicitly:

| Origin | Meaning | Default planning preference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interactive` | A human drove the working session, including an agent used interactively | Goes first |
| `autonomous` | The fleet independently executed the work | Ordinary queue |
| `unknown` | Origin was not reliably recorded | Ordinary queue; an operator can star it |

Origin is set at work/session creation and carried onto the PR. It persists through Doctor fixes, re-review, and merging; a later autonomous worker does not rewrite an interactive PR's origin. Approving a backlog issue for autonomous execution does not make its resulting PR interactive. Do not infer origin from GitHub usernames, bot flags, AI coauthor trailers, branch names, or the absence of a fleet marker.

Keep three separate concepts: origin (historical fact), planning preference (configurable policy), and the operator star (explicit stronger override).

### Scheduling contract

- Prefer interactive PRs at review, fixes, re-review, and merge, not merely the first review.
- Preserve existing explicit operator priority and applicable verified-red-main recovery precedence; interactive work precedes ordinary autonomous/unknown work.
- Finish work already running. Do not interrupt agents, cancel CI, or consume the operator star's overflow slot merely for being interactive.
- Prefer only work eligible for the next action. Drafts, holds, live claims, CI/dependency waits and required human responses continue to use existing gates. Fleet work proceeds while a preferred PR cannot advance.
- Preserve existing relative ordering inside each class. The preference must affect actual work selection, not only a displayed queue.
- Review/merge standards and eligibility for automated landing are independent of priority. Human origin grants no approval or permission to modify an arbitrary contributor branch.
- Discover eligible interactive PRs without relying on the labeled fleet queue first becoming empty. Reuse the existing admission/ownership rules rather than silently enrolling arbitrary unlabeled PRs for auto-merge.
- Start with non-preemptive preference. New quota systems, aging/burst tuning, extra concurrency, fleet-wide pauses, and human-first issue/build scheduling are out of scope.

### Configuration

Add the planning setting `planning.preferHumanPrs`, default `true`. Setting it to `false` restores the ordinary PR ordering/admission behavior and retains origin metadata. Explicit operator stars continue to work. Use the normal effective configuration layers so fleet defaults and repository overrides work consistently.

## Implementation direction (to verify during Curator)

- Reuse Loom's provenance/PR creation and session/sweep launch surfaces for origin capture and propagation. Old records remain readable and classify as `unknown` unless explicit reliable origin exists.
- Introduce one shared origin parser and PR ordering policy, used by the actual Judge/Doctor/Champion selection paths and any rendered explanation; avoid three independent prompt heuristics.
- Use trustworthy source metadata; malformed, conflicting, missing, or untrusted origin declarations must not earn automatic priority.
- Update documentation with the definition, handoff persistence, scope, ordering, config disable behavior, and how manual/interactive callers record origin.

Relevant current seams: `loom-daemon/src/provenance/`, `defaults/scripts/create-pr.sh`, daemon sweep/role launch, `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/`, `defaults/roles/{judge,doctor,champion}.md`, their canonical command sources, and the existing operator-priority ordering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interactive agent sessions can explicitly record `interactive`; autonomous launch paths reliably record `autonomous`; unrecorded work remains `unknown`.
- [ ] PR origin round-trips and survives autonomous repair/re-review without being overwritten.
- [ ] One consistent ordering selects an eligible interactive PR before ordinary fleet PRs through review, repair and merge, preserving stronger explicit priority and stable class order.
- [ ] Turning `planning.preferHumanPrs` off restores baseline behavior without deleting origin or changing stars.
- [ ] A full fleet queue does not hide an eligible interactive PR; existing admission/authorization boundaries remain intact.
- [ ] Holds, drafts, active claims, failing/pending checks and dependencies cannot be bypassed by origin; waiting human work does not idle other actionable work.
- [ ] Missing, invalid, conflicting and untrusted origin records receive no implicit preference; author identity alone never implies human-directed work.
- [ ] Tests exercise actual creation/launch/selection integration as well as policy, including the same PR passing from interactive creation to autonomous Doctor and back to Judge.
- [ ] User documentation explains all three concepts and the enabled-by-default disable switch; prompt changes are pressure-tested against a resisting queue scenario and audited for rule conflicts.

## Authorization

The operator explicitly requested: document this discussion in an issue, then implement it. Run Curator → Builder → Judge → Doctor if needed → Merge under the repository workflow.

## Curator implementation findings

Curated per the operator's explicit request against checkout `d6dd1941b`. Premise gate: out of scope (exit 0). Duplicate/related-work scan: no duplicates found (exit 0); no sibling micro-issues or open numbered dependencies identified. Keep this as one cohesive policy change: origin capture without actual role selection would not fulfill the request.

- **PR selection is not the work-finder issue queue.** Judge and Doctor select PRs through their role instructions; Champion drains `loom:pr` through `champion-pr-merge.md`. Sorting `work_finder::candidate_cmp` or its dashboard projection alone would not change those choices and would expand scope into issue/build scheduling.
- **Implement a shared executable queue policy.** A Rust module plus a `loom-daemon` CLI port can expose ordered PR candidates and origin/reason to every role. Use the existing executable-extension surface (`src/cli/script_ports.rs`) rather than growing the frozen `main.rs`. Keep normal role-specific actionable-work checks at claim/action time and continue past skipped rows. Preserve existing queue order as the stable tie-breaker within each preference class, including Doctor's conflict/changes-requested baseline and Champion's oldest-first merge order.
- **Unlabeled discovery has two independent gates.** `role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs::forge_queue_probe` only sees the configured label queues; Judge's fallback additionally runs only when the labeled queue is empty. With the preference enabled, a trusted explicit interactive PR eligible for fallback review must be discoverable alongside labeled PRs and must open the Judge role-runner gate when it is the only pending work. With the preference disabled, preserve the current admission behavior. Continue to run `judge-fallback-guard.sh` for bot exclusion, lifetime cap, and SHA dedup; fallback review does not add workflow labels or authorize automated landing.
- **Trust is separate from origin.** Use `comment_trust::TrustPolicy` on a forge response carrying `user`/author association (a pull-list response has these). `forge_listing::RestIssue` currently loses association/type, so its author login alone is insufficient. A trusted bot can carry explicit interactive origin; a human username without a valid declaration remains unknown. Reject duplicate/conflicting origin declarations rather than choosing whichever appears first.
- **Provenance is a compatible persistence seam.** `provenance/marker.rs` has a v1 parser accepting unknown fields and one existing optional field (`installs`). An optional typed `origin` field can preserve old markers as unknown without inventing a second body-parser convention. `create-pr.sh` already adds exactly one provenance marker, preserves an existing marker, and adopts an existing PR before creation. Explicit interactive context must reach this path; repair/adoption must retain the PR's existing origin rather than restamping it from the current Doctor process.
- **Autonomous launchers must pin their context.** `sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs` and `role_runner/launch.rs` assemble child environments; explicitly stamp autonomous work there so an interactive value inherited by a long-running daemon cannot promote every future fleet PR. Use an explicit documented interactive session/creation argument or environment entry point; absence of an autonomous marker is never evidence of interactivity.
- **Use the effective config resolver.** `config_resolver::resolve_effective_config` supplies shared/private defaults, legacy repository config, project config and local overrides. Resolve `planning.preferHumanPrs` from that output with a true default; do not add a second direct `.loom/config.json` reader.
- **Preserve role-specific safety semantics.** Doctor deliberately allows `loom:operator` on changes-requested PRs for the existing stale-diff refresh route (#7660), while merge remains held. Pending/failing checks may block merge while still yielding actionable Doctor work. The preference must neither blanket-filter away these valid repair paths nor relax their existing authorization/claim checks.

Related implementation precedents: #9244 (operator priority), #9027 (provenance), #9391/#9392 (role-runner queue gate/demand), #5455 (fallback review guard), #7660 (Doctor hold semantics).

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/provenance/marker.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/cli/provenance.rs` — explicit typed origin capture, compatibility and round-trip handling.
- `defaults/scripts/create-pr.sh` — pass explicit creation context into provenance while preserving adoption and existing-marker behavior.
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/launch.rs` — autonomous child context, tested under inherited interactive environment.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs` — Judge admission for eligible interactive fallback work; preserve disabled behavior.
- A focused new Rust PR-planning module and `loom-daemon/src/cli/script_ports.rs` — shared trust-aware origin classification, effective configuration and stable ordered candidate output; reuse `comment_trust.rs` and forge listing/cache utilities.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/{judge,doctor,champion}.md`, `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md` and corresponding `defaults/roles/` sources/copies — actual queue selection and fallback integration. Regenerate managed agent skills with the existing generator; do not hand-edit generated `SKILL.md` files.
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` or a focused linked planning document, plus relevant provenance/session documentation — definitions, configuration, creation entry point, persistence and admission distinction.
- Rust unit/integration tests and `tests/test-create-pr.sh` (existing creation harness, if applicable) — creation, launch, selection, disabled baseline and handoff regressions.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Policy fixtures cover explicit stars, existing red-main priority where applicable, trusted interactive, autonomous and unknown PRs; stable order is retained within each class and disabled policy reproduces each role's baseline order.
- [ ] Parser/trust fixtures cover old markers, malformed/duplicate/conflicting records, absent author metadata, untrusted declarations, trusted bots declaring interactive, and trusted humans with no declaration.
- [ ] Launch tests begin with an inherited interactive environment and demonstrate that autonomous role/sweep children receive autonomous context; direct interactive creation emits interactive origin.
- [ ] Creation/adoption/repair integration carries the same interactive PR through an autonomous Doctor handoff and re-review with unchanged origin. Existing provenance and old PR bodies remain readable.
- [ ] Actual Judge/Doctor/Champion selection entry points consume the shared ordered candidates, including enough fleet work to keep the ordinary queue nonempty. An interactive-only fallback case opens the Judge launch gate when enabled and preserves the old closed-gate behavior when disabled.
- [ ] Guard fixtures exercise held, draft, claimed and non-actionable preferred work followed by actionable fleet work; no extra agent slot, CI cancellation, fallback workflow enrollment, or origin-based merge permission occurs. Include Doctor's authorized held stale-diff repair case.
- [ ] Configuration tests cover default true, explicit false, shared-default false with repository true override, and retention of origin metadata and operator-star behavior after disabling.
- [ ] Run focused Rust/creation tests, prompt synchronization and documentation checks. Pressure-test changed role prompts with a full fleet queue, one eligible interactive PR and one blocked interactive PR; verify the shared queue is used and existing action gates remain authoritative.
