issues.title: Auto-update: post-provision codesign check is unbounded and misreports a non-answer as a signature downgrade
issues.body:
## Bug Description

The post-provision signature-downgrade check in `defaults/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh`
(`verify_destination_artifact()`, around line 1235) has the same
"could not verify" vs "verified and it's bad" collapse that #8754 fixed one
layer up in `loom-daemon/src/release_fetch/signature.rs::verify_darwin` —
but in the shell, and with an additional unbounded-hang gap.

```bash
if [[ "$ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE_HAD_AUTHORITY" == "true" ]]; then
    ...
    dest_sig_desc="$(codesign -dvvv "$dest" 2>&1 || true)"
    if ! grep -q '^Authority=' <<<"$dest_sig_desc"; then
        err "Post-provision verification FAILED: ... Provisioning has DOWNGRADED the signature ..."
        exit 5
    fi
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Unbounded.** There is no `timeout` around `codesign -dvvv`. On exactly
   the contended host that motivated #8754 (where `timeout 20 codesign -dvv
   /usr/bin/codesign` on a stock Apple system binary was observed to hang),
   this invocation hangs the update script indefinitely with no deadline and
   no diagnostic. Every other `codesign` invocation in the update path now
   runs under a deadline (`VERIFY_TIMEOUT` in `signature.rs`); this one does
   not.

2. **Misclassified if it does not answer.** `|| true` swallows any non-zero
   exit (including a `timeout`-induced 124, were one added), leaving
   `dest_sig_desc` empty. The `grep -q '^Authority='` then fails, and the
   script reports **"Provisioning has DOWNGRADED the signature"** and
   `exit 5` — an alarming, specific accusation about what provisioning did,
   produced by a `codesign` that never reported anything at all. This is the
   #8754 conflation verbatim: "we could not check" rendered as "we checked
   and it is bad".

Note that this check runs only when the pre-provision download demonstrably
carried an `Authority=` line (`ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE_HAD_AUTHORITY == "true"`),
which is precisely the case PR for #8754 still sets `had_authority:
Some(true)` for when only the `codesign --verify` call times out — so a host
under enough load to time out the Rust-side verify can reach this unbounded
shell-side `codesign` on the very next step.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Read `defaults/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh` around line 1226–1243
   (`verify_destination_artifact()`).
2. Confirm `codesign -dvvv "$dest"` carries no `timeout` wrapper, unlike the
   `codesign` invocations in `loom-daemon/src/release_fetch/signature.rs`
   (which run under `cmd_out::run_command(.., VERIFY_TIMEOUT)`).
3. Confirm that an empty `dest_sig_desc` — the state produced by any
   `codesign` that fails to print its report, for any reason — takes the
   `exit 5` "signature DOWNGRADED" branch rather than an inconclusive one.

## Expected Behavior

- The invocation runs under an explicit deadline (matching the rest of the
  update path's `codesign` calls).
- A `codesign` that does not complete produces an **inconclusive** result —
  a `warn` and a skip of the downgrade check, the same disposition the
  branch already uses a few lines above when `codesign` is not installed at
  all (`"'codesign' not available -- cannot verify the destination binary's
  signature survived provisioning"`) — not `exit 5` with a downgrade
  accusation.
- Only a `codesign` that **ran to completion** and reported no `Authority=`
  line may take the `exit 5` downgrade path.

## Actual Behavior

A `codesign` that hangs blocks the update script forever; a `codesign` that
otherwise produces no output causes the script to report a signature
downgrade that was never observed, and abort provisioning with `exit 5`.

## Impact

Same class and same host conditions as #8754 (a busy macOS host makes
`codesign` slow), one layer further into the update, with a worse failure
mode: an indefinite hang rather than a bounded abort, and an incorrect
accusation about what provisioning did to the binary's signature rather than
about the release artifact.

## Scope note

Out of scope for #8754, which is bounded to `verify_darwin` in
`loom-daemon/src/release_fetch/signature.rs` plus its test file. Filed
separately per Builder scope discipline while implementing #8754.

<!-- loom:premise-check exists=yes deliberate=no reversal=no verdict=clear -->

issues.title: observability: session.summary record kind from transcript-ingest (G3 part 1 of #8714)
issues.body:
## Context

Sub-issue of #8714 (slice 2 of 5, "G3 `session.summary`"). Parent issue's own scoping — see #8714 for the full gap analysis. Rides on the multi-exporter sink list (the G1 slice, sibling sub-issue) to actually reach more than one backend, but the record kind itself does not require G1 to have merged first to be implemented — only to be validated end-to-end in both backends per Acceptance below.

## Problem

Transcripts are today read for token counts only (`activity/transcript_ingest.rs`). The only rollups are local SQL views (`cost_by_*`) and the dashboard's token-analytics page. There is no per-session record on the wire at all — nothing carries session-level shape (role, repo, issue, model, turn/tool-call counts) to any exporter.

## Proposal

A new record kind, `session.summary`, emitted by the existing transcript-ingest pass and shipped through whatever exporters are configured (the G1 sink list): one record per transcript (session or subagent), carrying:

- `session_id`, `parent_session_id`
- `runtime`, `role`, `repo`, `issue`, `pr_number`
- `model(s)` used
- four token counters (matching whatever the existing `activity.db` schema already tracks)
- `wall_ms`, `turns`, `tool_calls` (histogram by tool name), `tool_errors`
- `outcome`, if known

Attributes only from the existing `loom.*` allowlist plus the new ids #8664 already proposes. Must obey the epic's wire-safety rule: no prompts, generated code, raw tool arguments/output, keys or emails on the wire — this is a **summary**, not a transcript excerpt.

`session.analysis` (derived rollups: retry-loop detection, longest tool call, USD cost, anomaly flags) is explicitly a separate, later slice (sibling sub-issue, slice 5) — do not fold it in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `session.summary` record kind exists, populated by the existing transcript-ingest pass, containing exactly the fields listed above (no prompt/tool-output/key/email content).
- [ ] The record is shipped through the exporter(s) configured via the G1 sink list (validate against at least one sink end-to-end; full multi-sink validation depends on the G1 sub-issue landing).
- [ ] `session.summary` rows for a day of daemon work are queryable (by role, model, repo) in whichever indexed backend is available for testing — per #8714's parent Acceptance, ClickHouse is the target once #8529's fixture manifest / the G1 sink applies.
- [ ] Extend the existing redaction tests to cover the new record kind: no prompt, tool output, key, or email ever appears on the wire for a `session.summary` record.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/activity/transcript_ingest.rs` — existing transcript-ingest pass; extend to emit the new record kind alongside its current token-count-only reads
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/` — new record-kind definition, wherever `TelemetryEnvelope`'s existing record kinds are declared (exact module TBD — grep for the existing record-kind enum once scoping starts)
- Redaction test suite (exact file TBD — grep for the existing "no prompt/key/email on the wire" test, likely alongside `exporter.rs` or `otlp/`) — extend for `session.summary`
- `#8664`'s proposed new ids (referenced in this issue's own Proposal) — confirm exact attribute names before implementing, to avoid a second, incompatible id scheme

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a fixture transcript produces exactly one `session.summary` record with the documented fields populated correctly (including a subagent transcript producing a record with `parent_session_id` set)
- [ ] Automated tests: extend the redaction test suite — assert no prompt, tool output, key, or email appears in a `session.summary` record for a transcript that contains all four
- [ ] Manual verification: once at least one exporter is configured, confirm a day's worth of `session.summary` rows are queryable by role/model/repo in the indexed backend available for testing

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `complex`**: this is a new, additive record kind emitted from an existing, already-instrumented ingest pass — the shape is fully specified by the parent issue and by existing schema (`activity.db`'s token counters), and a mistake (a missing field, a redaction gap) would surface in the redaction test or in a straightforward review of the record shape, not as a silent architectural regression.

## Related

- Parent: #8714 (observability multi-sink export)
- Sibling sub-issue: G1 multi-exporter (this slice rides its sink list to reach more than one backend)
- Sibling sub-issue: G3 `session.analysis` (later slice, derived from this record — do not fold in here)
- #8664 (interactive-session ids this record's attributes should reuse)
- #8529 (fixture manifest referenced by the parent's validation approach)

issues.title: Champion: a killed merge-pr.sh --auto call leaves no forge-visible outcome (follow-up to #9091 item 2)
issues.body:
## Context

Split out of #9091 (item 2 of its checklist). #9091's fix (PR pending) removes the
common cause of a `merge-pr.sh --auto` run that never returns: the #6169 zero-row
check-runs guard used to re-poll until the full `LOOM_AUTO_MERGE_TIMEOUT` (600s)
elapsed on any repo with no CI on the changed paths. That is fixed in the script.

What #9091 deliberately did **not** fix is the Champion-side blind spot it exposed:

- `champion-pr-merge.md` Step 3 runs `./.loom/scripts/merge-pr.sh "$PR_NUMBER"
  --auto --redate-stale-checks` through a Bash tool call. The tool's default
  timeout is 120s and its cap is 600s — **equal to** `LOOM_AUTO_MERGE_TIMEOUT`'s
  default. So any genuinely slow settle-wait (a repo whose CI legitimately
  outruns the budget) is still killed before `merge-pr.sh` can report exit 5.
- When the call is killed, nothing is posted. Step 2's "Proceeding with squash
  merge…" comment is already on the PR, so the forge-visible state is a Champion
  that announced a merge and then went silent — indistinguishable from a crashed
  host. That is exactly what happened on 2AMLogic/2am#1267 (14:34:43Z comment,
  silence until a manual merge at 15:02:11Z).

## Proposed change

1. Call `merge-pr.sh` with an explicit `LOOM_AUTO_MERGE_TIMEOUT` **below** the
   Bash tool cap (e.g. 420s with the tool timeout set to 600s), so the script's
   own exit 5 always wins the race and Champion's existing exit-5 handling
   ("not merged this pass — re-queuing") is what the operator sees.
2. If the merge call returns no classifiable outcome (killed, timed out, empty
   output), post a short timeout/unknown-outcome comment on the PR so a stalled
   merge is visible on the forge instead of only in a worker log. This must be
   distinct from the "Merge Failed" path — nothing merged and nothing failed.

## Why this is its own issue

Both parts edit a role prompt (`defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md`),
which per CLAUDE.md's role-prompt-authoring discipline needs its own
pressure-testing pass against a resisting scenario plus a rule-conflict audit —
notably against Step 3's "Ordering invariant" and the existing exits 3/4/5
handling, and against the "never post a failure comment for a re-queue" rule.
That review belongs in a focused PR, not bundled with the script fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Champion's merge step passes an explicit settle-wait budget strictly below
      the tool timeout it runs under, with the relationship between the two
      documented at the callsite (so a later edit to one cannot silently invert it).
- [ ] A merge invocation with no classifiable outcome leaves a forge-visible
      notice that is explicitly NOT the "Merge Failed" / "human must investigate"
      wording.
- [ ] Pressure-test + rule-conflict audit notes included in the PR body per
      `.loom/docs/role-prompt-authoring.md`.
## Affected Files

- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md` — Step 3 ("Merge the PR", ~line 1958-2019): the `merge-pr.sh "$PR_NUMBER" --auto --redate-stale-checks` invocation needs an explicit `LOOM_AUTO_MERGE_TIMEOUT` set strictly below the Bash tool call's own timeout (document the relationship at the callsite per AC1), plus new handling for a killed/unclassified outcome (no `MERGE_RC` captured at all) that posts a distinct forge-visible notice — not the existing "Merge failed" comment path at the `elif [ "$MERGE_RC" -ne 0 ]` branch (line ~2001-2004).
- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — reference only; no code change expected. Its exit 3/4/5 contract (head-moved, stale-check re-date, settle-wait timeout) is what Step 3's existing `MERGE_RC` handling already keys on (lines 1991-2000) — the fix is giving that logic a chance to run before the wrapping Bash call is killed, not changing the script itself.
- `.loom/docs/role-prompt-authoring.md` — reference only; the pressure-test + rule-conflict audit this issue's own "Why this is its own issue" section requires is defined here.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Manual verification: with a test PR/repo whose CI legitimately exceeds the new lower `LOOM_AUTO_MERGE_TIMEOUT` budget (or by temporarily lowering the budget to force the race), confirm `merge-pr.sh` returns exit 5 and Step 3's existing "not merged this pass... re-queuing" handling fires — the script's own exit code must win the race against the Bash tool timeout in the intended case.
- [ ] Manual verification: reason through (an actual Bash-tool-level kill isn't reproducible in a test harness) the case where the call is killed with no classifiable `MERGE_RC` at all, and confirm the new forge-visible notice posts and reads distinctly from the "Merge Failed" comment.
- [ ] Automated tests: N/A — this is a role-prompt (markdown instruction) change with no directly executable surface; verification is the pressure-test/rule-conflict audit itself, per `.loom/docs/role-prompt-authoring.md`.
- [ ] Edge cases: confirm the new notice does not fire on a legitimate exit 3/4/5 (those already have defined, non-failure handling and must stay silent-to-the-forge exactly as today); confirm the pressure-test explicitly checks this against the "never post a failure comment for a re-queue" rule the issue itself flags as a conflict risk.

issues.title: feat: ETA as a Loom primitive — versioned start/finish/land estimates, logged to SigNoz and scored against outcomes
issues.body:
## Problem

Operators want to know, for any active issue, **when it will start, when the running sweep will finish, and when it will land** (PR merged / issue closed as completed). They also want to know how often those guesses are wrong, so the guess can be improved over time.

Today a downstream dashboard would have to guess from outside, re-deriving order, capacity and phase durations that only Loom actually knows. Operator decision: **ETAs are a Loom primitive.** Loom computes them, versions the heuristic, and logs every estimate and its outcome to SigNoz. Dashboards only display them.

This builds on #9288 (`dispatch_plan()`), since an honest start/land ETA needs the real order, capacity and sharding.

## Ask

**1. A versioned ETA primitive in loom-daemon**
- `estimate(issue) -> { kind, p25, p50, p75, parts[], inputs, heuristic }` for `kind ∈ {start, finish, land}`.
- Inputs:
  - the dispatch plan (rank, `max_concurrent`, sharding, repo caps);
  - Loom's phase-duration history, including human stages such as awaiting curation or approval;
  - the historical changes-requested rate, which drives how likely a Doctor pass is.
- Returns **no estimate** when there isn't an honest one (blocked, held, no baseline). Never a made-up number.

**2. Versioning**
- A heuristic registry with ids like `land-v1`.
- A shipped heuristic is immutable. Any change gets a new id.
- **Shadow mode:**
  - every registered heuristic is computed and logged;
  - one is marked `current`;
  - switching is a config change, made once the SigNoz accuracy data favours the new one.

**3. Telemetry: log every estimate, then score it, in Loom**
- `eta.estimate`: per active issue × kind × heuristic, on each work-finder tick or at a fixed cadence.
- `eta.outcome`: when the outcome happens (sweep start, sweep end, merge/close). Fields:
  - `error = actual − p50`;
  - `covered` (actual within [p25, p75]);
  - `horizon`, `heuristic`, `kind`, `repo`, `stage_at_estimate`, `samples`.
- Both go out through the daemon's existing OTLP exporter to SigNoz, so no new write path is needed. They are also sent through the same ingest path as `queue.snapshot`, so dashboards can show the *current* estimate without recomputing it.

**4. CLI**
- `loom eta <repo>#<n>` and `loom eta --repo <slug>`: the "landing next" list, soonest first.

**5. Docs**
- The model, the versioning rules, and how to add v2 and compare it in shadow mode using SigNoz accuracy queries: median absolute error, p25–p75 coverage and bias, per heuristic, kind, repo and horizon.

## Downstream

2AMLogic/loom-ui will render these verbatim:
- a "Landing next" table sorted by land p50;
- "starts in" / "lands in" ranges;
- an accuracy panel with live SigNoz queries over `eta.outcome`.

It will retire its interim dashboard-side estimates once this ships.

Related: #9288 (dispatch plan), #9238 (ranking inputs), #8525 (phase tracing), #9037 (per-issue story trace).

issues.title: [#9244 A] daemon core: loom:operator-priority ordering, starred listing, overflow slot, red-main-fix lane, telemetry
issues.body:
Parent: #9244 (split approved by the operator into three PRs: A, B, C). This is **A: daemon core (Rust)**.

## Goal

Make the work finder treat `loom:operator-priority` ("starred") as the top dispatch key, fleet-wide, with an overflow slot, a red-main-fix lane, and the telemetry loom-ui needs. `loom:urgent` stops affecting order.

## Scope

### 1. Label
- Add `loom:operator-priority` to **both** `.github/labels.yml` and `defaults/.github/labels.yml` (they're byte-identical today, 280 lines each). Put it next to the `loom:operator*` block (~line 161-236). Description must be at most 100 chars and include an `Applied by:` owner, e.g. `"Operator wants this landed ASAP, ahead of all other work. Applied by: humans (directly or via loom-ui star)."`. Colour `CA8A04` (matches loom-ui's copy).
- Add a YAML comment saying it is **not** `loom:operator` (the hold) and is **not a hold**: nothing may prefix-match `loom:operator` / `loom:operator-` as a hold.
- **Prefix-match audit (loom-ui asked for this):** `loom-daemon/src/pr_latency/mod.rs:117` (`hold_labels`) uses `l.starts_with("loom:operator-")`, so a starred PR would list `loom:operator-priority` as a hold label. Exclude it and add a test. No other daemon `starts_with("loom:operator` was found on `origin/main`. Re-run the grep before merging.

### 2. Ordering keys (`WorkItem` / `PriorityCandidate` / `candidate_cmp`)
- `WorkItem` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs`, `is_urgent` at :461) gains `is_operator_priority()` and a way to carry `operator_priority_at: Option<String>`. It also gains `is_main_red_fix()`, which is true when `body` contains `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` (same style as the complexity and recheck-interval markers).
- `PriorityCandidate` (:593) gains `operator_priority: bool`, `operator_priority_at: Option<String>` and `main_red_fix: bool`. The last one is already resolved against the repo's red state, so `candidate_cmp` stays pure.
- `candidate_cmp` (:624) becomes:
  1. starred first
  2. (starred only) `operator_priority_at` ascending, with a missing value falling back to `created_at` (use the `cmp_created_at` Some<None semantics, :637)
  3. `main_red_fix` first (set only while that repo's main is verified red)
  4. `workspace_priority` ascending
  5. `created_at` oldest first
  6. `number` ascending
- **Remove `urgent` from the order.** Keep parsing it harmlessly: `URGENT_LABEL` / `is_urgent()` may stay, an item carrying `loom:urgent` is never an error, and the wire `urgent` fields stay (see 7). Removing the Rust constant and wire field completely is a follow-up after one release.
- `ready_queue::key_of` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/ready_queue.rs:44-53`) builds the key. Populate the new fields there, so the view and dispatch can't drift.
- Update the sort comment at `work_finder.rs:1966` and the `candidate_cmp` rustdoc.

### 3. Starred-at source
- Primary source: the `labeled` event for `loom:operator-priority` in the issue's timeline (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/timeline` or `/events`). Fetch it **only for starred candidates** and cache it per (repo, issue). Invalidate the cache when the label is removed. A tick must not make one call per candidate per tick. `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal/label_timeline.rs` already reads label timelines and may be reusable.
- Fallback: `createdAt`.
- (C will add the loom-ui intent `requested_at` via a comment marker as a higher-precedence source. Leave a seam for it; don't implement it here.)

### 4. Second listing: starred issues outside `loom:issue`
- `GhWorkSource::list_ready_issues` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/forge.rs:82`) currently makes one `forge_listing::list_issues_cached(.., "loom:issue", "open")` call (`forge_listing.rs:82`). Add a second ETag-cached call with `label = "loom:operator-priority"`, drop PR rows, and **dedupe by issue number** against the `loom:issue` rows. A starred `loom:issue` appears in both.
- A starred issue whose workflow label is `loom:triage` or `loom:curated`, or that has **no workflow label at all** (#9244 liveness item 6, the loom-ui#281 shape), becomes a candidate. Dispatching it is already supported: `preflip_labels::classify_observed_labels` (`sweep_registry/preflip_labels.rs:108`) returns `NotYetApproved` for a non-`loom:issue` snapshot, and the child sweep runs the full lifecycle from Curator.
- A starred item carrying anything in `SKIP_LABELS` (`work_finder/labels.rs:69`: `loom:building`, `loom:blocked`, `loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator`) **or `loom:operator-decision`** must never be dispatched. **Note:** `loom:operator-decision` is *not* in `SKIP_LABELS` today; it's covered only because it always accompanies `loom:operator-only`. For starred candidates, check it explicitly (or add it to the skip set) and add a test.
- Keep the listing failure isolation (`report.listing_failed`) and the rate-limit breaker path. If the second listing fails, the `loom:issue` rows must still be used.

### 5. Overflow slot (one over-limit sweep per host, starred only)
- Multi-workspace path: `tick_multi_with_repo_cap` (`work_finder.rs:1639`), pass 2 at :1983-2033 (global cap check :1998, per-repo cap `cap.defer` :2014). Single-workspace path: `tick_with_saturation_brake` (:1109), cap check at :1339. **Both are live in production** (called at :2591 and :3203).
- A starred candidate refused **only** by the global `max_concurrent` cap and/or the per-repo cap (`maxConcurrentPerRepo`, `work_finder/repo_cap.rs`) may be admitted as the overflow sweep, provided that:
  - no live sweep on this host is already marked `overflow` (a new `WorkDispatcher` query, backed by the registry), and
  - `occupancy <= max_concurrent`. `resolve_dynamic_max_concurrent` can lower the cap below occupancy mid-flight; a host already over its limit for that reason must not add another sweep. This is how "at most one over-limit sweep" is enforced in practice.
- These gates still apply, unchanged: the saturation brake (checked first, :1987 / :1334), the host-class gate (`work_finder/host_class.rs`), token-pool preflight / exhaustion (`work_finder/pool_preflight.rs`), park and skip labels, quarantine, backoff, peer claim and the per-tick ramp cap (#4234). The ramp cap isn't a queue limit, so the overflow sweep doesn't bypass it; see the note in #9244.
- Normal (unstarred) work never uses the overflow slot. Red-main fixes don't get it either.
- Record `overflow: true` on the sweep record (`SweepInfo`, `loom-daemon/src/types.rs:904`, serde-default `false`). Thread it through dispatch: today `WorkDispatcher::dispatch(issue, complexity)` is at `work_finder.rs:910` and `forge.rs:376`. Surface it in `list_sweeps` / `get_sweep_status` (MCP) and `loom-daemon status`. Add a `TickReport` counter or `QueueDisposition` so the ready queue shows "dispatched (overflow)".

### 6. Red-main fixes and the main-health halt
- The key-3 boost applies only when the owning repo's main-health state is **verified red**: `WorkspaceHealthStates::is_halted(root)` (`main_health_gate.rs:698`). **Don't** use the `halted[]` slice for this. `dispatch_held_per_root` (:1442) also sets it while a gate run is in flight (`suppress_dispatch_during_gate`), which isn't a red main.
- With the gate disabled for a repo, fall back to the latest default-branch CI conclusion: one cached forge read per repo per tick, only when that repo has at least one marker-bearing candidate.
- Halt admits only fixes. Single-workspace: `if halted { … return }` at :1128. Multi: the per-repo `halted` branch at :1807 records every item as `WorkspaceHalted` and `continue`s. Change both so a halted repo still admits its `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` candidates, and **only** those. That includes starred issues without the marker: they keep `WorkspaceHalted`. `report.halted` semantics stay unchanged. If the gate is in flight (not verified red), admit nothing, as today.
- A marker on a green repo gets no boost.

### 7. Telemetry and CLI
- `queue.snapshot` rows: `QueueSnapshotRow` (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/queue_snapshot.rs:55`) gains `operator_priority: bool` (serde default false) and `operator_priority_at: Option<String>` (skip if none). `urgent` (:65) is **kept and emitted always-false** for one release. Populate them in `build_record` (`observability/queue_snapshot.rs:97`, row push at :115-128) from `TickQueueRow` (`types/ready_queue.rs:~214`), which gains the same fields.
- `host.health.managed_repos[]`: `ManagedRepoEntry` (`telemetry/mod.rs:1236`) gains `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] priority: Option<u32>` from `Workspace.priority`. Construct it in `collect_managed_repos_with` (`observability/collector.rs:1060`, push at :1092). This folds in loom-ui#153.
- `ready-queue` CLI: `cli/ready_queue_cmd.rs`. Update the ordering string at :100 and the help/header text at :125. The row flags at :155 gain `starred` (and `red-main-fix`), and the `urgent` flag goes. `main.rs:196` doc comment. `dashboard.html:367` flag. `types/ready_queue.rs:7` module doc.
- In-repo Phase-2 dashboard: `dashboard/web/src/views/workQueue.ts:137` (urgent badge becomes a starred badge) and `dashboard/web/src/workQueue.ts:144` (ordering comment).

### 8. Tests and docs
- New unit tests: starred in a priority-100 repo beats unstarred in a priority-0 repo; two starred issues order by starred-at, not age; missing starred-at falls back to `createdAt`; existing ordering is unchanged when nothing is starred; `loom:urgent` no longer changes order; a starred `loom:triage` / `loom:curated` / unlabeled issue is dispatched; a starred issue carrying `loom:blocked` / `loom:operator-only` / `loom:operator-decision` / `loom:operator` is not; overflow admits exactly one starred sweep over both caps, refuses a second, refuses unstarred work, and still yields to the saturation brake, host-class and pool gates; a marker on a green repo gets no boost; a halted repo admits its fix and nothing else; a starred issue in a halted repo waits; with the gate disabled, CI status is the fallback; wire-shape snapshot tests (`observability/queue_snapshot_tests.rs`, `telemetry/tests.rs`, `observability/collector/tests.rs`) are updated.
- Incidental `loom:urgent` fixtures in Rust tests (`host_affinity.rs:274`, `merge_pr/labels/tests.rs:14,43`, `observability/queue_blocked_tests.rs:37`, `work_finder/tests.rs`, `work_finder/ready_queue_tests.rs`) switch to a neutral label where the test doesn't care about urgency.
- Docs: `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (ordering at :1928, plus overflow and red-main-fix lane), `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (:1117, row table :1149, :1169; add `operator_priority`, `operator_priority_at`, `managed_repos[].priority`; mark `urgent` always-false/deprecated). Keep `scripts/check-docs-defaults-parity.sh` green.

## File-size ratchet (read before coding)

`scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` freezes `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` (1580 code lines), `work_finder/tests.rs` (3455), `main.rs` (1228) and `safehouse.rs`. They may not grow. Put new logic in **new sibling modules**, e.g. `work_finder/operator_priority.rs` (key, starred-at cache, overflow decision) and `work_finder/main_red_fix.rs`, leaving only small call sites in `work_finder.rs`, and put new tests in new sibling test files. Check `scripts/check-file-size-budget.sh` locally (no cargo needed). **Never run cargo on the Mac** (use the remote build box).

## Out of scope
- **B (roles and `loom:urgent` retirement):** every role prompt, `defaults/` prompt/doc mirrors, Guide's top-3 duty, `urgent-flip-guard.sh`, marking `loom:urgent` retired in `labels.yml`, and `.loom/docs/label-state-machine.md` / CLAUDE.md. A adds the new label; B edits the `loom:urgent` entry.
- **C (liveness contract and loom-ui intents):** landing state, `needs-operator` escalation, watchdog, blocker inheritance, `/ingest` ack `operator_priority_intents`, intent-comment starred-at source, replay check.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `loom:operator-priority` is in both `labels.yml` files (description ≤100 chars, `Applied by:` owner). `pr_latency::hold_labels` doesn't report it.
- [ ] `candidate_cmp` implements keys 1-6 above. `urgent` isn't a key. All ordering tests listed in §8 pass.
- [ ] The second ETag-cached listing makes starred `loom:triage` / `loom:curated` / unlabeled issues candidates, deduped against `loom:issue` rows. Skip/park/`loom:operator-decision` are never dispatched. Tested.
- [ ] Starred-at comes from the cached `labeled` timeline event (starred candidates only), falling back to `createdAt`. Tested with a fake source.
- [ ] Overflow: at most one over-limit sweep per host, starred only, in both tick paths. Safety gates are still honoured. `overflow: true` is visible in `list_sweeps` / `get_sweep_status` / `loom-daemon status`. Tested.
- [ ] Red-main fix: key 3 applies only on verified red (not gate-in-flight). A halted repo admits only marker issues in both tick paths. Gate-disabled falls back to CI. Tested.
- [ ] `queue.snapshot` rows carry `operator_priority` / `operator_priority_at`. `urgent` is always false. `managed_repos[].priority` ships. Wire-shape tests are updated.
- [ ] `loom-daemon ready-queue` ordering string, help text, `main.rs:196`, `dashboard.html` and `dashboard/web` reflect the new keys.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` and `telemetry-schema.md` are updated. `check-file-size-budget.sh` and `check-docs-defaults-parity.sh` pass.

issues.title: observability: scheduled transcript archive + local sink (G2 part 1 of #8714)
issues.body:
## Context

Sub-issue of #8714 (slice 3 of 5, "G2 scheduled archive + `local` sink"). Parent issue's own scoping — see #8714 for the full gap analysis. Explicitly independent of the other slices: no egress, no operator decision needed (unlike the sibling `s3`/R2 sink sub-issue, which is gated on D1/D2).

## Problem

Raw transcript archives stay in `~/.loom/transcript-archives` (`activity/transcript_archive.rs`, landed #8494) — but nothing schedules the archive pass. It is opt-in CLI only, with no config block and no scheduler. Claude Code deletes the transcript source at 30 days, so an unscheduled archive pass means archives are only created if someone remembers to run the command by hand before that window closes.

## Proposal

A `transcriptArchive` config block: `enabled`, `intervalSecs`, `minAgeHours`, `archiveDir`, `sinks: [...]` — so the daemon runs the existing archive pass on a schedule. This sub-issue covers the scheduler and the `local` sink only (the archive already lands locally today; this wires it to run unattended and ledgers the result).

Ledger the archive per `(archive, sink)` in `transcript_archive` so a re-run is idempotent — re-running after a partial failure does not re-archive what already succeeded.

The `s3`/R2 remote sink is deliberately **out of scope** for this sub-issue (sibling sub-issue, gated on operator decisions D1/D2 in the parent issue). This sub-issue's `sinks` list has exactly one member, `local`, at completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `transcriptArchive` config block exists (`enabled`, `intervalSecs`, `minAgeHours`, `archiveDir`, `sinks`), and when `enabled: true`, the daemon runs the existing archive pass on the configured interval without manual CLI invocation.
- [ ] `minAgeHours` is honored — a transcript younger than the threshold is not archived on a given pass.
- [ ] Archive results are ledgered per `(archive, sink)`; re-running the scheduled pass after a partial failure does not re-archive an already-successfully-archived transcript.
- [ ] With only `local` configured in `sinks`, behavior matches today's opt-in CLI archive pass (per #8494), just scheduled instead of manual.
- [ ] No egress occurs from this sub-issue's scope — confirmed by the absence of any network call in the `local`-only code path.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/activity/transcript_archive.rs` — existing archive pass (landed #8494, opt-in CLI only); add the scheduler and config-driven invocation
- Config schema (exact location TBD — wherever other scheduled-task config blocks like `autonomous.*` are declared) — add `transcriptArchive`
- `loom-daemon/src/main.rs` or the daemon's task-scheduling loop (exact location TBD — grep for how other interval-driven background passes, e.g. transcript-ingest's 15-minute cadence, are scheduled) — wire in the new scheduled pass

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: with `transcriptArchive.enabled: true` and a short `intervalSecs`, confirm the archive pass runs without manual invocation
- [ ] Automated tests: `minAgeHours` correctly excludes a transcript younger than the threshold
- [ ] Automated tests: idempotency — re-running after a simulated partial failure does not re-archive a transcript already ledgered as archived to `local`
- [ ] Manual verification: enable the config block on a host with existing transcripts, confirm archives appear in `archiveDir` on schedule with no manual CLI step

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `complex`**: this wires an existing, already-tested archive pass to a scheduler and a config block — no new egress, no new decision, no new external dependency. The idempotency ledger is the one subtlety, but it is a bounded, testable mechanism, not a judgment call.

## Related

- Parent: #8714 (observability multi-sink export)
- Sibling sub-issue: G2 `s3`/R2 sink (deliberately out of scope here; gated on operator decisions D1/D2)
- #8494 (existing archive pass, landed, reused not rebuilt)

issues.title: Extend dispatch_scoped_tail to poll_and_classify_spawned_child's preflight-death check (dispatch.rs)
issues.body:
## Context

#8716 / PR #8747 added \`crash_signals::dispatch_scoped_tail\` and wired it into the four call sites the reported incident (#8675/#8676) actually hit: \`reaper.rs\`'s checkpoint and checkpoint-less \`Crashed\` branches, and \`quarantine.rs\`'s \`insta_crash_is_account_exhaustion\` / \`record_preflight_streak\`.

A fifth, structurally identical call site was left on the un-scoped \`tail_lines\`: \`dispatch.rs\`'s \`poll_and_classify_spawned_child\` (around line 3473) reads \`tail_lines(log_path, EXHAUSTION_LOG_TAIL_LINES)\` and feeds the joined tail straight into \`classify_preflight_death\` — the exact "tail of a reused per-issue log, then classify" pattern the fix addresses everywhere else.

## Why this is lower priority, not a correctness bug today

\`classify_preflight_death\` already does its own internal \`rfind(DISPATCH_HEADER_MARKER)\` rescoping, so as long as the CURRENT dispatch's header falls within the last \`EXHAUSTION_LOG_TAIL_LINES\` lines of the whole file — true in practice here, since this call fires immediately after spawn, when the header was just written and the current dispatch's own log region is necessarily short — the existing rescoping already recovers the correct region. The narrow gap \`dispatch_scoped_tail\` closes (the N-line bound applied BEFORE header-scoping, so it can straddle two dispatches when the current region is long) is much harder to hit here than at the reaper/quarantine sites, where a hung or long-running dispatch is exactly the case that matters.

## Suggested fix

Swap \`tail_lines(log_path, EXHAUSTION_LOG_TAIL_LINES).ok().map(|lines| lines.join(\"\\n\"))\` for \`dispatch_scoped_tail(log_path, EXHAUSTION_LOG_TAIL_LINES).ok()\` in \`poll_and_classify_spawned_child\`, for consistency with the other four sites and defense-in-depth against the same log-reuse hazard, plus one regression test mirroring the existing \`crash_signals_dispatch_scope_tests.rs\` fixtures.

Non-blocking — filed during Judge review of PR #8747 per the "Issues Are Suggestions" follow-up convention.

issues.title: fleet-config: enforce fleet/state.yml (running / paused / stopped) at daemon start
issues.body:
Follow-up to the `loom-daemon fleet-config` PR (branch `feature/fleet-config`), whose `fleet-config state` only **reports** a host's desired run state from the store's `fleet/state.yml` (`running` / `paused` / `stopped`; a `hosts.<h>` entry overrides the `fleet:` default).

## Problem
Nothing enforces it. An operator who sets `stopped` still has to stop each host by hand, and a host that reboots or is restarted by a watchdog comes back dispatching regardless of what the store says.

## Proposal
When `fleet.repo` is set, at daemon start (and on the sync timer from the sync-at-start follow-up):
- `stopped`: refuse to start (clear exit reason; the watchdog must treat it as intended, not a crash) or, if already running, drain and exit.
- `paused`: stay up, admit no new dispatch or role ticks; in-flight work finishes. Reuse the existing drain / dispatch-pause machinery rather than a new flag.
- `running`: normal.

Safety: an unreachable forge at startup uses the last good snapshot's state (with the staleness warning), never defaults to `running` if the last known state was `stopped`. Unset `fleet.repo` is unchanged.

## Acceptance
- Each state is observable on a live host (`status` shows desired vs actual).
- Tests with an injected transport and fixture state files, including the unreachable-forge case.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-30, verified against `origin/main` @ `aa20fc045`)

**Rightsizing verdict (consolidation gate)**: kept separate from #9596 / #9597 / #9599 — a real feature slice with its own risk surface (refuse-to-start and drain semantics are safety-relevant). **Sequencing**: consumes #9596's startup sync + timer for the state read; reuses the existing drain / dispatch-pause machinery rather than adding a flag.

- **Affected Files (verified present on `origin/main` @ `aa20fc045`)**: `loom-daemon/src/cli/fleet_config.rs`; drain reuse sites live in the daemon's drain/pause path (not traced to specific lines — Builder confirms).
- **Points**: 3.

issues.title: test: premise-false interaction suite's gh stub predates #9548's REST trusted-comments path — 0/8 on main
issues.body:
## Observed

`Native Port Suites` → `classify-dependency-block premise-false interaction (#7904)` is red on `main` (0/8, every invocation of `classify-dependency-block.sh` exits **2** with empty stdout). Reproduced on the #9648 head and on main's own post-merge run (36675353986); a rerun reproduced it, so it is not flake. First pass locally at d10fbd59f (pre-#9548): 8/8 green.

**Main has been red on this suite since #9612 (#9548) merged.** The check is informational (non-required), so Champion merges rode over it — but the premise-false defer contract (a `[premise-false]` bullet must not disqualify an otherwise-deferrable set; premise-false-only falls to the close gate; mixed sets still escalate) currently has **zero passing coverage**.

## Root cause (diagnosed, not guessed)

#9548 (4094fb9f4, "route the High-severity Rust marker readers through comment trust") rewired `dep_classify::forge::read_issue_in`: when the requested fields include `comments`, they now come from `comment_trust::records::fetch_trusted_comments`, which invokes:

```
gh api repos/{repo}/issues/{N}/comments --paginate
```

The premise-false suite's `gh` stub (`test-classify-dependency-block-premise-false.sh`) handles only `issue view` / `pr view` and exits 3 on any other subcommand ("stub gh: unhandled args"). `run_gh` fails → the listing is "could not read" → the stub script's `LOOM_SCRIPT_HELPER_MISSING_RC=2` path → exit 2, empty stdout. The suite's `run_cdb` captures stderr to `$STUB_DIR/stderr.log` and never prints it, which is why CI shows blank actuals.

The sibling `classify-dependency-block (#5664)` suite passes 207/207 on the same runner and binary because its scenarios never read comments.

## Fix shape

1. Extend the suite's `gh` stub with an `api` case serving `repos/{repo}/issues/{N}/comments` from the existing `issue_fixture` comment data, reshaped to REST comment objects carrying a **trusted** author (`user.login` = the workspace roster's writer App slug with `[bot]`, `type: "Bot"` — the fleet's own writer is the one identity every `TrustPolicy` believes; see `comment_trust`'s `TEST_FLEET_AUTHOR` doc). `--paginate` must be tolerated in arg parsing.
2. Reproduce locally **against a fresh origin/main daemon build** before pushing — the pre-#9548 local checkout passes for the wrong reason (its `read_issue_in` still reads comments via `gh issue view`, which the stub serves).
3. While in there: consider making `run_cdb` echo `stderr.log` on an unexpected exit 2, so the next regression of this shape is diagnosable from CI output alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The suite is 8/8 against a post-#9548 daemon build (locally reproduced, not assumed).
- [ ] The stub's `api` case serves the trust-filtered fixture comments; no private or live-forge data introduced (hermetic suite stays hermetic).
- [ ] Native Port Suites goes green on the PR.

## Curation

Scope is exactly the fix shape above: one hermetic test file (stub `api` case + fixture authorship + the `run_cdb` stderr echo), verified against a freshly built origin/main daemon. The daemon's trust path itself is correct per #9548's security rationale — only the fixture is stale; do not touch `comment_trust`. Routed `routine`: the approach is fully specified and mistakes surface in the suite itself; the acceptance criterion forces a real reproduction, so a false-green cannot ship. Sized per the rubric: ~30 lines, 1 file → 1.

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

issues.title: drain: an operator drain that times out must stay paused, not silently resume dispatch
issues.body:
## Problem

When a drain times out without `--force-after-timeout`, the daemon **resumes dispatch** and stays up. The log line reads: `drain timed out with N sweep(s) still in flight — refused restart (no --force-after-timeout); dispatch resumed, daemon stays up`.

That is the right default for an auto-update roll, where resuming work beats sitting idle. It is the wrong outcome when an operator is draining the fleet to **stop** it. On 2026-09-30 the operator paused a whole fleet to clear a PR backlog. On one launchd host and one systemd worker the drain timed out, dispatch silently resumed, and both hosts went back to re-dispatching issues and starting new sweeps. Nobody noticed until a peer check found a live daemon on a host that was believed stopped.

## Proposal

Make the post-timeout behaviour depend on why the drain was started, and make it visible:

- **Operator-initiated drain** (`restart --drain --then-exit`, `fleet drain`, any drain whose intent is "stop"): on timeout, stay **paused**. Keep dispatch off and keep in-flight work running. Emit a loud `daemon.drain.timeout` event and a status field, and wait for an explicit `--force` or `--abort-drain`. Never resume dispatch without being asked.
- **Auto-update roll drain:** keep today's behaviour, but label it clearly in status and the log as "roll deferred; dispatch resumed".
- In both cases, `loom-daemon status` should show whether dispatch is paused, and why.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A timed-out operator drain leaves dispatch paused, and status and the event bus say so.
- [ ] Dispatch resumes only through an explicit operator action (`--abort-drain` / `restart --abort-drain`) or a completed drain.
- [ ] Auto-update roll drains keep their current resume-on-timeout behaviour, now clearly labelled.
- [ ] Tests cover both paths.

---

## Curator: technical detail and acceptance criteria (2026-09-30)

Scope folds in the watchdog-resurrection failure from the comment below and the escalation no-op seen in the same fleet stop (2AMLogic/2am#1687).

### Code map (current `main`)
- `loom-daemon/src/ipc.rs`: `DrainState::begin` pins `force_after_timeout` on the already-draining path unless `roll_pending` (#6007). A second `restart --drain --force-after-timeout` against a first-attempt drain is therefore a silent no-op ("existing deadline is unchanged").
- `run_drain_supervisor`, `DrainTick::TimedOutRefuse`: a **then-exit** drain calls `resolve_timeout`, which clears the pause flag ("dispatch resumed"). A **relaunch** drain retains a pending roll, but `refuse_roll_deadline` abandons it and resumes dispatch once `drain_pending_budget` is spent. Both paths apply the same way to an operator `restart --drain` and to the auto-update roll (`auto_update/drain_trigger.rs`), because the drain has no record of who started it.
- `autonomy-desired` marker: only `loom-daemon-stop.sh` removes it. A then-exit drain leaves it in place, so the watchdog (`watchdog/mod.rs::tick` -> `marker_present` -> outage/recovery) revives the daemon. Startup healing (`autonomy_marker::heal_on_startup`) would also re-create an absent marker on any supervised relaunch.
- `ipc.rs`, `fleet/drain.rs`, `daemon_service.rs`, `main.rs` and `types.rs` are frozen by the file-size ratchet. New logic goes in sibling modules.

### Acceptance criteria
1. **The drain records its origin.** `handle_drain_request` takes an origin: `Operator` for every IPC `DrainAndRestartDaemon` (CLI `restart --drain`, `loom-daemon-update.sh --drain`, `fleet drain`), and `AutoUpdate` for `auto_update/drain_trigger.rs`. An operator request against an in-progress auto-update drain promotes it one-way to `Operator`. The reverse never happens.
2. **An operator drain that times out stays paused.** If an `Operator` drain passes its deadline without force, whether it is then-exit or relaunch:
   - dispatch stays paused and the drain stays active;
   - the deadline is cleared and a `timed_out` state is recorded;
   - the note and a `daemon.drain.timeout` event (`paused: true`) list the stragglers by sweep id and issue;
   - the supervisor keeps polling, so the terminal action (stay down, or relaunch) still fires when in-flight reaches 0.

   Dispatch never resumes on its own. Only `--abort-drain` or a completed drain ends the pause.
3. **The auto-update roll keeps its current timeout behaviour, on purpose.** It keeps the #6007 pending-roll re-arm and budget, then abandons the roll and resumes dispatch. A version roll must not starve a host of work forever. The abandon note and the log line say "roll deferred/abandoned; dispatch resumed (auto-update roll)" so the reader can tell it apart from an operator drain.
4. **A later request escalates an in-progress drain.** It no longer no-ops:
   - `--force-after-timeout` escalates any active drain, not only a pending roll. If the drain is already timed out or pending, the deadline moves to now. Otherwise it becomes `min(existing, now + requested timeout)`, so it can move earlier but never later.
   - `--then-exit` keeps its #4521 one-way escalation, including on a timed-out paused drain.
   - The ack says ESCALATED.
5. **A durable operator-stop record.** When a then-exit drain is accepted or escalated, `<marker>.stopped` is written (with `stopped_at`, `reason`, `pid`) and the `autonomy-desired` marker is moved aside into it. The following honour it:
   - the watchdog tick: `.stopped` present -> report OK "operator stop recorded", no recovery, exit 0, even if a stale `autonomy-desired` also exists;
   - startup healing: no re-heal while `.stopped` is present;
   - daemon startup: a supervised relaunch such as launchd `RunAtLoad` or `kickstart` comes up with dispatch **held**, a note says why, and `--abort-drain` releases it.
6. **Clearing the stop record.** `restart --abort-drain` removes `.stopped` and restores the moved-aside `autonomy-desired`. An explicit start (`loom-daemon-start.sh` / `loom-daemon daemon-start`) clears `.stopped` before it launches.
7. **Status.** `loom-daemon status` (human and `--json` `drain` object) shows whether dispatch is paused and why: `origin`, `timed_out`. `fleet drain` maps a remote `timed_out: true` payload to its documented exit-2 "timed out" contract instead of waiting out its own deadline.
8. **Tests.** Unit tests cover:
   - an operator timeout holding (then-exit and relaunch);
   - an auto-update timeout keeping pending, then abandoning;
   - force escalation of a first-attempt drain and of a timed-out drain;
   - origin promotion;
   - stop-marker write, restore and clear;
   - watchdog tick exit 0 without recovery while `.stopped` is present (exercised in the watchdog shell suite under Native Port Suites);
   - heal skip;
   - `fleet drain` classifying `timed_out`.

issues.title: quarantine: escalate relapsed quarantines — probation + doubling TTL (rebuild of #8440, scope-limited)
issues.body:
Rebuild of the fix from PR #8440, which was closed (operator decision 2026-09-30) because its branch carried ~700 lines of out-of-scope quarantine-refactor code (turian's contamination hold). **Rebuild ONLY the two changes below, from current `main`**: no refactor of the quarantine module beyond what they need.

## Problem (vibesql#6639)

The insta-crash quarantine (#3939) flapped forever on a persistent breakage: **3 crashes → 1h TTL → release with a fresh 3-strike runway → 3 more crashes → repeat**. Observed 8+ cycles across vibesql #6170/#6172/#6174, each cycle costing three wasted `--claim-owned` dispatches. (The original trigger — cargo hangs on a wedged external volume — is long since recovered; this PR fixes the structural loop that let it cycle.)

## Fix — two changes, both scoped to the relapse path

**1. Probation.** A quarantine's *generation marker* survives its TTL release; only a healthy outcome (checkpoint/clean exit) or an operator `quarantine clear` removes it. While the marker exists, the **first** further insta-crash re-quarantines immediately (effective threshold 1). A relapse after a release is presumptive evidence the breakage persisted through the pause — the old behavior made it cost three more dispatches per cycle.

**2. Escalation.** Generation N serves `ttl × 2^(N−1)`, capped at the new `ttlMaxSecs` (default 24h, clamped up to `ttl`). The flap decays to at-most-daily retries instead of cycling every hour forever.

Transient breakages keep the exact old behavior: quarantine → TTL → one healthy run → ladder fully reset. Generation state is in-memory like the quarantine itself — a daemon restart resets the ladder (documented in code).

## Surfaces

- `loom-daemon quarantine list`: entries carry `generation`; `ttl_remaining_secs` reports against the **escalated** TTL
- The quarantine forge comment explains the escalation on generation ≥ 2 (the comment trail is what #6639's observers actually read)
- Config table row added to `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (`env > config > default`, per the module's convention)

## Tests (all green)

New: relapse-requarantines-on-first-crash (drives the real death-classification path, not just the tally API) · escalation math incl. cap and misconfigured-ceiling clamp · `quarantine_entries` escalated-TTL surface · healthy-outcome reset · operator-clear reset.

Modules: **sweep_registry 613/613** · health 213/213 · ipc 122/122 · reaper 76/76 · quarantine 52/52 · work_finder::tests 220/220. (The known environmental `registry_refresh` hot-apply failure is unchanged and pre-existing on base.)

Fixes vibesql#6639 (cross-repo — close the vibesql issue manually after this merges and deploys).

## Scope guard (from the operator decision)

- The diff must be limited to the relapse path: the generation marker/probation, TTL escalation with `ttlMaxSecs`, the `quarantine list` surface fields, the forge-comment wording, and the config doc row. Any unrelated restructuring of the quarantine or sweep-registry code is out of scope. Judge should check the diff size against this list.
- Cross-repo: after merge and deploy, close vibesql#6639 manually.

issues.title: ci-telemetry captain gate: the poller silently stops on any host with no fleet.captain, and a handoff leaves a stale arm (#9002 blocking findings, merged unaddressed)
issues.body:
## Problem

PR #9002 (for #8901) merged at 2026-09-26T04:18Z with two blocking findings from an independent Judge review still unaddressed: https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/pull/9002#issuecomment-5843121796. A `loom:operator` hold was added at 04:22Z, but the PR had already merged, so the hold had no effect.

### 1. The CI-telemetry poller silently stops on any host with no `fleet.captain` (blocking)

The captain gate (`fleet_captain::arm_singleton_job("ci-telemetry-poll", …)`) refuses on **any** host that has no `fleet.captain` declared, single-host setups included. The PR's migration note says only multi-host fleets are affected, which is wrong. No committed config declares a captain, and the Rollout section of `ci-observability.md` ("pick one fleet host") never mentions one. So following the documented rollout, or upgrading an existing opted-in host, captures zero CI data.

The refusal is visible in only one place, a per-tick WARN in the daemon log:
- `ci-telemetry status` reads `stale` / `never-polled` and gives no reason.
- Nothing appears in `host.health` / `loom-daemon health`.
- The dashboard "no captain reporting" flag only fires once *some* host has a captain.
- SigNoz simply stops receiving CI runs, jobs and logs.

Meanwhile duplicate polling, the thing the gate prevents, is harmless apart from API budget, because records are deduplicated.

### 2. A captain handoff leaves a false "armed on a non-captain host" alarm for up to 6h

When the command-path arm is refused, its saved shell-arm record is never cleared. After `fleet.captain` moves from host A to host B, A keeps reporting the job as armed until the 6h expiry, and the dashboard flag fires the whole time. #8901 warned about exactly this. The in-daemon path already clears within one tick.

## Fix

- [ ] Record the refusal so `ci-telemetry status` shows it as its own state (e.g. `refused: no fleet.captain declared`), and surface it in `host.health` / `loom-daemon health`. **Or** let `ci-telemetry-poll` run when no captain is declared, documented as an explicit exception.
- [ ] Correct the migration note, the module doc, and the `ci-observability.md` Rollout steps so they say a captain is required (or describe the exception).
- [ ] Clear the saved arm record when the arm is refused, with a regression test for the handoff case.
- [ ] Non-blocking: take a lock around the saved arm-record file update (concurrent arms on one host can lose an entry until the next tick).

## Current exposure

Low today. On the operator Mac `autonomous.ciTelemetry.enabled=false`, so nothing is lost yet. This must land before any host enables the daemon CI poller, or CI data will silently fail to reach SigNoz.

Related: #8901, #9002, #8848, harness-ops #193 (the separate CI poller).

issues.title: ci-telemetry: step spans, per-job queue wait, and shard/suite/test spans so CI sharding is observable in SigNoz
issues.body:
## Problem

#9069 split CI's long poles across runners: nextest `--partition count:k/N` legs, 2-way Shell Test Suites shards via `LOOM_CI_SHARD`, and a shared `build-daemon` artifact that other jobs wait on. Tuning that layout needs data we don't capture today.

`loom-daemon ci-telemetry` (`ci-observability.md`) already emits **one trace per run and one span per job**, plus run-level `queued_ms` (#9007). So each shard does show up as a job span. What's missing:

1. **Per-job queue wait.** Only the run has `queued_ms`. On 2026-09-26, per-job waits for a runner (`started_at − created_at`) reached p90 212s and a max of 1,064s during a burst, while the median stayed at 6s. That is the account's concurrent-job cap binding, and it is invisible in SigNoz today. It was measured by hand from the REST API.
2. **Step spans.** A job span can't say whether a Rust leg's ~250s went to compiling (~90–110s) or to running tests. Every CI tuning decision on #9065 needed step timings, and they were pulled by hand from the jobs API.
3. **Shard attributes.** Matrix legs are only distinguishable by display name. A leg needs structured attributes so SigNoz can group and compare legs, and spot imbalance:
   - `ci.shard.index` and `ci.shard.total` (from `strategy.job-index` / `job-total`)
   - `ci.shard.kind`: `nextest-partition`, `shell-suite-shard`, or `none`
4. **What made a shard slow.** Inside a leg, there are no per-suite or per-test durations:
   - `run-ci-suites.sh` already prints every suite's duration.
   - nextest can emit JUnit XML (`[profile.ci.junit]`) with every test's duration.

   Without these, rebalancing shards is guesswork. For example, the same Unit partition's test step has ranged from 50s to 139s between runs.
5. **Dependency wait.** Jobs that `needs: build-daemon` should show the time they spent waiting on it, separately from time spent queueing for a runner.

## Proposal (each step independently useful)

1. **Job queue time and shard attributes** on the existing `ci.job` record and span: `queued_ms = started_at − created_at` per job, plus the shard attributes above. For shard attributes, either parse the display-name pattern `(k/N)` or, more robustly, have the job write a small JSON annotation or artifact. Also add a standing query: p50/p90 job queue wait over time, alerting when p90 exceeds 60s.
2. **Step spans** as children of each job span, from the jobs API's `steps[]`, which carries name, status, and started and completed times. That costs no extra API calls, since the poller already fetches jobs.
3. **Suite and test spans from artifacts:**
   - Enable nextest JUnit output in `.config/nextest.toml`'s `ci` profile and upload it.
   - Have `run-ci-suites.sh` write its per-suite timings as JSON next to the retry log it already uploads (#7791).
   - The poller turns both into child spans of the shard's job span.

   This is also the data #7789's flake tracking wants.
4. **Saved SigNoz views:**
   - critical path per run (longest job, including queue);
   - shard balance (spread of legs within one run);
   - top 20 slowest tests and suites over 7 days.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `ci.job` record and span carries `queued_ms`, plus shard attributes for matrix legs.
- [ ] Step spans appear under job spans in SigNoz for a CI run on `main` (verify live, per #8913's convention — "healthy daemon" ≠ data in SigNoz).
- [ ] At least one sharded job (Rust Unit Tests or Shell Test Suites) shows per-test or per-suite child spans.
- [ ] Standing queries for job queue-wait percentiles and shard imbalance are added to `ci-queries.sql`.
- [ ] `ci-observability.md` documents the new attributes and spans.

## Context

- #9065 (CI wall time) and #9069 (sharding and build-once): the layout this measures.
- #9007: run-level `queued_ms`. This issue extends it to jobs.
- #7789 / #7791: flake tracking. Per-suite and per-test spans feed it.
- #8913: live verification of ingest in SigNoz.

issues.title: test(watchdog): start_confirmed_down()'s `wait` is a no-op — dead-pid fixture races the watchdog's kill -0, flaking case 46
issues.body:
## Summary

`start_confirmed_down()` in `defaults/scripts/tests/test-loom-daemon-watchdog.sh`
has no barrier guaranteeing the "dead" pid it plants in the pid file is actually
gone by the time the watchdog reads it. When the pid is still reapable, the
watchdog correctly concludes the daemon is **alive**, skips recovery, never trips
the breaker and never escalates — so every assertion in that case inverts.

Observed live on PR #9261, run 36435114396 job 108972088942 (case 46):

```
✗ #6272 branch-3 skipped when repo-scoped exists: the breaker-trip tick still exits 1 (expected rc=1, got rc=0)
✗ #6272 branch-3 skipped when repo-scoped exists: expected the repo-scoped stub to be called exactly once ()
```

A re-run of the **identical** head (129bb5b0, no code change) came back
`178 passed, 0 failed`. Case 48 — structurally identical to case 46, same
fixture, same env, ~300 ms later in the same process — passed in the *failing*
run. Both facts say nondeterminism, not a code defect.

## Mechanism

```bash
sleeper() { sleep 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $!; }
...
dead=$(sleeper); bg_proc_track "$dead"; kill "$dead" 2>/dev/null; wait "$dead" 2>/dev/null
```

`sleeper` is invoked in a **command substitution**, so `sleep 60 &` is a child of
the substitution subshell — a *grandchild* of the suite shell. `wait "$dead"` in
the suite shell therefore never waits:

```
bash: wait: pid 94047 is not a child of this shell
wait rc=127
kill -0 "$dead"  -> SUCCEEDS
```

(`2>/dev/null` hides the diagnostic, so the fixture looks synchronized.) The
`kill` is asynchronous and the orphan's reaping is up to pid 1, so the pid can
still answer `kill -0` when the watchdog asks.

The watchdog's Linux path treats the pid file as the sole signal
(`loom-daemon/src/daemon_install_state.rs`, `check_liveness_with_systemd`):

```rust
Some(pid) if pid_alive(pid) => Liveness::plain(true, ...)
```

and `pid_alive` is a `kill -0 <pid>` subprocess. One `true` there turns the
snapshot into `AliveButUnresponsive` instead of `ExpectedButDead`, which is
exactly rc=0 + empty `create-issue.sh` log + untouched poison log.

## Why it is rare but real

`start_confirmed_down` is called by ~20 cases; only the ones whose orphan is
slow to be reaped flip. The window widens under CI load, which is why this
surfaced on a busy runner and not locally.

## Fix direction

Give the fixture a real barrier instead of a no-op `wait` — e.g. start the
sleeper without a command substitution so it *is* a child (`sleep 60 & dead=$!`),
then `kill` + `wait` for real, and additionally poll `kill -0` until it fails
before writing the pid file. Do not paper over it by relaxing the assertions:
the cases are proving the #6272 create-issue.sh resolution order, and a case that
silently no-ops because the daemon looked healthy proves nothing.

Also worth considering: make the no-op `wait` loud rather than silent (drop the
`2>/dev/null`, or assert the pid is gone) so the next instance of this shape is
caught at write time.

## Provenance

Found while treating PR #9261 (`loom:changes-requested` dispatch via
`/loom:sweep`). Not fixed there deliberately: #9261 touches zero shell files and
is first in an operator-sequenced merge train, so a watchdog-fixture change would
be out-of-scope and force a re-review.

issues.title: Managed CLAUDE.md block: describe the session-mode PR workflow (Doctor → Judge → merge-pr.sh)
issues.body:
## Problem

The `<!-- BEGIN/END LOOM ORCHESTRATION -->` block that Loom writes into a
target repo's CLAUDE.md is a single paragraph pointing at the Loom repo. In a
repo run in session mode (roles invoked by an attended operator, no daemon or
interval terminals), a session agent has no local cue for the label workflow
it should follow. It may review PRs without applying verdict labels, merge
directly instead of using the repo's merge script, or never sync the labels.

Downstream repos can't add this inside the managed block, because the next
`install`/update overwrites it. Each repo ends up copying the same text into
its own section.

## Request

Have the managed block include a short, generic description of the PR label
workflow:

- Labels are created with `.loom/scripts/sync-labels.sh`. A Quick install
  ships `.github/labels.yml` but does not create the labels.
- **Doctor** (`/loom:doctor`) fixes PRs labelled `loom:changes-requested`,
  then returns them to `loom:review-requested`.
- **Judge** (`/loom:judge`) reviews `loom:review-requested` PRs and applies
  `loom:pr` or `loom:changes-requested`.
- Merge only `loom:pr` PRs, with `.loom/scripts/merge-pr.sh <pr>` rather than
  a raw forge merge command.
- Daemon mode (`loom.sh`, interval terminals) is optional. The same roles can
  be run by hand in a session.

Optionally, add an install-time flag or config key (e.g. `mode: session`) that:

- writes `"terminals": []` in `.loom/config.json`,
- leaves out the stock issue templates' external contact links,
- makes `loom.sh` refuse to start.

That way a repo that must never run unattended agents doesn't need a local
patch that later updates undo.

## Scope (Curator, 2026-09-25)

This issue now covers only the **required** ask above: extending
`LOOM_ROOT_POINTER`/`AGENTS_ROOT_POINTER` (`loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding.rs`)
with the short label-workflow paragraph. The **optional** install-time
`mode: session` flag (`terminals: []` + a `loom.sh` start refusal) is split
out to #8884. The issue-template contact-link bullet is dropped entirely —
see #8862, which covers it for every install, not just session-mode ones.
Full rationale in the enhancement comment below.

issues.title: test-loom-dispatcher.sh: LOOM_RUNTIME=codex sweep subtests fail locally (worktreeIsolation capability admission / missing role manifest fixture)
issues.body:
## Problem

Running `bash defaults/scripts/tests/test-loom-dispatcher.sh` locally on `main` (verified at both `b7f410c68` and `4899164bc`) reports:

```
test-loom-dispatcher.sh: 94/99 passed, 5 failed
```

All 5 failures are in Test 20 and Test 21 (the `LOOM_RUNTIME=codex loom sweep` cases):

- Test 20: `'LOOM_RUNTIME=codex loom sweep' exits 0` — got exit 78 instead. The runtime-admission layer refuses with `unmet capability: worktreeIsolation` before ever reaching the stubbed `spawn-codex.sh`, so the test's `STUB_CODEX`/passthrough-args assertions never get a chance to match.
- Test 21: `'loom sweep' with runtimes.default=codex (no env) exits 0` — same exit-78 refusal, this time additionally reporting `role manifest /tmp/.../defaults/roles/builder.json: No such file or directory` — the test's temp fixture directory doesn't fully mirror the real repo layout the admission check now expects.

## Scope note

Confirmed **pre-existing and unrelated** to PR #8854 / issue #8839 (the private-session control-boundary work) — reproduced identically on the commit immediately before that PR merged, and #8854 never touches `runtime_admission.rs`, `defaults/runtimes/codex.json`, or this test file. Found incidentally while running this repo's own `buildGate.command` (`.loom/scripts/build-gate.sh`) as the post-merge integration check for that sweep.

Not confirmed whether this also fails in the GitHub Actions CI environment (PR #8854's CI run was fully green across all 38 jobs) — possible the CI job either doesn't run this specific test path, sandboxes something this bare local run doesn't, or the local host environment (this is a shared dispatch worker, not CI) differs in a way that trips the `worktreeIsolation` capability check or the role-manifest fixture path resolution.

## Suggested next step (not prescriptive)

- Determine whether CI actually exercises Test 20/21 and passes, or whether this is silently red in CI too.
- If admission logic in `runtime_admission.rs` changed capability requirements for `codex` sweeps since this test was last updated (`d2ee6a8ef`, #8441), the test's Codex-runtime fixtures may need a `worktreeIsolation`-satisfying stub, or the test needs an explicit skip/xfail with a tracking note.
