issues.title: feat(dispatch): enforce strict host-class routing to prevent heavy sweeps on developer laptops
issues.body:
## Original Issue

### Problem Statement
Developers frequently observe local laptop hosts (e.g. `MacBook-Air.localdomain`) executing heavy autonomous builder sweeps and role attempts, disregarding instructions to offload to dedicated AWS/Hetzner remote workers. This leads to extreme local load (14+ load/core, 31+ GB swap thrashing) and trips admission brakes.

### Proposed Solution
Implement explicit host-class routing tags and a dashboard allocation panel to track and restrict sweep execution by host tier.

### Key Requirements
1. **Host-Class Routing Tags in Daemon Config:**
   - Allow tagging daemon instances (e.g. `host_class: "local-dev"` vs `host_class: "remote-worker"`).
   - In `work_finder`, gate heavy builder sweeps (`tier:goal-advancing`, heavy simulation/EDA) to `remote-worker` hosts only.
   - Restrict `local-dev` hosts to lightweight roles (Curator, triage, lint) or explicitly opted-in local sweeps.
2. **Dashboard Host Allocation Panel (`/dashboard/hosts`):**
   - Live breakdown showing active sweep distribution across hosts (AWS instances vs local laptops).
   - Alerting on unauthorized heavy sweep dispatch on developer laptops.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Daemon configuration supports `host_class: "local-dev" | "remote-worker"`.
- [ ] Heavy build sweeps refuse execution on `local-dev` machines unless `--allow-local` is explicitly passed.
- [ ] Dashboard displays host execution breakdown over time.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-27, verified against `main` @ `7e0a29b0d`)

### Problem Statement

The underlying complaint is real and consistent with prior art in this repo: `loom-daemon/src/admission_brake.rs`'s own module doc (lines 14-24) cites the *exact* incident this issue describes as its own motivating case — an 8-vCPU `loom-worker-1` observed at load-average 95 (12x overcommit, 0.07% CPU idle) from three in-flight `gf180-*` analog-simulation sweeps. The admission brake (#4903/#5270) is a **reactive, point-in-time** backstop: it holds *new* admissions once a host is *already* saturated. It does not — and structurally cannot — refuse a known-heavy sweep *before* it starts on a machine that was never meant to run it. This issue asks for the missing *preventive* half: let a host declare what class of machine it is, and refuse heavy dispatch on the wrong class before the sweep is even claimed.

### Grounding in current code (verified 2026-09-27 @ `7e0a29b0d`)

- **No `host_class` concept exists anywhere today.** `grep -rniE "host_class|hostClass|host.tier|remote-worker|allow_local"` across `loom-daemon/src` turns up only unrelated hits: the `host_tier` name in `loom-daemon/src/config_resolver.rs:630` (`test_resolve_effective_config_ignores_the_host_tier_with_the_override_unset`) refers to a *config-merge layer* (legacy vs. private-defaults tiers), not a machine classification; "laptop"/"remote_workers" hits are doc prose and the SSH fleet-status fanout's registry-vs-local split (`loom-daemon/src/fleet/status.rs:653-667`), unrelated to dispatch admission. This PR is filling a genuine gap, not duplicating an existing mechanism.
- **The closest existing mechanism is host-affinity (#7456, `loom-daemon/src/host_affinity.rs`), and it solves the opposite problem.** An *issue* pins itself to one *specific named host* via a `loom:host:<id>` label and/or a `<!-- loom:requires-host=<id> -->` body marker (open per-instance identity, any-of semantics). It's consulted via `WorkItem::host_constraint()` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs:406-407`) at the top of both tick loops — single-workspace `tick_with_saturation_brake` (`work_finder.rs:1192-1201`) and multi-workspace `tick_multi_with_saturation_brake`'s per-candidate loop (`work_finder.rs:1814-1822`) — and again client-side in `loom-daemon dispatch` (`loom-daemon/src/cli/dispatch.rs:99-206`), which refuses unless `--ignore-host-constraint` is passed. This issue needs the reverse shape — a *host* declares a *class*, and *any* candidate meeting a "heavy" test is refused on the wrong class — but the new gate should sit at the same two checkpoints and copy the same no-side-effect refusal contract (no claim flip, no comment, no cooldown/backoff record, since a `local-dev` host will never build this candidate without an operator action).
- **Per-repo concurrency cap / track affinity (#9090, PR #9125, commit `32eb57110`)** — `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/repo_cap.rs` — is the most recent precedent for exactly this shape of admission knob: `autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrentPerRepo` / `LOOM_WORK_FINDER_MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_REPO`, resolved **env > config > none** (absent = uncapped = zero behavior change; the module's own "Off by default" doc section explains why a non-`None` default would silently throttle every existing fleet on upgrade — the same reasoning this issue's `host_class` default must follow), re-read every tick via `ConfiguredMaxReloader` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/configured_max.rs`), and a capped candidate is *deferred, never dropped* via `QueueDisposition::DeferredRepoCap` / `TickReport::deferred_repo_cap`. The new module should mirror `repo_cap.rs`'s file shape and env/config resolution pattern directly.
- **Hot-reloaded `maxConcurrent` (#9060, PR #9066, commit `a71797baf`)** — `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/configured_max.rs` — established that `autonomous.workFinder.*` knobs can be re-read every multi-workspace tick without a daemon restart, while the env override stays restart-only (fixed at process launch) and, while set, shadows config with a one-time logged warning. **`host_class` should NOT follow this hot-reload pattern.** Unlike `maxConcurrent`, host_class is a daemon-*identity* fact (like `sweep_registry::host_identity()`) that does not change while a process runs — the closer precedent is `maxAdmissionsPerTick`'s deliberate startup-capture design (`resolve_max_admissions_per_tick_with_config`, `work_finder.rs:2328`, doc comment: "a startup-capture pattern `maxConcurrent` no longer shares... an operator retuning it takes effect on the next daemon restart"). Reclassifying a machine is a rare, deliberate operator action, so a restart requirement is acceptable and avoids adding this knob to the hot-reload path for no real benefit.
- **The load-based admission brake (#4903/#5270, `loom-daemon/src/admission_brake.rs`)** is reactive and point-in-time, keyed on measured `load_per_core` (default threshold `0.95`, `DEFAULT_ADMISSION_BRAKE_LOAD_PER_CORE`). It complements but does not replace this issue's ask — see Problem Statement above. `RoleTickResult::SkippedLoad` (`loom-daemon/src/observability/otlp/mapping.rs:108`, wire value `"skipped_load"`) is a related but separate reactive signal for role-runner ticks, not sweep dispatch, and is not reused here.
- **No mechanical "heavy" signal exists anywhere in the codebase today** (confirmed by the same grep pass — no repo/issue tag for "EDA", "simulation", or "resource-weight" of any kind). The only classification labels that exist are the priority tier set `tier:goal-advancing` / `tier:goal-supporting` / `tier:maintenance` (`.github/labels.yml:247-259`) — a **priority** axis, not a **resource-weight** axis. Note that #9034 itself carries `tier:goal-advancing` (applied by an operator's Chat-Ops priority bump, see the issue's own comment thread) — using that same label as the "heavy" signal, as the original issue's Key Requirements propose, would refuse ordinary prioritized work (a one-line config fix, a doc update) on every `local-dev` laptop the moment it is prioritized, which has no grounding in an actual resource-weight signal and is broader than what the reporter is describing. See "Rescoped Design" below for the label this PR introduces instead.
- **`/dashboard/hosts` does not exist.** The daemon has a general "fleet dashboard" (`loom-daemon serve`, opt-in/read-only, `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` §"Fleet dashboard") and a `fleet status` / `FleetStatusReport` (`loom-daemon/src/fleet/status.rs`) that already distinguishes the local host from `remote_workers` registered in `~/.loom/fleet.json` (lines 653-667) — but this is an SSH-registry-based concept unrelated to `host_class` or sweep-distribution-by-class. See "Out of Scope" below.

### Rescoped Design (single buildable PR)

1. **`host_class` config knob.** `autonomous.workFinder.hostClass` (string: `"local-dev"` | `"remote-worker"`; any other value, or the key absent, resolves to **unclassified**), env override `LOOM_HOST_CLASS`. Resolved **env > config > default**, mirroring every other `workFinder` knob's precedence. **Default: unclassified — the gate below never fires for an unclassified host.** This is the only default that produces zero behavior change for every existing install: no `.loom/config.json` in the fleet sets this key today, so nothing is refused anywhere until an operator explicitly marks a specific machine `local-dev`. (Do **not** default an unset host to `local-dev` — that would silently start refusing heavy sweeps on every unconfigured host in the fleet the moment this ships, including already-provisioned AWS/Hetzner boxes that haven't been given the new key yet — the same class of upgrade regression `maxConcurrentPerRepo`'s "absent = uncapped, not a number" design explicitly avoids, per `repo_cap.rs`'s "Off by default" section.)
   Resolve **once at daemon startup**, not hot-reloaded per tick (see grounding above re: `maxAdmissionsPerTick`'s precedent) — a restart to reclassify a machine is fine.

2. **The "heavy" signal: a new label, `loom:heavy`.** Since no mechanical heavy/resource-weight signal exists today (see grounding above), and `tier:goal-advancing` is the wrong axis to reuse (priority, not weight), this PR adds exactly one new, explicit, human/Architect/Curator-applied label: `loom:heavy` — "CPU/RAM-intensive build (e.g. sustained simulation/EDA); should not run on a `host_class: local-dev` machine without an explicit override." Add it to **both** `.github/labels.yml` and `defaults/.github/labels.yml` (byte-identical parity contract per #3896, CI-enforced by `defaults/scripts/check-labels-drift.sh`), inside the `BEGIN/END LOOM LABELS` block, near the `tier:*` labels (`.github/labels.yml:247-259`). Keep the description at/under GitHub's 100-char limit — `sync-labels.sh` fails a longer one with HTTP 422, the same constraint already called out next to `loom:operator-only` (`.github/labels.yml:157-160`).
   No issue carries this label today, so — combined with (1) — the gate is inert by construction until an operator opts BOTH a host and an issue in.

3. **The work-finder gate.** In `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs`, add a new step immediately after the existing host-affinity constraint check, at **both** places that check runs today:
   - `tick_with_saturation_brake` (single-workspace loop), right after the check at `work_finder.rs:1192-1201`.
   - `tick_multi_with_saturation_brake`'s per-candidate loop (multi-workspace), right after the mirrored check at `work_finder.rs:1814-1822`.
   Refuse — with **zero** side effects (no claim flip, no comment, no cooldown/backoff record; the candidate is not "in flight" in any actionable sense on this host) — exactly when **all** of: this host's resolved `host_class == local-dev`, the candidate carries `loom:heavy`, and neither override below is set. Log the same way the host-affinity check does (a single `log::info!` naming the issue, the host's class, and how to override) and add a matching `TickReport` / `WorkFinderTickSummary` counter (`skipped_host_class`, mirroring `skipped_host_constraint` at `loom-daemon/src/types.rs:1901`), folded into `WorkFinderTickSummary::reason_summary()` (`loom-daemon/src/types.rs:1949-1972`) as `"host-class-skip"`.

4. **New `QueueDisposition` variant** (`loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs`) — e.g. `HostClassRefused` — added to the `ALL` array (bump its doc comment's count past the current 22 — `ready_queue.rs:81-108`), `as_str()` (e.g. `"host_class_refused"`), and `reason()` (e.g. `"blocked: heavy sweep refused on local-dev host_class"`). Leave it OUT of the `state() == "ready"` arm (`ready_queue.rs:150-159`) — it falls to the `_ => "blocked"` default, matching `HostConstraint`'s treatment, since this refusal never self-resolves by waiting the way a capacity/ramp/saturation defer does. Also add it to `wait_class()`'s `None` arm in `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/dwell.rs:82-93` (alongside `D::HostConstraint`), so it is never tracked for starvation, for the same reason `HostConstraint` isn't. This makes the refusal visible for free in `loom-daemon queue` (`loom-daemon/src/cli/ready_queue_cmd.rs:176-177` renders `.state()`/`.reason()` generically — no separate touch needed there) and in `loom-daemon health`'s per-tick summary line (via `reason_summary()`).
   `QueueDisposition` is referenced in 17 files as of `7e0a29b0d` (`grep -rl QueueDisposition loom-daemon/src`); not all are exhaustive matches that need a new arm — let the compiler be authoritative, but check `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/queue.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/observability/queue_blocked.rs`, and `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/queue_snapshot.rs` (plus their test modules) first, since those are the ones most likely to match exhaustively on the enum.

5. **Explicit opt-in override, two independent paths** (either is sufficient):
   - **Autonomous work-finder loop**: `autonomous.workFinder.allowHeavyLocal: true` / env `LOOM_ALLOW_HEAVY_LOCAL` (env > config > default `false`), resolved once per tick alongside the other per-tick dispatcher-supplied sets (`extra_skip_labels` at `work_finder.rs:1145`, `held_capabilities` at `work_finder.rs:1149`), so an operator can un-gate one `local-dev` box's autonomous loop entirely.
   - **Explicit CLI dispatch**: `loom-daemon dispatch <issue> --allow-local`, mirroring `--ignore-host-constraint` exactly (`loom-daemon/src/cli/dispatch.rs:99-206` — same "fetch labels via `gh issue view`, best-effort, fail open on a fetch error" contract already implemented by `fetch_issue_for_host_check` / `host_constraint_refusal`). An operator hand-dispatching a known-heavy issue on their own laptop on purpose is not the case this issue is trying to stop.

### Out of Scope / Follow-up (explicitly deferred — not filed as a new issue per curation policy)

**`/dashboard/hosts` allocation panel** — a live view of sweep distribution across hosts by `host_class` (`remote-worker` vs. `local-dev`), plus alerting on a refused-heavy-dispatch event. This depends on the `host_class` knob and the new `QueueDisposition`/counter landing first, there is no existing `/dashboard/hosts` route to extend today (confirmed above — the fleet dashboard and `fleet status`'s `remote_workers` concept are unrelated), and it is a separable unit of work (an observability/dashboard surface vs. a dispatch-admission enforcement mechanism). Left as a named follow-up here per curation guidance rather than filed as a separate issue — a human or Champion should file it once this lands, if still wanted.

Also explicitly out of scope: the original issue's "Restrict `local-dev` hosts to lightweight roles (Curator, triage, lint)" line. That is a *role-runner* concern (`autonomous.roleRunner`), a completely different subsystem from the work-finder sweep-dispatch path this issue and PR #9125/#9066 both live in, with its own admission ceiling (`autonomous.roleRunner.maxConcurrent`, #6102) and no existing "lightweight vs. heavy role" classification to gate on. Bundling it here would roughly double this PR's surface for a second, independently-decidable design question; a follow-up issue should treat it separately.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `autonomous.workFinder.hostClass` (`"local-dev"` | `"remote-worker"`; anything else or absent = unclassified) and env override `LOOM_HOST_CLASS` resolve with **env > config > default (unclassified)**, resolved once at daemon startup; unit-tested for all three layers plus an invalid-value-falls-through case.
- [ ] `loom:heavy` label exists in both `.github/labels.yml` and `defaults/.github/labels.yml` (byte-identical, inside the `BEGIN/END LOOM LABELS` block, description ≤ 100 chars); `defaults/scripts/check-labels-drift.sh` passes.
- [ ] A candidate carrying `loom:heavy`, on a host resolved to `host_class == local-dev`, with no override set, is refused with **zero** side effects: no `loom:issue → loom:building` claim flip, no `gh issue comment`, no cooldown/backoff record — verified by a work-finder unit test asserting the mock dispatcher's spawn/dispatch hook is never invoked for that candidate, in **both** `tick_with_saturation_brake` and `tick_multi_with_saturation_brake`.
- [ ] The same candidate dispatches normally when `host_class == remote-worker`, when `host_class` is unset, or when the candidate lacks `loom:heavy` — regression coverage proving zero behavior change for every pre-existing fixture/test.
- [ ] `autonomous.workFinder.allowHeavyLocal` / `LOOM_ALLOW_HEAVY_LOCAL` (env > config > default `false`) suppresses the autonomous-loop refusal when set; unit-tested.
- [ ] `loom-daemon dispatch <issue> --allow-local` bypasses the refusal for an explicit operator dispatch, mirroring `--ignore-host-constraint`'s fetch-and-check contract; unit-tested with a fake `gh issue view` response carrying `loom:heavy`, both with and without the flag (mirror the existing `host_constraint_refusal_*` test shapes at `cli/dispatch.rs:391-428`).
- [ ] The new `QueueDisposition` variant has `as_str()` / `reason()` / `state()` (blocked, not ready) covered by the existing `QueueDisposition` tests, is added to `wait_class()`'s "never tracked" arm in `dwell.rs`, and a targeted test confirms it renders correctly through `loom-daemon queue` (`ready_queue_cmd.rs`'s existing test module is the pattern to extend).
- [ ] `WorkFinderTickSummary::reason_summary()` includes a non-zero `host-class-skip` term when the gate fires this tick; unit-tested.
- [ ] `cargo build -p loom-daemon` / `cargo test -p loom-daemon` pass — run on the remote build box, never on this machine (see `~/.claude/skills/loom-remote-build-box.md`; this repo's daemon test suite is not run as part of curation).
- [ ] Docs updated in `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (mirror to `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` if it has drifted from `defaults/` — diff first): a new row in the `autonomous.workFinder.*` config table (starts at `daemon-reference.md:4234`, alongside the `maxConcurrentPerRepo` row at `daemon-reference.md:4241`) for `hostClass` and `allowHeavyLocal`, plus a short new subsection near "Host-affinity constraint (#7456)" (`daemon-reference.md:4967`) explaining the gate, its default, both override paths, and the explicit non-goal (no `/dashboard/hosts` panel in this PR).

### Implementation Guidance

Model the new module on `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/repo_cap.rs` (#9090 / PR #9125) — a small `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/host_class.rs` with: an env-override reader, a `resolve(config: &WorkFinderConfig) -> ...` function following the same `env_x().or(config.x)` shape `resolve_max_concurrent_with_source` uses, and a `parse_config` helper for `autonomous.workFinder.hostClass`. A plain validated `String`/small enum for the class is the Builder's call — either is fine as long as an unrecognized value falls through to "unclassified" rather than erroring, matching every other soft-fail knob in this file. Add the corresponding field(s) to `WorkFinderConfig` (`work_finder.rs:2063-2100`) and parse them in `read_work_finder_config` (`work_finder.rs:2112` onward) exactly like every other field there. Wire the two gate call sites using the same patterns already in place for `Qd::HostConstraint`: the `let mut skip = |d: Qd, detail: Option<String>| { ... }` closure in the multi-workspace loop (`work_finder.rs:1814-1822`), and the direct `report.skipped_host_constraint += 1; ...; continue;` shape in the single-workspace loop (`work_finder.rs:1192-1201`).

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` — `WorkFinderConfig` fields, `read_work_finder_config`, the two gate call sites, new counter plumbing.
- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/host_class.rs` (new) — config/env resolution, mirroring `repo_cap.rs`.
- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/tick_report.rs` — new `skipped_host_class` field (alongside `skipped_host_constraint` at line 156 / `deferred_repo_cap` at line 208).
- `loom-daemon/src/types.rs` — `WorkFinderTickSummary::skipped_host_class` + `reason_summary()` (lines 1901, 1949-1972).
- `loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs` — new `QueueDisposition` variant (`ALL`, `as_str()`, `reason()`, `state()`).
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/dwell.rs` — `wait_class()` arm (lines 82-93).
- `loom-daemon/src/cli/dispatch.rs` — `--allow-local` flag, refusal check + message, mirroring `--ignore-host-constraint` (lines 99-206, 391-428 for the test pattern).
- `.github/labels.yml`, `defaults/.github/labels.yml` — new `loom:heavy` label (near lines 247-259).
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (and `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` if it has drifted) — config table row (line 4234 area) + new subsection (line 4967 area).
- Any exhaustive `match`/`if let` over `QueueDisposition` the compiler flags after adding the variant — grep hits as of `7e0a29b0d`: `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/queue.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/observability/queue_blocked.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/queue_snapshot.rs`, plus their test modules (`loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/tests.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/observability/queue_blocked_tests.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/observability/queue_snapshot_tests.rs`) — not traced exhaustively by the Curator; verify by compiling.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Unit tests for `host_class` config/env resolution (env > config > default, invalid-value fallthrough).
- [ ] Unit tests for the gate in both `tick_with_saturation_brake` and `tick_multi_with_saturation_brake`: heavy+local-dev refused; heavy+remote-worker dispatched; heavy+unclassified dispatched; non-heavy+local-dev dispatched; heavy+local-dev+`allowHeavyLocal` dispatched.
- [ ] Unit tests for `cli/dispatch.rs`'s `--allow-local` refusal/bypass.
- [ ] `QueueDisposition` round-trip/serde/coverage test extended for the new variant.
- [ ] Build and test on the remote box per `~/.claude/skills/loom-remote-build-box.md` (`cargo build -p loom-daemon`, `cargo test -p loom-daemon`) — never locally on this machine.

issues.title: worktree node_modules symlinks the primary clone, so pnpm's purge prompt invites deleting it
issues.body:
## Summary

`worktree.sh` symlinks a new worktree's `node_modules` at the primary clone's. That makes `pnpm run <script>` unusable inside the worktree: pnpm's pre-run dependency check decides the modules directory needs re-provisioning, tries to purge it, and aborts without a TTY —

```
ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY
Aborted removal of modules directory due to no TTY
If you are running pnpm in CI, set the CI environment variable to "true"
```

The message names its own workaround, and that workaround is the problem: `CI=true` tells pnpm to proceed with removing a directory that **belongs to the primary clone**, from inside a worktree, for a repo that shares one `node_modules` across every worktree.

## Observed

Every worktree in the affected repo:

```console
$ ls -ld .loom/worktrees/*/node_modules
.loom/worktrees/issue-200/node_modules -> /Users/.../rulehunt/node_modules
.loom/worktrees/issue-209/node_modules -> /Users/.../rulehunt/node_modules
.loom/worktrees/issue-215/node_modules -> /Users/.../rulehunt/node_modules
```

A Builder hit this running the repo's required pre-PR check (`pnpm run ci`) from its worktree and worked around it by invoking `npx tsc` / `npx biome` / `npx vitest` directly. It flagged the reason explicitly: pnpm "wants to purge it — which would delete the main repo's `node_modules`".

I did not verify whether `CI=true` actually deletes through the symlink or merely replaces the link, because that is not a thing to test destructively on a working clone. Either outcome is bad: deleting the target breaks every worktree and the primary checkout at once, and replacing the link silently gives one worktree a private `node_modules` while the others still point at a directory that no longer matches the lockfile they were installed from.

## Why it matters beyond one repo

The failure lands on the **documented happy path**. Loom's Builder workflow is "claim issue → `worktree.sh <N>` → implement → run the repo's checks → open PR". Any repo whose check script is a `pnpm run` target hits this on every single issue, and the error text actively recommends the dangerous flag. An agent that follows the message's own advice does the destructive thing.

It is also silent in the other direction: because the worktree shares the primary clone's `node_modules`, a branch that changes dependencies is tested against the *primary clone's* installed tree, not its own. A PR that adds or bumps a dependency can pass locally for reasons unrelated to its own lockfile.

## Suggestions

1. **Make the symlink safe to use, or do not create it.** If the intent is disk sharing, a pnpm-aware arrangement (a shared store with a per-worktree `node_modules`, which is what pnpm's content-addressable store already exists to provide) gets the space saving without the aliasing.
2. **If the symlink stays, guard the destructive path.** A worktree-local `.npmrc` with `confirmModulesPurge=false` would turn the abort into a refusal-to-purge rather than an invitation to force it.
3. **Document it in the Builder role.** Until it is fixed, `builder.md` should say plainly: inside a Loom worktree, do not run `pnpm install` or `CI=true pnpm ...`; invoke binaries directly. Right now nothing warns, and the pnpm error steers the reader the wrong way.

Related: #8927 (stale `loom:blocked`). Both are cases where the tooling's default path produces a wrong outcome quietly.

issues.title: story-points: adopt the experiment's validated v6 class definitions into the production rubric
issues.body:
Parent epic: #9429. Follows #9521 (which landed the SP1–SP4 confirmation run).

## Outcome

The production rubric (`defaults/docs/story-points.md`) is a medians table plus four steps. The story-points experiment's **rubric v6** — the wording that scored **ρ = 0.82 [0.74, 0.88]** on the Frame A holdout (n = 133; both models; 91% within-one-bucket; run-to-run mode agreement 85%) — carries validated **per-class qualitative definitions** (what makes a 1 vs 2 vs 3: named-edit vs one-extra-obligation vs one-real-judgment vs coordinated deliverables vs new-capability-with-verification vs independent-proofs), the measured **traps** (generated output, terse issues hiding real work, repo weight, templated breadth, prose deliverables), and a **deciding procedure** (count deliverables → what must be run to prove it → what must be discovered). None of that guidance is in the production doc; the Curator sizes from numbers alone.

The experiment also measured that wording variants differ by <0.04 ρ — so adopting v6's definitions is safe: they are the *definition* of the classes, not tuned prose, and they move no bound.

## Work

- [ ] Adapt rubric v6's per-class definitions, traps, and deciding rule into `defaults/docs/story-points.md` (a "The classes" section + traps, after the medians table; imperative Curator-facing prose).
- [ ] **Adaptation decisions** (v6 was written for an estimator; the doc is the Curator's rubric): drop v6's 21/34 *assignment* advice — the production vocabulary stops at 13 and the split rule ("never size 21") is authoritative; drop the "ratio scale, 1.6× per step" framing (the measured LSI ratios are not Fibonacci — #9434's calibration owns point values); strip every private-repo issue reference (the experiment repo is private; loom#8156 may stay, others genericize).
- [ ] Provenance line citing the holdout result and the wording-insensitivity result; the medians table, its provisional-lines status (#9521), and the calibration mirror are untouched.

## Constraints

- Doc-only diff (`.md`): no medians change → no `rubric_classes`/`rubric_revisions` rows → no contract-test or fixture churn (the execution fixtures hardcode the single v1 revision, so a formal v2 marker would needlessly break them for zero calibration value).

- [ ] No private-repo content in the public doc.

## Curation

Scope pinned: one file (`defaults/docs/story-points.md`), additive sections only — "The classes" (per-class definitions: 1 fixed floor / 2 one obligation / 3 one real judgment / 5 coordinated deliverables extending an existing mechanism / 8 new capability with a real verification loop / 13 independent proofs), "Traps" (generated output, terse-vs-verbose, repo weight, templated breadth, prose deliverables), and "Deciding" (deliverables → verification → discovery). Adaptations per the Work list: no 21/34 assignment advice, no ratio-scale framing, all private-repo examples genericized (aggregate numbers stay; the experiment repo's issue text never enters this public repo). The medians table stays byte-stable (contract-pinned), no revision marker (no bound moves — wording insensitivity <0.04 ρ is the experiment's own result), so no calibration-mirror or fixture churn. Related work checked: #9431/#9528 (the label wiring — unaffected), #9521/#9648 (numbers provenance — composed with, not modified); disposition: absorbed into the provenance line.

issues.title: main red: pr_planning real_fallback_guard_preserves_velocity_alerts_and_decisions fails since #9821
issues.body:
## Summary

`main` is red: `loom-daemon/tests/pr_planning.rs::real_fallback_guard_preserves_velocity_alerts_and_decisions` fails in **Rust Unit Tests (3/3)** and **Rust OTLP Feature Tests (3/3)**. This blocks every loom PR.

- First red: CI run 36802632898 on `626902e3d` (version bump after the #9821 merge, `02dd44dce`, 2026-10-01 01:45Z). The previous full CI on `dff33f29c` was green.
- Failing jobs: 110180641779, 110180642117.

## Evidence

```
panicked at loom-daemon/tests/pr_planning.rs:323:9:
assertion `left == right` failed: sha-alert: Output { status: ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(0)),
  stdout: "DECISION=EVALUATE\nREASON=no skip condition matched\n...MARKER_COUNT=0\nVELOCITY_ALERT=0\nVELOCITY_COUNT=0\n",
  stderr: "trusted-comments: could not authenticate comment authors ('loom-daemon forge trusted-comments' failed); loom:fallback-evaluated markers read as absent (#9548/#9716)" }
```

## Root cause

#9821 (#9548/#9716) made `defaults/scripts/judge-fallback-guard.sh` count `loom:fallback-evaluated` markers only from trusted authors. It does this by piping the REST comment listing through `${LOOM_DAEMON_BIN:-loom-daemon} forge trusted-comments`. If that call fails, the guard fails safe: every marker reads as absent.

The Rust integration test still fed the guard the pre-#9821 fixture, which fails in two ways:

1. **No daemon is reachable.** The test does not set `LOOM_DAEMON_BIN`, and its `PATH` (tempdir + runner PATH) has no `loom-daemon`, so `forge trusted-comments` fails. The guard then reports `MARKER_COUNT=0` and every SHA/cap/velocity expectation breaks.
2. **The marker comments have no author.** They carry only `body`/`created_at`, with no `user`/`author_association`. A working filter would reject them too.

#9821 updated the shell test (`test-judge-fallback-cap.sh`) but not this Rust test. The guard and the filter behave correctly. The bug is in the fixture.

## Fix (without weakening the filter)

- Point `LOOM_DAEMON_BIN` at `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_loom-daemon")` (the same pattern other tests in this file use).
- Give each fixture marker the REST shape the Judge's App really produces: `user: {login: "loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]", type: "Bot"}`, `author_association: "NONE"`. This is trusted through the fleet default-family rule.
- Add an outsider (`author_association: NONE`, user account) same-head marker to every case. It must change nothing. This pins #9821's guarantee in this test as well.

No test bypass is added to the filter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon --test pr_planning` passes, with and without `--features otlp`.
- [ ] The test asserts that an untrusted author's marker is ignored by the guard and by `pr-queue`.
- [ ] `comment_trust` / `judge_fallback` lib tests, clippy (`--features otlp`) and fmt are clean.

issues.title: Merge consolidation: specify eligibility, failure recovery and component ownership (9063 next-stage design)
issues.body:
## Parent and sequence
Part of #9063. Follow-up to #9686. The operator chose to start with automatic ordering and design toward automatically prepared combined PRs. This issue makes the next-stage contract concrete and reviewable; it does not enable combined merges.

## Deliverable
Commit a concise design/decision record plus worked lifecycle fixtures for a small combined-PR pilot. Use the ordering plan and observed groups from #9686; do not build another congestion scorer or queue. Resolve the following as one cohesive protocol so preparation and landing can be implemented separately.

Recommended baseline to evaluate:
- A group has one repository/target branch, explicit related scope, a bounded review size and a recorded compatibility rationale. Path disjointness alone is insufficient; file overlap alone is not an automatic exclusion. Construction must be clean and the combined diff gets an independent Judge review.
- Preserve the earlier operator exclusions for `loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator-decision` and workflow-editing components. Other existing holds and merge-risk rules continue to apply. Do not silently broaden the pilot's permissions.
- Pin every component's identity and head/base SHA. Use the #9378 gate for temporary source-PR reservations with authenticated ownership, idempotency, recovery and release. A source PR cannot land concurrently with the candidate that includes it.
- For the first version, a conflict or failed combined CI run aborts the attempt, preserves the original PRs and releases only reservations this attempt owns. Avoid an automatic evict/retry/bisect search in the first version; unrelated PRs proceed. Any retry policy is bounded and changes in input are explicit.
- Successful preparation creates a reviewable combined PR; original PRs/issues stay open until inclusion and landing are verified. A green component does not grant approval or CI success to the combined candidate.
- Git commit landing can be atomic; closing multiple forge PRs/issues cannot be one atomic API transaction. Specify resumable reconciliation, accurate merged-versus-superseded status, and protection for unrelated/stacked branches.

These are proposed engineering defaults, not additional operator rulings. Refine them through normal design review, documenting alternatives and why the chosen rules prevent lost work, starvation or stale approvals. If a decision would widen an existing hold/approval authority, expose that exact unresolved choice rather than silently assuming permission.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The committed record names eligibility inputs, bounds, state transitions, ownership, cancellation, retry limits and failure/recovery rules with no unspecified destructive step.
- [ ] Worked examples cover overlapping files, semantic dependencies, a substantive rejection, held/workflow PRs, a head push during preparation, duplicate workers, failed CI, and interruption during component closure.
- [ ] Define exactly what is measured: avoided base-only repairs/reviews, queue age, CI attempts and useful review findings; keep unknown causes explicit and avoid a claimed performance improvement without evidence.
- [ ] Preparation and landing implementation boundaries are specified with stable IDs/events that 2AMLogic/loom-ui#590 can consume.
- [ ] Review the design against existing #9378, #9416, #9372 and #9161 contracts rather than introducing conflicting sequencing, approval or hold mechanisms.

## Dependencies
- Depends on #9686: use its plan contract and replay evidence.
- Reuse #9378. #9416 is a separate optimization, not permission to reuse CI or reviews without its proof.

## Likely files and validation
New decision record under the repository's ADR/docs convention, with lifecycle examples or fixtures in the eventual Rust module's test surface (new paths to be chosen during implementation). Existing reference surfaces verified at 82891089530c721c6365033b2dde592302096c94: `loom-daemon/src/merge_pr/`, `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh`, and `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md`. No live branch, PR or issue closure is required to validate this design issue.

issues.title: Audit install-loom.sh/uninstall-loom.sh/install.sh git-add-A sites for the #8005 credential-bearing class
issues.body:
## Background

#8005 replaced `land-resync-commit.sh`'s and `resync-installed.sh`'s
hardcoded two-path gh-config guard with a single declared credential-bearing
class (`loom-daemon/src/init/post_init.rs` `CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS`, parity-
checked against both shell copies by `loom-daemon/src/init/credential_class_tests.rs`).

That PR's "Suspected scope (unverified)" section named several other
`git add -A` / `git add .loom` call sites that were flagged as *possibly*
benefiting from the same class-level guard, but explicitly deferred rather
than assumed safe or unsafe:

- `scripts/install-loom.sh:653` (and a similar block around :788, :1422) —
  `git add -A` when creating the initial commit for a brand-new install.
- `scripts/uninstall-loom.sh:1985` — `git add -A` in a worktree built for
  the uninstall-removal PR.
- `install.sh:1360` — same "initial commit" pattern as install-loom.sh.
- `docs/guides/ci-cd-setup.md:112` and `:326` — workflow template snippets
  that run `git add .loom CLAUDE.md .claude .gitignore`.

## What this issue is for

Audit each site above, individually, against the same question #7818/#8005
answered for `land-resync-commit.sh`: can this specific `git add` run in a
repo state where a credential-bearing path (`.loom/tokens/`,
`.loom/accounts.env`, `.loom/api-keys/`, `.loom/claude-config/`,
`.loom/gh-config/`, `.loom/gh-config-by-owner/`) already exists on disk,
untracked, with a stale-or-missing `.gitignore`?

For each site, either:

1. Confirm it is structurally safe (e.g. "initial commit" runs before `.loom`
   is ever populated with live credentials, or the worktree the add runs in
   is provably fresh) and record why in a comment near the call site, or
2. Apply the same class-level exclusion — reuse `loom-daemon
   is-credential-path` / `CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` (exposed via
   `loom-daemon/src/init/mod.rs`) or the same `:!`-pathspec pattern
   `resync-installed.sh` now prints — if the site turns out to be reachable
   with live credentials present.

The workflow-template snippets in `ci-cd-setup.md` are documentation, not
executable code — lower priority, but still worth a pathspec update if the
audit finds them realistically reachable with a stale `.gitignore`.

## Out of scope

Re-litigating #8005's core design (the `CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` const + parity
tests) — that's done. This is a per-site audit only.

Filed as a scoped follow-up per #8005's own "Suspected scope (unverified)"
section, split out to keep #8005 focused on the two call sites it was
actually filed against.

issues.title: verify-proposal-refs.sh reports BAD LINE RANGE for every .loom/docs/*.md citation (reads the symlink, not the document)
issues.body:
## What happens

`verify-proposal-refs.sh`'s line-range check reads the cited path **through git** (`git show "origin/main:$path" | wc -l`). Since #7842 every `.loom/docs/*.md` with a `defaults/docs/` counterpart is a **symlink** (tree mode `120000`), so that read returns the link-target string, `wc -l` measures the link, and every cited range under `.loom/docs/` is reported as a miss:

```
$ printf 'Cites .loom/docs/troubleshooting.md:100-200\n' > /tmp/probe.md
$ ./.loom/scripts/verify-proposal-refs.sh /tmp/probe.md
verify-proposal-refs.sh: 1 miss(es) in /tmp/probe.md
  - BAD LINE RANGE: `.loom/docs/troubleshooting.md:100-200` — origin/main:.loom/docs/troubleshooting.md has only 0 lines
exit=1
```

The real document has 3031 lines. Because the script **blocks filing** (`hermit.md` / `architect.md`: "Any miss blocks filing"), this pushes proposers away from citing the installed doc paths, or into "fixing" a citation that was correct.

This is the same root cause as #8593 (Champion's premise-false gate reading `.loom/docs/*.md` symlinks through git and closing sound proposals on a check that cannot match). #8593 fixed the Champion side — the prompt rules, `champion-premise-false-evidence.md`'s `resolve_main_path()` recipe, and fixture coverage — and deliberately left this half out: see below.

## Why it was not fixed in #8593's PR

A working shell fix was prototyped in PR #8655 and dropped. It adds ~40 **code** lines to `defaults/scripts/verify-proposal-refs.sh`, which is category `contract` in `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt`, and `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` refuses any growth of the portable pool **with no `Shell-Budget-Growth:` override** (`check_against_rev`: "Portable growth is NOT overridable, deliberately"). Per `.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md` the correct home for new logic behind a `contract` name is `loom-daemon`.

## Suggested shape

1. A `loom-daemon` verb that resolves a path against a rev — follow a `120000` tree entry to its real blob path (bounded hops; target is relative to the **link's own directory**; normalization must be **lexical**, since the path lives in a commit, not the working tree) and optionally report the resolved blob's line count.
2. `verify-proposal-refs.sh` calls it in the line-range branch, reports the **resolved** path in any `BAD LINE RANGE` message, and reports a dangling link as *unreadable* (e.g. `BROKEN SYMLINK`) rather than "has only 0 lines" — an unreadable file is an inconclusive check, not a disproof (the same distinction #8593 established for Champion).
3. Champion's `resolve_main_path()` snippet (`defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-premise-false-evidence.md`) can then point at the same verb instead of shipping a shell recipe in a prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A body citing an in-range line span under `.loom/docs/` exits 0 (no miss).
- [ ] A genuinely out-of-range span under `.loom/docs/` still misses, and the message names the **resolved** path and the real line count.
- [ ] A dangling symlink is reported as unreadable, not as a 0-line file.
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-verify-proposal-refs.sh` gains a symlink fixture covering all three (a draft of these fixtures exists in PR #8655's history).
- [ ] `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` stays at +0 portable growth.

issues.title: observability: capture all GitHub Actions runs/jobs of the 2amlogic org as OTLP telemetry via a loom-daemon ci-telemetry poller (SigNoz build/CI visibility, phase 1 of 3)
issues.body:
## What

Capture **every GitHub Actions run and job** of the `2amlogic` org as first-class OTLP telemetry from a new `loom-daemon ci-telemetry` poller. This is the foundation for standing build/CI observability in SigNoz: durations, outcomes, and per-run structure become queryable so we can retro on build/CI time regressions (motivation: build and CI times are currently felt but invisible — regressions only surface as "everything is slower").

Part of the SigNoz observability track (epic #8522): the transport (daemon OTLP exporter → neutral gateway → SigNoz) already exists; this issue adds the **CI source** that currently does not exist at all. Follow-on phases: full job-log capture with collector-side redaction (filed next), and SigNoz retro surfaces (filed next) — cross-linked at filing.

## Design (grounded in existing modules)

**New Rust module** `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/` + CLI subcommand `ci-telemetry` (per the shell-language policy: new executable logic is a daemon subcommand, not a `.sh`).

### CLI
- `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --once` — one poll cycle across the configured org; non-zero exit with a named reason on failure (a poll that cannot run must not look like a poll that passed — ci-principles rule 6)
- `loom-daemon ci-telemetry status` — ledger size, per-repo watermarks, last successful poll, records emitted/exported
- Daemon-integrated periodic poller when `autonomous.ciTelemetry.enabled=true` (default **false**, FLAGS-OFF; `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_*` env overrides, env > config > default via `config_resolver.rs`)

### Config block (`.loom/config.json` → `autonomous.ciTelemetry`)
| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` |
| `org` | `2amlogic` |
| `intervalSecs` | 120 |
| `excludedRepos` | `[]` |
| `logCaptureEnabled` | `false` (phase 2 flips it; must be a config gate, see scope) |

### Polling + dedup ("never do the same job twice")
- Discover repos via `GET /orgs/{org}/repos` (paginated, ETag/304-cached — the `forge_cached_list.rs` mechanism, never raw re-listing)
- Per repo: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs` with a `created_after` watermark from the ledger; for each unseen run → `GET /actions/runs/{id}/jobs`
- **Durable ledger** at `.loom/state/ci-telemetry/seen.jsonl`: append-only `(repo, run_id, job_id)` entries + per-repo watermark (latest observed `run.created_at`), fsynced before a record is emitted. A job is emitted **exactly once** regardless of restarts, re-polls, or re-runs. A crash between write and emit must never double-emit: the ledger write is the commit.
- Multi-host posture: polling may run on more than one fleet host, but records carry **stable identities** (`run_id`/`job_id` as the dedup key in attributes + local ledger) so a recipient can dedup; document the single-poller-as-normal-case assumption, per-repo lease coordination is explicitly out of scope unless fleet primitives make it trivial (one mechanism per behaviour — do not invent a second coordination layer)
- Rate limits: honour the existing rate-limit breaker; budget = repos × 2 request families per interval; a 403/secondary-limit backs off the whole org, not per-repo hammering

### Emission (through the existing `observability` OTLP exporter — no new transport)
- Record kinds: `ci.run` (repo, workflow, ref, head_sha, event, status, conclusion, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at) and `ci.job` (+ job name, runner label, attempts, timed_out) — mapped in `observability/otlp/mapping.rs` alongside the existing lifecycle kinds
- Metrics: `loom.ci.run.duration_ms` and `loom.ci.job.duration_ms` histograms; labels **only** `repo`, `workflow`, `job`, `runner`, `conclusion` (low-cardinality allowlist rule; never sha/ref/issue-number in metric labels)
- Traces: one trace per run, one span per job (parent/child like the sweep traces in `telemetry/trace/`), so Trace Explorer shows the CI waterfall
- **Local journal** `.loom/logs/ci-telemetry.jsonl` is written regardless of whether any exporter is configured (the `sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl` pattern) — the poller is useful offline

### Gateway allowlist
Extend `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` `keep_keys` with exactly the `loom.ci.*` attributes this phase emits; the fan-out contract test (`collector_fanout`) must assert each one. Nothing else admitted.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --help` documents the subcommand; building without the `otlp` feature still compiles (OTLP-gated paths behind the existing feature, like `exporter.rs`)
2. With a recorded-fixture GitHub API (wiremock-style or recorded responses, committed under the test dir — no live-network tests in CI), `--once` over a synthetic org with 2 repos × 3 runs × 4 jobs emits 2 `ci.run` + 3×4 `ci.job` records to the local journal with correct durations
3. **Idempotency (the money AC)**: a second `--once` over the same fixture emits **zero** records; killing the process mid-cycle and re-running emits each job exactly once total (ledger is the commit)
4. Unit tests cover: pagination continuation, `created_after` watermark advance, ETag 304 no-op on repo discovery, rate-limit backoff, ledger crash-recovery (torn trailing line is detected and repaired, not double-counted)
5. `status` distinguishes: never-polled / last-ok + age / failing + last error — silence never reads as healthy (house discipline)
6. `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` created (phase-1 section: config reference, dedup contract, local journal schema) with `.loom/docs/` parity copy (Docs/Defaults Parity Check must pass); `observability.md` map-of-docs table gains the row
7. Emitted metric label set and attribute allowlist match the collector `keep_keys` additions byte-for-byte (contract test)

## Explicit non-goals (this issue)

- **No job log download** — that is the follow-on phase; `logCaptureEnabled` exists as a gate that this phase must refuse to honour (config-gated off, named stub, no dead code that pretends to work)
- No re-hosting of GitHub's log UI, no per-step spans (job granularity is the unit)
- No per-repo lease/coordination protocol
- No changes to `sweep.*`/`tokens.*` record kinds

## Cross-links

- Epic: #8522 (SigNoz/ClickStack trial)
- Pipeline/transport docs: `.loom/docs/observability.md`, `.loom/docs/otlp-transport.md`
- Dedup/journal precedent: `.loom/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (local journal), #8669 (allowlist discipline)
- Policy home (follow-on issue): `ci-observability.md`

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/` (new module) - poller, dedup ledger, CLI subcommand
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/otlp/mapping.rs` - add `ci.run`/`ci.job` record mapping
- `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` - extend `keep_keys` with the new `loom.ci.*` attributes
- `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` - add the phase-1 section (config reference, dedup contract, local journal schema) to the existing policy doc
- `defaults/docs/observability.md` - add the map-of-docs row
- `.loom/config.json` schema - new `autonomous.ciTelemetry` block

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: fixture-based `--once` run (2 repos × 3 runs × 4 jobs) asserts correct `ci.run`/`ci.job` record counts and durations
- [ ] Idempotency test: second `--once` over the same fixture emits zero records; kill-mid-cycle + re-run emits each job exactly once
- [ ] Unit tests: pagination continuation, `created_after` watermark advance, ETag 304 no-op, rate-limit backoff, ledger crash-recovery (torn trailing line)
- [ ] Contract test: emitted metric label/attribute set matches collector `keep_keys` additions byte-for-byte
- [ ] Manual verification: `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --help` / `status` output reviewed for the never-polled / last-ok+age / failing+last-error states

issues.title: observability: standing policy — all 2amlogic build/CI logs and runs are captured in SigNoz (ci-observability policy doc + wiring; phase 4 of 4)
issues.body:
## What

Codify the **standing policy**: *all build and CI activity of the captured org is captured in SigNoz — runs, jobs, durations, outcomes, and full job logs — and stays captured as new repos/workflows appear.* Operator decision, stated outright: "It should be a standing policy that we capture all logs and CI there."

This issue is docs + config plumbing only (no new executable logic beyond a config default and the parity/budget constraints CI already enforces), and it can land independently of #8824/#8825/#8826 — it names what they build.

## Design

### `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` (canonical home, mirrored to `.loom/docs/`)
Sections:
1. **The policy** (one paragraph, non-negotiable wording): every `2amlogic` repo's GitHub Actions runs, jobs, durations, outcomes, and completed-job logs are captured in SigNoz via the ci-telemetry poller; org-scoped capture means new repos are in scope on day one (auto-discovery, no per-repo enrollment step); duration/outcome metrics are **never** excludable, log capture may be excluded per-repo only with a stated reason recorded in the config entry itself
2. **The pipeline, in one picture** (poller → OTLP exporter → neutral gateway redaction → SigNoz; diagram style matching `observability.md`) with map-plus-links to every detail doc (`telemetry-schema.md`, `otlp-transport.md`, collector README, signoz README) — a map, not a duplicate, per the operating-summary discipline
3. **Phases** (1: runs/jobs/metrics — #8824; 2: logs + collector redaction — #8825; 3: retro surfaces + retention — #8826) with status, each linking its issue
4. **Capture scope & exclusions**: the `excludedRepos`/`logCapture` config surface and the rule that an exclusion is a config entry *with a reason field*, reviewed like any other config change; no silent excludes, no undocumented ones
5. **Retention**: metrics ≥30d, logs/traces 7d, and why (trends outlive raw data) — owned by #8826, referenced here as policy
6. **Redaction policy**: the collector is the redaction boundary (operator decision), the scrub-class table (from #8825's design), and what this store is and is not (trusted private operational store, not the public dashboard projection — same framing as the collector README)
7. **Rollout**: how a fleet host enables capture (config block + observability OTLP endpoint already in the trial docs), the single-poller-normal-case posture, and the SigNoz trial itself as the destination (managed-cloud option stays optional per the signoz README)

### Wiring
- `CLAUDE.md`: one pointer line in the CI section ("CI is dumb and reliable" area) → the policy doc; **must pass `scripts/check-claude-md-budget.sh` and the Doc Table-of-Contents Freshness check** (run `scripts/check-doc-tocs.sh --fix` on the new doc before commit)
- `.loom/docs/ci-principles.md` "Related": one-line link — the policy doc is the observability face of the same "measure it or you can't trust it" family (the #7779 cancellation storm got a fix but had no time-visibility before this policy)
- `.loom/docs/observability.md` "Map of every detail doc" table: row for `ci-observability.md` (+ its phase issues)
- **Docs/Defaults Parity Check** passes (the doc ships in both locations, byte-identical per the parity convention)
- Config surface: after #8824 lands, `autonomous.ciTelemetry.org` defaults to `2amlogic` (the captured org) — this issue documents that default; if #8824 landed with a different default, reconcile in this PR, not by silent drift

## Acceptance criteria

1. `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` exists, mirrors to `.loom/docs/`, passes the parity check, TOC check, and dangling-link check; every doc it links to exists
2. CLAUDE.md pointer present, budget check green (CI proves it — the check is a required status check, so the PR can't merge red)
3. `ci-principles.md` and `observability.md` cross-links present in both locations they ship
4. The policy wording in §1 names the org, the signal set (runs/jobs/durations/outcomes/logs), the never-excludable metrics, and the reasoned-exclusion rule — the four things a new operator must be able to read in one paragraph
5. No executable-logic changes beyond a config default value (if #8824 is already merged) — if it hasn't, this PR is pure docs and says so in the PR description

## Explicit non-goals

- No alerting, no new queries (that's #8826)
- No changes to the redaction implementation (#8825) or the poller (#8824)
- No fleet-wide enablement action in this PR (rollout is a per-host config operation documented in the doc; the operator/role-runner performs it when #8824/#8825 are merged and the trial is confirmed receiving)

## Cross-links

- Phase 1: #8824 · Phase 2: #8825 · Phase 3: #8826
- Epic: #8522 · Policy family: `.loom/docs/ci-principles.md` · Map: `.loom/docs/observability.md`

issues.title: Shared App installation rate limit exhausted on all 4 dispatchers (~11k warnings/3d, 92 work_finder ticks skipped) — recurrence after #7606/#4429
issues.body:
## Summary

Shared GitHub App installation rate-limit exhaustion is live on **all four**
dispatchers of the 2AMLogic fleet, skipping 92 `work_finder` ticks over a 3-day window.
`#7606` and `#4429` both address this class and are both **closed**, so this is a
recurrence report rather than a new diagnosis.

## Measurements

`fleet-check.sh` 2026-09-25T18:16Z, installation `151241294`:

| Host | Warnings (3d) | Peak/hour | work_finder ticks skipped | Dominant logger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| robb-studio | 3685 | 380 @ 2026-09-25T01 | 34 | `claim_reconciliation (verdicts)` — `gh pr list --label loom:pr` (25x) |
| robb-pro | 2422 | 393 @ 2026-09-25T11 | 21 | `claim_reconciliation` — `gh pr list --label loom:treating` (15x) |
| loom-worker-1 | 2570 | 393 @ 2026-09-25T11 | 19 | `sweep_registry` — quarantine-release label edit for #127 exited Some(1): GraphQL (68x) |
| loom-worker-2 | 2586 | 338 @ 2026-09-23T09 | 18 | `claim_reconciliation (verdicts)` — `gh pr list --label loom:changes-requested` (14x) |

~11,000 warnings in 3 days across four hosts, all against one shared installation.

## What stands out

**`claim_reconciliation` is the dominant caller on three of four hosts**, each doing
per-repo `gh pr list --label <label>` reads. Across 56 fleet repos and several labels
per pass, that is a large, regular, per-tick fan-out against a single shared
installation quota — which looks like the same amplification `#7606` addressed for
`work_finder`'s guarded-issue re-probe, just in a different loop.

On loom-worker-1 the dominant entry is instead `sweep_registry` retrying one
quarantine-release label edit for `#127` 68 times with `exited Some(1): GraphQL` — a
single failing operation retried into the budget, which is a distinct problem from
fan-out volume.

**The failure is silent and self-worsening.** A skipped `work_finder` tick is not
retried work, it is lost scheduling; and the fleet showed 39 role ticks lost to token
exhaustion in the same window. Throughput still reads healthy (PACE 125% of the 7d
average), so nothing surfaces this except an explicit fleet check.

## Questions

1. Did `#7606`'s open-PR-guard change cover `claim_reconciliation`'s own `gh pr list`
   fan-out, or only `work_finder`'s issue re-probe?
2. Is `#4429`'s rate-limit-aware backoff active on these loops? Peaks of ~390/hour with
   thousands of warnings suggest the loops are not backing off once the budget is spent.
3. Should a repeatedly-failing forge mutation (the `#127` GraphQL case) have a retry
   ceiling, so one broken operation cannot consume a shared quota 68 times?

Happy to pull specific `daemon.log` excerpts from any of the four hosts if useful.


---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-27, verified against `origin/main` @ `3bc7991d`)

The three questions above are answered below with direct code citations (each
traced, not inferred — commands shown). This turns the recurrence report into
two concrete, independently-shippable fixes.

### Q1 — Did #7606's open-PR-guard cover `claim_reconciliation`'s own `gh pr list` fan-out?

**No — only `work_finder`'s issue re-probe.** `gh pr view 7619 --json files`
(the PR that closed #7606) shows it touched exactly:
`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs`, `guards.rs`, `types.rs`,
`work_finder.rs`. `claim_reconciliation.rs` — the dominant logger on 3 of 4
hosts in the measurements table above — was not touched.

Structurally: `claim_reconciliation::run_reconciliation_pass`
(`claim_reconciliation.rs:1779-1815`) calls
`rate_limit_breaker::global_is_suppressed()` exactly **once**, before the
`for root in &roots` loop (line 1788) — not per-repo inside the loop. So once
a pass has started (breaker not yet tripped at the top), every one of the
fleet's repos gets its own `gh pr list --label <verdict-label>` call for both
`VerdictKind::Approved` and `VerdictKind::ChangesRequested`
(`reconcile_pr_verdicts` at `claim_reconciliation.rs:3408-3426`,
`list_verdict_prs` at `claim_reconciliation.rs:3128-3158`), regardless of
whether an earlier repo in the *same* pass already tripped the breaker via
`global_observe_failure` (called on failure at `claim_reconciliation.rs:3420`).
The breaker protects the *next* pass, not the *rest of the current* one —
exactly the 25x/15x/14x `gh pr list` fan-out the measurements table shows as
the dominant logger.

### Q2 — Is #4429's rate-limit-aware backoff active/effective on these loops?

**Partially — active and effective for `work_finder`, incomplete for
`claim_reconciliation`, entirely absent for `sweep_registry`'s quarantine
retry (see Q3).**

The breaker (`rate_limit_breaker.rs`, env `LOOM_RATE_LIMIT_BREAKER`,
default-on) is consulted every tick in `work_finder`'s main loop
(`work_finder.rs:2436-2455`) and does work: the "work_finder ticks skipped"
column in the measurements table above (34/21/19/18 = 92) is generated by
exactly the `work_finder: tick skipped — shared GitHub API rate limit
exhausted (#4429)` log line at that site — i.e. the breaker *was* tripping
and *was* suppressing further `work_finder` polling during cooldown, as
designed.

It is also consulted once per pass in `claim_reconciliation::run_reconciliation_pass`
(line 1788) — but, per Q1, not per-repo inside that pass's own loop.

It is **not consulted at all** in `sweep_registry`'s quarantine-release retry
path (`grep -n rate_limit_breaker loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/quarantine.rs`
→ zero matches) — see Q3.

### Q3 — Should a repeatedly-failing forge mutation get a retry ceiling?

**Yes — this is the most clear-cut of the three, and matches the `#127`
example exactly.**

`SweepRegistry::retry_pending_quarantine_releases`
(`quarantine.rs:970-978`) runs unconditionally from `reap_once_impl` on
**every** reaper tick (`reaper.rs:1090`, default interval
`DEFAULT_REAPER_INTERVAL_SECS = 30s`, `reaper.rs:18`) for every issue still in
`pending_quarantine_release`. `attempt_quarantine_release`
(`quarantine.rs:986-1001`) never removes an issue from that set on failure —
it stays pending and is retried on literally every subsequent tick,
indefinitely, with:

- **no consultation of `rate_limit_breaker::global_is_suppressed()`** (zero
  matches for `rate_limit_breaker` anywhere in `quarantine.rs`),
- **no retry ceiling / attempt counter**, and
- **no backoff** (unlike the #4485 dispatch-backoff ladder the same crate
  already reuses elsewhere — see #7606's proposal for the shape).

`release_quarantine_label` (`quarantine.rs:1134-1188`) issues `gh issue edit
--remove-label loom:blocked --add-label loom:issue`, which is GraphQL-backed —
matching the observed `exited Some(1): GraphQL` failure text exactly. At the
default 30s interval, 68 observed retries for `#127` is ~34 minutes of
continuous per-tick GraphQL mutation attempts against the shared installation,
with nothing to stop it short of the underlying cause being fixed by a human
or the daemon restarting.

### Root cause summary

Two independent gaps in *callers*, not in the breaker itself (the breaker is
working as designed — see Q2):

1. **`claim_reconciliation`'s per-pass loop doesn't re-check the #4429
   breaker between repos.** A trip triggered by repo N doesn't stop repos
   N+1..56 in the same pass.
2. **`sweep_registry`'s quarantine-release retry has no ceiling and doesn't
   consult the breaker at all.** A single permanently-failing mutation (e.g.
   a label-permission or repo-config problem on `#127`) retries indefinitely
   at full tick cadence, burning the shared quota with every attempt.

### Proposed fix

**Fix A — `claim_reconciliation`: re-check breaker suppression inside the per-repo loop.**
- In `run_reconciliation_pass` (`claim_reconciliation.rs:1804`, `for root in
  &roots`), check `rate_limit_breaker::global_is_suppressed()` at the top of
  each iteration (or immediately after any in-loop `global_observe_failure`
  call) and stop processing the remaining repos for this pass once
  suppressed — the same "protect the rest of the current pass, not just the
  next one" shape #7619 already applied to `work_finder`'s own guard chain.
- Apply the same re-check inside `reconcile_pr_verdicts`'s per-`VerdictKind`
  loop (`claim_reconciliation.rs:3415`) if it can be reached independently of
  `run_reconciliation_pass`'s own check.

**Fix B — `sweep_registry`: bound quarantine-release retries.**
- Before calling `release_quarantine_label` from `attempt_quarantine_release`
  / `retry_pending_quarantine_releases`, consult
  `rate_limit_breaker::global_is_suppressed()` and skip the attempt (leaving
  the issue pending, not counting against any ceiling) while suppressed —
  cheap, and stops this path from being the thing that *keeps* the breaker
  tripped through an entire cooldown window.
- Add a bounded retry ceiling (a per-issue attempt counter alongside
  `pending_quarantine_release`, or reuse the #4485 backoff-ladder shape) so a
  single permanently-failing label edit stops escalating after N attempts and
  instead surfaces once (log at `warn`/`error` plus, if cheap, a one-time
  forge comment) for a human to unstick, rather than retrying forever at full
  tick cadence.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `claim_reconciliation::run_reconciliation_pass`'s per-repo loop stops
      issuing further `gh pr list` calls for the remainder of a pass once the
      rate-limit breaker trips mid-pass (test: simulate a mid-loop
      `global_observe_failure` rate-limit trip and assert repos ordered after
      the tripping one are never queried in that pass).
- [ ] `sweep_registry`'s quarantine-release retry consults
      `rate_limit_breaker::global_is_suppressed()` and **skips** (does not
      fail/count) an attempt while suppressed.
- [ ] `sweep_registry`'s quarantine-release retry has a bounded attempt
      ceiling; once reached, the issue stops being retried every tick and a
      single clear log line (at minimum) records that manual intervention is
      needed.
- [ ] Existing quarantine-release tests in `quarantine.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)]`
      module (already covering `retry_pending_quarantine_releases` /
      `attempt_quarantine_release`) continue to pass, plus new tests for the
      ceiling and the breaker-skip behavior.
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon claim_reconciliation` and `cargo test -p
      loom-daemon quarantine` (or the equivalent module test filters) both
      pass.

### Out of scope

- Re-deriving or re-verifying the raw fleet measurements in the issue body
  above (warnings/hour, ticks skipped) — those are operator-supplied
  `daemon.log` telemetry, not something this fix re-derives.
- #4428/#4430/#4431 (ETag caching, GitHub App identity, safehouse
  coordination) — siblings in epic #4432, not touched here.
- Any change to the breaker's own trip/cooldown logic in
  `rate_limit_breaker.rs` — it is working as designed for its existing
  callers (see Q2); the gap is callers not consulting it, not the breaker
  itself.

### Affected files

- `loom-daemon/src/claim_reconciliation.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/quarantine.rs`
- Possibly `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/reaper.rs` if the retry ceiling
  needs a field threaded from the reaper tick

(Verified present on `origin/main` @ `3bc7991d` — all three paths exist and
`origin/main` has no diff against local `HEAD` for them, so cited line
numbers are current as of this curation pass.)

### Test plan

1. `cargo test -p loom-daemon claim_reconciliation` — add a unit test that
   seeds two (or more) workspace roots, makes the first `gh pr list` call
   fail with a rate-limit signature, and asserts the second root's `gh pr
   list` is never invoked in the same pass.
2. `cargo test -p loom-daemon quarantine` (or the module's own test path) —
   add a test asserting `attempt_quarantine_release` stops retrying after the
   configured ceiling, and a test asserting it no-ops without consuming a
   retry while `rate_limit_breaker::global_is_suppressed()` is true.
3. Manual/fleet verification (optional, operator-driven): after deploy,
   re-run the same fleet-log aggregation this issue used and confirm
   `claim_reconciliation` and `sweep_registry` no longer dominate the warning
   counts during the next rate-limit window.

### Scope note

This issue's own text frames three open questions rather than a pre-decided
fix; the enhancement above converts them into two concrete, testable changes,
both confined to `loom-daemon/src/claim_reconciliation.rs` and
`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/quarantine.rs` (+ a possible small
`reaper.rs` touch). Combined this is estimated well under the >400 LOC / >8
file decomposition threshold (`.claude/commands/loom/curator.md` →
"Decomposing Oversized Issues"), so this stays a single issue/PR rather than
being split into sub-issues.
