issues.title: feat(observability): export standard TRACEPARENT + opt-in Claude Code OTel env to spawned workers (LLM vs tool sub-spans)
issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

<details>
<summary>Original issue</summary>

### Problem
Builder sweeps appear in SigNoz as monolithic 15–20 min spans, so there is no way to tell LLM time from tool time (iverilog, klayout, ngspice, pytest, git). Claude Code can already emit exactly those sub-spans natively:
- `claude_code.llm_request`, with `ttft_ms` and `duration_ms`;
- `claude_code.tool` / `claude_code.tool.execution`, with `duration_ms`, plus `bash_argv0` / `bash_command_class` under `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1`.

This needs `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1` and `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp`. Claude Code parents its spans on the **standard W3C `TRACEPARENT`** env var.

Loom only exports its own `LOOM_TRACEPARENT` to spawned children (`loom-daemon/src/observability/tracing.rs`, `TRACEPARENT_ENV`). `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh` sets neither `TRACEPARENT` nor any Claude Code telemetry env. So even with Claude Code telemetry on, its spans would land as orphan traces instead of under `loom.role_attempt`.

### Proposal
1. When spawning a Claude Code worker, also export standard `TRACEPARENT`, equal to the `loom.role_attempt` span context already carried in `LOOM_TRACEPARENT`. This is harmless when Claude Code telemetry is off.
2. Add an opt-in config block, **default off** with env > config > default, that injects Claude Code's OTel env into spawned workers. It should cover `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, an endpoint pointing at the host-local edge, and optionally `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS`. Never put prompt or user-content logging behind a default-on switch.
3. Document it in `defaults/docs/observability.md` / `trace-identity.md`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Spawned Claude Code children receive `TRACEPARENT` matching the role-attempt span (unit test on the spawn env builder).
- [ ] With the opt-in off, the spawn env is byte-identical to today apart from `TRACEPARENT`.
- [ ] With the opt-in on, the documented `OTEL_*` / `CLAUDE_CODE_*` vars are present, and the endpoint comes from config (test).
- [ ] Docs updated.

### Context
Came from 2AMLogic/2am#1329 (closed as a duplicate of 2AMLogic/2am#1321, which evaluates this for Builder/Judge role attempts). Seeing live spans on fleet hosts also needs the fleet OTel edge rollout, 2AMLogic/2am#1345. The code here is verifiable without it.

</details>

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-27)

Re-grounded against `origin/main` @ `96cf99d8f` (0.19.448). The mechanism described in the original issue is slightly out of date — `TRACEPARENT_ENV` is `"LOOM_TRACEPARENT"`, actually defined in `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/trace/store.rs:11` (re-exported/used from `loom-daemon/src/observability/tracing.rs`) — and the "matches the `loom.role_attempt` span" framing needs a correction below. Everything else in the proposal still holds.

### Corrected mechanism (read this before implementing)

`loom-daemon/src/observability/tracing.rs::prepare_child` is the ONLY place `LOOM_TRACEPARENT` is set today, called from exactly one dispatch surface: `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs::spawn_child_process` (the daemon's `/loom:sweep` child spawn — `spawn_bin` → `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh` → `claude` or `claude-wrapper.sh` → `claude`). Relevant body today:

```rust
pub fn prepare_child(command: &mut Command, root: &Path, execution: &str, issue: Option<u32>) {
    command
        .env_remove(TRACEPARENT_ENV)
        .env_remove(CONTEXT_FILE_ENV);
    if !enabled(root) {
        return;
    }
    let story = issue.and_then(|issue| resolve_story(root, issue));
    let store = TraceStore::new(root);
    match store.load_or_create_story(root, execution, story.as_ref().map(|s| &s.context)) {
        Ok(saved) => {
            command.env(TRACEPARENT_ENV, saved.context.traceparent());
            command.env(CONTEXT_FILE_ENV, store.path(root, execution));
            super::lifecycle::prepare_execution(command, root, execution, story.as_ref());
        }
        Err(error) => log::warn!("observability: trace context unavailable; child is untraced: {error}"),
    }
}
```

`saved.context` is the **sweep's own root context** (a `loom.sweep` span in the issue's story trace, or the sweep's own root trace outside a story — see `defaults/docs/tracing.md` "Identity and process boundaries") — **not** a `loom.role_attempt` span. That distinction matters here because, for a sweep dispatch, Curator → Builder → Judge → Doctor → Merge all run **serially inside the one spawned `claude -p "/loom:sweep N …"` process** — `loom.role_attempt` spans are synthesized *after the fact* by the daemon re-parsing that session's transcript/checkpoints, not by spawning one child per phase. So there is exactly one live env-var parent context available at spawn time (the sweep root), and mirroring `LOOM_TRACEPARENT` into `TRACEPARENT` gives Claude Code's own LLM/tool spans the correct parent for free — no new plumbing needed to pick "the right" context. Word the AC as "matches `LOOM_TRACEPARENT`'s value", not "matches the role-attempt span".

**Independently-scheduled role-runner ticks are explicitly out of scope.** `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/launch.rs::run_role_with_timeout` never calls `observability::tracing::prepare_child` — per `defaults/docs/tracing.md` § "Role-runner ticks join stories after the fact (#9168)", a Judge/Curator/Champion/Doctor tick run outside a sweep is deliberately its own root trace, stitched to a story after the fact by scanning the tick's `gh`-mutating actions, not via a live parent env var. There is nothing to mirror there today. Wiring live trace-context propagation into the role-runner dispatch path would be new plumbing (a bigger, separate design decision — whether/how to give ticks a real-time parent instead of after-the-fact stitching) and should be its own follow-up issue if wanted; do not fold it into this one.

### Item 2's config block: reuse the existing `observability.*` precedence, in Rust

`loom-daemon/src/observability/mod.rs` already defines the exact "env > config > default" pattern this issue asks for, for Loom's own OTLP export: `ENABLED_ENV = "LOOM_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED"` / `resolve_enabled`, `ENDPOINT_ENV = "LOOM_OBSERVABILITY_ENDPOINT"` / `resolve_endpoint`, `EXPORTER_ENV` / `resolve_exporters`. Nest the new opt-in under the same `observability` config block (e.g. `observability.claudeCodeTelemetry.enabled`, exact naming is Builder's call) and **reuse `resolve_endpoint(config)` as the default OTLP endpoint** for the injected `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` unless a more specific override is added — this is the same "host-local edge" the daemon's own OTLP sink already targets, so no new endpoint-config surface is needed. Per `.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md` (new executable logic is a `loom-daemon` subcommand, not a new `.sh`), implement this as a new Rust function (a sibling module under `loom-daemon/src/observability/`, called from `spawn_process.rs` right after the existing `prepare_child` call) rather than adding logic to `spawn-claude.sh`.

**Verify the exact env vars/values against current Claude Code docs before implementing** (confirmed 2026-09-27 against code.claude.com/docs monitoring-usage):
- `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` — master switch, required.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1` — required for `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` to do anything.
- `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp`.
- **`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`** — not named in the original issue body, but the docs mark it **required when using OTLP** (`grpc` / `http/json` / `http/protobuf`, no silent default). Omitting it is a real risk: the feature would look correctly wired (all the vars a test checks for "present") while silently exporting nothing. Set it explicitly to match whatever the host-local edge actually accepts (check the daemon's own OTLP sink config/`endpoint_policy.rs`, which only validates `http`/`https` schemes, for the matching convention) and add it to the acceptance criteria below.
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (generic) or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` (traces-only) — either is fine since only traces are in scope; prefer the generic form unless metrics/logs export is a concern later.
- `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` — optional, its own separate sub-toggle, never bundled into the master enable. This is the var the original issue's "never put prompt or user-content logging behind a default-on switch" warning applies to most directly (it gates Bash command/tool-input capture) — keep it default-off even when the rest of the block is on.
- Non-issue, confirmed not needed here: `CLAUDE_CODE_PROPAGATE_TRACEPARENT` only affects whether the `traceparent` HTTP header is forwarded to the model API through a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` proxy — unrelated to parenting Claude Code's own local spans, which happens purely by reading `TRACEPARENT` from the environment. No action needed even though Loom's credential-proxy path (`worker proxy-exec --docker-workspace`) does swap in a proxied `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`.
- Docs also confirm `TRACEPARENT` is read "in Agent SDK and `-p` sessions only; interactive CLI sessions ignore [it] to avoid inheriting ambient values" — the daemon always spawns `claude -p "…"`, so this propagation path is live for every sweep dispatch.

### Found gap: the containerized dispatch path silently strips these vars

`defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh`'s docker-containment path (`runtimes.containment.enabled`, opt-in, off by default) builds the container's env with an explicit forwarding allowlist, not a passthrough:

```bash
# defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh, ~line 813-819
while IFS='=' read -r _containment_var _; do
    case "$_containment_var" in
        LOOM_* | CLAUDE_* | SAFEHOUSE* | CODEX_* | GH_TOKEN | GITHUB_TOKEN)
            _containment_env+=(-e "$_containment_var")
            ;;
    esac
done < <(env)
```

A bare `TRACEPARENT` and every `OTEL_*` var fail this pattern (no matching prefix), so on any fleet host running containerized dispatch, both this issue's `TRACEPARENT` mirror and the entire opt-in OTel block would be silently dropped before reaching the containerized `claude` process — Claude Code would emit no spans at all, with no error, while the same host's bare-metal dispatch works fine. This is exactly the kind of gap that passes ordinary tests and review unseen (containment is off by default, so the default CI/test path never exercises it) — **extend the case pattern to also match `TRACEPARENT` and `OTEL_*`** as part of this issue, not a follow-up.

### Overlap check (no direct conflicts found)

Checked the three in-flight items named in scope: issue #9034 (open PR #9214, `cli/dispatch.rs` / `daemon_service.rs` / work_finder), issue #9056 (open PR #9216, `sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs`), issue #9122 (currently `loom:building`, no PR yet, `script_helpers/sweep_experiment.rs`). None touch `observability/tracing.rs`, `sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs`, or `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh` — no direct file conflict. `sweep_registry/` is a hot directory with #9216 also landing there; rebase onto current `main` immediately before opening the PR. Related open issues #9079 (deferred D33 provenance-marker follow-up — `lease_ensure.rs`/`worktree_ops/gh.rs`, unrelated surface) and #9204 (per-model token breakdown on `loom.runtime.usage` — `observability/runtime_usage.rs`, an `observability/` sibling but a distinct span/file) — both unrelated, no action needed beyond awareness.

### Acceptance criteria (supersedes the original issue's list)

- [ ] `loom-daemon/src/observability/tracing.rs::prepare_child` also exports a standard `TRACEPARENT` env var whenever it sets `LOOM_TRACEPARENT`, with the same value (`saved.context.traceparent()`) and the same `env_remove` on the disabled/error paths. Test: extend the table-driven test `actual_propagation_hook_handles_enabled_disabled_and_invalid_configuration` in `loom-daemon/src/observability/tracing/tests.rs` to assert `TRACEPARENT == LOOM_TRACEPARENT` in the enabled case and absent in every disabled/invalid case.
- [ ] With the new Claude-Code-OTel opt-in **off** (the default), a spawned sweep child's environment is unchanged from pre-#9215 behavior except for the added `TRACEPARENT` above — none of `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (or the `_TRACES_ENDPOINT` variant), `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS` are present. Test: unit test asserting an explicit env diff.
- [ ] With the opt-in **on** (config or env override) and a valid resolved endpoint, the spawned child's environment carries `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp`, an explicit `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, and an OTLP endpoint resolved through the same precedence chain as `observability.endpoint`/`LOOM_OBSERVABILITY_ENDPOINT` (reusing `resolve_endpoint`) unless a more specific override is set. Test: unit test for the "opt-in on" case.
- [ ] `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS` has its own independent sub-toggle, default off, never turned on merely by enabling the rest of the block. Test: unit test asserting it is absent with the master toggle on but the sub-toggle untouched.
- [ ] The new opt-in's precedence is env > config > default (`false`), mirroring `resolve_enabled`'s existing pattern. Test: unit test exercising all three tiers.
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh`'s containment env-passthrough case pattern (`_containment_env` loop) is extended to forward `TRACEPARENT` and `OTEL_*` into the container. Test: extend `defaults/scripts/tests/test-spawn-claude-credential-proxy.sh` (matching its existing `assert_contains "-e VARNAME " "$docker_log" ...` style) asserting the built `docker run` argv includes `-e TRACEPARENT` and `-e OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` when those are present in the parent shell's environment.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/tracing.md` (the current source of truth for the `LOOM_TRACEPARENT` propagation mechanism) documents the standard-`TRACEPARENT` mirror and the new opt-in config block; add only short pointers from `defaults/docs/observability.md` (config-block reference) and `defaults/docs/trace-identity.md` if needed rather than duplicating detail. None of these three docs are on `scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` (not yet frozen), so there is room, but keep additions proportionate.

### Explicitly out of scope

- Wiring live `prepare_child`-style trace-context propagation into `role_runner/launch.rs` for independently-scheduled ticks (Judge/Curator/Champion/Doctor outside a sweep). No existing context to mirror there today; a separate issue if wanted.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PROPAGATE_TRACEPARENT` / propagating trace headers through the credential-proxy's `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` swap to the model API — unrelated to this issue's goal (local span parenting).
- Any change to `claude-wrapper.sh` — it forwards argv/env through via `exec` and needs no change for this issue; it is also already on the file-size-ratchet baseline (1657 lines, frozen) and best left untouched.

### Affected files

- `loom-daemon/src/observability/tracing.rs` (+ `tracing/tests.rs`) — `TRACEPARENT` mirror.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/mod.rs` and a new sibling module — opt-in Claude Code OTel env config + resolution (Rust, per shell-language-policy).
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs` — call site for the new opt-in injection, alongside the existing `prepare_child` call.
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh` — one-line containment allowlist fix.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-spawn-claude-credential-proxy.sh` — new assertions for the allowlist fix.
- `defaults/docs/tracing.md`, `defaults/docs/observability.md`, `defaults/docs/trace-identity.md` — doc updates.

### Test plan

- `cargo test -p loom-daemon observability::tracing` (unit tests above) — **run this only on the remote build box, never on the Mac** (see the operator's own standing note on Loom's remote-cargo policy).
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-spawn-claude-credential-proxy.sh` (and `test-spawn-claude.sh` if the bare-metal env-forwarding path needs a matching assertion).
- Manual: with the opt-in enabled against a real host-local OTel edge, confirm `claude_code.llm_request` / `claude_code.tool` spans land under the sweep's `loom.sweep` span in the backend (out of scope to automate; note it as a manual verification step, not a blocking CI check).

issues.title: feat: one dispatch_plan() that owns the order Loom will work in, published fleet-wide (so dashboards never re-derive candidate_cmp)
issues.body:
## Problem

Each daemon's work-finder tick ranks its own ready issues with `candidate_cmp` and publishes `rank` in `queue.snapshot` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/ready_queue.rs`). That rank is real, but it has three gaps:

- **Per host only.** No fleet-wide order exists across hosts that manage overlapping repos.
- **Ready issues only.** Issues that are curated or still in triage have no rank.
- **Reflects only the last tick.** Sharding (`dispatcher-repo-sharding.md`), repo caps (`repo_cap.rs`) and capacity are applied to dispatch, but the snapshot doesn't say what the next ticks will take.

Dashboards that want to show "what will Loom work on next, in order" currently re-implement `candidate_cmp` in their own code, and that copy drifts silently whenever Loom's rules change. The ordering should live in exactly one place: Loom.

## Ask

1. **`dispatch_plan()`** (name up to Loom): the ordered list of issues Loom will dispatch. It uses the *same code* as the real dispatcher (`candidate_cmp` + sharding + repo caps + capacity), not a copy. Each row has:
   - `position`, `repo`, `issue`;
   - `state` (running / next / queued / blocked);
   - the expected host/workspace, when known;
   - a `reason` naming the keys that placed it (priority, urgent, age, cap, shard).
2. **Fleet scope.** A merged order across hosts. It can come from a coordinator, or from a documented, deterministic merge rule that Loom ships as a library function, so consumers don't invent one.
3. **Publish it** on each tick, either as a fleet position on `queue.snapshot` or as a new `dispatch.plan` record kind, so dashboards display it as-is.
4. **CLI.** `loom queue` (or similar) prints the same plan.
5. **Optional.** Define an order for pre-ready tiers (curated, triage) if Loom has one. Otherwise, state explicitly that they're unordered.

The shape is additive and optional. The downstream dashboard (2AMLogic/loom-ui) will render `position` verbatim and fall back to the per-host `rank` until this lands.

Related: #9238 (per-candidate ranking inputs in telemetry), #9244 (`loom:operator-priority`), #9017.

issues.title: [#9244 B] roles: starred-first rules in Curator/Champion/Judge/Doctor/Builder; retire loom:urgent (prompts, docs, shell)
issues.body:
Parent: #9244 (split approved by the operator into three PRs: A, B, C). This is **B: roles and `loom:urgent` retirement (prompts, docs, shell; no Rust)**.

## Goal

Every stage treats a starred (`loom:operator-priority`) issue or PR as "act now", and `loom:urgent` is retired from every prompt, doc and script so exactly one "land this ASAP" signal remains.

## Scope

### 1. Role rules for starred work (from #9244 "Semantics" and "Liveness contract" items 5 and 6, prompt side)
The canonical role files are `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/*.md`. `defaults/roles/*.md` are **symlinks** to them.
- **Curator** (`curator.md`): at the start of every pass, query starred issues first (`gh issue list --label loom:operator-priority --state open`). Curate them immediately. After curating a starred issue, promote it straight to `loom:issue`, skipping Champion's promotion evaluation (the star is the Tier-3 approval). A starred issue with **no workflow label** is treated as `loom:triage` and curated at once. Red-main-fix issues (`<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` in the body) come next, but get no promotion bypass.
- **Champion** (`champion.md`, `champion-pr-merge.md`, `champion-issue-promo.md`, `champion-common.md`): drain starred `loom:pr` PRs before the oldest-first pass (`champion.md:293` and `:295` say "oldest first"). A `mergeable` starred PR is merged on the next pass. A merge failure on a starred PR is retried at most once, then escalated. A starred PR on a merge-risk or critical-file hold (#9016) goes to the **top** of the pinned hold digest (#6877; digest logic in `champion-common.md` / `champion-held-pr-staleness.md`). Remove `loom:urgent` from issue promotion.
- **Judge** (`judge.md`) and **Doctor** (`doctor.md`): drain starred PRs before the normal oldest-first pass. Judge's bar is unchanged.
- **Builder** (`builder.md`, `builder-pr.md`): if the issue carries `loom:operator-priority`, add the same label to the PR it opens. Remove `loom:urgent` from Builder's priority order.
- **Doctor red-main filing**: when Doctor files an issue for a pre-existing failure it confirmed on `origin/main`, put `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` in the body instead of applying `loom:urgent`. Doctor's other `loom:urgent` uses ("feedback too complex" follow-ups) become plain `loom:triage`.
- **Guards unchanged, and say so in the prompts:** `loom:blocked`, `loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator-decision`, merge-risk and critical-file holds, the host-class gate and Judge's bar all still apply to starred work. The label is human-only: no role ever applies or removes it (Builder copying it onto its own PR is the one exception).
- Cover both the role-runner and the cron paths (`.github/workflows/loom-*.yml` prompts, if they restate queue order), and the interval prompts in `defaults/roles/{curator,champion,judge,doctor,builder}.json`.

### 2. Retire `loom:urgent` from `defaults/` and repo docs
`git grep -l "loom:urgent" origin/main -- defaults` lists 38 files. All of them are in scope:
- Commands: `architect.md`, `architect-patterns.md`, `architect-reference.md`, `builder.md`, `champion-issue-promo.md`, `curator.md`, `doctor.md`, `guide.md`, `help.md`, `hermit-patterns.md`, `imagine.md`, `loom.md` (all under `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/`).
- Mirrors: `defaults/.claude/agents/loom-{architect,doctor,guide}.md` and `defaults/.agents/skills/loom-{architect,builder,curator,doctor,guide,hermit-patterns,loom}/SKILL.md`. SKILL.md files are **generated**: regenerate them with `defaults/scripts/generate-agent-skills.sh` (it execs `loom-daemon generate-agent-skills`; use an installed binary and don't run cargo on the Mac). Don't hand-edit them.
- `defaults/.loom/CLAUDE.md`, then regenerate `defaults/.loom/AGENTS.md` via `defaults/scripts/generate-agents-md.sh` (`scripts/check-agents-md-sync.sh`). `defaults/.claude/README.md`.
- Role JSON: `defaults/roles/{architect,builder,doctor,guide}.json`.
- **Guide**: remove the whole top-3 duty, from the "Maximum Urgent: 3 Issues" section through "When to Apply loom:urgent". `guide.json`'s `description` ("…by managing loom:urgent labels") and `defaultIntervalPrompt` ("…update loom:urgent labels…top 3 priorities") get rewritten around Guide's remaining duties. Guide's WORK_PLAN generator emits a `section "Urgent" "Issues flagged as highest priority (\`loom:urgent\`)."` (`guide.md:~2480`). Replace it with an "Operator priority" section that **reads** `loom:operator-priority` (Guide never applies it), and regenerate `WORK_PLAN.md`'s section accordingly.
- Tests under `defaults/scripts/tests/`: `test-guide-urgency-rank.sh` (tests the retired duty; delete it or rewrite it for the read-only section), `test-guide-operator-only-exclude.sh`, `test-guide-work-plan-debounce.sh`, `test-merge-pr-verdict-label-guard.sh` (update the fixtures).
- Docs: `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md:4891` and `:10085` are incident history (reword or keep as history). The ordering text at `:1928` and `telemetry-schema.md` belong to **A**, so don't edit them here.
- Repo-level: `README.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `docs/agents.md`, `docs/workflows.md`, `docs/design/issue-332-label-state-machine.md`, `docs/philosophy/agent-archetypes.md`, `WORK_PLAN.md`. Leave `CHANGELOG.md` and `WORK_LOG.md` alone (they're history).
- Document the new label in `defaults/docs/label-state-machine.md` (installed as `.loom/docs/label-state-machine.md`) and the repo `CLAUDE.md` label state-machine line (keep `scripts/check-claude-md-budget.sh` green).

### 3. Delete `urgent-flip-guard.sh`
- Delete `defaults/scripts/urgent-flip-guard.sh` and `defaults/scripts/tests/test-urgent-flip-guard.sh`.
- Remove their `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt` entries (:459 and :487), the `defaults/scripts/tests/ci-wired.txt:203` line and the `scripts/pipefail-early-exit-baseline.txt:104` line.
- **Add both paths (and `test-guide-urgency-rank.sh`, if deleted) to `defaults/.loom-retired.list`**, or `scripts/check-retired-list-drift.sh` fails and installed repos keep orphaned copies (#8675).
- Fix the dangling comment references in `defaults/scripts/check-evaluating-staleness.sh:146` and `defaults/scripts/sweep-lease-fence.sh:277`.

### 4. Label
- Change `loom:urgent` in **both** `.github/labels.yml:147` and `defaults/.github/labels.yml` to `description: "Retired (#9244): use loom:operator-priority"`. Don't delete it yet: `sync-labels.sh` doesn't delete fleet labels, and the open issues still carry it. The operator migrates those issues by hand.

## Constraints
- **Role-prompt size ratchet:** `scripts/role-prompt-budget.txt` freezes whole-prompt budgets (builder 31065, champion 14381, curator 47166, doctor 33789, judge 56195, guide 50832 tokens), enforced by `scripts/check-role-prompt-budget.sh`. Guide's deleted top-3 duty frees room. Each other role's net change must stay within budget, so pay for the new rules by trimming `loom:urgent` text or moving detail to a sibling doc. See `.loom/docs/file-size-policy.md`.
- **Authoring discipline** (`.loom/docs/role-prompt-authoring.md`): pressure-test the Champion rule against a starred PR with a merge-risk hold (it must stay held, go to the top of the digest, and not be merged), and audit for conflicts with the existing oldest-first and hold rules.
- Parity checks: `scripts/check-docs-defaults-parity.sh`, `scripts/check-hooks-defaults-parity.sh`, `check-agents-md-sync.sh`, `check-retired-list-drift.sh`, the shell allowlist and budget checks. Resync installed copies with `./.loom/scripts/resync-installed.sh`.
- **No Rust.** Don't touch daemon-side urgent parsing (`loom-daemon/src/**`, `URGENT_LABEL`, the `urgent` wire field). A handles all of it, and `dashboard/web/`.

## Out of scope
- **A (daemon core):** the label *definition* for `loom:operator-priority`, `candidate_cmp`, the listings, overflow, red-main halt admission, telemetry, the ready-queue CLI, `daemon-reference.md` ordering text and `telemetry-schema.md`.
- **C (liveness contract and loom-ui intents):** daemon-side landing state, escalation, watchdog, blocker inheritance and intent application.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The Curator, Champion, Judge, Doctor and Builder prompts (plus their `.json` interval prompts) carry the starred-first rules above. Builder copies the label to its PR. Doctor uses the `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` marker.
- [ ] The pressure-test of a starred PR under a merge-risk hold is recorded in the PR description.
- [ ] `git grep -n "loom:urgent" -- ':!loom-daemon' ':!dashboard/web' ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!WORK_LOG.md'` finds only the retired `labels.yml` entries (and incident history, if kept verbatim). The daemon-side leftovers belong to A and its follow-up.
- [ ] Guide's prompt and `guide.json` no longer manage priority labels. WORK_PLAN's section reads `loom:operator-priority`.
- [ ] `urgent-flip-guard.sh` and its test are deleted. Allowlist, ci-wired, pipefail baseline and `.loom-retired.list` are updated.
- [ ] `loom:urgent` is marked retired in both `labels.yml` files. `label-state-machine.md` and `CLAUDE.md` mention `loom:operator-priority` (and that it isn't a hold).
- [ ] `check-role-prompt-budget.sh`, `check-claude-md-budget.sh`, `check-docs-defaults-parity.sh`, `check-agents-md-sync.sh`, `check-retired-list-drift.sh` and the shell allowlist check all pass. Installed copies are resynced.

issues.title: install.sh --full fails its own completeness check: .loom/credentials.md.example is recorded in install-metadata.json but never copied (--quick hides it)
issues.body:
## Summary

`install.sh --full` into a fresh target fails its own completeness check, because the installer records `.loom/credentials.md.example` in `install-metadata.json` but never copies it to disk. `--quick` has the same gap and **reports success anyway**, because it does not run the verification — so the bug ships silently on the path most people use.

```
Verifying all metadata-listed files exist on disk...
  MISSING: .loom/credentials.md.example
Error: 1 file(s) in install-metadata.json are missing from disk — install incomplete (see #3287)
Warning: Installation failed at step: Initialize Loom
```

## Reproduction

Loom source at `953de96a` (v0.19.423), clean `main`, target = any repo with no prior Loom install:

```sh
./install.sh --full -y /path/to/fresh-target    # fails as above, rolls back
./install.sh --quick -y /path/to/fresh-target   # "✓ Quick installation complete!"
ls /path/to/fresh-target/.loom/credentials.md.example   # ENOENT
```

Reproduced twice on two fresh clones of the same target.

## What I ruled out

- **It is shipped and tracked.** `defaults/.loom/credentials.md.example` exists (1376 bytes) and `git ls-files` returns it.
- **Not gitignored in the target.** `git check-ignore -v .loom/credentials.md.example` returns nothing after install, and the Loom-managed `.gitignore` block has no pattern matching it.
- **Not excluded by the payload lists.** `defaults/.loom-internal.list` has zero active entries (all comments); `defaults/.loom-retired.list` has no `credentials` entry.
- **Not a version regression.** `--quick` on v0.19.393 and on v0.19.423 both leave the file absent. The difference between the two flags is only whether anything checks.
- **Not target-specific.** The target's own `.gitignore` (`node_modules/`, `.wrangler/`, `.dev.vars*`, `dist/`, `*.log`, `wrangler.*.toml`, `.DS_Store`) matches nothing under `.loom/`.

So the manifest walk and the copy walk disagree: one includes the file, the other drops it.

## Why this matters beyond the one file

1. **`--full` is unusable for onboarding a new repo.** It is the reviewable path — issue, worktree, PR — and it is exactly the path you want for admitting a repo to the fleet. It fails at the last step and rolls back, so a repo cannot be onboarded the reviewable way at all.
2. **`--quick` produces a knowingly incomplete install that claims success.** This is the failure shape FLEET.md §Admission verification already documents from #469: a repo that reports healthy everywhere while something structural never landed. `fleet-admission-check.sh` checks `.loom/` is committed and non-empty — it would not catch a single missing payload file.
3. **The asymmetry is the real defect.** Whatever the copy/manifest disagreement is, `--quick` skipping the verification means the only signal is on the path people use least.

## Suggested fix direction

Find where the two walks diverge — `_emit_installed_files_manifest` / `_emit_loom_ownership_set` versus whatever materializes `.loom/` into the target — rather than special-casing this filename. A single dropped file is the symptom; the walks being able to disagree at all is the bug.

Running the same verification under `--quick` (warn, or fail) would have surfaced this at the first install rather than at the first `--full`.

## Context

Found while onboarding `2AMLogic/loom-ui` for fleet admission. No workaround applied — installing via `--quick` would have put a knowingly incomplete install into a repo about to enter fleet custodianship, which is the #469 pattern this project already has a gate for.

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

### Where the copy actually happens (verified against `origin/main` @ `953de96a`)

The failing step is named **"Initialize Loom"**, and the payload is materialized by the **Rust `loom-daemon init`**, not by `scripts/install-loom.sh`. This matches #3287, whose title names the same `init` step for the same class of defect (`.loom/scripts/lib/*.sh` silently skipped despite being recorded).

Starting points:

- `loom-daemon/src/init/file_ops.rs` — `copy_dir_with_report` (:80) and `copy_dir_with_report_filtered` (:105). The latter takes a per-file `skip: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool` predicate; the former passes `&|_| false`. Directories are walked unconditionally and the predicate decides per file.
- `loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding.rs` — the callers that materialize each tree (`:828` and around), which is where a `.loom/`-specific path list or predicate would live.
- `loom-daemon/src/init/mod.rs:765` — the other `copy_dir_with_report` call site.

**The likely shape:** `.loom/` is materialized from an enumeration that reaches subdirectories but misses top-level files inside `.loom/`, or a skip predicate excludes it. Find the enumeration that feeds the copy and compare it against whatever feeds `install-metadata.json`'s `installed_files`. **Do not special-case this filename** — the bug is that the two enumerations can disagree at all.

### Verify the fix against the asymmetry, not just the file

`--quick` and `--full` run the *same* copy. The only difference is that `--full` verifies afterwards. So a fix that makes this one file appear, without making the walks agree, leaves the next dropped file equally silent.

### Affected Files

Verified present on `origin/main` @ `953de96a`.

- `loom-daemon/src/init/file_ops.rs` — copy primitives and the skip-predicate contract.
- `loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding.rs` — the per-tree materialization callers; most likely home of the defect.
- `loom-daemon/src/init/mod.rs` — the other copy call site and where the manifest is recorded.
- `scripts/install-loom.sh` — the post-init verification that catches this (`--full` only today); the `--quick` path is where the check is missing.
- `defaults/.loom/credentials.md.example` — the dropped file (reference only; do not move or rename it to make the symptom go away).

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: a Rust test asserting the init copy enumeration and the `installed_files` manifest enumeration produce the **same set** for a fresh target. This is the regression guard — it fails for any future dropped file, not just this one.
- [ ] Automated: an init test over a fixture tree containing a top-level file inside `.loom/` (alongside subdirectories), asserting the file lands.
- [ ] Manual: `./install.sh --full -y <fresh clone>` completes without the MISSING error, and `.loom/credentials.md.example` exists afterwards.
- [ ] Manual: `./install.sh --quick -y <fresh clone>` also produces the file (proving the fix is in the copy, not in the verification).
- [ ] Edge case: a target that already has a `package.json` whose `name` is not `loom-workspace` still keeps it untouched (`file_ops.rs:72` preserve-existing semantics must not regress).
- [ ] `cargo test -p loom-daemon init` and clippy pass.

### Out of scope

Running the completeness verification under `--quick` is worth doing and is named in the problem statement, but it is a **second** change: it turns a silent failure into a loud one, it does not fix the copy. If it lands here, it must not be the only fix.

## Verified corrections

- **2026-09-26, verified against `origin/main` @ `953de96a`**: `defaults/.loom/credentials.md.example` is tracked (`git ls-files` returns it, 1376 bytes). It is NOT in `defaults/.loom-internal.list` (which has zero active entries, all comments) or `.loom-retired.list`. After a `--quick` install, `git check-ignore -v .loom/credentials.md.example` in the target returns nothing. So the file is shipped, un-excluded and un-ignored, and still absent.
- **2026-09-26, reproduced twice** on two fresh clones of the same target, on Loom v0.19.393 and v0.19.423: `--quick` leaves the file absent on both and reports success; `--full` fails its verification. Not a version regression.
- **2026-09-26, NOT yet traced**: the exact line at which the enumeration drops the file. The module pointers above come from reading the call graph, not from stepping through a failing run.

issues.title: feat(merge): default Loom merges to merge commits — preserve full commit history
issues.body:
## Context

Operator decision (2026-09-26): from now on, Loom merges PRs with **real merge commits** across the board — not squash.

Rationale: squash is strictly worse for a fleet whose job is shipping code. It discards the branch's actual history — every intermediate commit, its authors, timestamps, and review journey. We need to know **what happened and when**; agent history in particular must never be squashed away. Multi-commit agent work (implement → judge feedback → doctor cycle) is exactly the record the blame/audit tooling joins on (`blame-issue.sh`).

## What changes (every Loom merge-strategy decision point)

Today the default is squash-first everywhere:

1. Runtime auto-detect `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-merge-method.sh` (`forge_detect_merge_method`, used by `merge-pr.sh`): preference **squash > merge > rebase**, fail-open to `squash` on probe failure / degenerate all-disabled.
2. Daemon resolver `loom-daemon/src/forge_merge_method.rs` (`forge merge-method`): same cascade + fail-open.
3. `loom-daemon auto-merge --method` CLI default: `squash`.
4. `forge_merge_pr`'s default method arg (`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh`): `squash`.
5. Installer bootstrap twin `detect_merge_method` (`scripts/install/forge-detect.sh`): same cascade + fail-open.
6. Installer repo-settings fallback (`scripts/install/setup-repository-settings.sh`): a repo with no strategy enabled gets **squash-only** enabled.
7. `blame-issue.sh` offline PR resolution only recognises squash-style `(#PR)` subjects, so under a merge-commit history every line would fall through to the slow GitHub API lookup.

This flips the default to merge commits at all of the above:

- Preference becomes **merge > rebase > squash**; fail-open becomes `merge` — a loud merge failure on a repo that genuinely disallows merge commits beats silently rewriting history.
- Installer fallback enables **merge-commit-only** (GitHub: `allow_merge_commit` only; Gitea: `allow_merge_commits` + `default_merge_style: "merge"`).
- `auto-merge --method` default becomes `merge`.
- `blame-issue.sh` also resolves `Merge pull request #N …` subjects offline.
- An explicit `--merge-method` is still honored and validated against the repo's actually-allowed set (unchanged, #8845).
- Existing repos are NOT silently reconfigured (the #7754 respect-existing guarantee stays); switching an operator-configured repo is an operator action. The dogfood repo (rjwalters/loom) is switched live by the operator as part of this PR.

## Out of scope

- Squash-aware cleanup/reaper logic (branch-landed checks, worktree reaping, `reconcile-stack.sh` rebase math) — already correct under merge commits.
- Per-repo config for merge method — a repo may still be rebase-only or squash-only by operator choice.
- `merge-pr.sh`'s exit-3 "head moved" guard and the "squash-merge detection trap" guardrail — unchanged; docs note where the merge-commit default relaxes the manual verification story.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `forge_detect_merge_method`, `detect_merge_method`, and `resolve_merge_method` return `merge` when the repo allows multiple strategies, and return `merge` (not `squash`) on probe failure / degenerate all-disabled.
2. `setup-repository-settings.sh` fallback enables merge-commit-only; dry-run text says so; a live PATCH for a repo that already has a strategy is byte-unchanged (respect-existing preserved).
3. `loom-daemon auto-merge --method` defaults to `merge`.
4. `blame-issue.sh` resolves `Merge pull request #N from …` subjects to PR N offline (no `gh` call).
5. Role prompts / docs that say "the repo squash-merges" are corrected (builder, builder-pr, champion, sweep wave docs, daemon-reference, reconcile-stack header); ADR records the decision.
6. Touched test suites pass; `loom-daemon generate-agent-skills --check` is green; shell budget not grown.

issues.title: [Epic #9429] story-points: points:* labels and Curator assignment
issues.body:
Parent epic: #9429. Requires: the rubric from the phase-1 issue (#9430, `defaults/docs/story-points.md`).

## Goal

Make story-point assignment part of curation: the Curator applies exactly one `points:*` label at enhancement time.

**Storage decision (adjudicated, supersedes the original body-marker proposal): points live in labels.** Labels are server-side filterable (`gh issue list --label points:3`), the labels connection is already fetched by existing queries, and the Curator already performs label mutations — so the marginal API cost is ~zero. The body alternative cannot be filtered server-side, so every points-aware workflow degrades to fetch-everything-and-regex as issue volume grows, and body rewrites race concurrent editors; both failure modes scale with throughput. When GitHub's org-level typed Issue Fields (Effort field, previewed 2026-03) are GA and daemon-readable, `points:*` → Effort is a documented one-command bulk migration — labels are that migration's explicit upstream source.

## Work

- [ ] `.github/labels.yml` (authoritative): add `points:1`, `points:2`, `points:3`, `points:5`, `points:8`, `points:13`, each documenting `Applied by: Curator only`; land via `./.loom/scripts/sync-labels.sh`
- [ ] Curator role prompt (`defaults/roles/curator.md` — the canonical copy; installed copies refresh via `resync-installed.sh`): add a short "assign story points" step to Curation Activities — pick one points label per the rubric and attach it in the same `gh issue edit` label mutation that flips the issue to `loom:curated` (no second API call); re-assignment **replaces** the prior points label rather than adding to it
- [ ] Respect the size ratchet: the prompt change is a pointer to the rubric doc, not an inlined rubric (`defaults/docs/file-size-policy.md` — role prompts may shrink, not grow)
- [ ] Rescoping path: when an issue is rescoped (relabel to `loom:triage`/`loom:curated`), the points label is updated or removed — stale points must not survive a scope change silently
- [ ] Points-aware listings use `since:`-filtered incremental sweeps; no workflow may fetch the full issue list just to read points

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A newly curated issue carries exactly one `points:*` label, applied in the Curator's existing label mutation
- [ ] `gh issue list --label points:3` returns exactly the 3-point issues — no body parsing anywhere in the workflow
- [ ] The label workflow docs mention where points sit in the curation flow
- [ ] Curator discipline keeps an issue at one points label (replace, never stack); the hard one-per-issue guard lands daemon-side in the telemetry phase

issues.title: defaults/.claude/settings.json: Bash(./scripts/**:*) allow rules are malformed (dead + startup warning)
issues.body:
## Problem

`defaults/.claude/settings.json` (and the repo's own `.claude/settings.json`) ships two Bash allow rules that current Claude Code rejects as malformed:

```json
"Bash(./scripts/**:*)",
"Bash(./.loom/scripts/**:*)",
```

Every `claude` launch in a consumer repo prints:

```
Permission allow rule (.claude/settings.json): Bash(./scripts/**:*) mixes * with the trailing :* prefix syntax, so it is matched as a literal prefix (the * is not expanded) and matches only commands containing a literal * at that position. Replace that * with the exact value you mean.
Permission allow rule (.claude/settings.json): Bash(./.loom/scripts/**:*) mixes * with the trailing :* prefix syntax, ...
```

Beyond the noise, the rules are **dead**: the `**` is matched literally, so they never allow `./scripts/...` or `./.loom/scripts/...` invocations -- agents get the permission prompts the rules were meant to suppress.

Observed in rjwalters/kicad-tools (patched locally). Note: this issue was spuriously auto-closed at 2026-09-29T03:35Z by a cross-reference from unrelated PR #5796 and reopened by the operator; the bug is still live on `main`.

## Fix

Replace with the wildcard form (`*` matches any sequence, including `/` and spaces):

```json
"Bash(./scripts/*)",
"Bash(./.loom/scripts/*)",
```

## Curator findings (verified against `origin/main` @ 83abe1f97)

- A repo-wide scan for any `Bash(...)` rule mixing `*` with a trailing `:*` (`git grep -nE '\*[^)"]*:\*\)'`) finds exactly these four lines and nothing else (the only other hit, `defaults/scripts/lib/worktree-forge-pr-check.sh:88` `*@*:*)`, is a shell `case` pattern, not a permission rule). No other `defaults/` settings/JSON file carries a malformed rule.
- `.claude/settings.json` is **independent**, not a resync-installed copy of `defaults/.claude/settings.json`: it is a separate tracked file (it additionally carries loom's own `hooks` block) and `resync-installed.sh` only *checks* its hook wiring, never rewrites its permissions. Both files must be edited by hand.
- `defaults/.claude/settings.json` is not `include_str!`-embedded anywhere; no test fixture, snapshot, or shell test asserts these exact rule strings.
- **Install-merge gap (why editing defaults alone is insufficient for existing consumers):** on reinstall/update, `loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding.rs` `merge_settings_json` -> `merge_permissions` (~L648) **unions** `permissions.allow` with exact-string dedup. A consumer that already has the malformed strings from a prior install would get the new `Bash(./scripts/*)` rules *added* but keep the dead `**:*` ones, so the startup warning would persist forever. Likewise `remove_loom_permissions` (~L736, uninstall) matches the *current* defaults exactly, so after this change it would no longer strip the legacy strings. Fix: a small `LEGACY_LOOM_PERMISSIONS` list (`"Bash(./scripts/**:*)"`, `"Bash(./.loom/scripts/**:*)"`) that `merge_permissions` drops from the existing `allow` array before the union, and that `remove_loom_permissions` also removes. Only these two exact Loom-shipped strings are removed -- never any user-authored rule.

## Affected Files

- `defaults/.claude/settings.json` -- lines 10-11: replace the two rules.
- `.claude/settings.json` -- lines 93-94: replace the two rules.
- `loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding.rs` -- `merge_permissions` / `remove_loom_permissions`: strip the two legacy strings.
- `loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding/tests.rs` -- unit tests for the legacy strip (see test plan).
- `defaults/.claude/README.md` and `.claude/README.md` -- line 34 "Repo scripts" bullet: change `` `./scripts/**` and `./.loom/scripts/**` `` to `` `./scripts/*` and `./.loom/scripts/*` `` so the doc names the real rule form (keep the two READMEs identical).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `git grep -nE 'Bash\([^)]*\*[^)"]*:\*\)' -- defaults .claude` returns no output (no Bash rule mixes `*` with trailing `:*` in any shipped or repo settings).
2. `grep -c '"Bash(./scripts/\*)"' defaults/.claude/settings.json .claude/settings.json` reports `1` for each file, and the same for `"Bash(./.loom/scripts/\*)"`.
3. `jq -e . defaults/.claude/settings.json .claude/settings.json >/dev/null` exits 0.
4. `merge_settings_json` applied to an existing settings value whose `permissions.allow` contains `Bash(./scripts/**:*)` and `Bash(./.loom/scripts/**:*)` plus a user rule (e.g. `Bash(make:*)`) yields an `allow` array that contains `Bash(./scripts/*)`, `Bash(./.loom/scripts/*)`, and `Bash(make:*)`, and contains neither legacy string -- asserted by a new unit test.
5. `remove_loom_permissions` removes the two legacy strings as well as the current defaults, and leaves user rules intact -- asserted by a new unit test.
6. `cargo test -p loom-daemon init::scaffolding` passes (including existing `test_remove_loom_permissions*` and merge tests).
7. `diff defaults/.claude/README.md .claude/README.md` shows no new divergence introduced by this change, and neither README mentions `scripts/**` in the "Repo scripts" bullet.

## Test Plan

- Run AC 1-3 and 7 as shell commands.
- Add the two unit tests in `loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding/tests.rs` (next to `test_remove_loom_permissions`, ~L2339) and run `cargo test -p loom-daemon init::scaffolding`.
- Optional manual check: in a scratch consumer repo with the old rules, run a Loom install/update and confirm `claude` no longer prints the "mixes * with the trailing :* prefix syntax" warning.

## Out of Scope

- Changing any other permission rule or the `deny` list.
- A general linter for malformed permission rules (could be a follow-up if more appear).

issues.title: docs(security): ci-integration.md shows a script-injection pattern; role workflows need an enable-at-your-own-risk warning
issues.body:
## Problem

1. `defaults/docs/ci-integration.md` (~L95-97) -- shipped to every install -- shows `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` / `.body` interpolated directly inside a `run:` script. GitHub expands those before the shell runs, so PR-author-controlled text becomes shell source. This is the script-injection pattern GitHub's own hardening guide warns against, and readers copy examples verbatim.
2. `.github/workflows/loom-{judge,champion,curator,guide,auditor}.yml` are dispatch-only with the `schedule:` trigger commented out as a "fork opt-in". Nothing warns that enabling them runs an agent with permissive tool access and a write-scoped token over outsider-authored issue/PR text on a public repo.

## Fix

- Rewrite the doc example to pass the values through `env:` and reference `"$PR_TITLE"` / `"$PR_BODY"`, with a short note on why.
- Add a header comment to each of the five role workflows stating the trust tradeoff: only enable where you accept it, and never under `pull_request_target`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] No `${{ github.event.* }}` user-controlled expression inside `run:` in `defaults/docs/ci-integration.md`
- [ ] All five role workflows carry the warning header

issues.title: bug(outcome-journal): rework.rs drops the reflog UTC offset, shifting rework events and failing the reflog test on non-UTC hosts
issues.body:
## Problem

`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal/rework.rs` (~L152-157) parses a git reflog timestamp with `NaiveDateTime::parse_from_str(..., "...%z")` and then calls `.and_utc()`. `NaiveDateTime` parsing accepts `%z` but discards the offset, so a local timestamp like `2026-09-29 10:00:00 -0700` is recorded as `10:00Z` instead of `17:00Z` -- every reflog-derived rework event is shifted by the host's UTC offset.

Visible symptom: `sweep_registry::outcome_journal::rework::tests::a_real_rebase_is_observed_from_the_worktree_reflog` fails on any non-UTC host (it passes in CI only because runners are UTC). Reported on PR #9511 before it merged.

## Fix

Parse with offset-aware `DateTime::parse_from_str` and convert with `.with_timezone(&Utc)`. Add a unit test that pins a non-UTC offset, and verify the existing reflog test under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` and `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Reflog timestamps with a non-zero offset are converted to the correct UTC instant
- [ ] The reflog test passes under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` and `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`
